From romance, longing and movie-inspired moments on the city’s beaches to the dramatic shift from celluloid reels to digital projection, Chennai’s relationship with the big screen has constantly evolved. At the heart of that journey are theatres that became landmarks in their own right, including Royapettah’s Pilot Theatre. Episode 4 of Chennai Canvas, for Madras Week, revisits these spaces, memories and technological changes to explore why, for generations of Chennai residents, the city and cinema have been inseparable.

stories.title: Girl slaps men 14 times with slippers over harassment:Kidnapping attempt in Bijnor; accused seen limping and apologising at police station
stories.summary: In Bijnor, a student returning from tuition beat up two young men for harassing her. Both of them were trying to force her onto a motorcycle. The enraged student then took off her slippers and struck the two boys 14 times with them in 25 seconds in the middle of the road. During the beating, both young men were seen trying to hide their faces. The incident took place in the Sherkot area on Tuesday evening, and a video of it surfaced around 5 pm. on Wednesday. Police arrested one of the accused based on a complaint filed by the student's father. He was seen limping and apologising at the police station. Read the full incident… The girl’s father, a resident of a village in the Ramsahaywala area, filed a police complaint alleging that his daughter was harassed. He said his 16 year old daughter was returning home on a bicycle after tuition on Tuesday evening. Near the Ramsahaywala crossing, two youths from the village, Ahte­sham and Zeeshan, allegedly began following her on a motorcycle. Tried to force her onto the motorcycle According to the girl’s father, the two youths allegedly harassed his daughter near a garden in the village and tried to forcibly take her away on their motorcycle. The girl raised an alarm to escape, following which people from the area reached the spot. She then took off her slippers and started beating the two youths. Video of youths being beaten surfaces A video of the two youths being beaten has also surfaced. The footage shows some people and a red motorcycle near bushes along the roadside. A girl wearing a white kurta, blue jeans and a dupatta appears angry over something in the video. She then picks up her slipper and starts beating the boys standing in front of her. The boys cover their faces with their hands and try to move away from her. The youths can also be seen apologizing to the girl and promising not to repeat their mistake. Police arrest one accused Based on the victim's father's complaint, the police registered a case and arrested Ehtesham, a resident of Ramsahaywala. A video of the accused's arrest has surfaced. In it, he can be seen limping at the police station. He is seen apologizing with folded hands before the police. He says that he will not make such a mistake again. The police are searching for the other accused, Zeeshan. The police said that a team is conducting raids to find him. He will be arrested soon.

stories.title: UP TET result out, 62,000 teachers fail:Govt to hold special exam to save their jobs
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission (UPESSC) released the UPTET 2026 results on Wednesday. According to the results, 80.07% of candidates passed the primary-level exam (Classes 1–5), while 71.85% passed the upper-primary exam (Classes 6–8). The UPTET 2026 exam was held on July 2, 3 and 4 at 955 centres across 60 districts in five shifts. A total of 19.94 lakh candidates had registered for the examination. 5.71 lakh candidates successful at the primary level A total of 7,13,648 candidates appeared for the primary-level examination. Of these, 5,71,435 candidates have been declared successful. The overall pass percentage at this level was 80.07. 7.59 lakh candidates pass at the upper primary level Of the 1,057,021 candidates who appeared for the upper primary-level examination, 7,59,513 candidates were successful. The overall pass percentage at this level was recorded at 71.85. Performance of working teachers also better Of the 1,22,405 working teachers who appeared for the primary-level examination, 93,387 were successful, representing a total of 76.29 per cent. Meanwhile, of the 1,46,394 working teachers who appeared for the upper primary-level examination, 1,13,384 were successful, with a pass percentage of 77.45. Results prepared using the normalisation method The Commission's Deputy Secretary stated that the examination was conducted in multiple shifts and that the number of candidates was also quite large. Therefore, to balance the potential differences in the difficulty levels of the question papers across various shifts, the comparative evaluation (Normalisation) method was adopted under Point No. 09 of the . Based on this, the candidates' marks were normalised and the final results were prepared. Scorecard Available on the Website Candidates can view their results, scorecards, and cutoff marks by visiting the commission's official website, UPESSC. The commission has also provided a helpline and email facility for technical assistance and other information. Detailed information is available on the website. The UP TET 2026 results have been released. The Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission (UPESSC) released the figures at 9 p.m. on Wednesday. More than 13 lakh candidates cleared the primary (Classes 1–5) and junior (Classes 6–8) level exams. The primary-level pass percentage was 80.07%, while the junior-level pass percentage was 71.85%. A total of 2,06,771 teachers passed the TET exam, while 2,68,799 teachers appeared to protect their jobs. As many as 62,028 teachers failed. The state government is now preparing to conduct a special TET exam for these teachers to help them retain their jobs. The TET exam was held on July 2, 3 and 4 at 955 centres across 60 districts in the state. It was conducted in five shifts, two for the primary level and three for the upper-primary or junior level. A total of 19,94,661 candidates registered for the exam this year. Now know the key details… Primary-level candidates recorded the highest pass rate Result prepared using normalization system Commission Deputy Secretary Manoj Kumar said the exam was conducted in multiple shifts and had a large number of candidates. Since the difficulty level of question papers varied across shifts, the commission used a normalization process to eliminate the disparity. The final result was prepared after bringing the scores of all candidates to a comparable level through this process. CTET date postponed, UP TET-failed teachers can also appear The CTET exam date has been postponed. The CBSE will now conduct the exam on September 6. Teachers who failed the UP TET will also be eligible to appear for the CTET. If they clear the CTET, their jobs will not be at risk. The last date to apply for the CTET is September 1. Meanwhile, the Uttar Pradesh government is preparing to conduct a special TET exam for these teachers, giving them another opportunity to qualify. The notification for the special exam is expected to be issued in September.

Police are attempting to identify the attackers using CCTV footage. Ankit gained widespread popularity with his song 'Bhari Court Mein Goli Maarenge Meri Jaan'. stories.title: Rajnath Singh to stay in Lucknow from August 28-30:To inaugurate Fragrance Park, unveil Rani Avantibai Lodhi statue
stories.summary: Defence Minister and Lucknow MP Rajnath Singh will be in Lucknow from August 28 to 30, during which he will attend several programmes and inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for development projects across the city. According to Lucknow BJP president Anand Dwivedi, Singh will arrive at Lucknow airport at 4.30 pm on August 28. He will then visit bereaved families in Sadar Bazaar, New Ganeshganj and the Mahanagar area. He is scheduled to reach his residence on Kalidas Marg at around 6.20 pm. To attend Ambedkar University convocation On August 29, Singh will attend the 11th convocation ceremony of Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University at 11.30 am. At 1 pm, he will inaugurate a senior citizens’ home in Vishal Khand, Gomti Nagar. At 4 pm, he will inaugurate the Fragrance Park at Lajpat Nagar crossing. During the programme, he will also unveil statues of Lala Lajpat Rai and Shaheed Bhagat Singh. He will attend other programmes before returning to his Kalidas Marg residence at around 6.05 pm. Development projects in Lucknow Cantonment On August 30, Singh will reach Dilkusha Lawn at 10.55 am and listen to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Mann Ki Baat programme at 11 am. He will then inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for several development projects in the Lucknow Cantonment area. At 12.30 pm, he will unveil a statue of Rani Avantibai Lodhi near Prerna Sthal on the Dubagga-Sitapur Road bypass. At 4 pm, Singh will attend the Prime Minister’s Skill Education and Training Development workshop at Hotel Taj. He will leave for Lucknow airport at 5.25 pm and is scheduled to depart for Delhi at around 6.30 pm.

stories.title: VIDEO|Girl appeals to DM, 'Uncle, please get our road repaired':Potholes fill with rainwater, asks how she will reach school
stories.summary: A four-year-old girl in Barabanki appeals to the district magistrate to repair the road near her home, saying potholes fill with dirty rainwater and make it difficult to reach school Girl appeals to DM in video A video of a four-year-old KG student in Barabanki has surfaced in which she appeals to the district magistrate (DM) to get the road near her home repaired. Standing on the road she uses to go to school, the girl, Ayesha Raj, says, “DM uncle, please get the road near our house repaired. There are very big potholes. Dirty rainwater collects here. It is very difficult to travel on this road.” The video was recorded two days ago. After it surfaced, Barabanki DM Ishan Pratap Singh took note of the issue and said SDM Nawabganj Gunjita Jaiswal would be sent to inspect the spot. He said necessary action would be taken after assessing the condition of the road. See 3 pictures- Road repair begins after DM’s order Road repair work began on Wednesday. A team started filling the potholes and improving the condition of the road. Ayesha lives in Nabinganj in the Nagar Kotwali area with her family. She studies in KG at Anand Bhawan School near Crystal Garden. Her father, Raj Mohammad, takes her to school every morning. The recent heavy rain has worsened the condition of the unpaved road. Large potholes have formed at several places and remain filled with rainwater. Raj Mohammad said his daughter uses the same road to go to school every day. She was upset after seeing its poor condition and learned that the district magistrate could help resolve the problem. He said Ayesha insisted on speaking to the DM herself. “Two days ago, I was recording a video of the road to raise a complaint. Ayesha said she wanted to speak too. She then appealed to the DM in the video to get the road repaired,” he said. SDM reaches spot with JCB On the DM’s instructions, SDM Nawabganj Gunjita Jaiswal reached the spot with a JCB at around 2:30 pm on Wednesday. Based on Ayesha’s complaint, repair work was started at the site. The SDM said all the potholes on the road were being filled. She added that PVC work would also be carried out on the road as directed by the DM.

stories.title: Muslim activist Nazia Khan receives throat-slitting threat:Made children urinate on poster; had commented on Prophet Muhammad
stories.summary: Supreme Court lawyer and Muslim activist Nazia Ilahi Khan has received a threat to have her throat slit. She filed a police complaint at Indirapuram police station in Ghaziabad on Tuesday night. Nazia has alleged that a man named Shahil Ahmed abused her on his Instagram account and threatened her. She also alleged that he made children urinate on posters carrying her photograph, filmed the act and uploaded the video on Instagram. Nazia is associated with the BJP’s Minority Morcha and is originally from Kolkata. She has spoken publicly about Islamic customs and practices. She has also submitted complaints to Uttar Pradesh Home Secretary Sanjay Prasad and ATS officials. Threat to slit her throat According to Nazia’s complaint, an Instagram account named Shahil Ahmed used abusive language while commenting on her photograph and threatened to slit her throat. She alleged that the accused also made statements about harassing her through minor children and inciting violence against her. He allegedly shared an offensive video on his Instagram account showing a poster carrying her photograph. Nazia said she feared for her life and sought action against the accused. Police have registered a case under relevant sections related to criminal threats and the Information Technology Act. They have also started examining the Instagram account. Nazia commented on Prophet Muhammad two months ago In June 2026, Nazia Khan made comments during a podcast about the Muslim community, the rights of Muslim women, Prophet Muhammad and Aisha. After a video of her remarks was shared on social media, several Muslim organisations and individuals expressed their anger. Complainants alleged that Nazia had deliberately made remarks that hurt the religious sentiments of Muslims. An FIR was also registered against Nazia on August 25 in connection with the remarks. Who is Nazia Ilahi Khan? From lawyer to politician, gained recognition through triple talaq case Nazia Ilahi Khan has been in the spotlight for her work as a lawyer in the Supreme Court and on issues concerning women’s rights. She has also been politically active. She was previously a spokesperson for the Trinamool Congress before later joining the BJP. Born in Kolkata, studied law Nazia was reportedly born in Kolkata on February 11, 1989. She studied BA and LLB at the University of Calcutta before beginning her legal career. According to publicly available information, she works as an advocate in the Supreme Court. Her name also came up in connection with the triple talaq case involving Ishrat Jahan. She raised issues related to women’s rights and gender equality during the case and later became vocal on issues concerning women. Political journey from TMC to BJP Nazia began her political career as a spokesperson for the Trinamool Congress. She later joined the Bharatiya Janata Party and represented the party’s views at various forums in West Bengal. According to publicly available information, her husband died when she was around 20 years old. She subsequently raised her son, Yamin Khan, who is also reportedly a lawyer. Keeps personal life private Public information about Nazia’s parents and other family members is limited. She has generally kept her personal life away from public discussion. Police begin probe into Instagram account ACP Indirapuram Suryabali Maurya said a case had been registered under relevant sections based on Nazia Ilahi Khan’s complaint. He said police had started investigating the Instagram account allegedly used to issue threats and post abusive comments against Nazia. Police are working to identify the accused and determine further legal action.

stories.title: Noida teen killed in attack similar to Surya case:Mother refuses last rites, demands encounter of three minor suspects
stories.summary: A murder in Noida has drawn comparisons with the Surya murder case in Ghaziabad. Thirteen-year-old Ayush Shukla was allegedly killed by three minor acquaintances after they lured him out of his home on the pretext of a birthday party. The teenagers allegedly attacked Ayush with a knife and dumped his body in a forest to avoid being caught. Ayush’s mother and relatives have been sitting outside the post-mortem house for nearly 20 hours and have refused to take his body. More than 50 people are supporting the family, following which heavy police deployment has been made at the post-mortem facility. Mother demands justice, refuses to perform funeral Ayush’s mother, Yogmaya Shukla, said she would perform her son’s last rites only after the killers are killed in a police encounter. “I will perform my only son’s last rites only when his killers are killed in an encounter. They stabbed him repeatedly. His hands and legs have not even been found. Despite recovering the body, police did not inform us.” She appealed to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for justice. “My two daughters keep asking where Ayush is. I have no answer for them,” she said. Police have so far detained three minor suspects in connection with the murder. Ayush, a resident of Sector 20 in Noida, was a Class 7 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya in Sector 24. His father, Pankaj, has been unwell and is undergoing treatment in Lucknow. He has not yet been informed about his son’s death. See 2 photos Ayush left home for a ‘birthday party’ Yogmaya, who is originally from Lucknow, lives in a rented house in Sector 20 with her two daughters and Ayush. She works as a contractual attendant at Bhungel Community Health Centre. According to the family, Ayush left home at around 4pm on August 16 after telling his mother and sister that he was going to a friend’s birthday party. He was accompanied by two classmates from Chaura village in Sector 22. He did not return home that night. Mother kept visiting police stations When Ayush failed to return, his family began searching for him. Yogmaya said she filed a complaint at the Sector 12/22 police post on August 18. She was then directed to Sector 24 police station and later to Sector 20 police station. “I kept going from one police station and police post to another looking for my son,” she said. Decomposed body found in forest Police found the decomposed body of an unidentified boy in the Sector 54 forest on the night of August 21. The body was taken for post-mortem two days later. Police showed the family a photograph of the body on Monday night. The family visited the post-mortem house on Tuesday and identified Ayush from his sacred thread, belt and clothes. Police say dispute over money led to murder ADCP Noida Manisha Singh said the investigation so far indicates that Ayush knew the minor suspects. According to the police, the suspects called Ayush to a park on the pretext of a party. A dispute over a financial transaction broke out there, following which Ayush was allegedly killed. The three detained minors are being questioned and further legal action will be taken, police said. Police investigating key questions Investigators are trying to establish: What happened in the Ghaziabad Surya murder case? Seventeen-year-old Surya was killed in Ghaziabad on May 28, on Eid al-Adha. According to a minor suspect, the main accused, Asad, called Surya and surrounded him with his associates before allegedly attacking him with a knife. CCTV footage of the incident also emerged. Police later killed Asad in an encounter. Four other accused were arrested and sent to jail, including Asad’s father Nawab, 45, Farhan, 19, Atif, 19, and Sarik. Farhan allegedly told police that Nawab had encouraged Asad to kill Surya and had told him to “finish Surya’s story” on Eid al-Adha.

stories.title: NEET student dies by suicide:Takes step after cousin claims she’s his girlfriend; harassed her for 6 months over his one-sided love
stories.summary: A NEET aspirant allegedly died by suicide after hanging herself in her room in Kanpur on Wednesday (26 Aug) morning, with her family claiming she had been harassed for six months by her maternal cousin, who was allegedly in one-sided love with her. Her brother found her hanging from a noose after she went into the room to get dressed around 10.30 am, while the family has not yet filed a police complaint against the accused. The brother said that, “At around 10:30 a.m., his sister went into the room to get dressed. However, she did not come out for a long time.” When he looked inside through the grille, he saw her hanging from the noose. The family alleged that the son of their paternal aunt had been harassing her for six months. They said, “The accused pressured their sister to talk to him. He would tell her friends that she was his girlfriend.” The family is from Chandauli. So far, the family has not filed a complaint with the police against the accused. The incident took place in the Ganganagar area of Shyam Nagar, under the jurisdiction of Chakeri police station. Now read the details... Narendra Pratap, a resident of Sakrakarari in Dhanapur, Chandauli district, works in a private job in Delhi. His family includes his wife, Neelam Devi, two daughters, Khushboo Singh (17) and Khushi Singh, and son Abhishek Singh. They all live in a rented house in Ganganagar, located in Shyam Nagar, Chakeri, Kanpur. Khushboo was preparing for the NEET exam. Her brother Abhishek said, "Mother was performing puja in the morning. My sister Khushboo was bathing in the bathroom. She came out and went into the room to get dressed. However, she did not come out for about an hour. I called out to her, but received no response. I then looked into the room through the window and saw Khushboo hanging from a noose." This caused an uproar in the house. Hearing the noise, people from the surrounding area also reached the spot. The family members informed the police. The aunt's son lives in Gujarat Abhishek said, “My aunt's son lives in Gujarat. He had been harassing Khushbu for nearly six months. He used to call Khushbu and force her to talk to him. Three months ago, we also complained to my aunt about him.” He added, "After this, he stopped harassing Khushbu for some time, but a few days ago, he started harassing her again. He used to message Khushbu's friends and tell them that Khushbu was his girlfriend." After learning about this, Khushboo was deeply hurt. She was depressed and had also reduced her food and water intake. She has now died by suicide after hanging herself. Police investigating the allegations Chakeri police station in-charge Ajay Prakash Mishra said that, “The student's body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The family has not yet submitted a written complaint. If they do, action will be taken. stories.title: Posters against Akhilesh in UP:Samajwadi workers tear them down in Baghpat, surround SP office; allege BJP conspiracy
stories.summary: Posters targeting Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav have appeared in Baghpat, Ghaziabad and Hapur, triggering protests by Samajwadi workers. The posters carried the message, “Abuse everyone, insult everyone — this is the identity of the Samajwadi Party.” They also referred to Yadav’s remark about “turning a 25-paise coin into a rupee”. In Baghpat, Samajwadi Party workers tore down the posters after learning about them and surrounded the Superintendent of Police’s office. Around 50-60 workers staged a protest and raised slogans. When some tried to enter the SP office, security personnel stopped them, leading to a scuffle between the police and protesters. SP Suraj Rai spoke to the workers and calmed them down. He assured them that those responsible for putting up the posters would be identified and action taken within 48 hours. The protesters then called off their demonstration. SP district president Manoj Chaudhary warned that they would launch a stronger protest if no action was taken within two days. SP workers remove posters in Baghpat Posters targeting Akhilesh Yadav were spotted along the Delhi-Saharanpur Highway in Baghpat on Wednesday morning. An SP worker noticed the posters around 7 am and informed district president Manoj Chaudhary and former district president Billu Pradhan. They arrived with supporters at around 8.30 am and began removing the posters. The workers removed posters from eight locations between Vandana Chowk and Pali village. They then marched to the SP office with around 50-60 workers, raised slogans against the government and submitted a memorandum to the SP seeking action against those responsible. See the pictures Police remove posters in Ghaziabad Posters targeting Yadav were put up overnight at several locations in Modinagar and along Hapur Road in Ghaziabad. Police removed them from the locations. However, police have not yet established who put up the posters. SP district president Faizal Malik alleged that the posters were part of a BJP conspiracy to damage the party’s image ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. He claimed the move was prompted by the SP’s growing strength. Aman Yadav, national general secretary of the SP youth wing, also alleged that the BJP was worried about the growing support for the party under Akhilesh Yadav’s leadership. Posters torn down in Hapur Similar posters appeared at 8-10 locations in Hapur. SP workers tore them down and later submitted a memorandum to the SP seeking action against those responsible. Around 20-25 workers reached the SP office. SP district president Anand Gurjar said police had assured them of an investigation and action. He warned that the party workers would take to the streets if no action was taken.

stories.title: Akhilesh announces laptops for Class 12-pass girls:Says ‘Our plans are being leaked to BJP’; Dimple says, 'Don’t be bound by restrictions'
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday announced that if his party returns to power in Uttar Pradesh, it will provide a laptop to every girl who passes Class 12. He also promised an annual payment of ₹40,000 to every woman and said the party would resume distributing bicycles, as it did during its previous government. Akhilesh further announced that 26,000 schools that were shut down would be reopened if the SP forms the government again. During a press conference at the SP office in Lucknow, he also took a dig at the Yogi government's Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra Scheme, which provides free bus travel to elderly women. He said- We will have to keep our office fully shielded. Our schemes are reaching there, (the government). I do not understand how we make some plans and the information gets leaked and reaches them. As a result, free bus travel has been arranged for elderly women. Earlier, Samajwadi Party MP from Mainpuri, Dimple Yadav, appealed to women across the state, saying, “Do not follow society’s old customs or let yourselves be bound by restrictions. Break through them, pursue your goals with full determination and move forward. We are with you.” Highlights from Akhilesh's Press Conference 1. 'We will increase the amount under the Stree Samman Samriddhi Scheme' The SP chief said, “A delegation from Japan recently visited us. The government showed them the 1090 helpline and said, ‘Look at what is being done here for women's safety.’ The 1090 helpline was launched by the SP government. We never compromised on issues concerning women and will not do so if we return to power. Under the Stree Samman Samriddhi Scheme, we will increase the annual financial assistance of ₹40,000.” 2. ‘Those who understand nothing are distributing tablets’ Akhilesh said, “The laptops distributed under the SP government are still working today. Those who understand nothing are now distributing tablets. They had distributed something earlier as well, but even if you rub your finger across it, nothing works." He added, "For the BJP, women have been reduced to merely a slogan. The Women's Reservation Bill has already been passed, so why is its implementation being delayed? We demand that women's reservation be implemented from the very next election.” 3. ‘Daughters face the most injustice in Uttar Pradesh’ The SP chief said, “BJP leaders often talk about respecting women, but they should remember the Hathras victim and how her body was cremated. No one has forgotten the daughter who was running away with her books when her house was being set on fire." Further alleged, "Khushi Dubey was sent to jail and humiliated. Daughters are facing the most injustice in Uttar Pradesh. The government has nothing left except filing FIRs.” 4. 'In PDA, ‘P’ stands for prostate; it also means stomach pain' Speaking about the hijab controversy, Akhilesh said, “These people even question people's attire and decide what one can and cannot wear. The PDA slogan is meant to unite people. In PDA, ‘P’ stands for prostate; PDA also means stomach pain.” He added that if the SP returns to power, primary schools and Anganwadi centres will be made world-class. “Go and see the toilets at Janeshwar Park you will see how well the SP government built them. If you compare the infrastructure created under the SP and BJP governments, the difference will be evident.” 5. SP supported the Jantar Mantar protest from day one SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said the party had supported the Jantar Mantar protest from the very beginning. He said, “We had said from the start that this was a fight between the BJP and the CJP. Our MPs Dimple Yadav, Priya Saroj and Iqra Hasan also joined the protest and stood firmly with the students.” Dimple says, 'If we fight together, defeating BJP won’t be difficult' Speaking about the student protest, Dimple Yadav said, “After visiting Jantar Mantar, we felt that these were our own children. No one was instigating them; they were fighting for their rights." She added, "The way Sonam Wangchuk was detained and wrapped in white clothes made it look as if a dead body was being carried away. We were all deeply moved. That is why we decided to visit the students on the 20th.” She said, “When we reached there, there was a huge crowd. After crossing the barricades, we saw students being beaten with batons. The girls were crying that their clothes had been torn. As mothers and human beings, we stood our ground and encouraged the students. she continued saying, "They shattered the government's arrogance. Who would not be moved after seeing such a situation? We felt the pain of the students. If we fight together, defeating the BJP will not be difficult. This movement has proved to be a lifeline for the entire country.” The news is being updated continuously...

stories.title: Took loans in names of criminals he monitored:Also cheated people in Dubai; inside story of Gorakhpur’s fraudster cop
stories.summary: Several shocking details have emerged during the interrogation of constable Nitish Kumar Yadav, who was arrested at Delhi Airport with a ₹25,000 reward on his head. Police found that he allegedly used the pretext of police verification to collect Aadhaar and PAN details of 15 notorious criminals, history-sheeters and gangsters. He then allegedly used forged documents to obtain personal loans of ₹3-5 lakh in their names. One of those targeted was Ajay Sahni, a district-banned criminal from Maharajganj, in whose name a ₹5 lakh loan was allegedly taken. Police also suspect that Nitish may have been involved in hawala operations in Dubai and allegedly committed fraud there as well. The matter is currently under investigation. ‘He wanted to get rich through shortcuts’, says the police The investigation revealed transactions worth around ₹55 lakh in the constable’s bank accounts. Despite paying EMIs of nearly ₹1.1 lakh, he had accumulated debts of around ₹80 lakh through loans and borrowings. According to police, he went on the run in December 2024 after losing money to a gambling addiction. Police said, "He wanted to become extremely wealthy quickly, which drove him to engage in various fraudulent and illegal activities." Arrested after lookout notice A constable carrying a ₹25,000 reward, who had been absconding for two years, was arrested at Delhi airport. The SSP had issued a lookout notice against him. According to police, he arrived in Delhi on Sunday on a flight from Dubai, where airport security personnel detained him and informed Gorakhpur police. Cantt police brought him to Gorakhpur on Tuesday on transit remand. After questioning, he was sent to jail. Attempted suicide while on the run During questioning, the constable said, "He first reached the Sonauli border while evading the police and broke his mobile phone to avoid being tracked. He later attempted suicide by consuming 60 fever tablets but survived. He then contacted a friend in Lucknow and went there in search of work. For a few days, he worked carrying cardboard boxes, earning ₹100 a day. From Lucknow to Patna, Kolkata and Dubai According to the constable, he stayed in Lucknow for a few days before travelling to Patna and then Kolkata. There, he found information online about a job as a bike rider in Dubai. He travelled to Dubai through an agent in May 2025, spending around ₹75,000. He claimed that he initially stayed in hiding because he did not have a visa. Later, he obtained a work visa through the agent and began working. Contacted his sister after the accident During questioning, the constable said, “I had met with an accident in Dubai about two months ago. After that, I contacted my sister, who lives in Delhi." When he arrived at Delhi Airport on Sunday, the police arrested him. Fraud in Dubai also suspected Police found several aspects of the constable's account suspicious based on his behaviour and responses during questioning. They suspect he may have been involved in hawala transactions or other fraudulent activities in Dubai. Police are also investigating these allegations and gathering information about his overseas contacts, financial transactions and the network that helped him travel from India to Dubai. Deoria resident, first posted in Azamgarh The accused constable was identified as 33 year old Nitish Yadav, a resident of Jogaour village under Bhatpar Rani police station in Deoria. City SP Nimish Patil said, “Yadav belonged to the 2019 batch and initially joined the 20th Battalion of the PAC in Azamgarh before being transferred to the police department.” His first posting was in Maharajganj in 2023. While posted there, Yadav allegedly fraudulently obtained loans from Bank of Baroda's Betiahata, Golghar Main Branch and Medical College Road Branch in Gorakhpur. How the fraud was carried out By misusing the MoU between the Uttar Pradesh Police and the bank, Nitish allegedly prepared forged documents, including a fake police identity card, salary slips, Form 16, bank statements and employee verification reports. He then opened PSP savings accounts in the names of his alleged accomplices, Pramod Kumar Yadav, Sandeep Kumar Yadav, Laxmikant Yadav, Ajay Sahani and Sandeep Agrahari and obtained personal loans using the forged documents. The combined monthly instalments exceeded ₹1 lakh. He managed to pay the instalments for two to three months before absconding from the Maharajganj Police Lines in December 2024. Fraud case registered in Maharajganj Despite an extensive search, police could not trace him. Subsequently, Ashish Singh, Deputy Regional Head of Bank of Baroda, lodged an FIR against Nitish Yadav at Kotwali police station in Maharajganj. According to the FIR, Nitish allegedly obtained loans totalling ₹39.70 lakh from three Bank of Baroda branches ₹5 lakh from the Medical College Road branch, ₹23 lakh from the Golghar branch and ₹11.70 lakh from the Betiahata branch. The case was later transferred to Gorakhpur Cantt police station.

stories.title: SIT reaches Kanpur Municipal Corporation, questions chief engineer and XEN:Files scrutinised, several discrepancies found
stories.summary: Following the Chief Secretary’s directive, action against the Kanpur Municipal Corporation continued on Wednesday, with a police SIT team visiting the civic body to investigate alleged irregularities. The SIT, led by in-charge ADCP Dr Archana Singh, is examining records at the Chief Engineer’s office. The team is scrutinising files related to payments and firm registrations. During the investigation, discrepancies were found in documents linked to payments made to the Kaila Devi firm. SIT members are also taking photographs of documents they consider suspicious for further examination. Several Municipal Corporation officials are being questioned as part of the investigation, including Chief Engineer SFA Zaidi, XEN Diwakar Bhaskar and RK Singh. The investigation comes a day after six FIRs were registered against contractors associated with the Municipal Corporation. The civic body has also cancelled tenders worth ₹100 crore. The SIT’s investigation is continuing, with officials examining documents and seeking further details from Municipal Corporation personnel. The news is being updated.

stories.title: Bike falls into 15-ft-deep pit in Agra:Road caves in at night, water supply disrupted; residents demand barricading
stories.summary: Motorcycle fell into a 15 foot deep, 12 foot wide pothole in Agra after a section of road suddenly caved in around 3 a.m. on Tuesday night. The massive crater was discovered in the middle of the road in the morning, with the motorcycle lying inside it. The incident took place in Dhobi Pada locality near Dhankot Fountain. After receiving information, the Ward 96 councillor reached the spot around 6 a.m. and informed the Municipal Corporation, Torrent Power and police. The water supply to the affected area was shut off to prevent further danger to commuters. Local residents have demanded an investigation into the cause of the road collapse and immediate barricading of the site. Bike parked at night found in the pit in the morning According to local residents, the bike was parked near the Torrent box at night. There was no pit there at the time. A loud noise was also heard early Wednesday, but no one came outside because it was nighttime. When the residents came out of their homes in the morning, they saw a deep pit in the middle of the road. On taking a closer look, they found the bike lying inside it. The pit was so large that people from the surrounding area began gathering at the spot. Residents fear that the weakened section of the road could cave in further. They have therefore asked the administration to make safety arrangements at the site as soon as possible. Councillor had the water supply shut off After receiving information about the incident, Councillor Aarti Sharma reached the spot around 6 a.m. She informed the Municipal Commissioner, Torrent Power and the police. The water supply to the affected area was subsequently shut off to prevent the situation from worsening in case an underground pipeline had been damaged. The councillor also asked officials to investigate the cause of the road collapse and determine why the section of road caved in. She demanded immediate barricading around the pit to prevent commuters and pedestrians from falling into it. Advocate takes a dig at ‘Space Technology’ Taking a sarcastic dig at the road collapse, advocate Apoorv Sharma called it an example of “space technology.” He said the condition of the road raises serious questions about the arrangements and maintenance by the Municipal Corporation.

stories.title: Abaan’s car crashed at 130 kmph:Technical committee report reveals details; Atiq’s son died in Jhansi crash
stories.summary: Details have emerged in the death of Abaan, son of late gangster Atiq Ahmed, who was killed in a road accident in Jhansi. According to a technical committee report, Abaan’s Creta was travelling at around 130 kmph when it crashed. However, the report does not establish the exact cause of the accident and suggests that the driver may have dozed off. The committee inspected the accident site and conducted a detailed technical examination of the damaged car, including its braking system, steering, suspension, wheels, body-crush pattern, airbags and seat belts. It also checked for any mechanical fault that could have contributed to the crash. The report has been sent to police officials in Lucknow. The accident occurred around 5 a.m. on 6 August, when the car crashed into a highway divider about 70 km from Jhansi. Abaan and a friend were killed, while three others sustained serious injuries. Abaan was going to meet his brother lodged in Jhansi jail Twenty one year old Abaan had left Prayagraj to meet his elder brother Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi jail. He was travelling in a Creta with four friends and had left home around 5 a.m. on 6 August. Around 10:30 a.m., in the Poonch police station area, about 70 km from Jhansi, the car crashed into a highway divider. The impact was so severe that the car was thrown nearly 10 feet before falling down. Debris from the vehicle was scattered across nearly 40 feet of the highway, while its left side was badly damaged. All five occupants were trapped inside. Police and passersby broke open the car and rescued the occupants. Abaan, who was seated in the front, and his friend Sonu, who was sitting behind him, died on the spot. The injured Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Faruk Ahzam were taken to the medical college for treatment. Eyewitnesses and injured gave different accounts of the accident After the accident, eyewitnesses and the injured gave different accounts of what caused the crash. According to eyewitness Deepak, a calf suddenly came onto the highway, prompting the driver to swerve left to avoid it. At that moment, a motorcyclist came in front of the car, forcing the driver to swerve again, after which the vehicle crashed into the divider. However, injured passenger Umar Ahmed said a brick lying on the highway caused the driver to lose control, leading to the crash. Now, find out what the technical committee’s investigation revealed A technical investigation committee was formed under the leadership of Transport Department RI Raghav Kumar and MT (Technical) in-charge Shiv Kumar. The team thoroughly examined the car’s mechanical condition and the damage caused by the crash. The investigation found that the car’s left-front section hit a hard concrete safety barrier, causing severe deformation that extended up to the rear seat. In technical terms, this is known as front-end deformation crush, which can be extremely dangerous for a person seated in the front. Car was traveling at a speed of 130 km/h According to the committee, the car was traveling at around 130 kilometers per hour at the time of the accident. This is equivalent to approximately 36.1 meters per second. This means that even if the driver had just one second to react after an obstacle appeared ahead, the car could travel about 36 meters. Due to the high speed, as soon as the car collided with the concrete safety wall, the front crumple zone extended back to the passenger compartment. The tie rod, which controls the wheels through the steering, was also damaged in the collision. Despite the airbags deploying, Abaan could not be saved. Car jumped 10 feet after the collision According to the report, after hitting the divider, the car bounced to a height of about 10 feet and then landed on its right tire. As a result, the right wheel and suspension were suddenly subjected to an extremely high vertical impact load. In other words, when the vehicle fell to the ground, its weight suddenly shifted to the right side. This is why, despite the impact occurring on the left side, the tire and suspension on the right side of the car were also damaged. So far, the technical investigation has confirmed that the car was traveling at high speed, but the exact cause of the accident has not yet been determined. Abaan’s liver and lungs were ruptured in the crash According to the post-mortem report, the impact ruptured Abaan’s liver, lungs and spleen and fractured his ribs. He died from severe internal bleeding. Sonu, who was seated behind Abaan, suffered a fatal skull fracture. Abaan was buried beside his father Atiq’s grave Abaan was buried in Prayagraj on 8 August, beside his father Atiq Ahmed’s grave. His three brothers, Ali, Umar and Ahzam carried his bier. His mother, Shaista Parveen, did not attend the funeral. She had also been absent from the funerals of her husband Atiq and son Asad. Shaista has been on the run since 2023. The Allahabad High Court granted parole to Ali and Umar to attend their brother’s funeral. Police brought Ali from Jhansi and Umar from Lucknow, with curtains placed over their vehicles to keep their faces from being visible. It was the first time in four years that Ali and Umar had been granted parole.

stories.title: Sold potatoes to save money, studied from friend’s notes:Altaf set to become doctor, takes part in NEET counselling process
stories.summary: After the declaration of the NEET results, the counseling process is now underway. Along with the results, many inspiring stories of students are also coming to light. One such story is that of Altaf Hussain, a resident of Nawabganj tehsil in Bareilly district of Uttar Pradesh, who has cracked NEET in his 8th attempt. He has scored 563 marks. With this, he has fulfilled his dream of becoming a doctor. After passing the 12th grade, Altaf started sitting at a roadside potato stall with his father. Life was going on in a normal routine, but one night, while bringing potatoes from the market, his elder brother met with a horrific accident. This incident shook Altaf to his core. He realized that life could not be kept limited in this way, and it was from this turning point that the motivation to become a doctor ignited in his mind. Studied from friends' notes, sold potatoes to go to Kota The financial situation was not such that he could directly pay the fees of any big coaching institute. Altaf took the NEET exam for the first time in 2019 without any coaching and scored 323 marks. After this, he continued his preparation consistently. He kept studying by taking study material and notes from students in the town who had returned after studying in Kota, and by watching online lectures. In the year 2022, he secured 516 marks, while in 2023 and 2024, the marks increased to 590. However, due to the high cutoff at that time, he could not get admission to a medical college. In 2025, he obtained 501 marks. He achieved 85 percent marks in both 10th and 12th grades from the UP Board. A 2-room house and a family of 12 members Altaf's family background is full of struggles. His father, Iqbal Hussain Ansari, has only studied up to the 9th grade, and his mother, Kubra, is illiterate. Until 2015, the family lived in a mud house. Later, 12 family members lived in a two-room concrete house. Due to the marriages of eight sisters and a limited income, his father could never save money, but he did not let his son's dream break. Altaf's father, Iqbal Hussain, said, ''We never thought our son would become a doctor. We make a living by selling potatoes. Altaf worked hard, and we supported him as much as we could.''

stories.title: Owaisi opposes school Hijab restriction, calls it ‘Attack on Islam’:Mayawati says, ‘Leave the courts aside’, urges amicable resolution
stories.summary: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has strongly criticized the Allahabad High Court’s decision not to allow students to wear hijab (headscarves) in schools, calling it an “attack on Islam.” He said the High Court should not have passed such an order while the Sabarimala case is pending before the Supreme Court, where the constitutional issue of “essential religious practice” is being examined. Meanwhile, BSP supremo Mayawati said, Issues related to women's dignity, self-respect and attire should be understood with great sensitivity. Instead of taking matters such as hijab in schools to the courts and turning them into major legal issues, they should be resolved at the local level itself. The school management and local administration should hold discussions and find a solution through mutual understanding, so that the issue is not politicized. The Allahabad High Court on Monday dismissed a petition filed by a minor girl seeking permission to wear a hijab to school. The court held that adhering to the prescribed school uniform is essential to maintaining a uniform environment free from religious discrimination. It said students cannot insist on changing the dress code set by the school. Owaisi says, ‘Who are you to decide what is mandatory in Islam?’ AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi said in Hyderabad on Tuesday that he disagreed with the Allahabad High Court’s decision barring a girl from wearing a hijab to school. He said the Sabarimala case is pending before a nine-judge Supreme Court bench, which is examining what constitutes an essential religious practice. Owaisi said the High Court’s decision violates Articles 19 and 25 of the Constitution. Questioning the court’s authority to determine what is essential to Islam, he said, “Who are you to decide what is essential to Islam?” He added that girls wear the hijab on their heads, “not on their minds.” Mayawati says, ‘Do not interfere in others’ religious sentiments, respect them’ Mayawati wrote on ‘X’ on Wednesday that Dr. B.R. Ambedkar gave the country a Constitution that guarantees equal rights to people of all castes and religions. She said the Constitution gives every citizen the right to live peacefully according to their religion, customs and beliefs. Therefore, no one should interfere in the religious sentiments of others. The BSP chief said her party believes that, in the interest of the country and its people, everyone should refrain from making unnecessary remarks about any religion or its traditions. Referring to the controversy over the installation of an Ambedkar statue, Mayawati said the administration should immediately intervene in the ongoing dispute in Budaun district and resolve the matter peacefully. Now, learn about the entire matter in detail, step by step The student who filed the petition is a Class 11 student at a private school in Prayagraj. She approached the Allahabad High Court through her mother, claiming that she had worn a hijab to school from Classes 6 to 10 and had never faced any objection. She attached her previous school identity cards and a group photograph as evidence. The student said, “I wanted to continue wearing the hijab in Class 11, but the school refused to allow it. My family also approached the District Magistrate, following which the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) sought a report from the school. The principal said the institution has a uniform dress code applicable to all students and granting an exemption to one student could affect school administration.” The petitioner argued that wearing the hijab is part of her religious beliefs and that she has fundamental rights to privacy, personal liberty and freedom of speech. She therefore sought a direction from the court preventing the school from stopping her from wearing the hijab. Court says, ‘Only school administration has the right to decide dress code’ Court says,‘There is no restriction on faith; we expect rules to be followed’ The Allahabad High Court referred to earlier judgments of the Kerala, Bombay and Karnataka High Courts. In Fatima Tasneem v. State of Kerala, the court held that while students have the right to choose what they wear, schools and educational institutions also have the authority to enforce their own rules and regulations. When individual choice conflicts with institutional discipline, the broader interests and discipline of the institution take precedence. The court also referred to the Supreme Court’s Ayesha Shifa v. State of Karnataka case, in which a two-judge bench delivered a split verdict, leaving the issue unresolved. The Allahabad High Court said the school was not restricting the student’s faith but was only requiring her to follow its uniform and disciplinary rules. The court subsequently dismissed the petition.

stories.title: Speeding car crashes into tree in Sitapur:2 brothers killed, mother and driver injured; family had come from Banaras to Naimisharanya
stories.summary: Two biological brothers were killed, mother and driver seriously injured after a speeding car went out of control and crashed into a roadside kadam tree in Sitapur around 8 a.m. on Wednesday (26 Aug). The accident took place on the Kalli-Naimish road in the Mishrikh Kotwali area. According to reports, four people were travelling in the car when the driver suddenly lost control, causing the vehicle to ram into the tree. Nearby residents rushed to the spot after learning about the accident and began rescue efforts. Police also reached the scene and, with the help of locals, took all four injured people to Machhrehta Hospital. At the hospital, doctors declared Varanasi residents Akash Gupta (30), son of Rajiv Gupta, and Yash Gupta (25), also son of Rajiv Gupta, dead. Their mother, Nandini Gupta (50), who was travelling with them, was critically injured. After receiving first aid, she was referred to Sitapur District Hospital. The car driver also sustained serious injuries. The accident caused panic at the spot, with chaos prevailing for some time. Police took the bodies into custody and sent them for post-mortem examinations before informing the families of the deceased. stories.title: Champat says FIR on donation theft delayed due to polls:Questions Nripendra Misra’s 14 interviews; asks who was the real mole? Diary reveals details
stories.summary: Former Ram Temple general secretary Champat Rai's diary contains several startling remarks. According to sources, Rai wrote that an FIR was not filed immediately after the donation theft came to light because he feared a police investigation could drag on and affect the upcoming Assembly elections. Rai also raised questions over the role of Nripendra Misra, chairman of the temple construction committee. He wrote that Misra described the donation theft as "dacoity" in interviews with media channels, which could send a wrong message to society. Rai questioned why an experienced person like Misra gave interviews to 14 channels within four days and at whose direction. Rai further wrote that Misra had never raised questions about arrangements or accounts during temple construction committee meetings over the past six years, so what right did he have to speak about them now? Rai also questioned how and through whom the information reached former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav. He wrote, "Who is the real mole? This is the biggest question before me. It needs to be found out." Champat wrote, ‘He had told Nripendra Misra everything’ According to the diary, on 8 June, a day after the donation theft case came to light on June 7, Temple Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Misra and former National Buildings Construction Corporation Limited (NBCC) Chairman Anoop Kumar reached Ayodhya. They held discussions for nearly two hours. Champat Rai wrote that he, along with former trustees Dr. Anil Misra and Gopal Rao, provided them with complete details of the developments. Nripendra Misra asked why an FIR had not been registered with the police. Rai replied that once the matter was handed over to the police, all authority to question people and take further action would rest with them, making the eventual outcome difficult to predict. Saints were also informed about the matter After the meeting, Champat Rai said, “I spoke to several saints over the phone and informed them about the theft of offerings. The saints were also invited to Ayodhya, where a meeting was held with them at the Sheshavatar Temple on the temple premises.” Describing the reports about the incident as baseless, Rai appealed to the saints not to pay attention to them. According to the diary, the saints accepted his explanation. However, it does not mention which saints attended the meeting. Rai also wrote that after the theft came to light, he recovered a substantial portion of the stolen offerings by working for nearly 11 hours a day for three consecutive days. Reached Lucknow to meet bhaiyaji Joshi despite being unwell According to the diary, Champat Rai was unwell on 9 June but still worked for nearly 10 hours at the PFC building on the temple premises. By 10 June, his condition had worsened and he was unable to get out of bed. That night, Gopal Rao received a call from Bhaiyaji Joshi, who asked Rao, Anil Misra and Rai to reach Lucknow by the evening of 11 June. When Rao informed Joshi that Rai was unwell, Rai insisted that he should also go to Lucknow so that all the facts related to the matter could be presented accurately. The three subsequently travelled to Lucknow and met Joshi. Why did Nripendra Misra suddenly cancel his trip to Ayodhya? Champat Rai wrote that Nripendra Misra was scheduled to visit Ayodhya for the trust meeting on July 6, and his flight ticket had already been booked. Driver Radheshyam had also been informed to receive him. However, on July 4, a message suddenly arrived saying that Misra’s visit had been cancelled. As a result, he did not attend the meeting. Rai wrote that why Misra cancelled his visit and did not come to Ayodhya also remained a question. Why did Nripendra Misra's statements change? In the diary, Champat Rai also mentioned the statements Nripendra Misra gave to the media. Initially, he said that his responsibility was limited to the construction of the temple, but later his statements changed. After 23 June, Nripendra Misra's statements suddenly stopped coming. He wrote in the diary that the reason for this would have to be ascertained. On 14 July, I met Anup Mittal for two hours. I told him that the saints were asking me whether Nripendra Misra was playing the role of a villain. I had no answer to the saints' question. Therefore, I am informing you about the details of the matter.

stories.title: Baba Vishwanath to sit on swing this Rakhi:Panchavadan silver idol procession to begin from Tedhi neem
stories.summary: On the auspicious occasion of Shravan Purnima and Raksha Bandhan, Varanasi will witness the traditional Jhulanotsav of Baba Vishwanath on 28 August. Baba Vishwanath, accompanied by his family, will be seated on a swing and give darshan to devotees and residents of Kashi for nearly six hours. Preparations for the festival have begun at the Mahant Residence in Tedhi Neem, where the swing is being cleaned and other arrangements are being finalized. On 27 August, the eve of Raksha Bandhan, the Panchavadan movable silver idol of Baba Vishwanath will be adorned with a special green-themed decoration at the Mahant Residence, followed by rituals and prayers as per tradition. On Shravan Purnima, the idol will be given royal adornment before being taken on a city tour. Procession to be held with music and fanfare Coordinator Vachaspati Tiwari said, "On the evening of 28 August, Baba's five-faced movable silver idol will be taken from the Mahant's residence to the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple with music and fanfare. During the procession, which will begin from Tedhinim, devotees will be able to have darshan of Baba along the route. The entire area will be filled with devotion to the tunes of traditional musical instruments, the playing of damrus, and religious chants. They said, “After the procession, Baba's movable idol along with his family will be installed in the sanctum sanctorum of the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple. After the rituals and worship are performed there, Baba's swing festival will be celebrated. A large number of devotees are expected to attend during this time.” Jhulanotsav will be held before the evening Saptarishi Aarti Shambhu Sharan, SDM of the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, said, On Raksha Bandhan, the swing festival of Baba's movable silver idol will be held before the Saptarishi Aarti. Baba, accompanied by his family, will be seated on the swing and give devotees darshan. Devotees will be able to have darshan until the Shayan Aarti. After this, Baba's movable idol will be taken back to the Mahant's residence.

stories.title: Railway staff protest removal of vehicles from platform:Say new parking spot is 500m from office; had earlier been allowed to park there
stories.summary: Railway employees protested on Tuesday after their vehicles parked near the sleeping pod area on the Platform 9 side of Gorakhpur railway station were removed. The action sparked resentment among the staff, who reached the spot and objected to the move. The employees said a designated parking area had already been allotted for their vehicles, yet the railway authorities had ordered them to be removed. Employees say distant parking is causing inconvenience Railway employees said, “The administration has provided parking near the booking office, but the designated area is far from our respective offices. We have to walk around 400–500 metres after parking their vehicles.” The employees said, “Walking this distance every day during duty is inconvenient." They urged the administration to arrange parking closer to their offices, keeping our convenience in mind. Area had been cleared earlier too Railway employees said, “The administration had previously taken action to remove vehicles parked beneath the sleeping pod. At the time, the employees co-operated with the administration and completely cleared the area.” Afterwards, they began parking their vehicles in an orderly manner at a designated spot beside the sleeping pod. The employees said, "We were following the administration's instructions and parking only in the allotted area. Employees protest removal of vehicles again On Tuesday, when the railway administration began removing vehicles from this location as well, the employees protested. They questioned why action was being taken when the area had already been designated for parking and they had been parking their vehicles there with the administration's permission. The employees said, “If a new parking arrangement had been introduced, they should have been informed in advance.” They alleged that the sudden action, after permission had initially been granted, was causing unnecessary inconvenience. Railway administration yet to comment Railway employees expressed strong displeasure over the matter and staged a protest at the spot. However, the railway administration has not yet issued an official statement on the issue.

stories.title: Alert in UP for Eid Milad-un-Nabi, drone surveillance:Devotees march with tricolour in Varanasi; 100 vehicles allowed in 5-km procession
stories.summary: Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi is being celebrated in Lucknow on the occasion of 12th Rabi-ul-Awwal. In the processions being taken out to celebrate the birth of Prophet Muhammad, the Indian tricolor is also being waved along with religious flags. Arrangements for Sabeel (water distribution) and Langar (community kitchen) have been made at various places along the procession routes. Along with welcoming the devotees, prayers for peace and harmony in the country are also being offered. In view of the crowd, a large number of police forces have been deployed on the procession routes. CCTV and drone cameras are being used to monitor the security arrangements. The traffic police have also implemented diversions to keep traffic organized during the processions.

stories.title: 12 hours of rain in Kanpur, VIP road sinks 5ft:Water enters homes; rain in 25 UP cities, 13 killed in 2 days
stories.summary: Heavy monsoon rain continued across Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday, with 25 cities receiving intermittent showers. Kanpur witnessed heavy rain for around 12 hours, leaving roads and residential areas waterlogged and causing a five-foot-deep crater to form on VIP Road. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts in the state. Meanwhile, 19 districts are facing flood-like conditions. Kanpur roads turn into lakes Heavy rain in Kanpur began around 12.30 am and continued until 1 pm, turning roads and lanes into pools of water. Water entered homes and shops in several areas. A five-foot-deep crater appeared on VIP Road, while the Additional Labour Commissioner’s office was also flooded. Lucknow received intermittent drizzle from the morning. In Mahoba, water entered the district hospital and started leaking through the roof of the emergency ward. CM Yogi issues order to local administration to remain vigilant near bordering Nepal areas Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath writes on X, "The damage caused by the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's Rasuwa region is extremely alarming. Prayers to Lord Pashupatinath for the safety and well-being of all. In view of the rising water levels in the Gandak and Narayani rivers and the possibility of flooding in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts due to its impact, instructions have been issued to the local administration to remain fully vigilant and ensure necessary preparations." Rain and flood pictures… 13 killed in rain-related incidents Thirteen people have died in rain-related incidents across Uttar Pradesh over the past two days. Two people each died after houses collapsed in Mahoba and Unnao, while one person was killed in Sultanpur. In Banda, three of the four people swept away in a drain have died. Earlier, five people were killed in separate rain-related incidents in Varanasi on Tuesday. Flood situation worsens in several districts In Badaun, the Ganga and Ramganga rivers have risen above the danger mark. A house was washed away after its foundation was eroded by the Ganga. The Ramganga is also flowing over the Badaun-Shahjahanpur highway. In Chandauli, the Musakhand and Latifshah dams are full, prompting authorities to open their gates. The Sukwa-Dhukwan Dam in Jhansi has started overflowing. In Lakhimpur, part of the Tamolin Purwa embankment on the Sharda River has been breached. In Lalitpur, the Khedar River is flowing around three feet above a bridge, while the Sirsi bridge has also been submerged. Water levels in the Ganga in Varanasi and the Yamuna in Prayagraj are currently stable. However, all ghats in both cities remain submerged. Cremations are being carried out on roads and rooftops because of the flooding. Heavy rain likely to continue for 2-3 days Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said a low-pressure area near the Bay of Bengal, along with active monsoon winds over Uttar Pradesh, could bring heavy to very heavy rain over the next 24 hours. “Heavy to very heavy rain is likely over the next 24 hours. The spell of rain is expected to continue for another 2-3 days,” he said. 105 Indians missing in Nepal floods 105 Indians are among the 291 foreign nationals reported missing during the Nepal floods, according to the Nepal Tourism Board's official statement. The statement also mentions that preliminary agency-wise records received from tourism and travel companies have identified 384 travellers and 93 Nepali nationals as missing from the affected areas. Additionally, the government has issued an advisory to citizens on the matter. Flood alert issued in UP and Bihar The impact of the floods has also raised concern in Bihar. Eight districts, including West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, and Saran, have been placed on high alert. The Disaster Management Department has warned of a possible flash flood wave of up to 3 metres in the Gandak River. Additionally, a news agency, while citing its government sources, has claimed that India is soon sending relief material to flood-hit Nepal. Meanwhile, in India, the government has also issued contact numbers for assistance. The official statement said, “To assist downstream citizens and coordinate emergency situations, the Uttar Pradesh Police Headquarters has activated a 24/7 Special Control Room." stories.title: Bodies cremated at doorsteps in Kashi:84 ghats submerged as Ganga levels rise; 5,000 shops shut, ₹3.75 crore loss in 15 days
stories.summary: Rising water levels in the Ganga have submerged 84 ghats in Kashi, including the Mahashmashan Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghats. More than half of the over 100 temples along the ghats are also underwater. A Dainik Bhaskar ground report found that the flooding has disrupted cremations, businesses and daily life in the area. Cremations are now being performed on rooftops about 15 feet above the ghats, while last rites are being conducted at people's doorsteps in the lanes opposite Harishchandra Ghat. The soot from the cremations has blackened several houses, forcing some residents to permanently brick up their entrances or shift their main gates to the other side. The flooding has also forced around 5,000 shops along the ghats to shut or relocate, while operations of nearly 3,000 small and large boats have been suspended. At an estimated average daily sale of ₹500 per shop, the 15-day disruption could impact business worth around ₹3.75 crore. Shopkeepers said they face a similar crisis every year between August and October. Where 50 bodies were cremated earlier, only 10 are being cremated now On normal days, more than 50 bodies were cremated simultaneously here, but now only 8 to 10 funeral pyres can burn at a time. According to members of the Dom community, people have to wait 3 to 4 hours for cremation. Families who have brought the bodies from far-off places are waiting for their turn at the ghat. Rishikesh Chaudhary of the Dom community says that the rising floodwaters have not only reduced the space available for cremations, but have also disrupted the arrangement for storing firewood. The wood kept in the lower areas is getting wet. It has to be moved to higher areas for safekeeping. As a result, space is also becoming scarce in the narrow lanes and on the rooftops of the cremation ground. Cremations in lanes near Harishchandra Ghat add to residents' difficulties Nanha Chaudhary, who conducts cremations at Harishchandra Ghat, said that “Cremations are being performed in the lanes out of compulsion. People bringing the bodies are facing considerable difficulties.” Locals say that the filth amid the rain and flooding has made the situation even worse. People are facing difficulties because the municipal corporation is not carrying out regular cleaning. There is not enough space to sit in the lanes. With no toilet facilities either, people are being forced to go toward the roadside. When it rains, they are compelled to get drenched in the open. Read what vendors along the ghat had to say... Assi Ghat shopkeepers say, 'How will we pay our children's school fees?' According to businesses associated with the ghats, around 5,000 small and large shops and vendors selling goods while walking earn a living every day at Kashi's 84 ghats. They include people selling tea and water, puja items, flowers and garlands, food, toys, and essential items for tourists. Arvind, who runs a flower and garland shop at Assi Ghat, said, "Now that work has stopped, my first concern is my children's education. We are daily wage earners, but how will we manage household expenses now? We have to pay the children's school fees. We have asked the school authorities for more time." 70 year old Gopal set up a shop in a lane away from the ghat 70-year-old Gopal sells damrus, bead necklaces, pooja items, and other goods. He has been setting up his shop at the ghat for several years. When the Ganga's water level rose, he had to move his shop away from the ghat. He has now started a small shop in a lane. He says, "We have been running our shop for several years. Three months are extremely difficult for us because we cannot set up our shop. Fewer customers come to the lane, and sales have declined." Tinku, who runs a tea and Maggi stall, said, “Even though our income has stopped, our expenses have not. Household groceries, electricity, children's school fees, and daily necessities remain the same as before.” He added, "If the shop is closed for a day or two, we can somehow manage. But when this situation continues for several weeks, our savings start to run out." They support a family of 10 by running a flower and garland shop Phoolwasi, who runs a flower and garland shop at the ghat, is now making a living for her family by setting up her small shop by the roadside because of the flooding. She Said the water level has not yet reached the road. However, if the water reaches the road, she will have to close this shop as well. He said that when shops were set up at the ghats, they used to save more than ₹500 a day, but their income has now declined considerably. There are 10 members in Phoolvasi's family. Some family members do other work, while most help run the shop at the ghat. The floods also affect the children's education. 3,000 boats of boatmen remain idle, earnings halted The administration banned boat operations from 10 August. Boatman Ajju says that for three months, they help one another. Around 40,000 boatmen's families live along all 84 ghats. Nearly 3,000 boats operate on the Ganges, but the flooding has now created serious difficulties. We also have employees working on our boats, but we are unable to pay them their salaries. The boatmen fear that if the boat's rope comes loose when the current is strong, the boat could be swept away. They also have to guard the boats at night. Ganga's water level 2.04 meters below the warning mark According to the Central Water Commission, the Ganga's water level at the Rajghat gauge stood at 68.22 metres at 10 a.m. on Tuesday. The water level is currently receding at a rate of 2 centimetres per hour. The warning level at Rajghat is 70.262 metres, while the danger mark is 71.262 metres. The current water level is around 2.04 metres below the warning mark.

stories.title: Officials overseeing govt schools send children to private schools:Only 1 education officer’s son studies in UP Board; find out where others’ children study
stories.summary: Officials responsible for managing government schools in Uttar Pradesh are not sending their own children to these schools. Dainik Bhaskar investigation found that the children of most Basic Education Officers (BSAs) and District Inspectors of Schools (DIOSs) posted across the state's 75 districts are studying in CBSE and ICSE schools instead of UP Board schools. At present, 148 BSAs and DIOSs are posted across Uttar Pradesh and are responsible for maintaining government schools and improving the quality of education. However, only the Farrukhabad DIOS has enrolled his child in a UP Board school. Find out where the officials' children are studying... Even rural officials send their children to Convent schools in Lucknow Lakhimpur Kheri DIOS Vinod Mishra has two sons. One is studying in Class 11 and the other in Class 8 at Delhi Public School in Lucknow. Of the three sons of Gonda DIOS Dr. Ramchandra, two studied under the ICSE board at St. Francis School in Lucknow, while one is pursuing graduation at Delhi University. The two sons of Deoria DIOS Harishchandra Nath are studying for high school and intermediate under the CBSE board in Lucknow. Both sons of Varanasi DIOS Bholendra Kumar are also studying at a convent school in Lucknow. All three children of Azamgarh DIOS Ajay Kumar Gupta are studying under the CBSE board in Lucknow. Of them, the elder daughter is in Class 7, the younger daughter is in Class 4, and the son is in Class 3. The two children of Prayagraj DIOS Santosh Kumar study at a private school in Lucknow. Only 1 chose the UP board, but sent his child to a private school Farrukhabad's DIOS Sanjeev Kumar is the only officer whose children study in a UP Board school. His children are studying at a private school in Barabanki affiliated with the UP Board. The son and daughter of Gorakhpur's DIOS Ajit Singh study at Little Flower School, an ICSE Board school. Both daughters of Hardoi's DIOS Arvind Kumar Pathak study at a convent school. One daughter and one son of Ghazipur's DIOS Upasana Rani Verma study at Mount Litera Zee School. The daughter is in Class 9, and the son is in Class 10. Both children of Saharanpur's DIOS Jaikaran Yadav study at private schools. BSAs also join the race for private schools Amethi's BSA Sanjay Tiwari's two sons, Samrat and Swaraj, are studying in Classes 4 and KG, respectively, under the CBSE board. Sonbhadra's BSA Mukul Anand Pandey's 10-year-old son is in Class 4 at a convent school in Ghazipur. The three daughters of Gorakhpur's BSA Dhirendra Tripathi have completed their education. Prayagraj's BSA Anil Kumar's son studies at Maharishi Patanjali School, while his daughter studies at St. Mary's Convent. Both are in the lower classes. The children of Noida's BSA Rahul Kanwar are studying under the CBSE board in Baghpat. The 10-year-old daughter of Sambhal's BSA Alka Sharma is also studying at a private school. Some officers' children are pursuing higher education or have completed their studies and are working Many officers' children have completed their schooling. The son of Sitapur's BSA Gorakhnath Patel is pursuing an MBBS degree. One son of Fatehpur's DIOS Rakesh Kumar is preparing for the civil services in Noida. Of his two daughters, one is in the first year of a BA program, while the other is pursuing graduation in Lucknow. Of the two children of Ballia DIOS Manoj Kumar Mishra, one has completed graduation, while the other is pursuing graduation. Both the son and daughter of Baghpat DIOS Rajiv Kumar Yadav have completed their education and are working. Some officers' children are still young Several BSAs and DIOSs in Uttar Pradesh also have children who are not yet old enough to attend school. Azamgarh BSA Rajiv Pathak's son is 3 years old, while Fatehpur BSA Prinshi Maurya's daughter and Bahraich BSA Ashish Singh's son are both 2 years old. The sons of Basti BSA Anoop Kumar and DIOS Sanjay Singh are also young. Chandauli DIOS Dharmendra Kumar's son is 1 year old, while Ballia BSA Manish Kumar Singh's daughter is 3 months old. The Bhadohi DIOS's child is 8 months old, and Jaunpur BSA Sameer Kumar's child is 6 months old. Sultanpur BSA Upendra Gupta's daughter is 3 months old. Lakhimpur Kheri BSA Praveen Kumar's twin children are also too young for school. The children of Pilibhit BSA Roshni Singh, Hardoi BSA Prabhash Mishra, Meerut BSA Asha Chaudhary, Varanasi BSA Bhupendra Singh and Mirzapur BSA Anil Verma are also still young.
