stories.title: Allahabad High Court orders relocation of Hathras victim’s family to Ghaziabad or Noida within three months
‘Resettle Hathras victim’s family in Noida or Ghaziabad’:Allahabad HC gives govt 3 months, warns against rigid stance
stories.summary: Allahabad High Court on Tuesday came down heavily on the Uttar Pradesh government over the rehabilitation of the Hathras victim's family. The court directed the state to settle the family in Ghaziabad or Noida within three months and provide them with necessary facilities. It also ordered the government to give one family member a government job in accordance with its July 2022 order. A bench of Justices Rajan Roy and Jaspreet Singh termed the state government's approach "obstinate" and quashed its 22 February, 2025 decision offering the family rehabilitation in Kasganj, Etah or Aligarh. The court noted that the decision did not address the family's request to be relocated to Ghaziabad or Gautam Buddh Nagar and said it could be treated as "no decision in the eyes of the law." The court has made the Additional Chief Secretary (Home) responsible for ensuring compliance and directed the official to file an affidavit. Failure to comply will require the official to appear personally before the court at the next hearing, scheduled for 30 November, 2026. Family sought relocation to Ghaziabad or Noida After the Hathras case, in July 2022, the family told the High Court that it did not feel safe in Hathras and wanted to settle in Noida. It had also demanded a government job in Noida for one of its members. Later, the family applied for rehabilitation in Ghaziabad or Noida. On 14 November, 2024, the High Court directed the family to submit a formal application before the District Magistrate of Hathras. The family applied for rehabilitation in Ghaziabad/Gautam Buddh Nagar on 2 December, 2024. However, on 22 February, 2025, the state government offered the option of rehabilitation only in Kasganj, Etah, and Aligarh. Victim's brother says, 'Government should comply with the order soon' The victim's brother said the High Court's order has given the family hope that they will finally be able to "breathe freely." He said nine members of the family are still living under suffocating circumstances. He urged the government to comply with the court's order at the earliest and relocate the family to Noida or Ghaziabad. "The atmosphere in the village and the surrounding area is very hostile. We no longer want to live here. We want to leave this place," he said. 3 accused acquitted 3 years ago, 1 sentenced to life imprisonment In the Hathras case, the SC/ST court delivered its verdict on 2 March, 2023. The court found only one of the four accused, Sandeep Sisodia, guilty, while acquitting the other three accused-Lawkush, Ramu alias Ramkumar, and Ravi alias Ravindra Singh. The court sentenced Sandeep to life imprisonment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The charge of gang rape was not proven against any of the four accused. Hathras case: The complete timeline from 2020 to present September 14, 2020: A case involving the rape of a Dalit woman came to light in a village in the Chandpa area of Hathras. September 26, 2020: Based on the victim's statement, the names of three more accused-Lavkush Singh, Ramu, and Ravi Singh-were added to the case. All four were arrested and sent to jail. Referred to Delhi for Treatment: In critical condition, the victim was admitted to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital after being treated at Aligarh's J.N. Medical College. September 29, 2020: The victim died during treatment. Her body was brought to Hathras, and the police conducted the cremation that same night. The family alleged that the cremation was carried out without their permission. October 2020: The case gained momentum after the cremation, triggering protests across the country. The Uttar Pradesh government suspended five police personnel, including the then Superintendent of Police and Circle Officer. October 11, 2020: On the recommendation of the state government, the CBI took over the investigation into the case. CBI investigation: The investigating agency questioned several people, including the victim's family members and the families of the accused. The crime scene was inspected and also re-created. December 18, 2020: After an investigation lasting approximately 67 days, the CBI filed a chargesheet against all four accused. Several serious charges, including murder and gang rape, were invoked. CBI's claim: The investigating agency based its case on the statement given by the victim before her death and alleged in the chargesheet that she was murdered after being gang-raped. Court Verdict: The charges of gang rape and murder were not proven in the trial court. 2022: Citing security concerns, the victim's family sought rehabilitation outside Hathras, particularly in Noida. 2024: The High Court directed the family to submit a formal application for rehabilitation before the District Magistrate. The family requested that they be settled in Ghaziabad/Gautam Buddh Nagar. February 22, 2025: The state government offered the family the option of settling in Kasganj, Etah, or Aligarh. No decision was taken on the family's demand for Noida/Ghaziabad. August 25, 2026: The Allahabad High Court quashed the government's decision and ordered that the family be rehabilitated in Noida or Ghaziabad within three months. Court's Displeasure: The High Court described the government's approach as "unnecessary resistance" and an "obstinate attitude." Government Job: The court also directed compliance with its earlier order to provide a government job to one member of the family. Next Hearing: The next hearing in the case will be held on November 30, 2026.

stories.title: Story of absconding shooters in singer Ankit’s murder:Satyam’s family worth billions, owns 150 acres; Aryan is Class 10 pass; both under 20
stories.summary: The investigation into the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan has now reached Karnal. The names of Satyam Kadyan and Aryan Sandhu have emerged in the UP Police investigation. Both accused are said to be absconding along with their families. Locks are hanging on the houses of both in Karnal. The police are continuously conducting raids in search of them. Their social media accounts are being scrutinized. According to sources, the police have also questioned several close associates. Shooter Satyam Kadyan is around 18-19 years old. Satyam comes from a business family, and the family owns more than 150 acres of agricultural land. He is the only son in the family. Meanwhile, the second shooter involved in this murder, Aryan Sandhu (20), is the youngest of five siblings. His father passed away several years ago. He had also dropped out of school after completing 10th grade. First, know the story of Satyam from the billionaire family Aryan's father is deceased, family has left the house The family of the second accused involved in this murder case, Aryan Sandhu (20), lives in the Kalandari Gate area. Aryan has an elder brother and three sisters. One sister is married. His father, Narendra, passed away several years ago. Aryan studied up to the 10th grade at a private school in the Subhash Gate area. He dropped out of school 2-3 years ago. Since dropping out, Aryan often used to hang out with Satyam. After his name appeared in the Ankit murder case, his house has been locked. Encounter of Sumit and Mohit from Sonipat In the Ankit murder case, the UP Police gunned down Sumit (22) and Mohit (24) from Sonipat in an encounter on Monday morning. The two had met about three months ago and started living together. On August 25, both came to Sumit's house with new clothes. While leaving, Sumit told his father, "Papa, I am helpless." The next day, when the video of the Ankit Baliyan murder case surfaced, the family identified Sumit by his clothes. On Tuesday, both were cremated under police protection.

stories.title: Army officer’s family harassed during Kashi visit:They sit on road in protest; were on way to watch a film
stories.summary: A case has reportedly emerged in which police personnel allegedly misbehaved with and pushed the family of an Indian Army officer who had come to visit Kashi. Following the incident, the angry family members sat on the road in protest and demanded action against the police personnel responsible. Speaking to the media, the Army officer said that he was going to watch the film "Hanuman Ansh," based on Neem Karoli Baba, with around 10 members of his family. According to him, the film show was scheduled for 6:30 p.m., and they had the tickets with them. The cinema was about 500 meters from the spot where the incident occurred, and the family was traveling by rickshaw. Two police officers forcefully pushed their rickshaw The officer alleges that during this incident, two police officers in plain clothes forcefully pushed their rickshaw. A woman around 70 years old was also sitting in the rickshaw and reportedly sustained injuries. When the family asked the police officers why they had pushed the rickshaw, the two officers allegedly began hurling abuses and behaved rudely with the family members, even grabbing them by the collar. According to the officer, when the family objected, another person arrived at the scene. After the incident, the family complained to administrative officials. They said that some people from the administration arrived at the scene and spoke with them for about 10 to 15 minutes, but they did not receive any immediate satisfactory solution. After this, the family decided to sit on the road and protest. Multiple pieces of evidence, including video, available The Army officer said they have multiple pieces of evidence related to the incident, including video footage. They demanded that the administration ensure that the police personnel who allegedly behaved improperly and pushed them admit their mistake and that action be taken against them in accordance with the rules. They said their main demands are action against the guilty police personnel and that the administration acknowledge the matter and provide appropriate justice. The family said they would continue their protest until proper action is taken on their complaint.

stories.title: Dakku booked in land-grab and assault cases:SP leader claims he went to remove debris from his own land
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Zafar Amin Dakku, who had contested the Assembly election from Gorakhpur Rural, has been accused of land grabbing, assault, and issuing death threats. A named complaint was registered against him at Rajghat police station late on Tuesday night. Samajwadi Party city president Shabbir Qureshi and several others have also been named as accused in the case. On Tuesday, a dispute broke out between Dakku and some women in Khokhar Tola over the removal of debris from a plot of land. A video of the incident also went viral on social media. The commotion continued at the spot for about 15 minutes. Police reached the scene and pacified both sides. Later that night, a case was registered on the complaint of Shahana Khatoon, a resident of Khokhar Tola. Woman claims: Occupying the house for 70 years In the written complaint submitted to the police, Shahana Khatun stated that she has been living in a house located in Khokhar Tola for nearly 70 years. She claims that the house was built on land bearing plot number 91 in Deeh. According to her, the land belonged to former zamindar Vallabhdas, who had given her ancestors the land to build a house and live there. Shahana alleges that in 2023, Zafar Amin Dakku occupied half of the house. On Tuesday, Dakku, Shabbir Qureshi and their supporters again arrived at the spot and tried to occupy the remaining portion. According to Shahana, she opposed this and stated that the matter concerning the land is pending before the court. It is alleged that she was subsequently verbally abused and assaulted. She was also threatened with death. She was rescued after people nearby intervened. The woman has requested the police to take action and provide security. Dakku says he bought the land and had gone to remove the debris Jafar Amin Dakku has rejected the women's allegations. He said that he bought the land in 2017. He occupies half of the property, while tenants live in the other half. According to Dakku, no one had been living in his portion for around 35 years. Residents of the locality had complained to the municipal corporation that the house was in a dilapidated condition. Following this, the municipal corporation issued a notice in 2020 to demolish the house. Another notice was issued in 2023, warning that if the house was not demolished, the municipal corporation would demolish it and recover the expenses from him. Dakku said that after the municipal corporation's action, that part of the house had been demolished. Debris had been lying there ever since. On Tuesday, he arrived with his supporters to remove the debris and carry out construction. During this, the female tenants began protesting. Dakku said the court did not grant a stay Dakku said that the tenants had approached the court, but they were not granted a stay. They were asked to produce documents related to the land, but they could not show them. The matter had also been brought before the police. He said that the inspector had also reached the spot three days earlier. In his presence, the tenants had said that they would get the land registered. Later, during the conversation, they had said that construction could be carried out without disturbing them. Dakku claims that this conversation took place in front of the police. He said that when he arrived to carry out construction three days later, the same women began protesting. Dakku accused the women of behaving indecently. He said that the CO has summoned him, and he will present all the documents related to his land there. Police install two CCTV cameras at disputed land Following the dispute, the police have increased surveillance at the site. Rajghat police have installed two CCTV cameras at the disputed location. Activities taking place on the land are being monitored through them so that action can be taken in the event of another dispute or an attempt to occupy. The Revenue Department has been instructed to examine the land records and the claims of both parties. SP City Nimesh Patil said that a case has been registered based on the woman's complaint. The matter is being investigated. The actual ownership and status of the land will be determined after examining the revenue records and relevant documents. The police have been instructed to maintain law and order at the site.

stories.title: Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh tests positive for swine flu:Goes into isolation at government residence, KGMU team arrives for tests
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh has contracted swine flu (H1N1). The minister had been running a fever for the past four to five days. Tests confirmed that he was H1N1 positive. He has been placed in isolation at his official residence in Lucknow. On Wednesday morning, a team of doctors from KGMU visited his residence. The team examined him and advised that he continue treatment at home for now. His condition is reported to be stable. Samples are also being collected from other family members and staff for testing. Earlier, on Tuesday morning, Minister Jaiveer Singh had submitted samples at KGMU's pathology department for swine flu testing.

stories.title: Army boat sinks at Hathnikund Barrage, 2 soldiers missing:3 rescued; 10-km Yamuna search operation runs overnight, aerial surveillance in Haryana-UP
stories.summary: Two soldiers who went missing after an army boat capsized in the Yamuna River near Hathnikund Barrage in Haryana's Yamunanagar district on Tuesday evening have not been located even after 15 hours. The search operation, which began at 5 PM on Tuesday, continued throughout the night. Surveillance was also conducted via helicopter. Apart from Haryana, SDRF teams from UP are also involved. Local divers have also been deployed. The banks of the Eastern and Western Yamuna canals originating from the barrage were monitored using searchlights. Efforts will be renewed today by reducing the water supply in the canals. The accident occurred during a flood rescue exercise by the Army's 1 Para Special Forces. Five army soldiers began to drown in the incident. Three of them managed to swim about 600 meters through the strong current and escape through the gates of the Western Yamuna Canal (WJC). The missing soldiers have been identified as Aryan Patil, a resident of Maharashtra, and Ajay, a resident of Akhnoor, Jammu and Kashmir. Photos of the search operation conducted at night... SDM reached the spot at night itself Following the information about the missing soldiers, the administration also intensified the monitoring of the rescue operation. Late at night, SDM Jaspal Gill and DSP Rajat Gulia reached the spot and took stock of the rescue operation. The officials took information about the search operation from the army, SDRF, and police officers present at the site. According to Pratapnagar Police Station In-charge Rohtash Singh, upon receiving the information, the SDRF team from Uttar Pradesh, in addition to Haryana, was also called to the spot. Army divers and local divers are also engaged in the search. Canal searched up to 10 kilometers ahead of the barrage Rescue teams have conducted a search operation for about 10 kilometers in the canal originating from Hathnikund Barrage. However, due to the strong current, it is proving to be extremely risky for the divers to enter the water at many places. There are also about seven bridges further along the canal originating from the barrage. The water is flowing at a very high speed under these bridges. In such a situation, searching around them has become challenging for the divers. Despite this, the teams are continuously searching for the soldiers in different sections. Village Sarpanchs also alerted According to the divers, the canal originating from the Hathnikund Barrage splits into several parts further ahead. There are also sluice gates (jhal) built on some of the smaller canals branching out from the main canal. In such a situation, if both soldiers have been swept away by the strong current from the main canal into these smaller canals and are stuck in the sluice gates, there is a possibility of them being found soon. Keeping this possibility in mind, different sections of the canal are being monitored. The administration has also informed the sarpanchs of all the villages located along the canal. They have been asked to keep a watch on the canal so that if either of the two soldiers reaches further downstream with the water flow or is spotted anywhere, the administration and police can be informed immediately. Accident occurred around 5 PM on Tuesday The accident took place around 5 PM on Tuesday in the upstream of the Yamuna, below Kalesar and shortly before Hathnikund Barrage. A flood rescue exercise by the Army's 1 Para Special Forces was underway here. This exercise had been ongoing since 30 August, and Tuesday was its final day. It is being reported that during the exercise, the soldiers jumped one by one from a helicopter into a motorboat stationed in the Yamuna. After the soldiers reached the boat, the motorboat did not start and suddenly began to sink. Meanwhile, the helicopter also departed from the area. After the boat sank, the soldiers were forced to enter the strong current and deep water. Three soldiers swam towards the gate of the Western Yamuna Canal and managed to get out after covering a distance of about 600 meters, but Aryan Patil and Ajay could not be located. Search operation to be conducted on a larger scale today Despite the overnight operation, no clues about the two soldiers were found, and preparations are now underway to conduct a large-scale search operation on Wednesday. Teams from the Army, SDRF, local divers, and the administration will search different sections of the canal. Special surveillance will be maintained at locations with strong currents, as well as along the canal banks, bridges, and the branch canals further downstream. At the time of the accident, the water flow in the Yamuna was very strong. A day earlier, the water level of the Yamuna at Hathnikund Barrage was recorded at about 26,000 cusecs, while about 14,500 cusecs of water were being released into the Western Yamuna Canal. Due to this strong current, the biggest challenge for the rescue teams remains reaching the soldiers and searching the water safely.

stories.title: Encounter specialist may become first CEO of Ram Mandir:Sharad Sharma to be spokesperson; third trust meeting in Ayodhya today after donation theft
stories.summary: Former IPS officer and UP's encounter specialist Rajesh Pandey could be appointed as the first CEO (Chief Executive Officer) of the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. Sources indicated that Rajesh Pandey's name might be finalized during the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust meeting on Wednesday. Rajesh Pandey, a native of Prayagraj, has experience working with the United Nations' Kosovo peacekeeping mission. During his service, he carried out over 80 encounters, including that of gangster Shriprakash Shukla. He has also been a founding member of two special units of the UP Police: the Special Task Force (STF) and the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS). Sharad Sharma, who has been the media in-charge for the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, could be appointed as the spokesperson for the Trust. This is the third meeting of the Trust since the case of theft of offerings came to light. The formation of a Prasad Committee and a Parikrama Committee may be announced during the meeting. A decision may also be taken to increase the number of members in the Religious Committee and to fill the 3 vacant positions in the Trust. However, the announcement of a permanent General Secretary for the Trust is considered unlikely during the meeting. Swami Govind Dev Giri, Chairman of the Ram Mandir Religious Committee and Treasurer of the Trust, along with the Trustee and General Secretary of the Trust, Krishna Mohan, have reached Ayodhya. Swami Govind Dev Giri visited the Ram Mandir and had darshan of Ram Lalla. The meeting will be held at 3 PM at Maniram Das Chhavni. Proposal to install 2 ACs in the sanctum sanctorum may get approval Two ACs have been ordered for the service of Ram Lalla. One of these is 1 ton, and the other is 3 tons. Both ACs will be installed in the sanctum sanctorum. To install them, holes will have to be drilled in the walls. The Religious Committee has submitted its proposal regarding this to the Trust. This proposal may also get approval in tomorrow's meeting. Why is the Prasad and Parikrama Committee being formed? What decisions were taken in the two meetings held after the theft of offerings... July 2 - Resignation of Champat Rai and Anil Mishra accepted The Trust had accepted the resignations of General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Anil Mishra. Retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan was appointed as the acting General Secretary in their place. Additionally, the Trust claimed the theft of 4 gold and silver items while displaying them. The Trust stated that it had received ₹3,264 crore through donations. Out of this, ₹2,370 crore has already been spent on temple construction and other works. July 22 - Religious committee of 9 saints formed The trust had taken two major decisions. First- A religious committee of 9 saints was formed. It included 5 saints from Ayodhya and 4 saints from the temple trust. The trust's treasurer, Swami Govind Dev Giri, was appointed as the chairman of the committee. Second- A spokesperson and a secretary for the trust will be appointed. The trust stated that despite several allegations and misinformation, there has been no decrease in the number of devotees visiting the Ram Temple. 16 people were interviewed in 2 days for the post of Ram Mandir CEO SIT submitted preliminary report on 23 June, 8 arrested 2 days later The theft case first came to light on 7 June. The UP government's SIT submitted a preliminary report to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on 23 June. An FIR was registered on 25 June based on the complaint of trust member Krishna Mohan. In this, 8 people, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were named. However, it did not include the names of senior office bearers like Champat Rai and Dr. Anil Mishra. A few hours after the FIR was registered, the police arrested 8 accused, including Tinnu. Currently, all of them are in Faizabad jail. All are accused of stealing cash and jewelry while counting the offerings. Following the SIT's preliminary report, General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra resigned, taking moral responsibility. The trust accepted both resignations and removed Gopal Nagarkatte from the list of special invitees. Supreme Court had ordered the formation of a second SIT Four separate petitions related to the offering theft case have been filed in the Supreme Court. In addition to handing over the investigation to the CBI, these petitions demand the formation of an expert committee to review various issues related to the management of temple donations. The old SIT was reporting to the state government level, whereas the new SIT will file status reports directly to the Supreme Court from time to time. The Supreme Court itself is monitoring the investigation of the entire matter. The Supreme Court had held that the role of police officers is direct and more effective in criminal investigations and technical probes of theft cases. Therefore, by making the DIG and SSP members, the scope of the investigation has been handed over directly to the officials of the police department.

stories.title: UP gets June-July rain quota in August:47 districts on alert in first week of Sept; monsoon to return from third week
stories.summary: After receiving below-normal rainfall in June and July, the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh broke the record of the past three years in August. The state received 106% of the normal rainfall in August, amounting to 292.2 mm. From June 1 to August 31, Uttar Pradesh should have received an average of 593.1 mm of rainfall. This year, it received 552.8 mm. The rainfall deficit so far this season was only 6.8%. According to the Meteorological Department, the spell of rain will continue during the first week of September. However, as El Niño strengthens, the monsoon may begin withdrawing from Uttar Pradesh after September 15. August broke three-year record The average normal rainfall in UP in August is 275.6 mm. In comparison, 292.2 mm of rain was recorded this year. This means that the state received above-normal rainfall (106%). In 26 districts of the state, rainfall was 20% above normal. Before this, 88.7% rainfall was recorded in 2025, 81.2% in 2024, and 82.4% in 2023. In other words, August 2026 was the best in terms of rainfall over the past three years. Bundelkhand received three times more rainfall than normal Normal rainfall in 34 districts including Lucknow and Varanasi Lucknow received 97.7% of its normal rainfall, Varanasi 103%, Agra 96.3%, and Bareilly 91.4%. Rainfall was normal in a total of 34 districts of the state. If a district receives between 80% and 120% of its average rainfall for the entire season, the weather department categorises it as a district with "normal rainfall." Alert for 47 districts in the first week of September According to the Meteorological Department, the impact of the low-pressure system that formed in August and the monsoon trough may continue into the early days of September. Between September 1 and 5, rain accompanied by thunderstorms is likely in 47 districts of eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. A warning has also been issued for heavy to very heavy rainfall and lightning in Gorakhpur, Deoria, Kushinagar, Maharajganj, Basti, Siddharthnagar, Sant Kabir Nagar, Gonda, Balrampur, Shravasti, and Bahraich. An alert for rain accompanied by thunderstorms has also been issued in Muzaffarnagar, Meerut, Bijnor, Sambhal, Bulandshahr, Saharanpur, Shamli, Baghpat, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddh Nagar, and Hapur. August Rains Bring Relief to Farmers The good rainfall in August has also benefited farming. The target for paddy transplantation has been achieved by 100.3%. This year, paddy has been transplanted across approximately 6.921 million hectares. Targets have been achieved by 103.6% for pearl millet, 104.1% for black gram, 107.1% for green gram, and 103.5% for sesame. Farmers troubled by the low rainfall in June and July will no longer have to worry about water for sowing wheat, mustard, chickpeas, peas, and lentils.

stories.title: Kanha outfits in demand from US to Russia:Costliest dress ₹20,000; 3,000 Hindu-Muslim artisans make them together
stories.summary: Shri Krishna Janmashtami will be celebrated on September 4. To make Kanha's 5,253rd birth anniversary special, the markets of Mathura-Vrindavan are fully decorated and ready. Ahead of Janmashtami, devotees are thronging the markets to buy outfits, crowns, and other adornment items for Laddu Gopal. The demand for Kanha's adornments made in Braj is not limited to the country alone. Outfits and adornment items prepared here are also sent to several countries, including the United States, France, England, Japan, Germany, Russia, Canada, and Australia. This time, business worth around ₹1,500 crore is expected around Janmashtami. Nearly 3,000 Hindu and Muslim artisans in Braj are working day and night to prepare Kanha's adornments. The artisans are creating outfits, crowns, and other adornment items for Laddu Gopal in various designs and sizes. Their prices range from ₹10 to ₹20,000. It takes up to eight hours to make a small zari outfit Outfit trader Shubham Gupta said that the business of outfits, crowns, and adornments for Thakurji has been thriving in the lanes of Mathura-Vrindavan for a long time. There are around 300 small and large workshops here. More than 3,000 artisans are working day and night to prepare outfits and adornment items. According to the artisans, it takes around 8 hours even to prepare a small zari outfit. Most of the intricate work is done by hand. As Janmashtami approaches, demand for outfits and adornment items increases. Traders start receiving orders about two months in advance. Along with the outfits, crowns, necklaces, anklets, armlets, bangles, and earrings for Thakurji are also being prepared. Devotees are enthusiastically purchasing these items, which are available in different sizes and designs. Outfit orders have also arrived from England, Japan, and Germany Another special feature of Braj is that Hindu and Muslim artisans work together to prepare Lord Thakurji's attire. Artisans from both communities create intricate embroidery and zari work. Before Janmashtami, this work presents an example of mutual brotherhood. Artisans are preparing attractive outfits for Kanha in different designs and colors. This time, orders for the outfits have been received from several countries, including the United States, France, England, Japan, Germany, Russia, Canada, and Australia. Outfits bearing the name 'Radha' are the most popular There are outfits for Laddu Gopal in many designs and colours available in the market. This time, outfits bearing the name "Radha" are in the highest demand. In different sizes, these outfits also feature the name Radha along with small images of Radha and Krishna. In addition, devotees are also liking outfits featuring the image of Shrinathji. On Janmashtami, Laddu Gopal is traditionally dressed in yellow outfits, while peacock-green outfits are being preferred for Radharani. Starting at Rs 10, prices reach up to Rs 20,000 Outfit trader Shubham Gupta said, "This time, demand for outfits is good compared to previous years. Outfits priced from Rs 10 to Rs 20,000 are available in the market. The price is determined by the outfit's size, design, and the work done on it." Machine-made outfits are somewhat cheaper, while outfits featuring hand-worked zari and embroidery are more expensive. Devotees are buying outfits for Laddu Gopal according to their preferences and budget. Little Kanha to be rocked in cradles priced from ₹100 to ₹5,000 After Kanha's birth on Janmashtami, there is a tradition of rocking him in a cradle. This is why cradles in various designs are selling widely in the market this time. Along with cradles made of vetiver, fabric and flowers, there are also cradles in round and square designs. They are priced from ₹100 to ₹5,000. In addition, wooden toys and special pots for offering butter and sugar crystals to the deity are also available in the market. As a result, the markets of Mathura have become livelier ahead of Janmashtami with preparations for Kanha's adornment and birthday celebrations.

stories.title: Nazia Ilahi says Rahul Gandhi should be arrested:‘I say what’s written in Quran; what will you gain by cutting or tearing me apart?’
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh-based Muslim woman activist and BJP leader Nazia Ilahi Khan is in the headlines after receiving death threats. She said, "I say only what is written in the Quran. If what I said about Prophet Muhammad is wrong, then the pages of the Quran containing those statements should be torn out. What will anyone gain by threatening me or cutting me up?" In an interview with Dainik Bhaskar, she accused Rahul Gandhi of insulting the Manusmriti. She said, "Rahul should be arrested. He is misrepresenting a chapter of the Manusmriti. If he is questioning religious texts, he should also speak about what is written in the Quran." Read the Bhaskar interview… Question: You come from a Muslim background, yet you talk about the economic and social exclusion of Muslims? Answer: I feel that by calling myself a minority, I am harming unity. I do not consider myself a minority at all. By my culture, traditions, way of speaking and clothing, I am an Indian woman. My nature and culture are entirely Hindu-oriented and Sanatani. In my view, there is no such thing as a minority. Today, I want to free Muslim sisters from the hijab. I speak out against triple talaq. I speak out against the malpractices in madrasas and the obscenity that occurs there. I speak about the issue of nikah. I speak out against child marriage. What unconstitutional thing am I saying? If someone is offended, let them be; what does it matter to me? Question: You have filed a complaint accusing Rahul Gandhi of defaming the Manusmriti? Answer: I feel that the police should have arrested Rahul Gandhi, but action is still underway. Rahul Gandhi is looking for caste in disposable glasses, but he is not looking for a terrorist mentality. On the one hand, he picks up a chapter of the Manusmriti and presents an incorrect translation. On the other hand, in a state governed by his own party, a cleric-cum-mufti says that Muslim daughters should stay inside the home. This double standard and political strategy will not work. Now decode those verses of the Quran that speak of killing daughters and beating women. According to the Quran, there are 1,24,000 prophets. Question: Was an FIR filed against you over your alleged remarks about Prophet Muhammad? Answer: I have not made any indecent remark. This is written in four authentic hadiths. The Quran states that our master married Aisha when she was six years old and had relations with her when she was nine. I have only repeated what is written there. If radical Muslims are offended by what I have said, they should tear out the pages where it is written. Nothing will be gained by cutting or tearing me out. If someone reads it again after me, they will say the same thing. Question: The terms "love jihad" and "land jihad" appear repeatedly in your speeches. Why is that? Answer: I believe there are around 20 to 25 cases in my chamber in Kolkata. I am currently handling the "love jihad" cases in the police stations of West Bengal as well. Let the opposition parties or Asaduddin Owaisi himself ask me whether there is any evidence, and I will present a huge collection of files on "love jihad" and "land jihad." What is the Waqf Board? It is a living, practical example of "land jihad." Question: What if the BJP leadership tells you that your statements are damaging the party's image? Answer: I don't think my language is bad. I don't think I say, like Rahul Gandhi, that Prime Minister Modi cannot sleep at night. I have never said that Rahul Gandhi is "Pappu." This kind of misbehavior is carried out by leaders of the Congress and parties associated with the Congress. Question: You often make headlines because of your statements. Is this a political ideology? You have also continued to make statements on triple talaq? Answer: I have worked on triple talaq. I wore out many pairs of slippers at a young age to get it banned. In 2019, I filed a case in the Supreme Court regarding halala. In 2024, I filed a case in the Calcutta High Court seeking an order that Muslim girls should not be married until they have passed Class 12. If any cleric conducts such marriages secretly, he should be arrested. I work on many cases inside the court, and if I am in the headlines because of my statements, then I consider myself very fortunate. Question: Do you have faith in Sanatan Dharma and its gods and goddesses? Answer: My complete faith is in Sanatan Dharma and its gods and goddesses. The universe knows that I am a devotee of Lord Shiva. I perform havan rituals for Mahakali. I also visit temples and perform prayers and worship. Women are prohibited from going to mosques. Muslim women and girls cannot go to mosques because when we pray and bow down, it invalidates the ablution of the men sitting behind us. This is a matter for clerics, muftis, and Islamic scholars. That is why we daughters do not go to mosques. In 2024, when I said in Kolkata that I wanted to offer Eid prayers, the imam there refused permission. I then obtained permission from the Calcutta High Court to visit the mosque. Now, learn about Nazia Ilahi Here's how Nazia made headlines with her outspoken statements Nazia said: “I am a pure Hindu...” Amid the continuous threats she has been receiving, Nazia says, "I recite the Kalma and the Shahada as well. When I sing Vande Mataram, I feel proud." Regarding Rahul Gandhi's comments on Manusmriti, Nazia said, "Rahul Gandhi is putting a hijab-wearing girl on stage and telling her to move away from patriarchy... Come on, that black tent itself is the biggest form of patriarchy. You did not tell that girl that the black tent she is wrapped in is not an essential part of Islam. She has been made to wear it deliberately to hinder her success." Nationwide protests after she spoke against Prophet Muhammad About two months ago, on June 19, Nazia Ilahi Khan was discussing Islam on a podcast. During the discussion, she made several objectionable remarks about Prophet Muhammad and his family. The videos went viral. This led to resentment among the Muslim community. Protests against Nazia began in every state, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Maharashtra. On 22 June 2026, an FIR was registered against her at the Shantinagar Police Station in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra. The next day, an FIR was filed at the JJ Marg Police Station in Mumbai. A third FIR was filed in Malegaon and a fourth in Hyderabad. In Uttar Pradesh, protests were held in Bareilly, Muzaffarnagar, and Bulandshahr. Journey from TMC to BJP

stories.title: 70,000 new jobs in UP before elections:1 lakh youths to get joining letters; govt woos Gen Z
stories.summary: Before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Yogi government is preparing to announce around 70,000 new recruitments. The s for these posts may be released soon. Meanwhile, the government has set a target of issuing appointment letters (joining letters) to more than 100,000 young people over the next four months. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal is personally monitoring the process. He has instructed departments to send information about vacant posts to the concerned recruitment commissions as soon as possible. For the vacancies whose details have already reached the commissions, preparations are underway to release notifications and announce examination dates soon. If the 69,000 assistant teacher recruitment case is resolved by the Supreme Court, the government may announce fresh recruitment for more than 40,000 posts in schools in rural areas under the Basic Education Council. In fact, the opposition wants to make unemployment among Gen Z a major issue ahead of the elections. On the other hand, the government is trying to win the support of young people through new recruitments. Preparing to achieve the 'magic figure' of 10 lakh in 10 years The Yogi government claims to have provided government jobs to more than 930,000 young people during its nine-and-a-half-year tenure so far. If another 1,00,000 appointment letters are distributed over the next four months, the figure will cross the 10-lakh mark. The government will prominently highlight this figure at its election rallies. It will tell the public that approximately 350,000 young people received government jobs under Mayawati's BSP government between 2007 and 2012, and around 200,000 under Akhilesh Yadav's SP government between 2012 and 2017. In contrast, the current government has already crossed the figure of 10 lakh government jobs. 70,000 New Recruitments to Be Made in These Departments 1. Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission (UPESSC): The Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission may issue s for around 40,000 new recruitments by December. Preparations to issue s for recruitment to 38,290 posts have already been completed. Deliberations are under way regarding approximately 1,710 posts. Here is the translation of the image content formatted as a table: 2. Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC): Preparations have been completed for recruitment to more than 13,474 vacant Group C posts in various government departments. 3. Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC): Recruitment is to be conducted for around 10,000 to 12,000 posts through UPPSC. Preparations for issuing the recruitment for these posts have now been completed. More than 100,000 candidates will receive appointment letters by December 33,000 appointments through UPSSSC: The results for 1,640 Gram Panchayat Officer posts and 1,462 Auditor posts have already been released. Major share in the police, Home Guard, and other departments: Appointment letters from UPPSC and the Education Services Commission: 69,000 Teacher Recruitment Case Could Pave the Way for 44,000 Posts A senior government official said that the number of recruitments in the Education Department could exceed 100,000. If the case concerning the recruitment of 69,000 assistant teachers is resolved by the Supreme Court, it could clear the way for a new primary teacher recruitment drive for approximately 44,000 vacant posts in rural areas under the Basic Education Council. Besides, there is pressure to announce recruitment in primary schools even after the TET 2026 results are released. Now it remains to be seen how much this employment gambit can bring young people to the government's side in the election.

stories.title: Women confront SP leader Dakku during debris removal:Uproar over alleged encroachment; he says, ‘Had gone to carry out construction on my own land’
stories.summary: Video from Gorakhpur city went viral on Tuesday showing women protesting against senior Samajwadi Party leader and former Gorakhpur Rural Assembly candidate Zafar Amin Dakku. The women accused him of trying to encroach on a piece of land, while Dakku denied the allegations, saying the property belonged to him and that he had gone there to clear debris and begin construction. The video, reportedly recorded in Khokhar Tola in the Rajghat area, shows Dakku, SP metropolitan president Shabbir Qureshi and some of Dakku’s supporters attempting to remove debris from the land. Three women and several men can be seen opposing them. The women appear angry and can be heard using abusive language against the SP leader. The women alleged that they were assaulted, although no such incident is visible in the video. They also claimed that the land belonged to the government and accused Dakku of attempting to forcibly occupy it. When some of his supporters tried to clear the debris, the women removed it again. Police later reached the spot and tried to calm both sides. The supporters initially stepped aside. Dakku rejected the allegations, saying, “I had gone to clear debris from my land and carry out construction. Three days ago, these women had agreed to the construction in the presence of police, but today they started protesting and making false allegations. I have all the documents related to the land.” What did the SP leader say in response to the women’s allegations? SP leader Zafar Amin Dakku said he purchased the plot in 2017 and has possession of half of it, while the other half is occupied by a tenant. According to Dakku, no one had lived in his portion for around 35 years. He said local residents had complained to the municipal corporation about the house being in a dilapidated condition. Following this, the corporation issued him a notice in 2020 to demolish the structure, followed by another notice in 2023. He was warned that if he failed to demolish it, the corporation would do so and recover the cost from him. The portion was subsequently demolished, and its debris remains on the site. Dakku said the tenants occupying the other portion had approached the court but failed to obtain a stay order. He claimed they were also unable to produce ownership documents when asked by the police. According to Dakku, an inspector visited the spot three days ago, when the tenants agreed to allow construction provided they were not disturbed. He said this discussion took place in the presence of police. However, when he returned to begin construction, the same women started protesting. Dakku said the matter has now been referred to the CO, where both sides will present their documents. “I have all the documents and will present them there,” he said. ‘Both parties have been summoned’, says CO Kotwali CO Omkar Dutt Tripathi said the matter was related to a land dispute. He clarified that no assault had taken place at the spot. Both parties have been summoned to his office along with their documents.

stories.title: Rifle stolen, man stopped cutting hair, beard for 4 years:Wife left him too; says, ‘I’ll get a haircut now’
stories.summary: College operator made an unusual vow after his licensed rifle was stolen in Agra. Four years ago, thieves broke into his house and stole jewellery worth lakhs of rupees along with his licensed rifle. He was also mocked by people after the incident. Upset by this, college operator Uday Singh vowed that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until his rifle was recovered. He kept his vow for four years, leaving his hair and beard uncut. On Tuesday, police recovered Uday Singh’s stolen licensed rifle. After learning that the rifle had been found, Uday Singh thanked the police and said, “Now I will cut my hair and shave my beard.” The incident took place in Agra’s Saiyan area. See 2 pictures… Now read the full case Uday Singh, a resident of Saiyan, is a former village head and runs Maa Durga Devi Higher Secondary School. In 2022, his house was burgled. The thieves stole 22 tolas of gold, ₹4 lakh in cash, silver jewellery and his licensed rifle. Determined to get his rifle back, Uday Singh would visit the police station every day after finishing his work at the college. He was also mocked by villagers following the theft. They would taunt him, saying that his house had been burgled despite having a rifle at home. When the rifle remained unrecovered, Uday Singh vowed that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the rifle was found. He kept his vow for four years, leaving his hair and beard uncut throughout this period. 'My hair and beard reminded me of the rifle', says Uday Uday Singh said, “I bought this rifle in 2003. It was dearer to me than my children. I used to sleep with the rifle. On May 9, 2022, I was unwell and had severe pain in my leg, so I did not sleep with the rifle that night. I kept it in another room. My wife, Rekha Devi, forgot to bolt the inner room from the inside.” “My house was burgled that same day. The thieves stole the licensed rifle, ₹4 lakh in cash, 22 tolas of gold jewellery and 2.5kg of silver. I was more upset about losing my licensed rifle than the cash and jewellery.” Wife says, ‘If you don’t cut your hair, I won’t stay with you’ Uday Singh said, “My wife left me and went to her parents’ home. She told me that if I did not cut my hair, she would not stay with me. After a lot of persuasion, she returned home, but I did not break my vow. For the past four years, I had been living with long hair and a long beard. My family members also asked me several times to cut my hair, but I refused.” He said his wife, Rekha Devi, suffered paralysis on June 1 this year and remained hospitalised for about a month. She was later brought home, where she has been receiving care. His wife was also extremely happy after learning that the rifle had been recovered. He said her condition had also started improving. “Within a day of hearing that the rifle had been found, she started trying to stand and walk on her own. Now that my rifle has been recovered, I will fulfil my vow and get my hair and beard cut.” Accused arrested after 4 years Meanwhile, Kheragarh police, along with the SOG and surveillance teams, arrested wanted criminal Dhruv Singh, who was carrying a ₹25,000 reward, at the Fatehpurpura cut. Police recovered a stolen licensed rifle, two live .315-bore cartridges, ₹50,000 in cash and a motorcycle from his possession. Three burglary cases are already registered against him at Kagarol police station. DCP West Aditya Kumar said a ₹10,000 reward had initially been announced for Dhruv Singh, which was later increased to ₹25,000. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to committing several thefts along with his associates. Police are now searching for absconding accused Bablu and Aniruddh.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar says ‘SP-DM through reservation, CM-PM through votes’:Vows to live like a lion as long as alive
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar addressed a public meeting in Mau on Tuesday regarding the 2027 Assembly elections. He said, "The Azad Samaj Party will contest the Assembly elections with full strength. No power in the world can abolish reservation. Reservation is not anyone's charity; it is a right." During the meeting, he raised the slogan: "We will obtain SP-DM posts through reservation and choose the CM-PM through votes." Chandrashekhar told the youth that he would not live for 100 years, but as long as he lived, he would live like a lion. During the event, the party appointed Sagar Yadav as its in-charge candidate for the Madhuban Assembly seat. Chandrashekhar appealed to the youth to ensure Sagar Yadav's victory in the 2027 elections. Read the key points made by Chandrashekhar Azad Party has been preparing for elections since 2022 Chandrashekhar Azad said, “In the first phase, the party has appointed in-charges for 45 Assembly constituencies. The organisation has been continuously preparing for elections since the 2022 Assembly polls.” Referring to the Lok Sabha elections, he said the party had contested from Nagina and Domariyaganj. While it won the Nagina seat, it secured more than 80,000 votes in Domariyaganj. Following these results, the party has stepped up efforts to further strengthen its organisation. Claim to give SC, ST, OBC and minority communities political representation Chandrashekhar said that in the 2027 elections, the party would seek to give people from weaker sections an opportunity to take on leadership roles. He said no caste or community would be denied an opportunity, and the party would work to bring people from all sections into the Legislative Assembly. However, when asked how many Assembly seats the party would contest, Chandrashekhar said the decision would be taken at the party level. Chandrashekhar also claimed that the party's candidate, Shivsagar, would win the Madhuban Assembly seat. He said Shivsagar had been active in the area for a long time and had staged sit-ins and protests over people's issues. He claimed that the public had faith in him and that the Azad Samaj Party would win the Madhuban seat by a significant margin. Takes dig at ‘Spain’ remark about Gorakhpur Chandrashekhar Azad also took a dig at the ‘Spain’ remark made about Gorakhpur. He said, “Earlier, we used to hear about Spain in Gorakhpur, but now they are saying that Gorakhpur has become Spain. When I came here, I thought I might need a visa to enter Spain.” He said he was concerned about the people of Uttar Pradesh, where young people are migrating in search of jobs due to unemployment. He alleged that paper leaks were occurring repeatedly and that those raising their voices against injustice were being prevented from holding protests. He also said several parts of the state continue to struggle with waterlogging and flooding. Referring to Madhuban as a flood-affected area, he alleged that funds are released every year in the name of flood management, but adequate preparations are not made in time. People's problems are more important On the question of the AI video related to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Chandrashekhar Azad said that such videos can be created using AI. Political parties continue to trade allegations, but this will not solve the actual problems of the people. Our party is fighting for the issues concerning the public. Reservation, employment and law and order are major issues in UP Chandrashekhar described reservation, jobs for the youth, and law and order as major issues in the state. Taking aim at the government over law and order, he mentioned the broad daylight murder of Ankit Baliyan. He said, “Ankit Baliyan was murdered, and the shooters were later killed in an encounter. Two shooters have been killed. Should Ankit Baliyan have been murdered? Does the government have any answer to this?” He alleged that the state's law and order situation is poor. Uttar Pradesh has been turned into a "jungle state." The public is troubled by the current government and is waiting for the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: Facebook friendship leads to ₹97 lakh fraud of retired JE:Promised huge profits in dollars, posed as Tamil Nadu crime branch officer to threaten him
stories.summary: Fraudsters allegedly cheated an 80-year-old retired junior engineer of ₹97 lakh on the pretext of share-trading investments in Lucknow. The scammers first contacted him through Facebook and persuaded him to invest money. They later showed huge profits on a fake app and demanded several million rupees more in the name of taxes, conversion charges and insurance to release the money. Harimohan, 80, a retired junior engineer with the Irrigation Department and a resident of Ashiyana Sector-H, said he was using Facebook on April 26 when he came into contact with a man named Ganesh Agrawal. The man lured him with promises of making huge profits in dollars through share trading and persuaded him to download an app. On May 12, Harimohan deposited ₹26 lakh in two instalments for investment at the accused's instruction. After some time, the app showed a profit of $240,000 and stated that the amount had been deposited in London's Workley Bank. ₹71.20 lakh demanded to withdraw the profits When Harimohan tried to withdraw the profit, he received a call from an unknown number. The caller identified himself as Hardik Patel, a revenue officer with the Customs Department. He asked Harimohan to deposit ₹71.20 lakh towards capital tax, conversion charges and insurance to release the profit amount. Harimohan believed the fraudsters' claims and, under pressure, deposited the additional amount. However, neither his principal amount was returned nor was the profit shown on the app released. Threatened with FIR when he asked for his money When Harimohan asked Hardik Patel to return his money, the accused allegedly became angry. He claimed that ₹9 lakh out of the ₹26 lakh invested by Harimohan was fraudulent money. The accused then intimidated him, claiming that his entire investment amount had been sent to the RBI in Delhi and that the matter would be investigated. He also threatened to have an FIR registered against Harimohan by the Tamil Nadu Crime Branch. Alarmed by the threats, Harimohan did not tell his family about the fraud. When his family members noticed that he was distressed and questioned him, he told them about the entire incident on Monday. He then went to the cybercrime police station with his family and filed a complaint. Inspector Alok Rai said considerable time had passed since the fraud, making it difficult to freeze the money.

stories.title: Man gets life term for raping, robbing minor:Victim was travelling to Kolkata to meet boyfriend; accused befriended her on Instagram
stories.summary: Young man who raped and robbed a 17-year-old girl while she was travelling to Kolkata to meet her boyfriend has been sentenced to life imprisonment. Additional District and Sessions Judge-20 Pawan Kumar Rai also imposed a fine of ₹1.47 lakh on the convict. The accused met the girl at Gorakhpur railway station. Claiming to be a railway employee, he lured her away and took her to a forest about 5km from the station, where he raped her. He then fled with her mobile phone, jacket and ₹10,000. The accused also allegedly threatened the girl's brother by calling him around 40 times. Left home after an argument The girl's father lodged a complaint at Jajmau police station, stating that his daughter had left home on January 11, 2024, upset and intending to meet her boyfriend. She had become friends with him through Instagram. On January 12, she met a man outside Gorakhpur railway station who introduced himself as Salim Khan and claimed to be a railway employee. According to the complaint, he lured her away and took her to a forest about 5km away, where he raped her. After the assault, the accused allegedly fled with the minor's mobile phone, jacket and ₹10,000. From January 12 to 16, he used the stolen phone to speak to his wife and the girl's brother. During these conversations, he allegedly threatened the girl's brother. The two spoke around 40 times during this period. Prosecution examined 7 witnesses Police traced and arrested the accused based on his location and sent him to jail. During questioning, he identified himself as Chauthi Gupta, a resident of Mahiganj in Deoria. The case was tried in the court of ADJ-20. Special Public Prosecutor Chandrakant Sharma said the prosecution examined seven witnesses during the trial. After considering the evidence, the court found the accused guilty and sentenced him to life imprisonment and a fine of ₹1.47 lakh.

stories.title: Water-Ethanol found in petrol pump tank in Kanpur:Tank sealed pending probe; money refunded to 22 customers
stories.summary: Video purportedly showing a water-like substance being dispensed from a petrol pump in Kanpur has surfaced. In the video, a petrol pump employee is seen filling a bottle through a pipe, but instead of petrol, a water-like liquid appears to come out. However, there has been no official confirmation so far that the petrol was adulterated with water or ethanol. Meanwhile, following complaints from customers, some were refunded their money. The management has also suspended operations of the concerned tank pending an investigation. The incident took place at Shivay Filling Station in Kadikheda, Kalyanpur. Petrol pump manager Anubhav Awasthi said, Complaints about irregularities in the petrol were received from members of the public. At present, it is not clear whether the petrol was mixed with water, ethanol or some other substance. The maintenance team of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Bhauti, Kanpur, has been called to check the fuel quality. 22 customers refunded for petrol According to the pump management, around 22 customers who had filled their vehicles with petrol at the concerned pump were refunded their money on Tuesday. The refunds were issued after the complaints came to light, addressing customers' concerns and easing apprehensions over the quality of the petrol. Tank to remain closed until investigation is complete The manager said the tank from which the petrol was supplied has been temporarily shut down. No petrol will be sold from the tank until the cause of the suspected quality issue is determined. A decision on reopening the tank will be taken based on the findings and report of the BPCL team. So far, there has been no confirmation that the petrol was adulterated with water, ethanol or any other substance. Therefore, it would be premature to draw any conclusion based solely on the viral video. The investigation report will establish the actual cause of the suspected quality issue. SHO, ‘Action will be taken based on investigation’ Kalyanpur Station House Officer Keshav Kumar Tiwari said police have not yet received any written complaint in the matter. Further action will be taken based on the investigation report submitted by the District Supply Officer. The petrol pump has currently been shut down, and further action will follow based on the findings.

stories.title: Man gets 10-year jail for abetting wife’s suicide:Victim took fatal step after harassment over dowry
stories.summary: In Agra, a court has sentenced a man to 10 years in prison for harassing his wife over dowry and driving her to suicide. Additional District and Sessions Judge-4 Pawan Kumar Srivastava also imposed a fine of ₹25,000 on the accused, Ravi Kumar. The case was registered at Khandauli police station. According to the complaint filed by Bitti Devi, her daughter Sadhana married Ravi Kumar, son of Jawahar Singh and a resident of Vas Agariya village in Khandauli, around six years ago. She alleged that Ravi Kumar and his family members harassed Sadhana over dowry as they were dissatisfied with what she had brought. Unable to bear the alleged harassment, Sadhana hanged herself at around 8pm on April 15, 2024, and died. Case pending in Agra court Following Sadhana's death, Bitti Devi's complaint led police to register a case against Ravi Kumar and his family members. Ravi Kumar was arrested on April 23, 2024, and sent to jail. During the investigation, police found insufficient evidence against the other accused and subsequently filed a charge sheet against Ravi Kumar alone on July 16, 2024. Verdict based on statements of 9 witnesses and post-mortem report During the trial, the prosecution examined nine witnesses, including complainant Bitti Devi, Sadhana's father Rameshwar Nagoria, her sister Anjali and ACP Piyush Kant Rai. The deceased's post-mortem report was also presented before the court. Assistant District Government Counsel Mangal Singh represented the prosecution. After considering the witness statements, post-mortem report and other evidence, ADJ-4 Pawan Kumar Srivastava found Ravi Kumar guilty. The court sentenced him to 10 years in prison and imposed a fine of ₹25,000.

stories.title: Former encounter specialist IPS officer may become Ram Mandir CEO:Trust meeting in Ayodhya tomorrow, several key decisions expected
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh IPS officer Rajesh Pandey, known as an encounter specialist, may be appointed as the first CEO (Chief Executive Officer) of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. His appointment could be approved at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust meeting on Wednesday. This will be the trust's third meeting since the Mandir donation theft case came to light. A native of Prayagraj, Rajesh Pandey carried out more than 80 encounters during his service, including the encounter of gangster Shri Prakash Shukla. He was also a founding member of two specialised UP Police units — the Special Task Force (STF) and the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS). The trust may announce the formation of a Prasad Committee and Parikrama Committee at the meeting. It may also decide to increase the number of members of the Religious Committee and fill three vacant positions in the trust. However, the appointment of a permanent general secretary is considered unlikely at this meeting. Swami Govind Dev Giri, chairman of the Ram Mandir Religious Committee and treasurer of the trust, and trustee and general secretary Krishna Mohan have reached Ayodhya. Swami Govind Dev Giri also visited the Ram Mandir and offered prayers to Ram Lalla. Proposal to install 2 ACs in sanctum sanctorum may be approved Two air conditioners have been brought for Ram Lalla's service one with a capacity of 1 tonne and the other 3 tonnes. Both are proposed to be installed inside the sanctum sanctorum. Installing them will require drilling holes in the walls. The Religious Committee has already submitted a proposal to the Trust for their installation. The proposal may be approved at Wednesday's meeting. Why are the prasad and parikrama committees being formed? What decisions were taken in the 2 meetings held after the offering theft? July 2: Champat Rai and Anil Mishra's resignations accepted The Trust accepted the resignations of General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra. Retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan was appointed acting general secretary in their place. The Trust also displayed four gold and silver items, claiming they had been stolen from the Mandir. It said it had received ₹3,264 crore in donations, of which ₹2,370 crore had already been spent on Mandir construction and other works. July 22: Religious committee formed with 9 saints The Trust took two major decisions. First, it formed a nine-member Religious Committee comprising five saints from Ayodhya and four members of the Mandir Trust. Swami Govind Dev Giri, the Trust's treasurer, was appointed chairman. Second, the Trust decided to appoint a spokesperson and secretary. It also said that despite various allegations and misinformation, there had been no decline in the number of devotees visiting the Ram Mandir. Interviews held for 16 candidates for Ram Mandir CEO post Interviews were conducted on July 11 and 12 for 16 shortlisted candidates for the post of Ram Mandir CEO. Three names were later recommended to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Each interview lasted around 40 to 50 minutes. Candidates were questioned about their administrative experience, responsibilities they had handled, their work in the religious sector and their faith in Lord Ram. According to sources, candidates were also asked whether they kept a shikha (tuft of hair), wore a janeu (sacred thread), were vegetarian or non-vegetarian, consumed alcohol, and whether they were devout Hindus or had an ordinary level of religious faith. More than 5,300 people had applied for the CEO post, of whom 16 were shortlisted for interviews. The interview panel included retired Justice Pramod Kohli, former scientist Dr Suresh Hawde and retired Lieutenant General Vishnukant Chaturvedi. 16 candidates interviewed over 2 days for Ram Mandir CEO post 5,585 people applied for the CEO post, of whom 16 were shortlisted for interviews. The interview panel included retired Justice Pramod Kohli, former scientist Dr Suresh Hawde and retired Lieutenant General Vishnu Kant Chaturvedi. The 16 shortlisted candidates were interviewed in Ayodhya on August 11 and 12. Following the interviews, the search committee submitted the names of three candidates to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Each candidate was interviewed for 40 to 50 minutes. They were asked questions about their administrative experience, responsibilities, work in the religious sector and faith in Lord Ram. According to sources, candidates were also asked whether they kept a shikha (tuft), wore a janeu (sacred thread), were strictly vegetarian or ate meat, consumed alcohol, and whether they considered themselves staunch Hindus or simply people of faith. SIT submitted preliminary report on June 23; 8 arrested 2 days later The offering theft case first came to light on June 7. The Uttar Pradesh government's SIT submitted its preliminary report to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on June 23. An FIR was registered on June 25 based on a complaint filed by Trust member Krishna Mohan. It named eight people, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, but did not name senior office-bearers such as Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra. Within hours of the FIR being registered, police arrested all eight accused, including Tinnu. They are currently lodged in Faizabad jail and have been accused of stealing cash and jewellery while counting offerings. Following the SIT's preliminary report, General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned, taking moral responsibility for the matter. The Trust accepted both resignations and also removed Gopal Nagarkatte from its list of special invitees. Supreme Court ordered formation of a second SIT Four separate petitions related to the alleged theft of Mandir offerings have been filed before the Supreme Court. Apart from seeking a CBI probe, the petitions also call for the formation of an expert committee to examine various issues concerning the management of donations at the Mandir. The earlier SIT was reporting its findings to the state government, while the newly formed SIT will submit periodic status reports directly to the Supreme Court. The court is monitoring the investigation into the matter. The Supreme Court observed that police officers play a direct and more effective role in criminal investigations, including the technical aspects of investigating theft cases. Accordingly, the DIG and SSP have been made members of the new SIT, placing the investigation directly under senior police officers.

stories.title: 16-year-younger lover chops woman into 18 pieces:Packs body in trolley bag and leaves it on train; Agra police arrest accused couple in Manipur
stories.summary: 18 body parts found in a trolley bag on the Tamil Nadu Express at Agra Cantt railway station 25 days ago belonged to a woman. She was allegedly in a relationship with a married man who was 16 years younger than her. As the dispute over the relationship escalated, the man and his wife allegedly murdered the woman. The accused allegedly cut the body into small pieces using a cutter. They then packed the remains into a trolley bag. Police said the woman's hands, legs and ribs were cooked with flour and vegetables, while the remaining body parts were placed in the train's general compartment. Rajeev Dixit, CO of the Agra GRP, said 22-year-old Manikuddin Laskar and his wife, Bhagwati Majhi, were arrested in Manipur. According to police, the accused believed the crime would never be uncovered, but CCTV footage exposed their entire conspiracy. The Chennai Police have taken both accused into custody. They are also investigating financial transactions and other aspects linked to the murder. Accused traced with help of footage from 350 CCTV cameras On August 5, the Tamil Nadu Express (12621), travelling from Chennai to New Delhi, reached Agra Cantt station. Passengers noticed a foul smell coming from a trolley bag in the general compartment and alerted the Government Railway Police (GRP). When the bag was opened, human body parts wrapped in polythene were found inside. The post-mortem examination revealed another shocking detail: some of the body parts had reportedly been cooked with flour and vegetables. Given the seriousness of the case, the Chennai Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Agra GRP launched a joint investigation. Footage from around 350 CCTV cameras installed in and around Chennai Central station was examined. The footage showed both accused placing the trolley bag on the train before fleeing Chennai for Manipur. The GRP CO said, “Accused believed they would never be caught, but CCTV footage exposed their entire conspiracy. Both were arrested in Manipur and brought to Chennai. We are now investigating the financial transactions and other aspects linked to the murder.” The GRP said questioning of the accused is underway and that the weapon allegedly used in the crime, along with other evidence, will be recovered soon. Deceased woman’s 17 year old son Hayatun Nisha, 38, from Jagatsinghpur, Odisha, had been living separately from her husband in Chennai. She had reportedly been in a relationship with Manikuddin for around six months. Around July 20, Nisha moved into a rented accommodation at Manik's house in Guduvanchery. Her 17-year-old son, Yusuf Khan, was also living with her. According to police, Manik was already in a relationship with Bhagwati Majhi, who lived with him as his wife in a live-in relationship. The investigation revealed that Bhagwati learnt about Manik and Nisha's relationship, leading to frequent arguments. As the dispute escalated, the couple allegedly conspired to kill Nisha. After the murder, her body was allegedly cut into 18 pieces. Some of the remains were placed in large containers and cooked, while the remaining parts, including the torso, were packed into a red trolley bag and placed on the Tamil Nadu Express, which travelled to Agra. Police found meat and body parts during search Yusuf was not at the house when his mother was allegedly killed. On 21 August, he went to the house to meet her. When he could not find her, he asked people in the neighbourhood but received no information. Manik and Bhagwati were also missing. Yusuf subsequently filed a missing-person report at Guduvanchery police station. Police searched the house and allegedly recovered meat and other human body parts from a large container. The investigation also revealed possible financial transactions between those involved. Yusuf reportedly told police that he did not approve of his mother's lifestyle and had therefore started living separately from her. He also expressed suspicion that Manikuddin and Bhagwati Majhi had killed his mother following an argument. 350 CCTV cameras checked, young man and woman seen with trolley bag Zero FIR was registered at the Agra Cantt GRP police station on August 5, the day the body parts were found. As the investigation progressed, links to Chennai emerged, following which the case was transferred to the Chennai GRP. Chennai Police then began investigating based on clues recovered from the trolley bag. CCTV footage from Chennai Central Railway Station was examined, including footage from Platform 4. At around 10 pm on August 3, a young man and a woman were seen carrying a red trolley bag. The same bag was later found in the general compartment of the Tamil Nadu Express at Agra Cantt on August 5, containing dismembered human remains. Based on the CCTV footage and other evidence, the investigation team traced the case to Guduvanchery, where the woman's dismembered body was subsequently recovered.

stories.title: 4 youths go missing from Gorakhpur MR Home:CCTV captures them leaving, search underway at bus stand and railway station
stories.summary: Four young men went missing from a government shelter home, known as the MR Home, in Gorakhpur's Rajghat area on Tuesday morning. All four are reportedly mentally ill and had been staying at the facility, which houses people with mental health conditions found abandoned. Staff searched for the four men for several hours after they went missing. When they could not be traced, the warden informed Rajghat police station in the afternoon. Police then launched a search across the city. According to the warden, all four men left the MR Home between around 9.30 am and 10 am and did not return. Staff searched the surrounding areas but found no trace of them. After being informed, police began examining CCTV footage from cameras installed at the shelter home and nearby locations. Search underway at railway station and bus stand Police are examining CCTV footage to establish which direction the four men took after leaving the shelter home. Searches have also been launched at key locations across the city. Information about the missing men has been shared with bus stands and railway stations, where police personnel have been asked to look for them based on their identities and physical descriptions. Police stations in neighbouring areas have also been alerted. SP City Nimish Patil said teams were conducting searches across the city to locate the four men. CCTV footage was being examined and information had been shared with bus stands and railway stations. He said efforts were underway to trace all four soon.
