stories.title: Agra inspector falls during scuffle with protesters:Enters lawyers’ chamber to escape; UGC regulation protest blocks highway
stories.summary: Clash broke out between police and members of the Savarna community and Karni Sena in Agra after around 300 protesters were stopped while marching towards the SDM office against the UGC’s new rules. An argument broke out between the protesters and police, which soon escalated into pushing and shoving. During the scuffle, an inspector fell on the road. Police then resorted to a lathi charge, further escalating the situation. The inspector ran into lawyers’ chambers for safety, after which police closed the chamber’s gate. Additional police forces from nearby stations were called in to bring the situation under control. The protesters later staged a sit-in on the Agra-Kanpur National Highway and began reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, causing a long traffic jam. When police tried to persuade them to clear the road, the protesters said they would not end the protest until the inspector was removed. Senior officials later intervened and managed to pacify the protesters. Karni sena district chief, inspector carried out lathi charge Karni Sena district chief Shivam Rathore said they were following the pre-decided route and marching peacefully to submit a memorandum to the SDM. He claimed police tried to stop them at least four to five times along the way, but the protesters continued because they represented people from all sections of society. He said, “We are Kshatriyas. We are neither afraid nor willing to back down. An inspector stopped us at the tehsil gate. While trying to prevent us from moving forward, he carried out a lathi charge on at least eight to 10 of our people. We will not move from here until Inspector Satyaprakash is removed. We will stay here and submit our memorandum.” Protest ends after assurance Anshuman Thakur, a member of the System Reform Organisation, said the UGC's new draft regulations could affect the principles of social and constitutional justice in universities. He claimed that the proposed committees did not ensure adequate representation of disadvantaged sections, which could affect students' interests. He alleged that the police administration misbehaved with the protesters and carried out a lathi charge when they reached the tehsil headquarters. In protest, the demonstrators turned their memorandum programme into a sit-in and demanded action against the police personnel involved. Administrative officials assured the protesters that the matter would be investigated and action would be taken if anyone was found guilty. Following the assurance, the protest was called off peacefully and the memorandum was submitted. ‘Police officers’ behaviour was highly objectionable’ Savarna community leader Gajendra Parmar said, “The behaviour of the police officers while we were submitting the memorandum was highly objectionable and inappropriate. When we protested, the police resorted to a lathi charge. If the concerned police officer is not suspended, members of the Savarna community will intensify their protest and gherao the Agra Commissioner’s Office.” Why are people opposing the UGC’s new rules? The UGC notified its new regulations on January 13, 2026, titled the Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026. The rules require colleges and universities to set up special committees, helplines and monitoring teams to prevent caste-based discrimination. These teams will specifically address complaints from SC, ST and OBC students. The government says the changes are aimed at improving fairness and accountability in higher education institutions. However, the regulations are being opposed by some groups, who claim they are biased against students from the General category. Critics argue that the rules could portray upper-caste students as “natural offenders”. General-category students have also expressed concerns that the regulations could encourage discrimination against them on college and university campuses and create unrest in educational institutions. He said their fight against the UGC regulations was not over but had only just begun. A meeting with fellow members would be held soon to decide the future course of action, and a larger-scale protest would be launched if necessary. Upper-caste community leader Gajendra Parmar said, “The behaviour of the police personnel during the submission of the memorandum was highly objectionable and inappropriate. When we protested against it, the police carried out a lathi charge. If the police personnel concerned is not suspended immediately, members of the upper-caste community will intensify the agitation and lay siege to the Agra Commissioner's office.”

stories.title: Ganga Expressway caves in, covered with shawl to hide it:7-ft-deep pit forms in Unnao; repair work begins after barricading
stories.summary: Nearly 7-foot-deep crater has appeared on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh. What has raised eyebrows is that a shawl was placed over the crater, apparently to conceal it, before the area was barricaded. A video of the crater, which appeared on the Prayagraj-bound lane near the Basiratganj toll plaza on Monday, has also surfaced. The company responsible for maintaining the expressway rushed to the spot and began repair work on Tuesday. Traffic has been diverted from the affected stretch during the repairs. Earlier, on August 17, a 200-metre section along the edge of the expressway near Sonik village was washed away after soil was eroded. Repairs took two days. The 594-kilometre Ganga Expressway directly connects Meerut with Prayagraj. The expressway was completed just four months ago and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Hardoi on 29 April, 2026. Take a look at 3 pictures… Now, understand the complete matter It has been raining intermittently in Unnao for the past five consecutive days. During the current monsoon season, the Ganga Expressway has caved in twice. The first incident occurred on 17 August, when the road collapsed at kilometre 421. Soil along a 200-metre stretch near Sonik village, under the jurisdiction of Dahi police station, was washed away, causing the road to cave in. Repair work continued for two days. Now, 14 days later, the road has caved in again. During heavy rain late on Monday night, a section of the expressway collapsed near the Basiratganj toll plaza, around 2.5 kilometres from the previous site near Sonik. This time, a pit measuring approximately 7 feet deep and 5 feet wide opened up on the road. The deep crater posed a serious risk to vehicles travelling along the expressway. Road repaired and restored Patel Infrastructure manager RS Mishra said a high-tension power line passes near the toll plaza. According to safety regulations, a distance of 14 metres must be maintained between the road and the overhead power lines. Therefore, the toll plaza could not be built any higher. He said the sudden heavy rainfall led to waterlogging in the area, causing the road to subside and a crater to form. Mishra added that the damaged section has now been repaired and the road restored. A protective wall will be built along the toll plaza to prevent water from accumulating there again. Teams have also been kept on alert to deal with any emergency and carry out immediate repairs if required. Employees on night patrol spotted the pothole Employees of Patel Infrastructure, the company constructing nearly 200 kilometres of the expressway, spotted the pothole during a routine night patrol. They immediately barricaded the damaged section, diverted traffic around 300 metres before the spot and began repair work. Meanwhile, a shawl was placed over the pothole. Passersby who noticed it on the expressway recorded a video, which has since surfaced. The video claims that the shawl, which was similar in colour to the road, had been placed over the pothole to conceal it. After the video went viral, the shawl was reportedly removed. However, there has been no official confirmation about who placed the shawl or why it was put there. Sanjeev Tiwari, manager of Patel Infrastructure said, Any issue that has developed on the expressway, including near the toll plaza, is being addressed. It will be repaired soon.

stories.title: People in Chitrakoot recall Nepal-like devastation:Mud now fills homes and shops, goods worth crores destroyed
stories.summary: “The memory of the terrifying flood situation makes our blood run cold. Only we know what the conditions were like at that time. For a moment, it seemed that after Nepal, a massive tragedy had struck here as well. We did not get even a moment to recover. Within 2-3 hours, there was water everywhere.” "Homes and shops had been submerged. People were trapped on the upper floors. Goods stored in shops, cylinders, tents, and the huts of temporary shops-all of it was swept away by the water. Even the massive bridges were submerged. We have been living here for the past 30 years, but we have never witnessed such conditions before." These are the words of the people of Chitrakoot who endured the devastating floodwaters of the Mandakini River for 48 hours. The flood wreaked such havoc that years of people's hard work were washed away, and they were forced to abandon their homes and shops and flee to save their lives. Now that the floodwaters have receded somewhat, the horrifying scene of devastation is clearly visible. When the people who returned to their homes saw their belongings destroyed, tears welled up in their eyes. More than 400 shops are covered in mud. A thick layer of dirt has settled inside the houses. Losses amounting to crores of rupees have been incurred. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the people to understand their pain. Read the report... Pictures of the devastation... Shopkeepers said they suffered losses worth crores Water reached the loft, causing losses worth crores Tulsi Prasad, owner of Uma Tulsi Puja Vastu Bhandar on Ratnavali Marg, broke down while describing the losses. He said that the entire fully stocked shop had been flooded. It contained goods worth at least ₹90 lakh. There is no way to know the exact extent of the damage. A shopkeeper, Raju Gaikwad, said that there had been a very severe flood. The water was flowing above the doors. Cylinders and other belongings were all swept away. He suffered a loss of at least ₹25,000-₹30,000. Meanwhile, a woman said, "My hut, utensils, taps-everything was swept away. Now we will have to start everything afresh. Where will the money for this come from?" Goods ruined after water entered the shops, mud everywhere inside Mahadev Food Plaza, located on Ratnavali Marg, also could not escape the floodwaters. Water entered the shops here, completely ruining the merchandise. Shopkeeper Lavlesh Kumar said that he alone suffered a loss of ₹2.5 million. After the flood, when he opened the shop and saw the condition inside, there was mud and destroyed goods everywhere. An elderly man was seen removing the remaining goods from his shop. When we spoke to him, he said, "Our house was on the second floor. Even there, all our belongings were destroyed. The neighboring shopkeeper's entire stock has also been wiped out." Temples also affected, appeal for help made to CM Yogi The floods have also affected monasteries and temples. The wheat, lentils, rice and flour stored at the Nirmohi Akhara were soaked in water and spoiled. Food used to be prepared here for the saints. Now, cleaning work is underway at the akhara after the floods. Rations and other items are being taken outside. Munna Shastri, who lives at the Nirmohi Akhara, said, "I assist Guruji. The akhara has suffered a loss of ₹50 lakh. Every day, 400-500 people receive prasad. Accordingly, supplies for the entire year were stored here, all of which have been destroyed. There were 200 quintals of rice, 200 quintals of wheat, lentils, sugar-everything. Nothing has been left." "All the supplies were submerged. Some people managed to retrieve a few things, while others could not. We have been living here for 30 years, but we have never experienced such a situation in our lives. In our villages, we say, 'Bhage bhui nahi milat rahi,' meaning there was not even a piece of land to be found where one could set foot and escape. Here, millions of people remained trapped wherever they were," Shastri said. Some people fled, but the elderly and the visually impaired were unable to leave and were left behind. The shopkeepers' merchandise was also left behind. The condition of the monasteries and temples has become extremely deplorable. Water and debris are lying everywhere. We will appeal to the government and administration, as well as Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, to look into the matter and help us. Projects worth crores also washed away in the floods, cooking fires remained unlit in homes Rising water level raises concern again, DM says people should move to safe places The water level of the Mandakini has started rising slowly again. At 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday, the river was flowing 6 meters above the danger mark. The Mandakini's water level is currently 133 metres, while the danger mark is 125 metres. Concern is still clearly visible on the faces of people living along the riverbank. Chitrakoot DM Pulkit Garg said, "The water level of the Mandakini River is rising very rapidly. According to the information we have received so far, there is a possibility that the water level may rise significantly this time as well. Therefore, sensitive areas are being evacuated." “An appeal is being made for people to move to safe places immediately. The administration has set up flood shelters; please go there. Staying on the upper floors of your homes may be somewhat risky. We are making announcements continuously. Our teams are active,” the DM said.

stories.title: Kanpur teacher recruitment scam to face vigilance probe:Fake panel of 9 teachers issued in 2024, 2 joined schools
stories.summary: A two-year-old case involving the issuance of a teacher recruitment panel through a fraudulent email in aided schools in Kanpur has once again made headlines. Following the government's orders, the Vigilance Department will now investigate the matter. The SP of the Kanpur Vigilance Department has sent a letter to the Joint Director of Education (JD), Kanpur Division, seeking records related to the case. The letter requests the submission of records on nine points. The matter came to light in 2024, when an email was sent to the Kanpur District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) from a fake email ID created in the name of the then Additional Director of Secondary Education, following which a panel of nine teachers was issued. Two of these teachers even joined the respective schools. One female teacher was also paid lakhs of rupees as salary for approximately four months. With the Vigilance investigation now beginning, activity has once again intensified in the Education Department. Documents sought from the JD on nine points The letter sent by the SP Vigilance sought documents ranging from the fake email to records related to the appointments. These include the forged email, appointment letters of the teachers related to the case, and other records. After receiving the documents, the Vigilance department will proceed with the investigation into the entire matter. Following the Vigilance department's activation in the two-year-old case, discussions have also intensified among officials and employees of the Education Department. Panel of nine teachers was issued through a fake email The case concerns fabricated appointments in unaided aided schools. In 2024, a fake email ID of the Additional Director of Secondary Education was created and an email was sent to the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS), Kanpur. Based on this email, a panel of nine teachers was issued. The then DIOS-II, Munnilal, mistook the email for the official ID of the Additional Director of Secondary Education and arranged for the appointment of one female teacher each at Madan Mohan Agrawal Inter College in Kidwai Nagar and Arya Kanya Inter College in Govind Nagar. One female teacher received a salary worth lakhs within four months Two teachers included in the panel joined the schools, while seven did not. The female teacher appointed at the Kidwai Nagar school continued to receive a salary for about four months. During this period, she was paid lakhs of rupees. Later, when the case of the fake email and the appointments came to light, an investigation into the entire matter was launched, and a case was registered at Colonelganj Police Station. The role of two clerks was also found to be suspicious During the investigation, the roles of an outsourcing clerk working at the RAMSA office and a female clerk from the DIOS office were also considered suspicious. Both were questioned, but no action was taken as no concrete documents were found against them. In addition, the ACP Colonelganj had summoned the then DIOS, Arun Kumar, in connection with the investigation. The name of a retired DIOS had also surfaced in the case. However, as time passed, the investigation lost momentum and the matter faded away. Nearly two years later, the case has once again come into the spotlight after the Vigilance Department took over the investigation on the government's orders. The SP Vigilance has sought the necessary records from the JD, Kanpur Division. Once the records are received, the entire process-from preparing the fraudulent panel to appointments and salary payments-will be investigated.

stories.summary: Around ₹17 crore worth of counterfeit notes have been found in the currency chest of a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The case came to light during a bank audit. Following the discovery, six RBI officials arrived at the branch in two vehicles at around 8 am on Tuesday. They have been inside the bank for around four hours and, according to sources, are questioning bank employees. Three bank officials have been suspended so far in connection with the case. A case has also been registered against four people, including three officials, following a complaint by Arun Kumar Chaubey, PNB's chief manager in Meerut and the investigating officer. ₹4.30 lakh less was found in the amount sent to Jaipur Following a shortfall in the amount sent from PNB's currency chest in Saharanpur to Jaipur, the matter came to light. A few days ago, part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar was assigned the task of arranging bundles of currency notes worth approximately ₹11.50 crore in the currency chest at the PNB branch located at Ghantaghar. These included soiled, mutilated and other types of notes. The bank was supposed to send this amount to the RBI's Jaipur currency chest. As per the prescribed procedure, the money was sent to Jaipur on 5 August. When the notes were counted there, ₹430,900 was found missing. The Jaipur currency chest informed PNB officials in Meerut about the discrepancy. Housekeeper seen taking out notes in CCTV footage After this, the bank sent Chief Manager Arun Kumar Chaubey to Saharanpur to investigate. Along with bank officials, he examined the footage from the CCTV cameras installed in the currency chest. The footage showed part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar taking money from bundles of notes. After the CCTV footage came to light, the bank removed Vishal Kumar from his job. It also filed a theft case against him for allegedly embezzling the money. Currency chest audit began on 9 August After the irregularity involving the housekeeper came to light, the bank began auditing the currency chest on August 9. The investigation team matched the cash present in the chest with the records. A major irregularity came to light during the audit. When the money kept in the currency chest was examined, counterfeit notes worth approximately ₹17 crore were found. The discovery of such a large quantity of fake currency caused panic among bank officials. Departmental probe launched against bank officials Nisha Singh, a senior manager at PNB's divisional office on Delhi Road, said the bank suspended all three officials after the matter came to light. A departmental inquiry has also been initiated. Police are now investigating how such a large quantity of counterfeit currency reached the bank's currency chest. They are also trying to establish when and how the fake notes were placed there, who brought them in and who else may have been involved. Policesays, ‘Case registered against 3 managers’ Saharanpur DIG Abhishek Singh said, Based on a complaint filed by the bank's chief manager, a theft case has been registered against three managers and a part-time housekeeper. The bank is conducting its own inquiry, while police are also investigating the matter. What is a currency chest and how are notes checked? Understand RBI’s 5-layer security system What is a currency chest? A currency chest is a secure cash centre maintained by a bank, where large quantities of currency notes are stored and supplied to other bank branches when required. Notes received at a currency chest are not merely counted; machines also check whether they are genuine or counterfeit and whether they are fit for circulation. As of February 28, 2025, there were 2,691 currency chests across the country. 5 layers of security to monitor cash Machine checks: Notes are checked to determine whether they are genuine or counterfeit. CCTV surveillance: CCTV cameras monitor areas where cash is stored and handled. Record-keeping: Detailed records are maintained of cash received, transferred and examined. Surprise inspections: Bank teams conduct surprise checks from time to time. Reporting and monitoring: If counterfeit notes are detected at a bank or elsewhere, the information is reported to the RBI.

stories.title: Firing on police in Gorakhpur leaves constable injured:Cop shoots criminal in leg in retaliation, accomplice escapes
stories.summary: Late on Monday night, an encounter took place between the police and criminals in the Pipraich area of Gorakhpur. During a checking operation, the criminals opened fire at the police with the intention of killing them, injuring a constable. In retaliatory firing by the police, one criminal was shot in the leg and arrested, while his accomplice took advantage of the darkness and fled into the forest. Encounter near Jungle Dhushan at 2:20 a.m. At around 2:20 a.m. on the night of September 1, 2026, the Pipraich station in-charge was checking suspicious vehicles and individuals in the Jungle Dhushan area along with a police team. Meanwhile, Anti-Theft Team in-charge Inspector Sunil Kumar Rai, Head Constables Mohammad Mohsin Khan, Dharmendra Nath Tiwari, Nitesh Bahadur Singh, Ramesh Kushwaha, Bhupendra Yadav, and Ankit Kumar Singh arrived at the spot in a government vehicle. During a joint checking operation, two suspects riding a motorcycle from the Padri Bazaar side were signalled to stop. On seeing the police, they made a U-turn and tried to flee. The motorcycle rider fell while escaping. When the police asked them to surrender, one of the criminals opened fire at the police, injuring Constable Hanuman. Shot in the leg during retaliatory police action The police again asked him to surrender, but the criminal refused. The police then opened retaliatory fire in self-defense. One bullet struck the criminal in the left leg, and he fell injured at the spot. His accomplice took advantage of the darkness and fled into the forest. The injured criminal was identified as 30-year-old Mumtaz Ahmed, alias Raju, a resident of Nizampur locality under the Tiwari­pur police station area. The absconding criminal was identified as Sarfaraz of Bakshipur, under the Kotwali police station area. Fourteen cases are registered against him at several police stations in the city. A country-made pistol, cartridges, a motorcycle, and stolen goods were also recovered from the arrested criminal. He had recently carried out a theft at Pipraich police station. SP North Gyanendra Kumar said that the injured criminal was brought to the Pipraich Community Health Centre for first aid, from where he was referred to the district hospital. The police are conducting a combing operation in the forest to search for the absconding accused.

stories.title: IIT-BHU professor wins ‘Metromm National Award’:Honoured for developing new technologies in medical and healthcare sectors
stories.summary: Professor Pranjal Chandra (FNASc), Associate Professor and Coordinator of the School of Biochemical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT BHU), has enhanced the institute's reputation at the national level. He has been honoured with the prestigious 'Metrohm National Award 2026' by the Electrochemical Society of India. The award was presented to him at a grand ceremony held on 29 August at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. Professor Pranjal Chandra received this major honour for his outstanding contributions to the fields of electrochemical biosensors, nanobioengineering, and advanced sensing technologies. The primary objective of his research is to transform scientific innovations developed in the laboratory into practical technologies, enabling them to directly benefit the fields of health and medicine. Several patented and translational technologies, innovative diagnostic platforms, and advanced sensing devices related to the healthcare sector have been developed in Prof. Chandra's laboratory under IIT BHU patents. On the special occasion of the award ceremony, Prof. Pranjal Chandra also delivered the 'National Award Lecture' at the prestigious JN Tata Auditorium of IISc Bengaluru. During the lecture, he highlighted his research work and the latest developments in electrochemical biosensing and nanobioengineering. A Matter of Pride for the Institute: Director Prof. Amit Patra, Director of IIT BHU, congratulated Prof. Pranjal Chandra on this major achievement. He said, "This honour is a matter of pride for the entire institute. This achievement reflects the high-quality and socially relevant research being carried out at IIT BHU." He further said that this success would further strengthen the institute's reputation in the fields of research, innovation, and technology.

stories.title: 6 UP devotees returning from Khatu Shyam die:Mother-son, aunt and father-in-law among dead; pickup crashes into truck on expressway, 14 injured
stories.summary: Pickup carrying 21 devotees from Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, rammed into a truck parked on the roadside in Haryana in the early hours of Tuesday. Six people, including a mother, her son, an aunt and a father-in-law, were killed in the accident, while 14 others were injured. The group was travelling to Vrindavan after visiting the Khatu Shyam Temple in Rajasthan. The accident took place on the KMP Expressway in Palwal. The impact was so severe that the pickup was badly damaged and several passengers were thrown onto the road. The neck of a passenger sitting beside the driver became trapped in the vehicle's body. Police reached the spot and admitted the injured to the Civil Hospital. According to the police's preliminary investigation, the accident occurred after the driver reportedly fell asleep at the wheel. The pickup had been modified into a double-decker using iron rods and metal mesh, which also increased its height. Police currently suspect that the driver falling asleep was the primary cause of the accident. Know how the accident happened, step by step… Vijay was an SP leader' brother News of the accident triggered grief in Kishanpur Muraiya village, where 65-year-old Vijay Yadav lived. His wife, Kamla Devi, and brother, Gajraj Yadav, were inconsolable after learning of his death. Vijay Yadav was the nephew of former Samajwadi Party district chief Baburam Yadav and was known as an active SP leader. The foundation stone for a statue of his uncle, Baburam Yadav, was laid in Chanda village by former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav. Meanwhile, Veeresh Yadav from Chanda village had travelled with his sister, Sudha Yadav (55), wife of Sheshpal Yadav. Sudha also died in the accident. Mahesh Yadav (60), son of Gharam Singh and a resident of Chanda village, was also killed in the crash. He had travelled with his wife, Gaura Devi. Mahesh's son Rahul Yadav said his uncle Dinesh called at around 5 am and informed the family about the accident. That was when they learnt that his father had died. Wife killed, husband, son and daughter-in-law injured Ramsevak Yadav of Muraiya village had travelled with his wife Kamla Devi (60), son Ravi Yadav and daughter-in-law Rekha Yadav. Kamla Devi died in the accident, while Ramsevak, Ravi and Rekha were injured. Similarly, Vinod Yadav from the same village had travelled with his wife, Reshma Devi (45). Reshma also died in the crash. Truck and pickup drivers flee after crash The truck driver fled the spot after the accident. The pickup driver, Sudhir, is also reportedly absconding. Police have taken the bodies into custody and sent them for post-mortem examination. A case has been registered against the drivers, and police have launched an investigation. The families of the deceased have also been informed about the accident.

stories.title: IAS officer Divya quits job in just two lines:Cites family reasons in resignation, stays in office for a few hours before leaving
stories.summary: UP's well-known IAS officer Divya Mittal (43) resigned from 13 years of service by submitting a resignation letter of just two lines. She is currently posted as Special Secretary in the Revenue Department in Lucknow. In her resignation letter sent to the Chief Secretary, she cited personal family reasons for leaving the job. However, there is speculation that she had been sidelined for the past four months. She wanted a field posting. She has previously served as the District Magistrate of Mirzapur, Basti, and Deoria. She was known for her extremely strict image and would reprimand officials on the spot. Just four months ago, she was transferred from Deoria to Lucknow. After resigning, Divya Mittal reached her office at the Annexy on Monday afternoon. According to sources, when employees asked her the reason for her sudden resignation, she simply smiled. Some employees also went into her cabin and spoke with her. After staying in the office for a short while, the IAS officer left. 2013-batch officer Divya Mittal still had 17 years left in her service. After completing a BTech from IIT Delhi and an MBA from IIM Bengaluru, she worked in London. She left a job offering a package worth lakhs of rupees and returned to India, clearing the UPSC examination twice in two years. She became an IPS officer the first time and was selected for the IAS the following year. Divya's husband, Gagandeep Singh, was a 2011-batch Indian Trade Service (ITS) officer. He too resigned from his post in 2022. Gagandeep has founded his own company called "Neurocap," which deals in trading in India and abroad. Resignation received by the Personnel Department; will be sent to the CM for approval No mention of the reason for resignation in the post. 3 discussions, including contesting elections... 3 widely discussed pictures of Divya Mittal Divya left her job in London to join the civil services Divya is originally from Rewari, Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she worked in London. She met Gagandeep Singh there. The two had a love marriage. However, a few years later, the couple left their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC examinations. Without coaching, she cleared the IPS examination on her first attempt. She was allotted the Gujarat cadre. Even during her IPS training, Divya continued preparing for the IAS examination. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya had brought water to Lahuriya Dah village in Mirzapur for the first time Divya Mittal's tenure as the District Magistrate of Mirzapur received the most attention. Divya became Mirzapur's DM on September 19, 2022. She served as Mirzapur's DM for 12 months. Through her initiative, water reached Lahuriya Dah village for the first time. This was one of her greatest achievements. She also mentioned this village in a post she wrote after resigning. There had been reports of resentment from Union Minister and local MP Anupriya Patel's camp over the inauguration and credit for this project. It was alleged that public representatives were ignored at the event. She was transferred on September 1. During her farewell, people showered her with flowers. Divya became emotional at the ceremony. The video went viral. Some senior officers expressed displeasure over this. She did not join in Basti and went on extended leave. The government also cancelled her posting to Basti. She was kept on waiting for 10 months (from September 2023 to July 2024). She did not get along with elected representatives in Deoria; complaints reached the government Read about the IAS officer's book, ‘The Crafted Genius’, Divya has written a book titled 'The Crafted Genius'. The book was published this year. It is intended for students preparing for the civil services examination. The book discusses creating a 60-day plan to begin preparing for the UPSC examination. It also explains how to understand questions in the prelims and offers strategies for attempting questions in the examination. For the mains examination, it explains methods for preparing General Studies, ethics, essays, and answer writing. The book also discusses how to cope with failure and continue preparing consistently. Divya's husband is from Punjab and cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt Divya's husband, Gagandeep Singh, comes from Gidderbaha in Punjab's Bathinda district. He pursued a B.Tech. in Chemical Engineering at IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002. After that, he studied management at IIM Bangalore from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC examination on his very first attempt in 2010. He was allotted the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned from the post of Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

stories.title: Ganga rises above warning level in Varanasi:1,574 people flee their homes as experts report August’s highest rainfall in 35 years
stories.summary: Rain and flooding have increased the difficulties faced by people in Varanasi. The Meteorological Department has issued an all-day rain alert for Tuesday. Amid continuous rain since around 2 a.m., the temperature was recorded at 29 degrees Celsius in the morning. According to meteorologist Manoj Srivastava, cloudy skies and rain are likely to continue for the next 48 hours. Meanwhile, the Ganga's water level was recorded at 70.27 meters by 8 a.m. This has crossed the warning mark. Record rainfall in August after 35 years This year's August has been particularly significant for Varanasi in terms of rainfall. The highest rainfall in August has been recorded after 35 years. Normally, Varanasi receives 245.1 millimeters of rain in August, whereas 448 millimeters of rain was recorded this year. This is 82 per cent above normal. Last year, 412 millimeters of rain was recorded in August. Meanwhile, 570.9 millimeters of rainfall was recorded in August 1991, the highest ever recorded. This year, from June 1 to August 31, Varanasi recorded 633.3 millimeters of rainfall against the normal 615 millimeters. According to meteorologist Manoj Srivastava, the city received good rainfall this time due to a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal and the monsoon trough remaining over northern Uttar Pradesh. Floodwaters reached 12 neighborhoods; families in relief camps 12 neighborhoods situated along the Varuna River are facing the threat of flooding. More than 150 flood-affected families have taken shelter in relief camps, while other affected families are staying at relatives' homes or in rented accommodations. The administration is continuing efforts to move affected families to safe locations. Clean and fresh food is being provided three times a day at the relief camps. Milk and bananas have also been arranged for children and the elderly. Travel between Nagwan and Assi Ghat affected Due to the rise in the Ganga's water level, floodwaters have also reached the route from Nagwa toward Assi Ghat and the Jagannath Temple. This has disrupted normal traffic. Floodwaters have reached near Rameshwar Math through the Nagwa drain. Boat in Manikarnika Lane, difficulties increase for last rites The rising water level of the Ganga has also increased the difficulties faced by people arriving for cremations. Boats are operating in the lane leading to Manikarnika Ghat. People have to wade through waist-deep water to reach the ghat. At Harishchandra Ghat too, the cremation site is being changed daily due to the continuously fluctuating water level.

Passengers traveling from Varanasi, Gorakhpur, and Gonda to Nepalganj Road via Bahraich-Nanpara will benefit directly from this facility. The railway administration has extended the routes of four trains, including the Varanasi City-Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Express. The Varanasi-Nepalganj Road Express will run daily from Varanasi starting August 31 and from Nepalganj Road in the return direction starting September 1. In addition, the Varanasi-Bahraich Express and two Gonda-Bahraich DEMU trains have also been extended up to Nepalganj Road. Varanasi-Gorakhpur Express now extended up to Nepalganj Road The route of train 15132/15131 Varanasi City-Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Express has now been extended up to Nepalganj Road. The train will depart from Varanasi City and reach Nepalganj Road via Gorakhpur, Siddharthnagar, Barhni, Balrampur, Gonda, and Bahraich. Travel Time from Varanasi to Nepalganj Road Train 15132 Varanasi City-Nepalganj Road Express will depart daily from Varanasi City at 10:35 p.m. After passing through Sarnath, Aunrihar, Sadat, Jakhanian, Dullahapur, and Mau, the train will reach Gorakhpur. The train will arrive at Gorakhpur at 4:10 a.m. It will then pass through Nakaha Jungle, Pipiganj, Campierganj, and Anandnagar before reaching Siddharthnagar, Shohratgarh, and Barhni. After that, it will pass through Tulsipur, Balrampur, and Gonda, followed by Payagpur, Bahraich, Risia, and Nanpara, reaching Nepalganj Road at 11:45 a.m. It will depart at 4:30 p.m. on the return journey 15131 Nepalganj Road-Varanasi City Express will depart daily from Nepalganj Road at 4:30 p.m. starting September 1. The train will reach Gonda via Nanpara, Risiya, and Bahraich. It will then reach Gorakhpur via Balrampur, Tulsipur, Barhni, Shohratgarh, Siddharthnagar, and Anandnagar. After arriving here at 12:20 a.m., the train will reach Mau via Chauri Chaura, Gauri Bazar, Deoria Sadar, Bhatni, Salempur, Lar Road, and Belthara Road. The next day, the train will reach Varanasi City at 5:30 a.m. The express train will have 18 coaches The Varanasi City-Nepalganj Road Express will have a total of 18 coaches. These will include one generator-cum-luggage van, six general second-class coaches, five sleeper coaches, two air-conditioned third-class coaches, two air-conditioned third-class economy coaches, one air-conditioned second-class coach, and one LSLRD coach. Gorakhpur-Bahraich special train will no longer operate Following the route extension of the Varanasi-Nepalganj Road Express, the operation of the 05131/05132 Gorakhpur-Bahraich-Gorakhpur Special Train has been cancelled from 1 September 2026. Passengers travelling from Gorakhpur to Bahraich and Nepalganj Road will now have the Varanasi-Nepalganj Road Express as an alternative. Routes of three more trains extended Other trains whose routes have been extended up to Nepalganj Road include the 14213/14214 Varanasi-Bahraich Express. It will also now run up to Nepalganj Road. In addition, the routes of the 75109/75110 Gonda-Bahraich-Gonda DEMU and the 75111/75112 Gonda-Bahraich-Gonda DEMU have also been extended up to Nepalganj Road. Direct travel facility for passengers travelling to and from Nepal With the extension of these trains, direct rail connectivity from Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Gonda to Nepalganj Road has been strengthened. Passengers from Bahraich, Nanpara and nearby districts will also have better options for travelling to Nepal. This connectivity will also be useful for passengers traveling from Nepal to India. People in the region had long been demanding better rail services to Nepalganj Road. With the extension of the routes of four trains, passengers on this route now have access to direct and regular rail services.

stories.title: Property dealer duped of ₹2.19 crore over office:Misled with fake NOC in Lucknow; LDA has ₹21 crore outstanding
stories.summary: Property dealer Dinesh Gandhi, a resident of Tulip Apartment on Ashok Marg in Hazratganj, Lucknow, has accused three people, including the directors of Bhavya Creators Private Limited, of defrauding him of ₹2.19 crore. On the court's order, a case has been registered at Hazratganj police station against the company's directors, Ambresh Tiwari, a resident of Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, and Varnika Sharma, along with Soni Sonkar, a resident of Chhitwapur Bhuiyan in Hussain Ganj. According to Dinesh, the accused had allotted him two offices in Plot No. TC-24 of the Bhavya Corporate Commercial Tower in Vibhuti Khand. They took ₹2.19 crore from him between 2016 and 2021, assuring him that construction of the building would be completed. It is alleged that the construction work was not completed even after the money was received. Accused of showing fake NOCs and certificates The victim alleges that the accused showed him the Fire Department's NOC, the LDA Board certificate, and documents related to obtaining the NOC. Later, an investigation found all these certificates to be forged. It is alleged that despite more than five years having passed by June 2026, the builder had not obtained a completion certificate for the concerned property from the LDA. According to Dinesh, the investigation also revealed that approximately ₹21 crore was outstanding against the accused builder with the LDA. After learning this, he questioned Ambrish Tiwari, Varnika Sharma, and Soni Sonkar about the money and the property. It is alleged that all three abused and assaulted him. They also threatened him. Complaint to the police station and Police Commissioner, FIR registered on court's orders The victim submitted a written complaint to the Hazratganj police station and the Police Commissioner seeking action against the accused. It is alleged that when no action was taken, he approached the court. Following the court's orders, Hazratganj police registered a case against all three accused under relevant sections, including cheating, and began an investigation.

stories.title: UP student gang-raped in Delhi, had fled after mother’s scolding:Accused from Kanpur; his wife says 'husband is being framed'
stories.summary: A 16-year-old student from Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, was gang-raped on a moving sleeper bus in Delhi. The men who committed the crime are also from Uttar Pradesh. Bus driver Kuldeep Sharma (45) is a resident of Ladpur Paith village in Kanpur Dehat, while conductor Sandeep is a resident of Katri village in Kanpur city. The police arrested both of them from the bus parking area in Timarpur, North Delhi. The bus used in the crime belongs to Vishwanath Tour and Travels of Firozabad. Its owner is Anil Jadon. He said, "I run a travel agency under the name Vishwanath Tour and Travels. The bus (UP 83 AT 3789) is registered in my name. I had sent the bus to Delhi for repairs and servicing on July 27. The driver and conductor had gone along with the bus. I had not had either of them police-verified. I have provided the police with all the information related to the driver and conductor." The gang rape incident took place on August 4, but the police disclosed the information on August 31. According to the police, the student boarded a bus at Pari Chowk in Greater Noida. The driver and conductor dropped her at Kashmere Gate. During this time, the bus traveled approximately 47 km. Curtains had been installed on the bus windows. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to bus driver Kuldeep's mother, wife, and daughter. Read who said what... Wife said, “My husband is being framed” Kuldeep's wife Archana said: "My husband left home on August 3. The incident took place on the 4th. Kuldeep is being framed unlawfully. Kuldeep does not stay away for even 15 days; he often returns home. He has diabetes." Kuldeep frequently travels between Punjab and Delhi for work. The conductors accompanying him also keep changing. Archana has raised doubts about the conductor's role. She said, "It is possible that my husband was framed because of him." Mother said, “There were never any complaints against my son” Kuldeep's mother, Shyama Murti, said, "My husband died two or three months ago. False allegations are being made against my son. My son has been driving for the past 10-15 years, but there has never been any complaint against him. Before the incident, my son had been at home for 8-10 days. The very day he left home, a case was registered against him. My son is being deliberately framed." Daughter said, “Father takes good care of the family” Kuldeep's daughter said: “My father takes good care of the family. The allegations that he raped the girl are false. My father is not like that. My father was implicated in this case just a few days after Baba's murder. My father left home a day before the incident. We have not spoken to him since then.” The girl's house was found locked The Class 11 student who was gang-raped is a resident of the Kishni police station area in Mainpuri. Her house is currently locked. We tried to speak to people living near her house, but they refused to say anything. The student's father was in Panipat (Haryana) at the time of the incident. He lives there and works. Her mother and the student, however, live in the village. The student's brother works at a private company in Delhi. Upset by her mother's scolding and beating over her studies, she had left to go to her brother. Now understand the incident step by step Victim left home after an argument and got off at the wrong place According to the police, the student left Mainpuri by bus for Delhi without informing her mother after a quarrel in the family. The distance from Mainpuri to Noida is more than 300 km. Because of the heavy rain and darkness, she mistakenly got off at Pari Chowk. She then began waiting for a vehicle to take her to Noida. Meanwhile, an empty sleeper bus passed by. She signaled for the bus to stop. Driver and conductor let her board the bus, then gang-raped her The driver and conductor let the student board the bus. They told her that the bus was going to Noida Sector 63. Some time after the bus started moving, the conductor tried to behave obscenely with the student. The student told the police that the driver and conductor raped her. When she resisted, both threatened to kill her. Driver and conductor fled after abandoning her near Kashmere Gate Late on the night of 4 August, the two dropped the student on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal. They then fled the scene. That same night, the student contacted the Kashmere Gate police and reported the incident. According to the complaint, investigators formed a team under the leadership of Kotwali ACP Shankar Banerjee. The team examined CCTV footage from along the route to identify the bus and track its route. Police arrested the driver, Kuldeep, and the conductor, Sandeep, from a bus parking area in Timarpur. The sleeper bus used in the incident was also seized. Forensic examination of the bus was conducted. 3 photos of the inside and outside of the bus... According to police sources, on the day of the incident, after the bus broke down, the accused took it to a workshop in Surajpur (Noida) for repairs. Once the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur when the student signaled them to stop at Pari Chowk. Police said that the two used the curtained interior of the bus to conceal the crime during the late-night journey. People passing by outside could not see inside. 14 years ago, the Nirbhaya case took place in Delhi, when a woman was gang-raped on a moving bus On the night of 16 December 2012, a 23-year-old woman was gang-raped on a moving bus in Delhi. An iron rod was inserted into her private parts. Due to her critical injuries, the woman was referred to Singapore, where she died in a hospital on 29 December. Protests took place in Delhi and across the country over the case. The media dubbed it the Nirbhaya case. Six people were accused in the case. One accused was a minor, while another died by suicide in jail. Four convicts-Mukesh Singh, Pawan Gupta, Vinay Sharma, and Akshay Kumar Singh-were sentenced to death. All four were hanged at Delhi's Tihar Jail on 20 March 2020.

stories.title: Kaushambi firecracker factory owner arrested after encounter:He was trying to flee the city; blast killed 11 people
stories.summary: Naushad, the owner of the firecracker factory at the Prayagraj-Kaushambi border where an explosion occurred, has been arrested by the police after an encounter. Naushad was trying to flee the city. The encounter took place at 4 a.m. on Tuesday in the Saiyad Sarawan area. According to CO Chail Shivank Singh, the police received information from an informer that Naushad was in the Saiyad Sarawan area. When the police cordoned off the area, he opened fire at the team. In the retaliatory firing, he was shot in the leg. He has been admitted to a hospital. An illegal country-made pistol and cartridges were recovered from Naushad. The police are now investigating where Naushad hid after the explosion at the firecracker factory and who helped him escape. The incident took place at around noon on August 31 in Manauri market under the Pipri police station area. The explosion at the firecracker factory was so powerful that it was heard up to about 2 kilometres away. The factory caught fire after the explosion, and the continuous bursting of firecrackers caused panic in the surrounding area. So far, 11 people have died in the incident, while five injured people are undergoing treatment at a hospital. According to the police, fireworks were being manufactured and stored at the illegal fireworks factory in violation of safety regulations. After the explosion, a case was registered against six people. Manauri Market Was Rocked by an Explosion on August 31 At around noon on August 31, a fire suddenly broke out at an illegal fireworks factory operating out of a house in Manauri Market. Before long, the fireworks began exploding. The blasts were so powerful that panic spread among the nearby villagers. A cloud of smoke continued to rise from the scene, while fireworks kept exploding intermittently for a long time. At the time of the incident, several people were believed to be inside the factory. As soon as the information was received, police forces from Pipri and nearby police stations reached the spot. Firefighting teams began efforts to bring the blaze under control. After the fire was extinguished and the debris was cleared, a search was conducted for people trapped inside. 11 dead, 5 undergoing treatment at hospital So far, the deaths of 11 people in the explosion have been confirmed. Five others were injured and are undergoing treatment at a hospital. The factory and surrounding areas were also severely damaged in the accident. Police and administrative teams collected evidence from the scene and gathered information about the deceased and injured. In addition to relief and rescue operations, the administration arranged treatment for the injured. The police are now investigating the cause of the accident, the quantity of firecrackers stored at the factory, the disregard for safety standards there, and other aspects. Case filed against six, including Naushad A case has been registered at Pipri police station against six accused under serious charges. They include Naushad, son of Nizamuddin; Shakeel, son of Nizamuddin; Shabana, wife of Shakeel; Kahkasha Bano, wife of Naushad; Adil, son of Naushad; and Saina, daughter of Shakeel, all residents of Mahmoodpur Manauri. After the incident, the police took Shabana, wife of Shakeel, into custody and began questioning her. The police will now question the arrested Naushad to gather information about the operation of the factory, the purchase and sale of firecrackers, and the role of the other accused. Action taken against four police personnel, including the station house officer, for negligence Following the incident, Superintendent of Police Satyanarayan Prajapat took action against four police personnel, including the Pipri police station in-charge, for negligence in the performance of their duties. The SP had formed four police teams to investigate the case and arrest the accused. After Naushad's arrest, the police will step up efforts to locate the other accused linked to the case. An investigation is also underway to determine how long the illegal firecracker factory in Manauri had been operating and whether the responsible local authorities were aware of it.

Who is responsible for 13 deaths in Kaushambi?:Factory owner’s licence suspended 2 years ago, he went to jail; how did factory keep running?
stories.summary: Massive explosion at a firecracker factory in Kaushambi, Uttar Pradesh, has claimed 13 lives, raising serious questions over the functioning of the entire regulatory system. The biggest question is: who is responsible for these deaths? The licence of the factory where the blast occurred had been suspended two years ago. At the time, its owner was also sent to jail for allegedly storing explosives illegally. After being released from prison, the owner allegedly resumed operations and continued storing large quantities of firecrackers and explosive material in a densely populated area. Yet the departments responsible for monitoring such activities apparently had no knowledge of it. The investigation will now focus on how the owner managed to restart the business despite the licence suspension, and why the authorities failed to detect the illegal storage and operation. See the pictures related to the incident... Village with a population of 25,000, a new settlement is coming up Manori village is located in the Pipri police station area, 35 km from Kaushambi. The village has a population of around 25,000. A new settlement is coming up about 1 km outside the village. Eight to 10 houses have already been built. Naushad Ali had obtained a license to run a firecracker factory here several years ago. During an inspection on October 8, 2024, around 12 kg of gunpowder and other explosive materials were recovered from his warehouse. The next day, Naushad was arrested and sent to jail. His license was also suspended. An explosion occurred at Naushad's own factory on August 31 (Monday). The blast was so powerful that the entire factory was reduced to rubble. Eight houses within a 100-meter radius were damaged. Three of them completely collapsed. Released from jail and then restarted the 'gunpowder game' After coming out of jail, Naushad resumed his fireworks business. This time, other members of the family also joined him, including his brother Shakeel, son Adil, and the women in the family. The storage of fireworks continued. The result was an explosion that turned several houses into rubble within seconds and took loved ones away from 11 families. Find out who the 4 people responsible are 1- Pipri Police Station In-Charge Vikas Singh The site of the explosion falls under the jurisdiction of Pipri Police Station. Station In-Charge Vikas Singh was responsible for monitoring and taking action against illegal activities occurring in his area. The question is: hundreds of kilograms of explosive material and a large quantity of firecrackers were being stored amid a populated area, so why did the police remain completely unaware? 2- Chail Circle Officer Shivank Singh As the Circle Officer (CO), Shivank Singh was also responsible for monitoring the functioning of the police stations under his jurisdiction. Despite this, how did a person who had been sent to jail two years ago on charges of illegally possessing explosive material continue to stockpile large quantities of explosives within the same circle? Why did the police remain unaware? Was the action taken at the police station level reviewed? Were sensitive license holders and individuals previously involved in cases under the Explosives Act monitored? The investigation will now have to find answers to these questions. 3- SDM Chail Prerna Gautam Serious questions are also being raised at the administrative level in this matter. How did the firecracker business continue to operate in a populated area? Did the tehsil administration ever inspect the site? What was the land-use designation of the property where the warehouse and factory were operating? Was such an activity permitted there? If the firecracker factory's license had already been suspended, what action did the administration take afterward to ascertain the situation at the site? 4- Chief Fire Officer Mangesh Kumar Fire safety is of utmost importance in activities related to firecrackers. In this context, questions are also being raised about the role of Chief Fire Officer Mangesh Kumar. After the license was suspended, did the fire department inspect the site? Did it verify that explosives or firecrackers were not being stored there illegally? Did local firefighters ever report on this location? Horrific intensity of the blast exposed the storage of explosives The intensity of the explosion itself indicates how great a danger had accumulated at the site. The sound of the blast was heard nearly 2 kilometers away. Debris and remnants of the explosion were found scattered up to about 500 meters away. Along with factory materials, bricks, steel rods, and debris from houses were also scattered over a wide area. Walls of a three-story house 200 meters away were blown away An RCC pillar from a house damaged in the accident was also thrown nearly 500 meters away. The force of the explosion can be gauged from the fact that the walls on one side of the first and second floors of a three-story house located about 200 meters from the factory were blown away. The rear sections of five nearby houses were also completely flattened. Tower of a 33,000-volt power line was also damaged The force of the explosion was so great that even the tower of a 33,000-volt electricity line located about 200 meters away was damaged. Debris and other materials reached the tower. The power line was also damaged. Electricity workers remained engaged in repairing the damaged line until late evening. Rescuers searched for survivors in the debris for 9 hours The biggest challenge after the accident was to search for people trapped under the debris. The rescue operation, which began at noon, continued until 9 p.m. Fire brigade and NDRF teams continuously removed the debris and searched for survivors. Ten JCB machines, 11 fire engines, and 14 ambulances were deployed at the site. Neighbour said I fled with my family Shivam Gupta, who lives 50 meters from the firecracker factory, said, "At around 11:35 in the morning, I was taking a bath. First, the electricity went out. I thought there must have been a fault. Then the explosions began, but we had no idea what was happening. My house at the back also collapsed, but I didn't realize it." “As soon as I found out, I ran outside with the two nieces, sister-in-law, and sister who were present in my house. This saved us. The people living in the nearby houses were caught in the blast. Firecrackers had been manufactured in that factory for the past six to seven months. Earlier, they were made in the factory opposite it. When that factory was sealed, they started manufacturing them here,” he said. Villager says, ‘Everything has been destroyed’ Munish Kumar Pandey, an elderly resident, said, “All the houses around the firecracker factory have been destroyed. My house was also here. It had a tubewell, but everything has been reduced to rubble.” Ajay Singh said, “As soon as I learnt that an explosion had occurred at the place where my brother worked, we rushed here. When we arrived, we found out that he had died. My brother's name was Gyan Singh. A boondi-making unit was operating next to the factory, and he was working there.” Woman says "It destroyed the entire settlement and its children" Rani, who reached Swaroop Rani Hospital in Prayagraj, said that after an electric pole fell, a powerful explosion occurred in the explosives stored at the factory. It is being said that there was a factory there for making firecrackers or bombs. The electric pole reportedly fell there. The entire blast was caused by a spark. It destroyed the entire settlement and our children. Railway employee’s entire family killed, only daughter survives Among the deceased were Manjeet Kumar's two children, Priyanjali and Praveen Singh. Gaya Prasad's three children — Jahnavi, Aditya and Ravi — also died in the blast. Gaya Prasad's wife, Anita (38), was injured and has filed an FIR against the factory owner. She said, “My entire family has been wiped out in the accident.” Similarly, railway employee Vikram had come home for lunch when the explosion occurred. Vikram, his wife Anju, daughter Anshu and son Nanha were all killed. Their eldest daughter, Sanjana, had gone to a nearby grocery shop to buy some items and therefore survived. FIR filed against 6 people, 4 teams engaged in making arrests Commissioner M. Lokesh said, "For now, the entire focus was on the rescue operation. An investigation will be conducted into how a firecracker factory was operating in a residential area." DM Amit Pal Sharma said that action would be taken against anyone found responsible for negligence. Kaushambi SP Satyanarayan Prajapati said that an FIR has been registered against six people in this case. Four teams have been formed to arrest the accused. The factory was being operated illegally. Its license had already been canceled two years ago.

stories.title: No waiting lists in UP government recruitments:Posts remain vacant; 6 states create extra lists of up to 25%
stories.summary: There is no rule for a "waiting list" in the recruitment of government jobs in Uttar Pradesh. As a result, thousands of posts remain vacant in every recruitment drive. These vacancies fall into three categories. First- posts for which the selected candidate does not join. Second- posts vacated by candidates who leave the job within a year of joining. Third- posts vacated by candidates who are dismissed after a departmental inquiry due to some mistake. Meanwhile, six neighbouring states-Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand, and Bihar-have a rule to prepare waiting lists covering 15 per cent to 25 per cent of the posts. There, if a post falls vacant for any reason within a year of the selection, a candidate from the waiting list is given the opportunity and selected for the post. About three months ago, the Personnel Department of the Rajasthan government made a major change regarding waiting lists. Now, the demand to implement waiting lists in government recruitments in Uttar Pradesh is also gaining momentum. Candidates have already met Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak regarding this issue. Youths eliminated by a fraction of a decimal are not getting a chance In Uttar Pradesh, the same candidate is often selected for different recruitments or higher-level posts. After getting a better job, they choose one post and leave the other job or do not join it. In such cases, the posts they leave remain vacant. These vacant posts are included in the next recruitment drive. This disadvantages young people who are not selected by a margin of a few marks or decimals. If there were a waiting list, they could have had a chance at these vacancies. However, they now have to wait for years until a new recruitment drive is announced. This costs the government both time and money. Consider some examples of this: How does selection take place through a waiting list in neighbouring states? In Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand, and Bihar, a waiting list of 15% to 25% additional candidates is prepared along with the final selection list. If a selected candidate does not join, is disqualified during document verification, or resigns after joining the job, the next candidate on the waiting list is given an opportunity to fill the vacant post. In these states, the waiting list generally remains valid for 12 to 18 months. During this period, any vacancies that arise are filled on the basis of merit from among the candidates included in the waiting list. Here is what you should know about the rules in each state- 1. Rajasthan: In the state, until June 4, 2026, the rule was that if a selected candidate did not join, the post could be filled from the waiting list. The time limit for this was six months. However, vacancies arising after joining were not filled. Students protested against this in Rajasthan. Some students also approached the High Court. After this, the state government's Personnel Department issued a new order. If a post becomes vacant within one year of joining a government job due to resignation, death, or dismissal, it will now be filled from the category-wise waiting list instead of being included in a new recruitment drive. This will save the time required for recruitment. Government expenditure incurred on conducting examinations repeatedly will also be reduced. 2. Madhya Pradesh: In recruitments conducted by the Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (MPPSC) and MPESB (Employee Selection Board/Vyapam), a waiting list of 15% to 25% is prepared along with the main selection list. In MPPSC, the final list and waiting list remain valid for 12 to 18 months. If a selected candidate does not join or leaves the job, the next candidate on the waiting list is given an opportunity based on merit. 3. Haryana: The recruitment processes of the Haryana Public Service Commission (HPSC) and the State Staff Selection Commission (HSSC) include a waiting-list provision. A waiting panel of up to 25% of the main posts is prepared. In Haryana, the waiting list is valid for up to one year. During this period, if a candidate leaves the job or does not join, the vacant post is filled from the waiting list on the basis of merit. 4. Bihar: The recruitment processes of the Bihar Staff Selection Commission (BSSC) and the State Public Service Commission (BPSC) also include a waiting-list provision. For vacant posts left after counseling or posts where candidates do not join in various departments and teacher recruitments, a supplementary result is issued. Through this, candidates included in the waiting list get an opportunity. Its validity is generally up to one year. 5. Uttarakhand: The Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission (UKSSSC) and the State Public Service Commission (UKPSC) have a provision for issuing a waiting list or an "extra selection list." After the final selection result, a panel of up to 25% additional candidates is kept ready. Its validity is up to 1 year. 6. Delhi: The Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) has a provision for creating a waiting panel. An additional panel of up to 20% of the posts is prepared. Its validity is 1 year. If a candidate on the final list is disqualified during document verification or does not join the post, the next candidate is selected from the waiting list. UP Deputy CM has been confronted 3 times Competitive exam aspirants in Uttar Pradesh are also demanding that UPSSSC and other recruitment boards make waiting lists mandatory. They have staged protests several times and have surrounded Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak three times so far to press their demand. The students say that if a 15-25% waiting list is implemented in Uttar Pradesh, as in other states, thousands of young people could get an opportunity for government jobs. At the same time, vacant posts in various departments could also be filled more quickly. Why recruitment through a waiting list is not easy in Uttar Pradesh Implementing a waiting list can lead to several kinds of disputes in the recruitment process. Understand this with 2 examples- 1- If some selected candidates do not join the PCS recruitment and candidates selected for the PPS claim PCS positions, the government may have already started their training by then. In such a situation, if they are given positions in PCS, the entire list of candidates selected below them could be affected. 2- Cases have also emerged in Uttar Pradesh in which candidates on the waiting list were accused of filing false cases against candidates included in the selection list in order to get them disqualified from recruitment and damage their police records. The aim was to secure a place on the waiting list for the vacant seat.

stories.title: Can Yukesh become BSP’s new Gen Z face?:Mayawati puts Umashankar’s son in frontline; likely to team up with Akash Anand
stories.summary: After the death of Umashankar Singh, who was a three-time BSP MLA from Rasra in Ballia, it is now clearly evident that preparations are underway to hand over his political legacy to his son, Prince Yukesh Singh. BSP chief Mayawati has not only indicated that she intends to establish him politically, but by placing Yukesh, who attended the meeting of Uttar Pradesh office-bearers for the first time, in the front row, she also proved that he will receive special importance in the party. He may be made not just Umashankar Singh's successor, but also the party's young face. Umashankar Singh passed away from blood cancer on 5 August 2026. On August 6, Mayawati paid floral tribute to his mortal remains. During this, visuals of Yukesh touching Mayawati's feet twice to seek her blessings also drew attention. At the time, Mayawati had said that if the family wished, Umashankar's son would be brought forward in politics and that the party would extend its full support. The same sentiment was visible today at the party office during the meeting of representatives from all 75 districts. Representing Gen Z and Tuning with Akash Anand Could become the face of Gen Z- Yukesh Singh is young. He is around 26 years old. Akash Anand, the national coordinator of the BSP, also belongs to the Gen Z generation. Like Akash, Yukesh has also returned after studying abroad. The similarities in their age and thinking could strengthen young leadership in the party. Through this pairing, Mayawati not only wants to make up for the absence of Umashankar Singh, but the BSP is also trying to offer a glimpse of its future by promoting young faces in the party. It may be noted that Uttar Pradesh has around 2.07 crore Gen Z voters. Will fill the void in Kshatriya leadership- That is not all; Mayawati also wants to address the lack of Kshatriya leadership in the BSP. Umashankar Singh had been playing the role of the party's Kshatriya face. Now, with the help of his young son, Mayawati will try to strengthen that position once again. Family and Business Background Prince Yukesh Singh is the only son of Umashankar Singh. The family originally hails from Khanwar village in the Rasra area of Ballia. His mother, Pushpa Singh, is the managing director of the family's company, CS Infra Construction Limited, while his sister, Yamini Singh, is married. Yukesh's wedding to Kanika Singh took place in February 2024. Kanika is the daughter of Brijesh Singh, the brother of Uttar Pradesh government minister Dinesh Pratap Singh. The wedding was held at the Taj Hotel in Lucknow, and Mayawati herself attended it. Yukesh Singh is also active on the business front. He is the CEO of CS Infra Construction Limited. He served as the company's president from 2020 and was appointed CEO in 2025. The company's turnover in 2024-25 is reportedly around ₹1,000 crore. Chose trust-based politics like his father Yukesh, who had not been very visible in active politics earlier, became active in the area during his father's illness. Now, with Mayawati's support, his political role is likely to grow rapidly. Speculation has also intensified that he may be made the BSP candidate from the Rasra seat in the 2027 Assembly elections. The way people turned out in Ballia for the final funeral procession of Yukesh's father, Umashankar Singh, shows how strong his father's legacy is. Party lines were blurred among those who came to bid farewell to Umashankar Singh. From Chief Minister Yogi to several cabinet ministers and other leaders, many attended the funeral. Yukesh also had the option of joining the BJP and moving forward, but like his father, he chose the politics of trust. Yukesh's 2 Special Posts on Raksha Bandhan On August 28, Raksha Bandhan, Yukesh shared two posts on his social media X page. The first post features a picture of his father, Umashankar Singh, with BSP chief Mayawati. The picture is from last year, when Umashankar Singh had visited the BSP chief to have a rakhi tied by her on Raksha Bandhan. In the second post, Yukesh uploaded a picture of himself. He can be seen with many daughters and sisters from the area. A large number of rakhis are tied on both his hands. He wrote, "Today, on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, a large number of sisters visited our residence in Khanwar, tied rakhis, and blessed me." A picture of Umashankar Singh hanging on the wall can also be seen in the photograph. He, too, used to arrange mass weddings for daughters from the area. Every Raksha Bandhan, the sisters of the area would similarly visit him to tie rakhis. Yukesh has now carried this tradition forward. Is the BSP Preparing to Promote Gen Z? Senior journalist Syed Qasim provides the answer. He says that Akash Anand was already representing Gen Z in the BSP. Now, Yukesh Singh has also joined this group. Kapil Mishra, the son of the party's general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra, is also young. He too appears to be socially active. His medical camp remains a topic of discussion during major BSP events. Similarly, the son of state president Vishwanath Pal, Aruvendra Pal, is also becoming active in the party. He is a very good speaker. Aruvendra, who is studying at BHU, is also young. Syed Qasim says that if we also look at the social backgrounds of the four young faces, they fit into the dynamics of a state like Uttar Pradesh. Akash Anand comes from the core Dalit Jatav community. He is the nephew of BSP chief Mayawati and is progressing under her guidance. Kapil Mishra comes from the Brahmin community. Yukesh belongs to the Kshatriya community, while Aruvendra Pal comes from the extremely backward Gadaria community.

stories.title: Tehsildar and police pelted with stones during anti-encroachment drive:Highway blocked in Bhadohi, women injured; 8 booked
stories.summary: A crowd allegedly pelted stones at a tehsildar and police personnel who had reached the Gopiganj area of Bhadohi on Thursday afternoon (27 Aug) to remove an alleged encroachment. The protesters blocked the road and attacked the administration team soon after the action began around 3pm, following which additional police forces were deployed to disperse the crowd, and the encroachment was removed under police protection. More than six people, including women, have been detained in connection with the incident. The officials and police personnel somehow managed to save themselves. Forces from several police stations reached the spot and dispersed the people creating a ruckus. Here is the full story It is related to 14 biswa of private land located near the Lalanagar toll plaza. The landowner, Alakh Narayan Pathak, had filed a complaint six months ago. The case was being heard in the SDM Court. Following the court's order, the team had issued a notice directing the removal of the encroachment. On Thursday afternoon, Tehsildar Mishri Singh Chauhan, Revenue Inspector Ram Asare Vishwakarma, Lekhpal Praveen Srivastava, and a team with a JCB arrived at the site. Protests and stone-pelting began as soon as the action started As soon as the team began removing the encroachment, the people present started raising slogans. A short while later, stones were thrown at the tehsildar and police personnel. Chaos broke out at the site. The protesters blocked the road, causing a long line of vehicles to form on both sides. Additional police force brought the situation under control As soon as he received the information, Gopiganj police station chief Sachchidanand Pandey reached the spot with a police force. The police tried to reason with the protesters, and when they refused to comply, they used force to disperse them. The illegal encroachment was then removed from the land in the presence of the police. Prevented the highway from being blocked with the help of women police officers Gopiganj Kotwal Sachchidanand Pandey said that, “On the instructions of Divisional Commissioner Rajesh Prakash, attempts were made to remove the encroachment twice, on August 18 and 22. During this, the people occupying the land asked for more time.” The encroachment was removed on Thursday. He said that, “Some women were attempting to block the National Highway while carrying stones in their hands. With the help of women police officers, the highway was prevented from being blocked. A case has been registered against eight people in the matter, including three women. All of them belong to the same family. Police personnel have been deployed at the site as a precautionary measure.” The team returned three times due to the women's protest Tehsildar Mishri Singh Chauhan said that influential people had encroached on the land in Lalanagar. After the court's order, the team went three times with the police to remove the encroachment but had to return due to the women's opposition. Even after this, people continued to occupy the land. On Wednesday, about one-third of the encroachment was removed in the presence of police forces. Instructions have been issued to register a case against those accused of pelting stones at the police team.
