stories.title: BJP state secretary asked for ₹2 lakh extortion:Assault, stone-pelting over land dispute; accused of threatening with gun
stories.summary: The dispute over land encroachment and construction in Wajidpur, under the Jajmau police station area of Kanpur, has now escalated to extortion, assault, and death threats. Based on a complaint filed by Kiran Lodhi, the Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh state minister, police have registered an FIR against Avichal Kumar aka Mukul and his mother, Vimal Kumari. Kiran Lodhi alleges that the accused are trying to forcibly seize her husband's jointly owned land. During the construction work, the labourers were assaulted and attacked with bricks and stones. Accused of occupying the land even after the partition Kiran Lodhi told the police that the family land in Wajidpur had been divided amicably by mutual consent. Everyone is living on their respective share. Despite this, Avichal Kumar, alias Mukul, allegedly attempts to occupy her share of the land and continually obstructs construction work. She said that, “On August 9, she was having the roof of a staircase constructed on her land. During this, Avichal Kumar, alias Mukul, allegedly assaulted the labourers working there." He is also accused of attacking them with bricks and stones. Threatened to kill her if she did not pay two lakh rupees Kiran Lodhi alleged that the accused abused her and demanded extortion money of two lakh rupees. He threatened to kill her if she failed to pay the amount. She also alleged that the accused has a licensed gun, which he uses to intimidate and threaten her. According to Kiran Lodhi, the accused had also been accused of assault on November 20, 2025. The police had taken action in that case. Despite this, he has allegedly continued to harass her. Demand for Children's Safety Too The BJP state secretary has sought protection for himself and his children from the police. He has appealed for strict action against the accused. FIR Registered on the Basis of Complaint, Investigation Underway Jajmau police station in-charge Sanjay Pandey said that an FIR has been registered on the basis of the complaint. The matter is being investigated. Further legal action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Student dies in road accident in Lucknow:Villagers thrash driver, cleaner; stop police vehicle, block Bani-Mohan Road
stories.summary: A Class 6 student was killed in a road accident in Lucknow after a speeding DCM allegedly ran over her while she was returning home on her bicycle after eating noodles. The accident took place at around 6.25 pm on Thursday (27 Aug). The girl died on the spot. Angry villagers chased and stopped the DCM after witnessing the accident. The driver and cleaner were pulled out of the vehicle and allegedly beaten by the crowd. The incident triggered a major protest and traffic jam on Bani-Mohan Road near Kanpur Road. Even by 8.30 pm, the road remained heavily congested, with vehicle queues stretching for nearly 2 kilometres on both sides. Police from Banthra police station and ACP Krishna Nagar were trying to persuade the family and villagers to clear the road. Around two hours after the protest began, Tehsildar JP Singh also reached the spot to speak with the family. The family and villagers are demanding ₹10 lakh in compensation and have said they will not clear the road until their demand is addressed. 4 pictures related to the accident… Youngest of four children The deceased was identified as Priyanshi, aka Manu, the youngest daughter of Ram Sahay, a daily wage labourer from Mirzapur in Banthra, Sarojini Nagar. Ram Sahay has four children. His eldest daughter, Ruchi, is married, while his other daughters, Pooja and Lakshmi, and his only son, Ritesh, are still studying. Priyanshi was a Class 6 student at Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya in Benti village, near Mirzapur. On Thursday evening, she went on her bicycle to eat chowmein near Shivani School on Bani-Mohan Road, around half a kilometre from her home. After eating, she began cycling back home when a speeding DCM travelling from Haroni towards Bani allegedly ran over her. People who witnessed the accident raised an alarm and chased the vehicle. The driver eventually stopped the DCM, after which locals allegedly pulled him out and assaulted him. The incident led to a major traffic disruption on the road. Driver and cleaner in police custody, compensation talks underway The police, reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, took the driver and cleaner in a vehicle and started taking them to the police station. However, by then, the number of villagers at the spot had increased. They stopped the police vehicle and demanded that the driver and cleaner be handed over to them. ACP Krishnanagar Abhishek Pandey is trying to persuade the people to end the road blockade. The vehicle in which the police put the driver and cleaner is also stuck at the spot. The protesters are insisting that the DCM driver and cleaner be handed over to them, along with demanding compensation. The tehsildar is assuring them that they will be given compensation of ₹2 lakh from the government, but the people are refusing to leave. Demanding written assurance and cash compensation The tehsildar assured the protesters that they would receive ₹2 lakh as financial assistance from the government and that action would be taken against the truck driver. The protesters then demanded the assurance in writing and, after some time, insisted on receiving the compensation in cash. The road remained blocked over the issue until 10pm, while the tehsildar and police continued trying to persuade the people.

stories.title: Rush to go home for Raksha Bandhan:Trains packed, waiting list crosses 60 till August 30
stories.summary: Due to the rush to reach home for Raksha Bandhan, there is intense competition for seats on trains. Long-distance trains are packed to capacity, from sleeper coaches to general coaches. Getting a confirmed seat has become difficult. The Railways has introduced three pairs of special trains and provided temporary halts at several stations, yet passengers are still not getting any relief. Passengers are pushing and shoving to board the overcrowded coaches. Many travellers are being forced to journey while hanging from the doors. The situation is such that even sleeper coaches look like general coaches. No room in major trains until August 30 Long-distance trains passing through Agra have no room in several classes until August 30. On August 28, the Jhelum Express has no room in the second AC, third AC, and sleeper classes. On August 27, there is no room in the second AC, while the third AC and sleeper classes have 26 and 39 passengers on the waiting list, respectively. In the South Express, there are 2 passengers on the waiting list in the second AC on August 28, while the third AC and sleeper classes have no room. In the Karnataka Express, on August 29, the first, second, and third AC and sleeper classes have 3, 14, 21, and 26 passengers on the waiting list, respectively. In the Malwa Express, there are 59 passengers on the waiting list in the sleeper class on August 28. About 300 trains pass through Agra every day. Waiting lists are continuously increasing on several trains, including the Punjab Mail, Mumbai Rajdhani, Chambal, Shridham, AP, Chhattisgarh, Jhelum, Mangala, and Bhopal Shatabdi. Around 48,000 passengers travel daily from Agra Cantt and 23,000 from Agra Fort. Railway PRO Sanjay Kumar Gautam said that special trains are being operated for the convenience of passengers.

stories.title: Woman tells guard, 'I'll make you clean my shoes’:Gets angry when stopped, raises leg to kick him
stories.summary: A woman allegedly abused and used casteist slurs against a security guard at a Greater Noida society after a delivery boy was stopped at the main gate, even raising her leg to kick him. The incident took place at Amrapali Centurian Park Terrace Homes Society on Tuesday night (25 Aug), and police later took action against the woman for disturbing the peace and made her furnish a ₹5 lakh bond. She vented her anger at the guard and even raised her leg to kick him. She told him, “You have no standing in front of me. I'll make you clean my shoes.” The incident took place on Tuesday night at Amrapali Centurian Park Terrace Homes Society. A video of it surfaced late Wednesday night (26 Aug). In the video, the woman can be seen hurling abuses at the guard at the society's main gate. She was angry because the delivery boy had been stopped at the gate. Residents of the society immediately informed the police about the incident. The police, who reached the spot afterward, took action against the woman for disturbing the peace. She was also made to furnish a bond of ₹5 lakh as bail. See 2 pictures... Residents said the woman had been drinking A woman living in Amrapali Centurion Park Terrace Homes Society ordered sanitary pads and food items online on Tuesday night. The delivery boy reached the society with the items. As per the society's rules, the security guard stopped him at the gate for verification. As soon as she learned that the delivery boy had been stopped, the woman reached the society gate. There, she began arguing with the guard. The woman is alleged to have been drunk. Shortly afterward, she started hurling abuse at the guard. Tried to kick one guard and slap another A video of the woman has also surfaced. In it, she appears to be trying to kick a guard who is sitting on a chair. She then raises her hand to slap another guard. People present at the scene somehow stopped her. The woman allegedly hurled caste-based abuses at the guard stationed at the society gate. However, the allegation was not substantiated during the police investigation. According to the police, during the dispute between the woman and the guard, someone recorded the incident on a mobile phone. According to Bisrakh police, after receiving the information, a police team reached the society. Action was taken against the woman for disturbing the peace. She was also made to furnish a bond of five lakh rupees.

stories.title: Electricity to be 7.93% cheaper in UP in September:Consumers get direct ₹604 crore benefit on bills
stories.summary: Crores of electricity consumers in Uttar Pradesh will get relief on their bills in September after the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) ordered a 7.93% reduction in the Fuel and Power Purchase Adjustment Surcharge (FPPAS). The reduction will provide consumers across the state with a direct rebate of around ₹604 crore on their electricity bills. Electricity prices reduced for the third consecutive month According to the order issued by UPPCL, consumers are being given the benefit of the reduction in power purchase costs recorded in June 2026 through their September bills. Before this, a reduction of 4.43% was implemented in July and 2.92% in August. Now, with a 7.93% reduction in September, consumers are set to receive significant financial relief for the third consecutive month. Benefit made possible through transparent calculation According to Consumer Council Chairman Awadhesh Kumar Verma, the objective of FPPAS is to pass on to consumers the savings in electricity purchase costs. He has demanded that, in accordance with the rules of the Electricity Regulatory Commission, adjustments should be made solely on the basis of the actual purchase cost for the relevant period. This is how the calculation of electricity purchases for June 2026 and the FPPAS for September was made

stories.title: Raid on illegal sweet factory in Lucknow:200 kg spoiled sweets destroyed, 180 litres of soybean oil seized
stories.summary: One day before Raksha Bandhan, the Food Safety Department raided an illegal sweets-making factory in Lucknow’s Neeva Qasim Kheda on Thursday (27 Aug) and destroyed 200 kg of spoilt sweets. The team also seized 180 litres of refined soybean oil over suspected quality issues and shut down the factory after finding that it was operating without a licence. Samples of sweets and raw materials collected The Food Safety Department had received information about an illegal sweets-making factory. A joint team of officials then conducted a raid. The sweets being prepared at the factory and the raw materials being used were inspected. Samples of peda, SMP, refined soybean oil, and silver foil were collected to test the quality of the food products. All these samples will be sent to a laboratory for testing. After the report is received, it will be determined whether any of them violated the prescribed standards. 200 kg of sweets stored in unhygienic conditions During the inspection, around 200 kg of sweets were found stored in such a place and in such a condition that officials deemed them completely unfit for human consumption. According to the officials, they were worth approximately ₹20,000. The sweets were destroyed. During the investigation, 180 litres of refined soybean oil were also found to be spoilt. Its estimated value was reported to be ₹40,860. The team seized the oil and collected samples as well. The nature of the problem with the oil will be determined based on the laboratory report. Factory owner unable to show licence During the action, the factory owner was asked to produce the licence required for conducting a food business, but he was unable to present a valid licence. Following this, the factory was shut down under the Food Safety and Standards Act.

stories.title: Etah DM did not answer minister’s calls 18 times:Baby Rani Maurya says, ‘Are you senior to us in protocol?’; refused bouquet
stories.summary: The DM of Etah did not pick up the phone of UP's Minister of Women's Welfare, Baby Rani Maurya, even after 18 calls on Thursday. The minister got furious over this. Expressing her displeasure to the DM, she said, No, this is wrong. This will not do. You should pick up the phone. The minister said that she was calling to get information about the arrangements. She wanted to know what the program was. Not only this, the angry minister also refused to accept the bouquet offered by the DM at the event. This created an awkward situation at the venue for some time. Minister expressed objection regarding the arrangements Minister Baby Rani said to the DM, I wanted to ask you what the arrangements are? You are not even talking to me. Following this, she also questioned the DM's attitude and protocol. The minister asked, Are you senior to me in protocol? Is that why you won't talk to me? Mentioned repeated calls from an associate During the conversation, the minister also mentioned RD Yadav. She said, ‘Poor RD Yadav has been calling us repeatedly…’ The matter is in the spotlight after the video/dialogue of the minister's displeasure surfaced. Similar case had also surfaced in Jhansi It is being reported that a similar incident regarding the attitude of officials towards Baby Rani Maurya had previously occurred in Jhansi as well. After the Etah incident, questions are once again being raised about the coordination between public representatives and administrative officials. However, the administration has not issued a detailed official response on the matter so far.

stories.title: Constable jumps from SP office roof:Suffers fractures; posted on X, ‘Officers are forcing me to die by suicide’
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, a constable jumped from the roof of the SP office. The injured constable was taken to the medical college's trauma center, about 3 kilometers away, in an e-rickshaw. According to the doctors, Ankit Deshwal has suffered fractures in one arm and one leg. His X-ray and CT scan have been done, and a plaster has been applied. The incident occurred on Thursday at 12:30 PM. However, the ASP claims that Ankit fell while peeking from the roof. About 16 hours before this incident, Constable Ankit had made a post on the social media platform 'X'. It read, You people are forcing me to commit suicide. Officers are supposed to provide justice, aren't they? In his post, Ankit had tagged several police officers, including the Kanpur Dehat Police. Now know the whole matter Angry with the police over sister's disappearance Ankit Deshwal is originally from Firozabad. He is posted in the Kanpur Dehat Police Lines. His sister went missing a few years ago. Police registered an FIR in Firozabad in this matter. Ankit alleges that the police did not take effective action. An FD of about one lakh rupees in the sister's name was also withdrawn. Kept raising questions on social media Regarding his sister's case, Ankit continuously questioned the police's actions on social media. According to officials, he was transferred to police lines several times because of this. Despite this, he continued to express his views on social media. Sister's case is pending in court The case regarding Ankit's sister's disappearance is currently pending in the Firozabad District Court. It is reported that on the court's instructions, the Kanpur Dehat police were asked to record Ankit's statement. He was also issued a notice for his statement from the office of Sadar CO Sanjay Singh. However, police officials have not clarified whether Ankit had come to the SP office in connection with this notice or for some other work. ASP said - Fell while peeking from the roof Kanpur Dehat ASP Alok Prasad said - Ankit was peeking down from the roof. During this, he fell down. A few days ago, Ankit had also tried to commit suicide by hanging himself in the police lines. At that time, I had reached the spot myself and counseled Ankit. The ASP stated that the Firozabad police are investigating the case of Ankit's sister going missing. He frequently posts about this matter on social media. Meanwhile, in his statement, Ankit has admitted to jumping from the roof himself. He is undergoing treatment at the medical college. Security arrangements at the hospital have been increased following the incident. The police are investigating the entire matter.

stories.title: Air Chief Marshal in Gorakhpur:Says, ‘Make children good human beings’; visits Mathbari village with wife, students stage ‘Operation Sindoor’ play
stories.summary: Air Chief Marshal Amarpreet Singh, along with his wife Sarita, arrived at Mathabari village, about 30 km from Gorakhpur city, on Thursday. They were welcomed at the Saraswati Gurukul with a shower of flowers. The Air Chief Marshal's wife inaugurated the library built at the Gurukul. The students of the Gurukul performed a play titled 'Operation Sindoor'. It depicted the initial terrorist attack in Pahalgam followed by India's military action. During the performance, slogans of 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' were also raised. The Air Chief Marshal said, Whatever you make of these children, first and foremost, we must become good human beings. If we can make them good human beings, they will do good work in the future. If everyone has their dream surname after their name, then their middle name should be 'Insaan' (human). For example, Mohit Insaan Doctor, Arpita Insaan IAS. See the pictures... 5 big points from the Air Chief Marshal 1. It is a great pleasure to meet the young generation Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh said, It is a great pleasure whenever you meet the young generation in any school. You all are the future of the country. If this country does something good, it will be because of you. If it does not do well, it will also be because of you. You all have to grow up and run this country.When children plant a pole, they first dig a hole. Then, after planting the pole, concrete is poured around it. Once it dries, no matter how much you shake the pole, it will not move. This is because its roots become strong. Today, while you are studying, that is your foundation. How capable you become when you grow up will depend on this foundation. 2. Keep telling children about the value of freedom The Air Chief Marshal told the children's parents and teachers, If you do not tell children about the country, then tomorrow when they grow up, they will not know what our country is. Then they will not know the value of freedom. Therefore, it is the duty of elders to tell this again and again.Learn well what is being taught to children today. Whatever the teachers say, whatever the parents say at home, you have to do it. If you practice, you will become better. Efforts should always continue. Once you have made up your mind, keep striving for it. 3. Whatever you make of children, first make them good human beings The Air Chief Marshal said that always remain a good human being. You must become a good citizen. Values must always be maintained. We should also behave well in our neighborhood. We should participate in their joys and sorrows. If there is a need in the colony, we should contribute to it, whether through physical labor or money. Where we reach is not important; how we walk is important. We must walk on the path we intend to go. If someone explains something good to you, you should follow it. Whatever your parents tell you at home, they say it for your benefit, so you should follow it. If you feel like asking for something else, then ask for it. If they find it appropriate, they will give it to you. 4. Whether you wear a uniform or not, you can always serve the country Whether we wear a uniform or not, we can always serve the country. No matter what we become when we grow up, we must dedicate some time and some money to the nation. Do something beyond just paying taxes. We must not forget this. We are afraid of failing. We are afraid before even trying. Falling is not wrong. But not getting up after falling is wrong. It is not necessary to come first in a race, but it is necessary to participate in the race. Even when people grow up, they think about becoming this or that. Do your duty, do not worry about the results. Focus on your studies and health at this time. 5. Think of the country before yourself The Air Chief Marshal said, I wanted to become a doctor. But I ended up somewhere else. Perhaps I could not have done what I have done here if I had become a doctor. I made my effort. Effort is our duty. If our values are good, our foundation will be better, and that will be good.In education, knowledge should be given more importance than marks. Marks are also important, but it is not that one should achieve them only by rote learning. It should remain in our minds that we have to live unitedly and think of this country before ourselves. Serving society and the country is your worship. Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission Chairman Sanjay Singh Srinet, while addressing the children, said - Groom yourself in such a way that the one who finds you feels proud and the one who loses you feels regret. He said - No one writes a surname in this Saraswati Gurukul. Whatever their dream is, that is their surname.

stories.title: AAP spokesperson arrested for posting video of school’s poor condition:Shared video on X in Varanasi, accused of spreading misinformation
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party state spokesperson Mukesh Singh was arrested in Varanasi on Thursday (27 Aug) in connection with a case alleging that he spread misleading information about a government school as part of the party’s ‘Fix the Schools’ campaign. Adampur Police detained him while he was conducting public outreach, with the case registered after the headmaster of Konia Primary School alleged that Singh falsely claimed the school was closed when it had actually been shifted following a roof collapse in 2023. He is currently at Kabichoura Hospital for a medical examination. A case had been registered against him at the Adampur police station a few days ago on charges of disseminating misleading information. The case was filed by Kamlesh Dutt Pandey, the headmaster of Konia Primary School. It alleges that Mukesh Singh posted misleading information about the school on his social media account through his X handle. He stated that the school had not been closed but had been shifted to the building of another school because the roof of this school collapsed in 2023. After the arrest, Adampur police took Mukesh Singh to Kabirchaura Hospital for a medical examination, after which he will be produced in court. The police have gathered sufficient evidence against the accused AAP leader, but AAP leaders have said that they will continue the campaign. Post Shared on X on August 21 The headmaster, Kamlesh Dutt Pandey, said that Mukesh Singh posted a 2-minute-and-10-second video from his X account, @MukeshSingh42, at 11 a.m. on August 21. The video was posted from the campus of the Primary School at Koniya Panchayat Bhawan, Adampur Zone, Nagar area. It claimed that the school had been closed to deprive poor people of education. Children now have to travel a considerable distance to study. Not Closed, but Shifted in July 2023 The headmaster said that the primary school at Koniya Panchayat Bhawan in the Adampur Nagar area had not been closed. A large portion of the school's roof collapsed on July 3, 2023. As a result, on July 19, 2023, the school was shifted to the nearby Koniya Satti Primary School on the instructions of the Block Education Officer. At present, 52 students are registered at the school, and they are taught by one headmaster, two assistant teachers, and one education facilitator. Building case pending in court The principal also said that a case concerning the school building and land is pending in the court of the Civil Judge IV (Junior Division). The opposing parties have obtained a stay order. Therefore, the building cannot be reconstructed. As a result, classes have been suspended here. X user Mukesh Singh posted about the matter incorrectly and spread misleading information. Complaint submitted at Adampur police station Kamlesh Dutt Pandey said that a complaint was submitted at Adampur police station seeking the registration of a case against Mukesh Singh and his unidentified associates, based on a misleading post made in connection with the matter. The video is completely misleading and contains no factual information. Police registered an FIR Adampur police station in-charge Vimal Mishra said that a case has been registered based on the complaint. Information about X user Mukesh Singh is being gathered. Other people accompanying him are also visible in the video. Everyone will be investigated, and arrests will be made soon.

stories.title: Akhilesh gets Rakhi tied, gives 'Shagun' as gifts:Slams JPNIC lease, says ‘If they could, they would sell BJP too’
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav celebrated Rakshabandhan in Lucknow on Thursday. More than 100 women and young girls tied rakhis to him at the party office. Many Muslim women were also among them. Akhilesh gave a shagun envelope to the women and girls who tied the rakhi. After the rakhi ceremony, in a press conference, he took a dig at the BJP over the decision to hand over JPNIC to private hands. He said, The BJP has sold JP; if they had their way, they would sell the BJP too. But they are not finding any buyers. The Yogi cabinet had decided on Tuesday to hand over the responsibility of operating JPNIC to a private company. It was constructed during the Samajwadi Party government. In view of the SP's protest, the police have increased security around JPNIC and deployed a heavy force. Key highlights of Akhilesh Yadav's press conference 1. BJP is not a government, but a shopkeeper: Akhilesh Yadav Akhilesh Yadav says the BJP has sold the ‘JP’ from its own name. He says, If they had their way, they would sell the BJP too. Before selling JP, they used to speak about the same JP whose two letters are part of BJP. At the time of the party's formation, they respected him and placed his picture on the stage. It seems the BJP is not a government but a shopkeeper. That is why these people are selling everything. Or rather, if they do not find a buyer, they would sell the BJP as well. 2. Allegations are made to sell public property The SP chief says, If there was any shortcoming or corruption for some reason, what were these people investigating for 10 years? Their ministers were so wise that when they reached the top floor and saw the helipad, they asked what the need for it was. Then they went downstairs and kept digging, but the pickaxe did not work. So they started digging near an edge. They make these allegations because they want to sell property built with public money and hand it over to their own people. 3. Corrupt officials will be investigated Akhilesh Yadav says officials involved in such massive corruption will be investigated when the time comes. He says an investigation is necessary because those officials are also involved in the matter. He says the official in question was once the CDO of Gorakhpur and later received direct charge of the LDA. He says, The entire episode will be investigated. In fact, payments worth several hundred crores have also been made. That will also be investigated. 4. If BJP wanted, JPNIC work would be complete Akhilesh Yadav says the BJP government could have completed the work on the JPNIC building if it wanted to. The building is constructed with public money, and the contractor has already been paid in full. Despite this, the project remains incomplete. He says Netaji Mulayam Singh Yadav and several senior socialist leaders were present when the foundation stone of JPNIC was laid. After the government changes, the project is stopped. When the socialist government returns to power, the work resumes. Akhilesh says the vision at the time is to create a building that conveys the contributions of Jayaprakash Narayan and those associated with his ideology. JPNIC is designed with modern facilities to provide better amenities to people. Construction starts in 2013 Construction of JPNIC begins in 2013 under the SP government. After the BJP comes to power in 2017, the work stops before completion. Work worth around ₹50 crore, including finishing, remains pending. It is reported that the LDA does not receive the required budget from the government. As a result, JPNIC remains closed for around nine years and gradually falls into disrepair. Around three years ago, Akhilesh Yadav visits JPNIC on Jayaprakash Narayan's birth anniversary and garlands his statue. Now know about JPNIC JPNIC is a multistorey, multipurpose building offering several facilities, including a sports complex, a hotel with an open restaurant, a museum and a convention hall with a capacity of 2,000 people. An open restaurant is also located on the terrace. A helipad is constructed on the premises for VIP helicopter landings. The sports block includes facilities for tennis, badminton, squash and table tennis. The aquatic block has international-standard swimming and diving pools, along with a separate pool for children. Separate seating is provided for spectators. A convention hall is built at the centre with a seating capacity of around 2,000 people, while the conference hall has 1,477 seats. The complex also has two seminar halls and a conference lobby with a capacity of 1,100 people. The centre is equipped with 16 lifts, 10 escalators, parking for 600 cars, 100% power backup, centralised air conditioning, Wi-Fi, CCTV surveillance and a sewage treatment plant. A confluence of culture, health and technology The JPNIC museum block is designed to preserve the city's cultural heritage. It includes a 460-square-metre museum, an open-air theatre, a library and a yoga centre. The health club includes a gym, yoga hall, spa and other health facilities.

stories.title: Visually impaired girls tie Rakhi to Agra DM:Collector accepts their affection, gives them chocolates; students invite him to their school
stories.summary: In an emotional gesture ahead of Raksha Bandhan, a group of visually impaired girls tied Rakhis on the wrist of Agra District Magistrate Manish Bansal on Thursday. The students from a residential school for visually impaired girls also invited the DM to visit their school, and he assured them that he would do so. Bansal accepted their affection, gave them chocolates and wished them a bright future. During the interaction, he asked the students about their studies, school facilities, food and accommodation. He also encouraged them to study with dedication. Free bus travel for women The district magistrate said the Chief Minister had launched the ‘Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra’ scheme on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan for women aged 60 and above. Under the scheme, eligible women will be able to travel free of charge on buses. He also said women would be allowed to travel free of charge on all Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) buses with one companion from 6 am on 27 August until midnight on 29 August. He appealed to women to make use of the facility. stories.title: Kanpur GRP returns 611 lost phones worth over ₹2.5 crore:Owners rejoice as phones returned on Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: Kanpur Government Railway Police (GRP) recovered 611 Android mobile phones worth more than ₹2.5 crore that had gone missing while passengers were travelling on trains and handed them back to their rightful owners under ‘Operation Muskaan’ ahead of Raksha Bandhan. 27 GRP teams worked for nearly six months using technical monitoring and surveillance to trace and recover the phones, following which Prayagraj Division Superintendent of Police (SP) Prashant Verma announced a ₹10,000 reward for the team. The phones were returned to passengers at a programme held at 1 p.m. on Thursday (27 Aug). 27 teams conducted the operation for 6 months GRP in-charge Omnarayan Singh said that, “Taking passengers' complaints seriously, a continuous campaign had been underway to recover the missing mobile phones. It took 27 teams nearly six months to recover 611 phones.” According to the police, the total estimated value of the recovered mobile phones is more than ₹2.5 crore. After identifying and verifying the actual owners, all the mobile phones were handed over to them. Passengers' faces lit up after their mobile phones were returned After receiving their mobile phones back, the passengers expressed their gratitude to the GRP. They said that the phones contained not only devices of monetary value but also important documents, photographs, contact numbers, and personal information. Thus, getting their phones back brought them great relief. GRP team awarded ₹10,000 Prashant Kumar Verma, Superintendent of Police, Railway Section, Prayagraj, praised the efforts of Om Narayan Singh, Inspector-in-Charge of GRP Kanpur Central, and his team. He announced a reward of ₹10,000 for the team. According to GRP officials, technical monitoring and surveillance are being used continuously to trace lost mobile phones. Action on passengers' complaints will continue under 'Operation Muskaan'.

stories.title: Research scholar trapped in lift at Lucknow University:Remained inside for 45 minutes; students accused the administration of negligence
stories.summary: Research scholar became trapped in a lift at the B.Ed department of Lucknow University after a power outage caused it to stop suddenly. The incident created a commotion on campus, with a large number of students gathering at the spot. She was rescued after around 45 minutes. Some students alleged negligence on the part of the university administration, claiming that students were being made to bear the consequences of poor supervision of construction work by the university’s construction department. Rescued after 45 minutes of efforts On Thursday afternoon, research scholar Anukta Singh had gone to the B.Ed department for some work when the lift suddenly stopped midway following a power cut. As news of her being trapped spread, students, along with departmental staff and employees, rushed to the spot. Rescue efforts continued for nearly 45 minutes before the lift was finally opened and Anukta was brought out safely.

stories.title: CM Yogi says UP among India’s top 3 economies:‘Economy, per capita income tripled in 9 years; riots were common before 2017’
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched the UP Startup Policy-2026 on Thursday, August 27. During the event, incentives worth more than ₹3.42 crore were awarded to 107 startups, while ₹1.79 crore was distributed among nine incubators supporting the launch and growth of startups in the state. Yogi said Uttar Pradesh was undergoing rapid transformation. “Uttar Pradesh, once known for poor law and order, riots and pothole-ridden roads, is now emerging as one of the country’s major startup hubs. The youth of the state are no longer looking for jobs; they are creating jobs.” 3 major announcements for youth 1. Startup Incentive Cards: Incentive cards were distributed to new and emerging entrepreneurs. 2. Financial assistance for incubators: Financial assistance was provided to incubators, while 12 new incubators were also recognised. 3. U-Hub to strengthen startup ecosystem: A roadmap for U-Hub was unveiled to further strengthen Uttar Pradesh’s startup ecosystem. ‘A population of 250 million is not a burden, but a strength’ Yogi said Uttar Pradesh’s population of nearly 250 million is often viewed as a challenge, but the government considers it the state’s biggest strength. He said Uttar Pradesh has the country’s largest young population. Nearly half of the state’s more than 24,000 startups are being run by women, he added. Research funding increased for universities Yogi said the government launched a startup fund in collaboration with SIDBI in 2019. Under the new startup policy, financial incentives for young entrepreneurs have also been increased. He said universities and degree colleges had been asked to ensure that education does not remain confined to books and syllabuses. Institutions should create an environment that promotes research and innovation, he said. The government has also increased research funding for universities. Economy and per capita income tripled in 9 years Yogi said that before 2017, Uttar Pradesh was counted among the country’s backward or ‘BIMARU’ states. Today, he said, the state is among India’s top three economies. He claimed that Uttar Pradesh’s economy has tripled over the past nine years, while per capita income has also increased threefold. The number of large industries has also more than tripled, he said, from around 12,000 earlier. Centre of Excellence to be established at SGPGI Yogi said SGPGI has proposed setting up a Centre of Excellence, for which the government has agreed to provide support. He said work is also underway on emerging technologies such as green hydrogen and robotics. There are currently 12 Centres of Excellence operating in the state. UP accounts for 10% of startups; target set at 20% Yogi said Uttar Pradesh currently accounts for around 10% of the country’s startups, and the government aims to increase this share to 20%. He said the state is working towards its goal of becoming a $1 trillion economy through technology, innovation and industry. “This is a new Uttar Pradesh, and it will not turn back,” he said. ‘Earlier, it would be dark by evening and festivals meant curfews’ Yogi also criticised the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh before 2017. He said the state was then known for poor roads, power shortages and riots. He said people would fear unrest whenever festivals approached, while schools, colleges and markets would remain closed for extended periods because of curfews. In such an environment, it was difficult to discuss employment, research and innovation, he said. According to Yogi, an environment conducive to investment, employment and startups can develop only when law and order is strong.

stories.title: Husband catches wife with lover naked in Jhansi:Makes boyfriend apply sindoor and garland her; gives them no time to dress
stories.summary: Husband allegedly caught his wife with her lover in a compromising position and then forced the two to marry. He allegedly did not allow them to get dressed before making the lover apply sindoor to his wife’s forehead. The couple then exchanged garlands, after which the woman touched her lover’s feet. The incident took place on 23 August in the Chirgaon police station area, around 28 km from the district headquarters. The husband allegedly caught his wife and her lover together in a room. A video showing the subsequent marriage surfaced. According to the husband, they were married in June 2026. He alleged that ever since the wedding, his wife used to give him sleeping pills. After he fell asleep, she would talk to her lover on the mobile phone. See 3 photos.. Know the full story... Rajesh Prajapati, a resident of Talabpura Mohalla, said, “I married Abhilasha, a resident of the Bhander area in Datia, on 24 June. About a month after the wedding, I began suspecting her behaviour. I allege that she used to give me sleeping pills. After I fell asleep, she would talk to her lover on her mobile phone.” Rajesh further alleged that some jewellery went missing from the house on 19 August. When he questioned his wife, she could not give a satisfactory explanation. He later learned that she had allegedly given some of the jewelry to her lover. Maternal uncle’s accident led him home, where he uncovered the affair Rajesh said his maternal uncle met with an accident on 23 August, prompting him to leave his wife at home and go to Jhansi Medical College. When he returned at around 2 p.m., he found the main door locked from the inside. Suspicious, he entered the house through the roof. According to Rajesh, he found his wife and a young man lying on a bed inside the room. He recorded photos and videos of the two. They allegedly noticed him, caught hold of him and pushed him. Rajesh said he managed to free himself, came outside and raised an alarm. Neighbours gathered at the spot, following which he called the police emergency number 112. Rajesh alleged that the people who gathered at the scene arranged flowers and sindoor and forced the two to marry. Police subsequently took both of them to the police station. He alleged that only preventive action for breach of peace was taken against the lover, while his wife was allowed to leave. Rajesh said, “I would hand over the photos and videos of the incident to the police.” Husband alleges father-in-law threatened to kill him Rajesh said that after the incident, he called his wife’s father and brother and told them what had happened. According to him, his father-in-law admitted that the family had known about their daughter’s relationship before her marriage. They had even taken away her mobile phone. However, after she promised to stop contacting her lover, the family considered the matter resolved and later arranged her marriage to Rajesh. Rajesh alleged that when he questioned his father-in-law about marrying her to him despite knowing about the relationship, he became angry and threatened to kill him. Rajesh said he also has a recording of the conversation. Police advised both parties to approach family court Chirgaon police station in-charge Baliraj Shahi said, The married woman and the young man were brought to the police station following the husband’s complaint. She refused to return to her husband and was taken away by her maternal family. Both sides were later called for discussions, but neither appeared. They were advised to approach the family court for further legal action.

stories.title: Mother beats 2 sons to death with rod:Stuffed cloth in their mouths, played loud music; 9 year old daughter reveals crime
stories.summary: Shocking double murder has been reported in Ghazipur, where a mother allegedly killed her two minor sons, aged 14 and 12, inside their home. She allegedly stuffed cloth into their mouths and struck them on the head with an iron rod. To prevent neighbours from hearing their screams, she played devotional songs at a high volume. When her 9 year old daughter witnessed the killings, the woman allegedly threatened to kill her as well and silenced her. The incident took place on Tuesday night in Rajhati village under the Khanpur police station area, around 40 km from the district headquarters. The murders came to light on Wednesday evening when police arrived to investigate a missing-person complaint and had the lock on a room in the house opened. The blood-soaked bodies of the two children were found lying on a bed. After the killings were discovered, the woman allegedly attempted to die by suicide by hanging herself in another room, but villagers intervened and caught her. Police later arrested her. According to police, she had been distressed because her husband had married another woman. See the pictures... According to SP Dr Iraz Raja, Arjun Rajbhar, a resident of Rajhati village, works as a painter in Odisha. His family includes his mother Lalpuri, father Lalji, wife Pooja, two sons Karan (14) and Aryan (12) and his 9-year-old daughter Pratibha. Karan was a Class 7 student and Aryan was in Class 6 at the Composite School. Pratibha, a Class 5 student, studied at Adarsh Shiksha Niketan near the village. According to villagers, Arjun married for the second time around three years ago while working in Mumbai. He subsequently moved to Odisha with his second wife and had not returned home for around seven years. He would occasionally send money to support his first family. Villagers said Arjun’s first wife, Pooja, was distressed by the situation. She lived in the village with her three children and in-laws. According to them, she often remained irritable and would also physically assault the children. Played devotional songs loudly to mask the children’s screams According to police, around 11 p.m. on Tuesday, Pooja locked her two sons inside a room and played devotional songs at a high volume to prevent their screams from being heard outside. Police said she first stuffed a cloth into Karan’s mouth and struck him on the head with an iron rod. When Aryan tried to escape, she allegedly knocked him down, stuffed a cloth into his mouth and fatally struck him on the head with the rod. The couple’s 9 year old daughter, Pratibha, later told police that she saw her mother taking the iron rod to the field behind the house to dispose of it. Pooja allegedly threatened to kill her if she told anyone. Frightened, Pratibha went and lay down beside her grandparents. After some time, Pooja repeatedly called Pratibha to her room. However, her grandfather told her that since she was already sleeping there, she should be allowed to stay. Pooja then left. Told village head, ‘I can’t find either of my sons’ Village head Om Prakash said that on Wednesday evening, he was on his way to buy medicine for his father when Pooja approached him in tears. She said both her sons had been missing since morning and that there was no trace of them. She suspected they had been either murdered or kidnapped. The village head then went to Pooja’s house with another villager. Both rooms were locked. When he asked for the keys, Pooja said she could not find them. Soon after, a foul smell began coming from the window of one of the rooms. Suspecting something was wrong, Om Prakash discreetly informed Khanpur police station in-charge Rajeev Kumar. Meanwhile, Pooja’s daughter Pratibha told him, "My two brothers had been murdered." In the presence of police, villagers broke open the room’s lock. A sheet was covering the bed inside. When it was removed, the bodies of both children were found. Cloth had been stuffed into their mouths, while dried blood was visible around their head injuries. Tried to hang herself after seeing the crowd Crowd of villagers gathered after news spread that the bodies had been found. Seeing the crowd, Pooja panicked and went into another room, where she allegedly tried to hang herself. Villagers intervened and stopped her. Police reached the spot soon after being informed and arrested her. During a search of the room, officers also recovered a bottle of pesticide. Police suspect the children may have been poisoned before being attacked. Blood samples from both bodies have been collected to verify this. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examinations. SP Dr Eraz Raja said, According to the preliminary investigation, both children appear to have been killed by blows to the head with an iron rod. The murder weapon and the circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated. Police are also probing whether anyone else was involved.

According to initial information, the aircraft was twin-engined and reportedly exploded mid-air before crashing to the ground. The aircraft belonged to Kanpur’s Garg Aviation Flying Training Academy, where more than 100 trainees are undergoing flight training. The academy operates both single-engine and twin-engine aircraft. Police and administrative teams reached the spot soon after receiving information about the crash. The deceased have been identified as trainer Sachin Bhatia from Gujarat and trainee pilot Abhishek Pujari from Karnataka. A large crowd gathered at the site as authorities began investigating the circumstances that led to the crash. Videos from the crash site have also surfaced. They show the aircraft reduced to wreckage after plunging from a height. One pilot’s body can be seen near the cockpit, while the other is lying bloodied a short distance away. stories.title: CCTV captures Haryana singer’s murder in UP:Shot 5 times outside gym; killers claim responsibility on Instagram, say ‘everyone’s turn will come’
stories.summary: Murder resembling the killing of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala has been reported in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, where 32 year old Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan was shot dead outside a gym on Wednesday evening. The attackers allegedly fired around 18 rounds as he stepped out, hitting him five times in the head and abdomen. CCTV footage from the incident has surfaced, showing four suspected attackers arriving on two motorcycles outside the gym. Meanwhile, the Haryana-based Gogi gang has claimed responsibility for the murder. Bholu Shahpuriya of Sonipat, who is allegedly associated with the gang, shared a post on Instagram claiming responsibility, I, Bholu Shahpuriya from Sonipat, take full responsibility for Ankit Baliyan’s murder in Shamli. He supported our enemies and made a song about the incident involving our brother Gogi. He has paid the price. Whoever supports our enemies will meet the same fate. This is just the beginning. The police have begun investigating the Instagram post. Ankit Baliyan rose to fame with his song "Bhari Court Mein Goli Marenge Meri Jaan". In 2023, he was also embroiled in controversy over a roadshow in Shamli. These days, Ankit was preparing for the district panchayat elections in Shamli. Although he became famous for Haryanvi songs, he was born in Shamli itself. It may be noted that Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala was shot dead on May 29, 2022, in Jawaharke village in Punjab's Mansa district. Gangster Goldy Brar, based in Canada, and jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi claimed responsibility for the murder. See 3 pictures… Find out what has happened so far in the murder case See 3 pictures related to the incident... Posted a new song an hour before the murder Police investigating multiple possible angles During the initial investigation, police learned about an argument between Ankit and another singer in Rohtak around six months ago. Following the dispute, Ankit reportedly reduced the time he spent in Rohtak and began staying more often in Bantikheda. However, he continued to visit Rohtak and nearby areas for work. Police are investigating whether the dispute could be linked to his murder. Police are also checking whether Ankit had received any threats in the past and are gathering information about his previous disputes and contacts. Investigators are examining old enmity, personal disputes, contract killing and other possible motives. CCTV footage, mobile phone locations and his recent contacts are also being analysed. Akhilesh says political rivalry angle should also be probed Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has raised questions over law and order in Uttar Pradesh. In a social media post, he said the Jat community was angry over the incident and viewing it as an attack on the community. He also called for the murder to be investigated from the angle of political rivalry.

stories.title: ₹50,000 reward criminal arrested after Gorakhpur encounter:Shot in leg while trying to flee, wanted in robbery case
stories.summary: Police arrested wanted criminal Guddu Dadhi, who carried a ₹50,000 reward, following an encounter near Sisai Ghat in Gorakhpur’s Pipiganj area. Guddu sustained a gunshot wound to his leg when police returned fire after he allegedly opened fire at them. He was taken to hospital for treatment. Absconding in robbery case According to police, Guddu had been absconding in a robbery case. On Thursday morning, a police team received information that he was present near Sisai Ghat. Acting on the tip-off, the team cordoned off the area. Police said Guddu opened fire when he spotted the team and attempted to flee. The officers returned fire in self-defence, hitting him in the leg. Police then apprehended him and recovered a firearm and cartridges from his possession. The injured accused was taken to hospital, where he is currently receiving treatment. 12 cases registered against Guddu Police said Guddu Dadhi, a resident of the Pipiganj area, has 12 cases registered against him at various police stations. In view of his alleged involvement in criminal activities, a reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for information leading to his arrest. He had been wanted in a robbery case, and police had been searching for him.

stories.title: Woman dies by suicide after repeatedly seeking justice:DM, CP, DCP failed to resolve road dispute in Varanasi; family holds body for 14 hours
stories.summary: Woman troubled by a blocked access route to her home and a land encroachment dispute in Varanasi died by suicide after hanging herself at the age of 50 years. The family alleges that Kavita Upadhyay repeatedly complained to the District Magistrate, Commissioner of Police, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Gomti), and tehsil-level officials to have the route reopened. When her complaints were not heard, she even told the officials that she would take her own life, but the problem was not resolved. On Wednesday evening, Kavita hanged herself in the toilet of her home. Because the route for taking the body outside the village is blocked, the body has been lying outside the house for the past 14 hours. The situation is such that police and administrative officials are trying to arrange the woman's last rites, but the family remains adamant that they must first be given access to the route. Family says house exit has been blocked for 2 years Santosh Upadhyay, a resident of Aharak village under the Badagaon police station area, lives with his family in a house located in the middle of the village. The family alleges that neighbours encroached on the passage leading out of their house and built structures over it, blocking their access. Vishal Upadhyay, the deceased woman’s son, said the family had been visiting government offices for nearly two years seeking restoration of the passage. They submitted complaints to several officials, including the District Magistrate, Commissioner of Police, DCP Gomti and SDM Pindra, but the issue remained unresolved. She repeatedly pleaded with officials for an access road Family members said Kavita was deeply distressed because she did not have a proper access route to her home. They said she had raised the issue with officials several times. When no solution was found despite her complaints, she even told the authorities that she would take her own life if she was not given a way to reach her house. The family alleges that her warning was also not taken seriously. On Wednesday, Kavita died by suicide. Body found hanging in toilet on Wednesday evening According to Vishal, his mother Kavita had been missing since Wednesday afternoon. The family searched for her in and around the house. At around 7 p.m., they found her hanging in the toilet. The discovery triggered cries and panic in the house. The family immediately informed the police. Officers reached the spot and brought the body down. Husband tried to save her, but could not According to the family, they had already been worried about Kavita. Her husband Santosh and other relatives had also tried to reason with her. However, the road problem continued unabated. The family says that if the authorities had acted on their complaint in time, perhaps this situation would not have arisen. Now even the last rites face the question of a road After Kavita's death, her family members placed the body outside the house. The family says that the last rites will not be performed until the access-road issue is resolved. As of Thursday morning, the body had been lying outside the house for around 14 hours. Police and administrative officials are trying to persuade the family to conduct the last rites, but the family members remain firm on their demand. Accused of encroaching on new fallow land The family members have accused Manish Upadhyay, son of the late Chandrika Upadhyay, of encroaching on new fallow land. They say that the dispute led to the closure of the access route from the house. The family claims that they repeatedly filed complaints regarding the access-road dispute, but no permanent solution was found. Husband works in Delhi, son is pursuing an MA Kavita's husband, Santosh Upadhyay, works for a private company in Delhi. Their son, Vishal Upadhyay, is pursuing an M.A. According to family members, the late Lakshmi Narayan Upadhyay had four sons: Santosh, Ajay, Akshyavar Nath, and Kedar Nath Upadhyay. The family has been facing problems regarding access to the road for a long time. Body not taken away even in the presence of police and administration Baragaon police have been deployed at the spot since the incident. Administrative officials are also speaking with the family. The officials are trying to persuade the family to proceed with the last rites. However, the family says that Kavita's demand for a road was not heard while she was alive. Now, even after her death, if they are not given access to a road, they will not remove the body. The incident has also raised questions about the administration's functioning: why could the road dispute, which had been ongoing for two years, not be resolved, and why was the matter not taken seriously despite the woman warning that she would die by suicide?

stories.title: ‘Ganesh-Veera’ silver, ‘Stone-Doraemon’ fancy rakhis in demand:Kanpur prices range ₹500-3,000; rates up 30%
stories.summary: With Raksha Bandhan approaching, Kanpur’s rakhi markets are buzzing with activity. Along with traditional silk and cotton rakhis, silver, AD-stone and light-up rakhis are drawing strong demand this year. Despite inflation and rising silver prices, the festive enthusiasm among sisters remains undiminished. Rakhi dealers say religious and cultural designs are more popular among adults, while cartoon-themed rakhis featuring popular characters are the top choice among children. Silver Rakhis gain popularity, priced between ₹500 and ₹3,000 Bullion dealer Anoop Singh said demand for silver rakhis has increased significantly this year alongside traditional thread rakhis. Many people are also choosing silver rakhis as gifts. Rakhis featuring a small silver piece on the thread are available for ₹400–₹500, while heavier, intricately designed ones are priced up to ₹3,000. Among the most popular designs are the ₹1,800 Doraemon silver rakhi for children, the ₹2,000 Shri Ganesh silver rakhi for adults, and the ₹1,700 ‘Veera’ silver rakhi, which is particularly popular among the Punjabi community. Shopkeepers say that despite rising silver prices, people are slightly adjusting their budgets to shop for the auspicious festival, which comes only once a year. Fancy Rakhis available from ₹5 to ₹450 Fancy rakhi seller Veeru said regular rakhis are available in the market for ₹5 to ₹450. The premium ₹450 rakhis feature American Diamond (AD) stones), which are durable and do not easily break or come off when caught in clothing. This year, simple and elegant rakhis, rudraksha designs, peacock and floral motifs, and Seenjari-style rakhis are particularly popular among young people and adults. Doraemon, Ben 10 and PUBG rakhis are a hit among children Special arrangements have been made in the market to attract children. Doraemon, Ben 10, teddy bear and PUBG-themed rakhis are selling quickly in the fancy market. Children are also showing great interest in light-up rakhis, which glow in the dark. Rain slows market, rakhi prices rise by 20–30% Rakhi traders said prices have increased by 20–30% compared with last year. Continuous rainfall over the past few days has also slowed market activity. However, with only a few days left until Raksha Bandhan, traders expect a large influx of customers.

stories.title: Bus stops suddenly on Purvanchal Expressway, 3 killed:Driver got off to use toilet, truck rammed bus; passengers were heading home for Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: Horrific road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur on Thursday left three people dead and 20 others injured. Five of the injured are said to be in critical condition. The bus was travelling from Gurgaon to Bihar via Gorakhpur, carrying 80 passengers who were returning home to celebrate Raksha Bandhan. Passengers said they had booked seats on a private sleeper bus from Gurgaon. The bus left at 4 p.m. on Wednesday. During the journey, the driver repeatedly stopped the bus on the Purvanchal Expressway. Despite passengers asking him several times not to do so, he stopped the bus on the roadside and went to the bathroom. As the bus door was locked, none of the passengers could get off. Meanwhile, a speeding truck approaching from behind rammed into the bus. The impact was so severe that it sounded like an explosion, completely mangling the rear of the bus. The last two seats were crushed as far as the rear wheels. Screams filled the bus following the collision. Passers-by immediately alerted the police. Police personnel and UPEIDA security staff reached the spot and launched rescue operations. All the injured were taken to a nearby hospital. The bodies of the deceased were sent for post-mortem examinations. The accident took place around 5:30 a.m. near milestone 96.6 in the Baldirai police station area, about 35 km from the district headquarters. See pictures of the accident, Truck driver fled after collision, police scanning CCTV footage Police said the deceased have been identified as Shyamlal Mandal, Vinod Mandal (50), a resident of Jhagda Complex, Prempuri, Gurgaon, and Kiran Devi (60), wife of Maheshwari and a resident of Kumarkhand, Bihar. The cause of the accident is being investigated. The truck driver fled the spot with the vehicle after the collision. Police are scanning CCTV footage to identify and trace the truck involved. Bus operates daily from Gurgaon to Bihar Passengers said the Jai Maa Sheetla Travels bus operates daily from Gurgaon to Bihar. It travels via Gorakhpur and also picks up passengers along the route. The fare ranges from ₹1,100 to ₹1,400, and the bus has only regular seating, with no sleeper berths. Mother killed, son injured in accident Injured passenger Sushil Mandal said, “My mother Kiran Devi and I boarded the bus from Rajiv Chowk in the evening. We were travelling to our home in Supaul. We paid ₹2,800 for both tickets. The bus was crowded, so we were seated towards the rear. We were expecting to reach home by afternoon. “We live with our family in Haryana and work as labourers at a factory here. Raksha Bandhan was on August 28, and my mother had to go home to tie a rakhi to her brother. So we left for home two days early. However, the accident on the highway claimed my mother Kiran’s life.” Loud crash woke sleeping passengers Injured passenger Akash Kumar said, “We were sleeping on the bus when a loud crash suddenly woke us up and people started screaming. When I woke up, I realised my head was bleeding. After getting off the bus, I saw that it had been badly damaged. “People told us that the driver had stopped the bus on the highway and gone to the toilet. Meanwhile, a speeding truck approaching from behind rammed into the bus. The impact shattered the rear window. The bus was dragged for some distance, while the truck driver fled the spot.” Balldirai Circle Officer Ashutosh Kumar said, “Eleven passengers were injured in the accident, while three people died. The bus was removed with the help of a crane, following which traffic returned to normal. The families of the deceased have been informed. Further action is being taken in the case.” News is being updated...

stories.title: Labourer beaten to death over theft suspicion:Brick-kiln owner and associates killed him in Varanasi
stories.summary: Brick-kiln worker in Varanasi’s Cholapur was allegedly beaten to death over suspicion of theft. The postmortem of 45 year old Ram Janam Vanvasi, whose body was found under suspicious circumstances in Gosaipur five days ago, has confirmed that multiple injuries caused his death. Police have also recovered a short video of the incident, in which the worker can allegedly be seen being brutally beaten. Two suspects have been detained in connection with the case, and further investigation is underway. Worker secretly recorded video, exposing the truth According to police, the brick-kiln owner and three associates allegedly assaulted Ram Janam after accusing him of theft. During the beating, another worker secretly recorded the incident from behind. The video has now emerged as key evidence in the investigation. After obtaining the footage, police began identifying the accused and reconstructing the sequence of events. The postmortem report also confirmed that the injuries sustained during the assault caused Ram Janam’s death. Body found unidentified 5 days ago Ram Janam’s body was found abandoned in the Gosaipur area five days ago. Police took the body into custody, conducted a postmortem examination and began efforts to establish his identity. Later, his family members reached the hospital and identified the body. Ram Janam was a resident of Dharayan village in Chandauli’s Dhanapur police station area. Worked at a brick kiln while living at his in-laws’ home Ram Janam Vanvasi had been staying at his in-laws’ home in Badkibari village of Gosaipur for some time. He lived with his father-in-law, Kamla Vanvasi, and worked as a labourer at a local brick kiln to support the family. Allegedly held captive and beaten over theft According to allegations, the brick-kiln owner and three associates accused Ram Janam of theft, held him captive and beat him with sticks. The assault allegedly continued even after he sustained serious injuries. Police said their investigation indicates that Ram Janam’s condition deteriorated following the assault, eventually leading to his death. His body was later abandoned in the Gosaipur area. 2 accused in custody, search on for 2 others Police detained Ajay Singh, son of Rajendra Prasad Singh and a resident of Shivdasa, and Vishal Singh, son of Ramesh Singh and a resident of Garthouli under Choubepur police station, around midnight on Wednesday in connection with the case. Police said the two would be produced in court on Thursday and sent to judicial custody. The roles of the other accused are also being investigated. Police are treating the video footage and postmortem report as key evidence and are taking further action in the case.

stories.title: Bihar worker dies by suicide in cowshed:Took extreme step over family problems; had started job just 20 days ago
stories.summary: Wednesday morning, the body of a labourer was found hanging inside a cowshed in Parmanandpur, under the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi, triggering panic among local residents. They immediately informed the police. Police reached the spot and identified the deceased as Sanoj Sharma, a resident of Rahta village under Kumarkhand police station in Bihar’s Madhepura district and son of the late Damodar Sharma. Sanoj had arrived in Varanasi around 20 days ago to work at the cowshed and help with household chores. Family found him hanging when they went to give breakfast According to homeowner Shiv Shankar Pandey, Sanoj fed the animals and got them milked at the cowshed on Wednesday morning, as usual. He then went to bathe and wash. At around 8:30 a.m., when family members went to the cowshed to give him breakfast, they found him hanging from an iron angle fixed to the tin shed with a rope. They immediately informed the police. Shivpur police reached the spot around 10 a.m. The police brought down the body and sent it to the mortuary for a postmortem examination. Sanoj was married and had children. His family in Bihar has been informed about his death over the phone. Police investigating the reason behind the death According to police, the exact circumstances surrounding Sanoj’s death are yet to be ascertained. Officers reached the spot, conducted an investigation and questioned nearby residents for information. A forensic team also collected evidence from the site. Police brought the body down, completed the inquest proceedings and sent it to the morgue for a postmortem examination. Sanoj’s family members in Bihar were informed about the incident over the phone. Sanoj was married and had young children. Police said further legal action will be taken after his family reaches Varanasi and submits a written complaint.

stories.title: Ganga water enters school, 50-bigha crop submerged:Children shifted to nearby school; danger rises in Katri villages
stories.summary: As the Ganga’s water level rises in Kanpur, flood concerns are growing in the Katri region. Water has entered Lodhwakheda village near the Ganga Barrage, with nearly two feet of water accumulating outside the primary school and some water reaching the school premises. For the safety of the children, classes are now being held at a nearby upper primary school. See 2 pictures... Water enters vegetable fields and guava orchards Apart from Lodhawakheda, Ganga water has also started reaching Chainpurwa and Devnipurwa. Around 50 bighas of crops in the Katri region have already been submerged. Vegetable fields and guava orchards have also been damaged. Villagers say the water level is rising rapidly. The water level rises faster at night, raising fears that floodwater could soon enter homes in the villages. Water rose at night, crops submerge Kusuma, a resident of Chainpurwa, said the water level rose significantly during the night, submerging standing crops in the fields. “Given the rate at which the water is rising, we fear it may soon reach our homes. We are increasingly worried as the water continues to rise, but this is a problem we face every year.” Water level rising for more than two days Nikhil, a resident of Lodhwakheda, said the Ganga’s water level has been rising continuously for the past two days. Water has entered both the premises and the building of the primary school, while nearby guava orchards and vegetable fields have also been submerged. As the river continues to rise, concern among residents of the Katri region is growing. Villagers are keeping a close watch on the water level, while the administration is also monitoring the affected areas.

stories.title: Heavy rain warning in 31 UP districts:Nepal floods trigger state alert; villages being evacuated in Maharajganj, Kushinagar
stories.summary: Flooding in Nepal has triggered an alert in Uttar Pradesh, with the impact expected to be felt in several districts. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has put Maharajganj and Kushinagar, both bordering Nepal, on high alert. All 36 gates of a barrage have been opened, causing the water level of the Gandak River to rise rapidly. DMs, SPs and other officials in both districts are on the ground. Sirens are being sounded to alert villagers, while police teams are urging people to stay away from the riverbanks and move valuables to safer places. Meanwhile, 19 districts in the state are already affected by flooding. In Badaun, the Ganga and Ramganga rivers have crossed the danger mark. A house was swept into the Ganga after being hit by erosion, while the Ramganga is flowing over the Badaun-Shahjahanpur highway. In Chandauli, the Musakhand and Latifshah dams are full, prompting officials to open their gates. The Sukwa-Dhukwan dam in Jhansi has overflowed, while a portion of the Tamolin Purwa embankment on the Sharda River in Lakhimpur has been breached. In Lalitpur, the Khedar River is flowing about three feet above a bridge, and the Sirsi bridge is also submerged. The water levels of the Ganga in Varanasi and the Yamuna in Prayagraj are currently stable, but all the ghats remain submerged. With cremation grounds underwater, last rites are being conducted on roads and rooftops. 31 districts under heavy rain warning today The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today, Thursday, with heavy rain expected in 31 districts. Since Wednesday morning, intermittent rain has been reported in 35 cities, including Ghaziabad and Jhansi. Kanpur witnessed heavy rain from around 12:30 a.m. to 1 p.m., leaving roads and streets waterlogged. Lucknow also received heavy rain from around 4 p.m. See pictures of the rain and floods… Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said, A low-pressure area near the Bay of Bengal, along with active monsoon winds over Uttar Pradesh, could bring heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours. The spell of rain is expected to continue for the next 2–3 days.

stories.title: Murder ransom accused freed in 24 hours:Convoy outside Lucknow jail, garlands and video shoot; 14 cases filed
stories.summary: Three accused arrested in the murder-for-ransom case involving Nadwa College cleric Maulana Irfan Ahmed Rizvi in Lucknow walked out of jail on bail within 24 hours of being sent to judicial custody. Hazratganj police had claimed to have solved the case on August 21 and arrested Mohammad Farhan Siddiqui, Sohel Ahmed Siddiqui and Aman Qureshi. ADCP Jitendra Dubey had announced their arrests at a press conference. They were subsequently produced in court. The court sent all three to 14-day judicial custody. However, they secured bail the next day and walked out of jail. They were welcomed outside the jail with garlands, had a video recorded and then left for home in a convoy. Police learnt about their bail only after seeing the video of their welcome outside the jail. According to police, neither the case diary nor a report was sought from them before the bail was granted. They were also not served a notice to present their side, and the bail bond was not verified. More than 24 cases are reportedly registered against the three accused. Police have now begun reinvestigating the case. See 2 pictures of the accused leaving jail… Video made outside the jail All three accused walked out of jail just 24 hours after being sent into judicial custody. They recorded a video outside the jail and uploaded it to Facebook. The video shows them being garlanded as a song plays in the background: “How can I praise myself now... I fear the Almighty.” Police learned about their bail only after seeing the video. The incident has also raised questions about the speed with which bail was granted. ADCP Central Jitendra Dubey said, “It is a court order, so it is difficult to comment on it. The police are conducting their investigation.” Here is the timeline of the entire case… 21 August: The ACJM-2 court sent the accused to 14-day judicial custody. 21 August: The ACJM-3 court, acting as the CJM, granted bail to Aman Qureshi, Sohel Ahmed Siddiqui and Farhan Siddiqui. 23 August: All three accused were released from jail. 2 accused have more than 14 cases registered against them More than 14 cases involving serious charges have been registered against Farhan Siddiqui and Suhail Ahmad Siddiqui at various police stations in Lucknow. Despite this, both managed to secure bail and were released within 24 hours of being sent to jail. How the case was uncovered On August 18, Hazratganj police arrested Mohammad Shahid and Mohammad Zamir with a stolen Passion Plus motorcycle. During questioning, the two allegedly revealed that they had been offered ₹2 lakh to kill a person. They said they had also been given a pistol and shown a photograph of the intended target to identify him. Aman’s arrest unraveled the entire chain Based on information provided by Shahid and Zamir, police began searching for Aman Qureshi. Using surveillance, five police teams arrested him from Laxman Mela Park at around 2:15 a.m. on 21 August. During questioning, Aman allegedly told police that advocates Sohail Ahmed Siddiqui and Farhan Siddiqui, residents of Chowk, had asked him to arrange young men to kill Irfan. They had also given him Irfan’s photograph. He was instructed to use a separate mobile phone and SIM card to conceal his identity. According to police, preparations for the murder had been underway for about a month. Murder plot linked to ₹6 crore property dispute According to police, Bilal Hashmi, manager of Jamia Al Noor Al Salamia madrasa, had allegedly plotted Irfan Ahmed’s murder over a dispute involving property worth ₹6 crore. Two shooters were reportedly hired for ₹2 lakh. Police said the area was surveyed before the planned attack using a stolen motorcycle. Six accused have been arrested in the case, and police have recovered a pistol, five cartridges and the stolen motorcycle.
