stories.title: Yogi says Akhilesh should apologise to people:Built JPNIC for 'luxury' says jobs bonanza coming in UP
stories.summary: In Deoria, CM Yogi Adityanath announced that a “treasure trove of jobs” is about to open up in Uttar Pradesh. Preparations are underway to provide jobs to one lakh young people within a year, including the recruitment of 32,000 police personnel. An for the 13 lakh candidates who cleared the UP TET examination is also expected soon. Yogi also launched a scathing attack on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, alleging that the SP “spent ₹862 crore like water” on the construction of the JPNIC. He claimed that a private limited company was formed in the name of JPNIC, involving Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and their associates. Yogi said, These people used public money for their own indulgence. They should apologise to the people for this. With such a huge amount, schools, roads and industries could have been built for millions of people. CM Yogi visited Deoria on Saturday. Before addressing the public meeting, he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 projects worth ₹305 crore in Majhauliraj village for the Salempur and Bhatpar Rani assembly constituencies. The projects include the inauguration of 23 projects worth ₹139.47 crore and the foundation laying for 57 projects worth ₹165.50 crore. See the pictures... Now, read the key points from CM Yogi’s speech… 1- ‘SP means a gang of dacoits’ Targeting the SP, Yogi said, “SP means a gang of dacoits. Before 2017, there was a saying in the state: ‘See a Samajwadi, and the daughter is frightened.’ Every parent used to worry about their daughter’s safety. But that is no longer the situation.” Yogi said the media is the fourth pillar of democracy and highlights wrongdoing in the government and draws attention to its shortcomings. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav had once put a sword to a journalist’s throat. He also mocked Akhilesh, saying, “Babu used to wake up at 12 noon. His tutors would teach him afterward, but even then he could not understand anything. If you wake up at 12 noon, your head will remain heavy, and out of frustration, you will say anything.” 2- ‘Before 2017, there was neither security nor respect’ CM Yogi said that before 2017, there was a government and bureaucracy in the state, but neither security nor respect. He alleged that even basic facilities such as toilets were unavailable to the poor and that schools had become centres of cheating. The poor condition of schools, he said, reflected the poor state of governance. Referring to encephalitis, he said fear prevailed across Deoria and the entire Purvanchal region during the month of Sawan. Hundreds of people had died after contracting the disease, but the governments of the time failed to take adequate action. He alleged that no Chief Minister or Prime Minister from the SP or Congress governments came to the region to assess the situation. 3- ‘Another ₹150-200 crore will be needed for JPNIC’ Referring to the JP National Integration Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow, Yogi said another ₹150-200 crore would be required to complete the project. He said the BJP government came to power in 2017 and subsequently handed the project over to the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), which conducted an investigation. Yogi alleged that the SP spent ₹862 crore “like water” on the construction of JPNIC. He further alleged that a private company was formed in the name of JPNIC, involving Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and people close to the SP. He said, “These people used public money for their own indulgence. They should apologise to the people for this. With such a huge amount, schools, roads and industries could have been built for millions of people.” 4- ‘The mafia has been reduced to dust’ Yogi said disturbances used to occur before festivals under previous governments. He alleged that governments sold ration meant for the poor and provided protection to the mafia, which ran parallel administrations. “The situation has changed now. The mafia has been reduced to dust. Those who threatened the safety of daughters are either in jail or in hell,” he said. Yogi added that Uttar Pradesh was no longer in a situation of “one district, one mafia” and claimed that under the double-engine government, mothers no longer fear for their daughters’ safety. He also referred to the encephalitis outbreak in Deoria and the Purvanchal region, saying hundreds of people had died but the governments of the time failed to take adequate action. 3. ₹150-200 crore more needed for JPNIC Referring to the JP National Integration Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow, Yogi said another ₹150-200 crore would be required to complete the project. He said that after the BJP came to power in 2017, the project was handed over to the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), which conducted an investigation that, according to him, brought the alleged irregularities in the project to light. 4. ‘Mafias have been reduced to dust’ Yogi said that disturbances were common before festivals under previous governments and alleged that the mafia enjoyed political protection. “The mafia has been wiped out,” he said, adding that those who threatened the safety of women are now either in jail or have met their end. He said the state is no longer dominated by “one district, one mafia” and claimed that under the double-engine government, parents no longer fear for their daughters’ safety. 5- ‘Poor getting ration, electricity and houses without asking’ Yogi said the poor are now receiving ration, electricity and housing without having to ask for them. Appointment letters are being issued to young people, and he claimed that the government has already handed appointment letters to 9.5 lakh youths. He said new enterprises are being established across the state, creating employment opportunities for local youth. 6- Mentioned free bus travel for women Yogi targeted the SP chief over the free bus travel facility provided to women on Raksha Bandhan. He said the facility was available to women from all communities, without any distinction between majority and minority groups. He claimed that 59 lakh women travelled free on July 27, while 60 lakh women availed themselves of the facility on Raksha Bandhan. 7- Praised former Congress MLA The Chief Minister praised former Congress MLA Raghav Baba for his stand during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. He said that despite the Congress government’s opposition to the movement, Raghav Baba had described Lord Ram as a symbol of honour, pride and glory and said opposition to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement in Ayodhya would not be acceptable. Yogi said Raghav Baba had opposed the Congress’s alleged appeasement politics during the movement. He said Deoria is now progressing, with a better connectivity network being developed across the district. Roads are being widened from four lanes to six and eight lanes in some areas, while schools are also being revamped. 8- ‘Preparing to provide jobs to 1 lakh youths within a year’ Yogi said the government is preparing to provide jobs to one lakh young people within a year. This includes the recruitment of 32,000 police personnel, 4,000 sub-inspectors and 45,000 Home Guards. He said the screening process for Home Guard recruitment is underway. He added that 13 lakh young people have cleared the UP TET examination and that the recruitment would be released soon. He said a “treasure trove” of employment and self-employment opportunities is set to open up for the state’s youth. 9- ‘Preparing to provide tablets to 2 crore youths’ Yogi said the government is preparing to distribute tablets to two crore young people, regardless of the subjects they are studying. Taking a swipe at the SP chief, he said, “This is what the SP chief is upset about.” He alleged that earlier, whenever government vacancies were announced, “the uncle and nephew” would set out with begging bowls, whereas young people in Deoria are now getting jobs.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at five-storey hospital in Bareilly:Wards fill with smoke, panic as families flee carrying children
stories.summary: Fire broke out on the top floor of the five-storey Navodaya Hospital in Bareilly on Saturday morning, sending thick smoke through the building and triggering panic among patients and their attendants. As the fire alarm sounded, relatives rushed patients out of the wards, while parents carried children in their arms and hospital staff evacuated critically ill patients on stretchers. The fire reportedly started around 10 a.m. in a room on the top floor, when the hospital was crowded due to OPD hours. Around 100 patients and attendants were present in the ICU and other wards at the time. Police and fire brigade teams reached the hospital soon after receiving the information and began rescue operations. The blaze was brought under control within around 30 minutes. The hospital administration arranged ambulances and shifted all patients to nearby hospitals as a precaution. The incident took place on Mini Bypass in the Izzatnagar police station area. A short circuit is suspected to have caused the fire. See pictures of the fire… Now, let’s understand the entire incident step by step 4-5 people trapped on upper floor, brought down through stairs Fire brigade employee Kapil Singh said 4-5 people were trapped on the upper floor. Heavy smoke made the rescue operation difficult. The team immediately reached the floor and safely brought everyone down through the staircase. He said the cause of the fire is being investigated. The hospital’s entry and exit routes, along with other fire-safety arrangements, are also being inspected. Patients shifted to nearby hospitals, staff monitoring them Hospital owner Umesh Gangwar said the top floor of the hospital has a rest room, where the fire broke out. The room had sofas and other furniture, which caused the fire to spread and generate thick smoke. The fire brigade arrived in time and brought the blaze under control, preventing it from spreading to other floors. However, the smoke triggered fire alarms on every floor. He said the hospital was evacuated as a precaution. The administration contacted nearby Raj Hospital and Prasap Hospital and shifted all patients there. Hospital staff were also moved to the nearby facilities and are monitoring the patients. Dr Umesh Gangwar said the top floor is generally not used and sees very little movement. The hospital has the necessary fire-safety arrangements in place. The canteen on the upper floor has also been closed for around one and a half years and has remained unused. So far, only one or two sofas are believed to have been damaged in the fire. No patient or other person was injured. Patients’ relatives worried outside the hospital Shahana, whose husband was admitted to the hospital: “My husband is undergoing treatment and was admitted to the general ward. I have just reached the hospital, so I don’t know where he is at the moment or which hospital he has been shifted to. I am trying to find out.” Haroon: “My father has been admitted to the hospital for the past 7-8 days. He had been suffering from a cough. I have just reached the hospital, so I don’t know what happened or how. I am trying to find out where my father is.” The news is being continuously updated....

stories.title: Singer Ankit’s wife breaks down, says, 'I’ll die by suicide':Demands encounter of husband’s killers, asks who will support family now
stories.summary: Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema broke down in tears while appealing for justice after her husband was shot dead in broad daylight in Shamli on 26 August. Appearing before the media for the first time on Friday, she questioned how four armed assailants could carry out the killing in the heart of the city and escape despite police deployment across the area. Seema appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure that the killers are arrested immediately or killed in an encounter. She also said that if justice is not delivered, she would take the extreme step of immolating herself along with her family. Meanwhile, police are examining newly surfaced CCTV footage to identify the shooters. The investigation has also been extended to suspected shooters linked to Panipat and Karnal, with the Haryana STF and Anti-Gangster Unit joining the probe. Singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema shared these details... Iqra Hasan arranged a call between Akhilesh Yadav and Ankit’s family Earlier on Friday, Kairana MP Iqra Hasan visited Ankit Baliyan’s residence and met his father, Satyaveer Singh Fauji, and other family members to offer condolences. She said a memorial would be built in Ankit’s name using funds from the MP Local Area Development Scheme. Questioning the state’s law-and-order situation, Iqra said that if the case was not solved within four days, her party would stage a sit-in protest. She also arranged a phone call between Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Ankit’s family. Actor who claimed responsibility for murder seen celebrating Meanwhile, actor Bhupendra Dhingra, who had claimed responsibility for Ankit Baliyan’s murder, went live on social media again on Friday. In the livestream, he appeared to be laughing and celebrating, while some people were seen congratulating him. A young woman also appeared in the video and said that even if someone has a dispute with another person, they should not resort to killing. During the livestream, Dhingra appeared to say that a challan had been issued and a case registered at the police station, but that it took him only a short time to return to his old swagger and style. Three days ago, Dhingra, who describes himself as a singer and actor, had claimed responsibility for Ankit’s murder. He alleged that Ankit had misbehaved with him and hurled obscene abuses at him, and claimed that he killed him in retaliation. Dhingra is reportedly a native of Gurugram. Police have traced his current location to Karnataka. Investigators are also trying to establish whether he was actually involved in the murder or merely made a false claim of responsibility on social media. Sonipat criminal Bholu also claims responsibility for the murder Meanwhile, Sonipat resident Bholu Shahpuriya has also claimed responsibility for Ankit Baliyan’s murder. According to reports, several criminal cases have been registered against Bholu in Sonipat and other places. Identifying himself as a member of the Gogi Gang, he made a post on social media claiming responsibility for the killing. In the post, Bholu alleged that Ankit supported the gang’s rivals and had released a song about an incident involving gang member Gogi. He claimed that Ankit had backed their rivals in criminal activities and had therefore “faced the consequences.” He also issued a threat to others, saying that those who support their rivals would meet the same fate. What has police done so far in the murder case?

stories.title: Leopard kills 35-year-old man in Moradabad:Drags him from hut while he slept; 4 killed in 25 days
stories.summary: Leopard allegedly mauled a 35-year-old disabled man to death after dragging him from outside his home into a nearby forest in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The animal bit his neck and tore into his chest, leaving his blood-soaked body about 100 metres from the house. Jagraj was sleeping on a charpoy outside his home on Friday night when the leopard reportedly approached him, grabbed him by the neck and dragged him into the forest. When his family did not find him on the charpoy on Saturday morning, they began searching for him and later found his body in the forest. The incident took place in Bahapur Balia village under Thakurdwara police station. Three days earlier, a leopard had allegedly killed a woman working in a field in the same village. Four people have now died in leopard attacks in the area over the past 25 days. 3 pictures from the incident site… Jagraj put his children to sleep inside and slept outside the hut Divyang Jagraj (35) had built a hut-like house on the outskirts of Balia village. His wife died three years ago, after which he had been raising his 8-year-old son and 6-year-old daughter on his own. He supported the family by driving an e-rickshaw. Since the hut had no door, he would sleep outside. On Friday night, Jagraj fed his children and put them to sleep inside before lying down outside as usual. The leopard attacked and killed him while he was sleeping. After being informed, the Forest Department team reached the spot and began efforts to capture the animal. The department has installed trap cameras in the area and laid nets at several locations to monitor the leopard’s movements and capture it as soon as possible. DFO says, ‘No flooding this time, so farmers are spending more time in fields’ Moradabad Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Dr Vinay Kumar Pandey said the area is a natural habitat for leopards and such attacks have occurred in the past as well. He said that earlier, limited means of communication meant information about such incidents did not reach many people. This year, there has been no flooding, allowing farmers to regularly visit their fields. As a result, encounters between people and leopards have increased, which has also led to more reported attacks.

stories.title: ‘Have sex with me, I’ll get you educated in city’:College manager’s son raped student, threatened to fail her; FIR registered
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a Class 10 student has accused the son of a private school manager of rape. According to the girl, the accused sexually exploited her for four months and allegedly abused and threatened to fail her when she resisted. The accused allegedly told her, “If you want to progress and study in the city, have a relationship with me. I will bear all your expenses.” When she refused, he allegedly threatened to fail her if she did not sleep with him. He later allegedly made an audio recording of their conversation viral. After the audio surfaced, the student attempted suicide. The case is from the Gola police station area, around 55 km from the district headquarters. After learning about the girl’s ordeal, her younger sister informed the family. On Friday, the victim went to the police station with her grandfather. Based on her complaint, police registered a case against the accused under charges of rape and the POCSO Act. Calls her to cabin, threatens her and allegedly rapes her The 15 year old girl from Gola is a Class 10 student at a private girls’ inter college. She says her father works in Mumbai and alleges that Prateek Tripathi, the son of the college manager and a teacher there, had been harassing her. According to the student, around four months ago, Prateek called her to his cabin after classes. When she went there, he allegedly grabbed her and behaved inappropriately with her. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to fail her if she did not have a physical relationship with him. He also allegedly threatened to defame her and assured her that no one would find out about their relationship. The girl alleges that Prateek raped her and took her phone number before contacting her regularly. He allegedly told her that he would help her progress, arrange for her to study in Gorakhpur city, get her a room and bear all her expenses. He also allegedly said he would speak to her grandfather. The girl alleges that he sexually assaulted her for four months. Distressed by the situation, she eventually told her younger sister, who counselled her. Now, know the full matter... A 15-year-old Class 10 student from the Gola area studies at a private girls’ inter college. According to the student, her father works in Mumbai, while she lives in the village with her mother, grandfather and younger sister. Prateek Tripathi, the school manager’s son, also teaches at the college. The student alleges that around four months ago, Prateek called her to his cabin after classes. He was alone in the cabin. She alleges that when she entered, he grabbed her and behaved inappropriately with her. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to fail and defame her if she did not have a physical relationship with him. The accused allegedly told her that no one would find out about what happened between them. He then allegedly raped her. The student did not tell anyone about the incident at the time. She alleges that the accused took her mobile number and began contacting her over the phone. According to the student, the accused told her that he would help her progress, arrange for her to study in Gorakhpur city, get her a room and bear all her expenses. He also allegedly said that he would speak to her grandfather. The student alleges that he sexually exploited her for four months. Distressed by the situation, she eventually told her younger sister, who counselled her. Student refuses to meet him, accused allegedly makes audio viral The student said Prateek called her to meet him again one day, but she refused. Angry over this, he allegedly abused her over the phone and threatened to defame her. He allegedly told her that since he was bearing all her expenses, she should have no problem meeting him. The student still refused, following which he allegedly made an audio recording of their conversation viral. After learning that the audio had been circulated, the student attempted suicide. Since she had already told her younger sister about the alleged abuse, her sister counselled her. The student then told her family everything. Her family members were shocked after learning what had allegedly happened. On Friday, the girl’s grandfather took her to Gola police station, where she reported the entire matter. Based on her complaint, police registered an FIR against the school manager’s son. Her grandfather said the accused had repeatedly threatened to fail his granddaughter. He alleged that she suffered severe mental distress after the audio was circulated and attempted suicide. Meanwhile, after the audio surfaced, villagers reached the school, surrounded the accused and created a commotion. As the situation escalated, Prateek reportedly fled the village. He got married around one and a half years ago and has a two-and-a-half-month-old daughter. Here’s what was said in the audio… CO says, ‘FIR registered, teams deployed to arrest accused’ Gola CO Darvesh Kumar said an FIR has been registered in the case and police teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. Raids are being conducted at his suspected hideouts, and the accused will be arrested soon.

stories.title: 2 new swine flu cases in Lucknow, govt on alert:Surveillance ordered across 75 districts; Deputy CM says patients’ travel history to be checked
stories.summary: Swine flu cases are increasing in Lucknow. A day after a woman infected with H1N1 died at Balrampur Hospital on Thursday, two more patients tested positive for the virus on Friday. Both have been admitted to the hospital’s isolation ward and are currently in stable condition. Balrampur Hospital Director Dr B.K.S. Chauhan said RT-PCR tests confirmed H1N1 infection in both patients. They are receiving treatment under the supervision of senior physician Dr Anand. The isolation ward at Balrampur Hospital has been reserved for swine flu patients. With new cases being reported, the health department is closely monitoring the situation, while the government has directed all 75 districts in Uttar Pradesh to step up surveillance. DMs of all 75 districts directed to remain alert In view of the swine flu situation, the Yogi government has stepped up vigilance across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed the Health Department and district magistrates of all 75 districts to maintain continuous monitoring. He has also asked officials to regularly review swine flu cases and ensure there is no negligence at any level. The Chief Minister has directed hospitals to maintain adequate treatment arrangements, including sufficient isolation wards, essential medicines, testing kits and other medical facilities, so that patients can receive immediate treatment when required. Travel history of infected patients to be checked Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said the number of patients reporting with fever has increased across the state, particularly in districts connected to the Delhi-NCR region. He has directed officials to check the travel history of all infected patients and advise them to undergo home isolation wherever necessary. He also instructed the Health Department to remain fully alert regarding swine flu. Get tested promptly if symptoms appear The Chief Minister has appealed to people across the state not to ignore symptoms of swine flu. Anyone developing symptoms should consult a doctor promptly and undergo the necessary tests. He said there is no need to panic, but timely testing and treatment are essential.

stories.title: CM Yogi orders strict action against land mafias and strongmen:Hears grievances of 200 people in Gorakhpur, assures justice for every victim
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath hears the grievances of around 200 people at a public grievance hearing at Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur on Saturday morning and directs officials to resolve their complaints promptly. People from several districts arrive with their grievances. The Chief Minister personally meets each complainant, listens to their concerns and accepts their written applications. He directs officials to take strict action against land mafias and influential individuals involved in illegal encroachments, while ensuring that every complaint is addressed sensitively and within the time frame. The Chief Minister says it is the government’s responsibility to ensure that every person receives justice without discrimination. Assures financial assistance for medical treatment Some people approached the public grievance hearing seeking financial assistance for the treatment of serious illnesses. The Chief Minister said, “No one’s treatment should be stopped because of a lack of money.” He directed officials to promptly prepare treatment cost estimates for needy patients so that government assistance could be provided without delay. The Chief Minister also took complaints related to revenue and law and order seriously and directed officials to resolve them promptly. In cases involving family disputes, he instructed officials to hear both sides and make efforts to resolve the issues amicably. Chief Minister performs cow service, feeds cattle jaggery and puri After the public hearing, the Chief Minister offered prayers and paid obeisance to Guru Gorakhnath at Gorakhnath Temple. He then paid his respects at the statue of his spiritual mentor, the late Mahant Avaidyanath, before touring the temple premises. The Chief Minister also visited the temple’s cowshed and performed cow service. He fed jaggery and puris to the cows with his own hands and inspected the arrangements at the cowshed.

stories.title: Bridge collapses in Moradabad, family swept away with bike:Mother dies, son missing, 3 rescued
stories.summary: Five members of a family riding a motorcycle fell into the Gagan River after a wooden bridge collapsed in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The woman died in the accident, while her young son remains missing. Villagers rescued her husband and two other children. The accident took place around 7:30 p.m. on Friday when the woman was returning from her parents’ home after tying a rakhi on her brother’s wrist for Raksha Bandhan. The family was crossing a small wooden bridge over the Gagan River at Chattha in Malkapur, under the Majhola police station area. As the motorcycle reached the bridge, some of the wooden planks suddenly broke. The motorcycle lost balance and plunged into the river along with the family. Hearing their cries for help, people nearby rushed to the spot and jumped into the river. The woman and one of her children were swept away by the strong current. Police launched a search for the mother and son with the help of local divers and an NDRF team. After around two hours, divers recovered the woman’s body. The child is still missing. Moradabad SSP Satpal Antil said teams are continuing the search for him. First, take a look at 3 pictures... Bike plunges into river, family cries out for help Labourer Anil Jatav (45), a resident of Mahmoodpur in Chhajlat, visits his in-laws’ home in Nanpur village of Kundarki on Raksha Bandhan with his wife Kiran (42), sons Keshav (7) and Priyanshu (3), and daughter Kafia (5). After the celebrations, the family begins their journey home on a motorcycle. As they reach the wooden plank bridge in Malkpur, three planks suddenly break. The motorcycle loses balance and plunges into the Gagan River along with the family. The family cries out for help. Hearing their cries, passers-by rush to the spot. Police also arrive with divers from Malkapur village. Anil, Keshav and Kafia are rescued, while Kiran dies. Priyanshu remains missing. Divers conduct search operation using flashlights According to the SSP, the rescue operation is difficult because it is already dark. Divers conduct the search using flashlights. Kiran is immediately taken to the district hospital, where doctors declare her dead. The search for the missing child resumes on Saturday morning, with an SDRF team also being called in to assist with the operation.

stories.title: Storm and rain alert in 47 UP cities today:5 swept away in river in Moradabad; crocodile drags youth into Betwa in Jhansi
stories.summary: Flooding has affected 16 districts in Uttar Pradesh. On Saturday, the Meteorological Department issued a storm and rain alert for 47 districts. According to the department, a cloud system has formed over eastern Uttar Pradesh, with satellite images showing cloud temperatures between -70°C and -90°C. Thunderstorms, rain and strong winds are likely. On Friday, rain was reported in 66 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Moradabad and Sambhal. Dense fog suddenly reduced visibility in Ghaziabad, with visibility falling to 50–60 metres at several places. In Moradabad, a temporary wooden bridge over the Gangan River suddenly collapsed. A couple travelling on a motorcycle with their three children fell into the river. Local residents rescued the father and two children, while the woman and one of the children were swept away by the strong current. After around two hours of rescue efforts, the woman’s body was recovered. The third child remains missing. In Jhansi, a 21 year old man who went to bathe in the Betwa River in the morning was attacked by a crocodile, which dragged him into deep water. In Hamirpur, the Chandrawal River has been in spate following four days of continuous rain. Rising water levels have submerged the Gurdaha-Sisolar main road, disrupting connectivity to more than 12 villages. In Kanpur, heavy rain causes a 25-foot section of a house courtyard to cave in. A girl falls into the pit and is pulled out after a seven-hour rescue operation. However, doctors declare her dead at the hospital. Meanwhile, monsoon rains have sent rivers into spate across the state. In Jhansi, the Sukhnai River suddenly floods after 48 hours of torrential rain. A van carrying six people is swept away in the raging waters, but locals manage to rescue everyone on board. Watch the photos of the rain and floods… Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, The low-pressure system over Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and southern Uttar Pradesh has brought heavy monsoon rain to the state so far. However, the system is now moving away, which will lead to a slowdown in rainfall activity. Rainfall is likely to decrease over the next 2–3 days, until 31 August. The rain is expected to resume in the first week of September.

stories.title: Asim Arun says, ‘AJGAR- MAJGAR existed before PDA’:Akhilesh’s formulas will fail; insulted great leaders when in power
stories.summary: Social Welfare Minister Asim Arun calls Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘PDA’ formula a political experiment destined to fail. In an interview with Dainik Bhaskar, he says, “There is no place for caste-based alliances in Uttar Pradesh politics. Formulas such as AJGAR and MAjGAR have been tried before. Now, Akhilesh’s PDA experiment will also fail.” Arun also backs the Gen Z movement at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak, while expressing concern over the violence during the protest. He speaks candidly about the police’s functioning and the government’s stance on the issue. Read the full interview... Will Akhilesh’s PDA formula affect caste equations in the 2027 elections? Asim: Those making a big issue out of PDA (Backward Classes, Dalits and Minorities) today should remember history. Similar caste-based combinations have been tried several times before in Uttar Pradesh politics. First experiment ‘AJGAR’: In the 1970s and 1980s, former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh used this formula to unite farmers and middle-class castes. He coined the term ‘AJGAR’ — Ahir, Jat, Gurjar and Rajput. Second experimen ‘MAJGAR’: Later, ‘M’, representing the Muslim community, was added to create ‘MAJGAR’, Muslim, Ahir, Jat, Gurjar and Rajput. After Chaudhary Charan Singh’s era, the formula was widely used during Mahendra Singh Tikait’s farmers’ movements and in the politics of that period. If the SP is contesting the 2027 election with the support of PDA, which social groups is the BJP focusing on? Asim: The BJP does not engage in caste-based political calculations. Our politics rests on four words: “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas” (Together with everyone, development for everyone). The essence of the Constitution given by Babasaheb is not that a government can be formed by appeasing three castes. Its spirit is that elected representatives should reach out to every neighbourhood and every section of society and seek their votes. When I contest an election, I know I may not receive votes from every household. But as an elected representative, I visit every doorstep. The result of this BJP approach is that sometimes we receive greater support from one neighbourhood, while at other times we receive overwhelming affection from both. People now understand caste-based divisive politics. Under the leadership of Modi and Yogi ji, every poor person is benefiting from government schemes without discrimination. Why does Akhilesh claim that Dalits and backward classes are being exploited under the BJP government? Asim: When Akhilesh Yadav became Chief Minister in 2012, he seriously insulted great leaders, I believe. He changed the names of districts, hospitals and institutions named after Babasaheb Dr Ambedkar, Sant Ravidas ji, Mata Mahamaya ji, Jyotiba Phule ji, Chhatrapati Shahu ji Maharaj and Kanshi Ram ji. They are not egalitarian leaders but family-oriented politicians. They want power only for themselves and their families. They remember Dalits and backward classes only when elections are approaching. How do you view Gen Z’s anger over the NEET issue? Asim: Technology changes with every era. The NTA system could not function properly during the NEET examination, and we acknowledged this. The government took immediate action and conducted the examination again. A CBI investigation was launched into the irregularities, and several accused are in jail. The Prime Minister has chosen Nandan Nilekani to help improve the examination system. He has developed major systems such as Aadhaar and UPI. I hope that in the future, the country will have a better examination system that does not raise questions. As far as Uttar Pradesh is concerned, we have changed the examination process and taken action against those responsible for paper leaks. How can a balance be struck between students’ anger and police action? Asim: I 100% agree with the students’ anger, but I do not support violent methods of protest. Parliament is very close to Jantar Mantar. If Parliament is in session and protesters try to break through barricades, damage vehicles or enter Parliament, no one will accept it. In such a situation, the police have to use water cannons, tear gas and other measures to maintain law and order. Images of violence are never pleasant. What message would you like to give to the youth? Asim: Under no circumstances should you resort to violence. Put forward your views firmly, but remain within the bounds of the law. I am in politics today. Whenever I have to protest against something, I first make it clear to my colleagues: “We are not a crowd or a mob. We are part of a system, a disciplined army.”

stories.title: Yogi reprimands power dept chairman:No record of 13,000 electricity connections; syndicate collects crores every month
stories.summary: Around 13,000 illegal electricity connections are reportedly operating in Chhijarsi village of Gautam Buddh Nagar, a. Meters have been installed outside the houses, and crores of rupees are being collected every month. But instead of reaching the government treasury, the money is allegedly ending up in the pockets of a syndicate. The alleged scam was brought to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s attention by Manoj Kumar Singh, CEO of the State Transformation Commission. The CM sought an explanation from Power Corporation Chairman Ashish Goyal and reprimanded an Energy Department official over the alleged negligence. Chairman calls it a ‘submergence zone, CEO shows photos of three-storey buildings The Chief Minister was holding a review meeting on the evening of 27 August (Thursday) when the alleged negligence was brought to his attention. Power Corporation Chairman Ashish Goyal tried to explain the situation, saying, “Sir, this is a submergence zone.” CEO Manoj Singh immediately showed photographs of three- and four-storey buildings and rejected the claim. He said, “This is not a submergence zone; it is a clear case of illegal connections.” The CM responded sternly, saying, “Electricity belongs to the government; no one produces it at home. Meters and illegal connections cannot be installed without the connivance of department officials.” The Chief Minister then reprimanded Power Corporation Chairman Ashish Goyal in front of other officials. Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma has also expressed his displeasure with the chairman several times. 3,800 legal, 13,000 illegal connections In Chhijarsi village (Feeder No. 4), there are only 3,800 legal electricity connections, while around 13,000 homes have illegal connections. Electricity meters are properly installed at these 13,000 homes, and payments are collected every month. However, instead of going directly to the government treasury, the money is allegedly being collected by a syndicate. According to estimates, even if a minimum of ₹1,000 is collected from each illegal connection, around ₹1.30 crore is allegedly being siphoned off every month. Review meeting 4 other major issues 1. Digital library existed only on paper: Bhadohi’s DPRO reportedly took a minister to show him a digital library, but no library was found at the site. The Chief Minister sought an explanation from the Panchayati Raj Department and set a September 30 deadline to complete all digital libraries. 2. ‘Zero Poverty’ campaign moving slowly: The distribution of houses, ration and Ayushman cards to eligible families was found to be progressing slowly. The Chief Minister directed officials to connect at least one member of every family with skill training and employment. 3. Basic facilities at labour hubs: Officials were directed to ensure basic facilities such as drinking water, toilets, cleanliness, medical assistance and food at labour hubs. 4. Need to accelerate the ‘Zero Poverty’ campaign: The review found that the process of providing houses, ration and Ayushman cards to eligible families was moving slowly. Officials were also asked to speed up efforts to provide skill training and employment opportunities to at least one member of each family. What action will follow? Following CM Yogi’s strict stance, the Energy Department is under pressure. Engineers and officials responsible for curbing power theft, fake billing and line losses are likely to face action. State Transformation Commission CEO Manoj Kumar Singh said the case of 13,000 illegal electricity connections in Chhijarsi is serious. He said meters have been installed at the houses, but the connections themselves are illegal, and strict action will be taken in the matter.

stories.title: Wife pleads to see constable husband’s body:‘Let me meet him one last time’; cop hanged himself to death in Rampur
stories.summary: "Let me go upstairs once… I am Arun’s wife. We got married at an Arya Samaj temple. I beg you, let me see Arun one last time." The woman pleading with the SP and police personnel was herself a police officer. On Thursday (27 Aug), Head Constable Arun Shukla, 40, died by suicide in Rampur. Just hours later, the woman arrived at the spot and pleaded to see his body. As the SP came down the stairs after completing his investigation, he came face-to-face with the woman and questioned her briefly. Police then took her away. The entire exchange took place in front of a Dainik Bhaskar reporter. The incident occurred under the jurisdiction of the Civil Lines police station. First, take a look at these 2 pictures... Went to call his friend, but found the door locked Arun, a constable from the 2005 batch, had been posted at the SP’s office in Rampur since 6 February, 2026. He lived on the first floor of a rented house in Awas Vikas Colony. At around 7 pm on Thursday, his friend Nitin arrived to invite him to play badminton. When Arun did not open the door despite repeated knocking, Nitin called him on his phone. After receiving no response, he contacted the landlord and had the door opened. Inside the bedroom, Arun was found hanging from the ceiling fan with a bedsheet. No one else was present in the house at the time. Senior police officers and other personnel reached the spot and brought the body down. Arun’s family, who live in Bareilly, were also informed. Family moved from Shahjahanpur and settled in Bareilly Arun’s family originally belonged to Shahjahanpur. His father, Shri Krishna Kumar Shukla, was also a police officer and has since passed away. Arun’s mother lives in Bareilly with his elder brother Anil and his family. He had two sisters, both of whom are married. Arun married Sukiti in 2012. Sukiti’s father is also a police officer. The couple have an 11 year old son. Couple began quarrelling soon after their son was born Arun and Sukiti began having frequent arguments about a year after their son’s birth. Initially, family members intervened and managed to reconcile them. However, a few days later, Sukiti returned to her parental home in Pilibhit, where their son also lives with her. Arun and Sukiti were divorced last year, but Sukiti did not accept the divorce and filed an appeal against it in the High Court. The case was still being heard. Woman arrived just as the SP reached the spot At around 9:30 pm, SP Anil Singh Sisodia reached the scene and went upstairs to the room where Arun’s body was found hanging. Just then, a woman wearing a yellow top and black trousers arrived in a panic. She insisted on going upstairs and argued with the people present. When a chair was brought out and she was asked to sit, she began pleading with folded hands. She then tried to rush towards Arun’s room. At the same time, the SP was coming downstairs. A police officer stopped the woman from going upstairs, after which the SP questioned her for a few seconds. She says, ‘I am already married to Arun’ The woman was determined to get upstairs and tried every possible way to do so. She told the SP, “Arun was my husband. We got married at an Arya Samaj temple. Please let me go upstairs.” The SP was aware of the ongoing divorce case between Arun and his wife. He therefore stopped the woman from going upstairs. Woman taken to police station in a police vehicle The woman was taken to Civil Lines police station in a police vehicle. As it was late at night, she was later sent to the women’s police station. SP Anil Singh Sisodia declined to reveal any details about the woman, saying only that she was also a police officer and was posted in Moradabad. On the morning of 28 August, the woman who claimed to be Arun’s wife was brought back to Civil Lines police station and questioned. Later, a sub-inspector and some police personnel took her to Moradabad in a black Scorpio. Meanwhile, some people, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the woman claimed that she and Arun had married at an Arya Samaj temple. She did not reveal when the marriage took place or how long she had known Arun. It is alleged that Arun had been in a relationship with the woman for a long time. However, she had also been in contact with a sub-inspector for some time, which had reportedly led to arguments between her and Arun. The two had reportedly argued on the day of the incident as well, following which Arun allegedly threatened to die by suicide. He then made a noose from a bedsheet and took his own life. The woman had apparently sensed that something was wrong. This may explain why she was among the first people who knew Arun to reach the spot. Elder brother arrived with their mother Police informed Arun’s family about his death. His elder brother Anil reached Rampur along with their mother, sister and brother-in-law. A day before Raksha Bandhan, his sister broke down and wept bitterly after learning of her brother’s death. At around 2:30 am, police conducted the post-mortem and handed Arun’s body over to his family. The family then left for Bareilly with the body. Additional SP Anurag Singh said: Arun’s family members have not submitted any complaint. Police are investigating all aspects of the case.

stories.title: Youth attacked over old rivalry in Kanpur:Beaten with sticks and sharp-edged weapons; skull and nasal bones fractured
stories.summary: 27-year-old man was allegedly attacked by around six people over an old dispute in Kanpur’s Om Purwa area on Monday night. Mohammad Sufiyan had gone out to buy milk when the attackers allegedly surrounded him near Shiva Park and assaulted him with sticks, clubs and sharp-edged weapons, leaving him seriously injured. Sufiyan’s brother, Farhan, said the attack left him with serious injuries to his head and nasal bone. He also suffered two broken teeth and a severe injury to his left leg. The attackers allegedly took away his two mobile phones and the cash in his pocket. Police initially took Sufiyan to Kanshi Ram Hospital, where doctors referred him to Halet Hospital considering his condition. He was shifted there for further treatment around 10 pm. Farhan alleged that the accused had been roaming around the area and threatening people for several days. He claimed they had attacked others in the past as well, but continued their activities due to a lack of concrete action. Local residents also alleged that the group assaulted people to establish its dominance in the area. Jajmau police station in-charge Sanjay Pandey said Sufiyan had been sent to hospital for treatment. Police are examining CCTV footage from cameras installed around the scene and will take legal action after receiving a written complaint.

stories.title: Fake notes worth ₹7.40 crore found in PNB:CCTV shows housekeeper taking out cash; 3 officials suspended in Saharanpur
stories.summary: Fake currency notes worth approximately ₹7.40 crore were found in the currency chest of Punjab National Bank (PNB) in Saharanpur during a bank audit. The matter came to light after auditors detected the suspected fake notes. Around 3 pm on Monday, the bank suspended three officials in connection with the case. During the investigation, CCTV footage reportedly showed a part-time housekeeper removing cash from bundles of notes. An FIR has been registered against four people at Sadar Bazaar police station on the complaint of PNB Meerut Chief Manager and Investigating Officer Arun Kumar Choubey. The FIR names Senior Divisional Manager Ravi Kumar Kans, Currency Chest Manager Sushil Kumar, Currency Chest Manager Amit Kumar, who is posted in Yamunanagar-Jagadhri, and housekeeper Vishal Kumar. The bank has suspended three officials and launched an internal investigation into the alleged irregularities. ₹4.30 lakh found missing from amount sent to Jaipur The case came to light after a shortage was detected in the cash sent from PNB’s currency chest in Saharanpur to Jaipur. A few days earlier, part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar had been assigned to arrange currency bundles worth around ₹11.50 crore at the PNB branch near Ghantaghar. The cash included soiled, mutilated and other types of notes. The bank was required to send the amount to the RBI’s Jaipur Currency Chest. As per the prescribed procedure, the cash was sent to Jaipur on August 5. During counting, officials found ₹4,30,900 missing and informed the PNB officials in Meerut. Housekeeper seen taking notes on CCTV Following this, the bank sent Chief Manager Arun Kumar Chaubey to Saharanpur to investigate the matter. Along with other bank officials, he examined CCTV footage from cameras installed inside the currency chest. The footage reportedly showed part-time housekeeper Vishal Kumar taking cash from bundles of notes. After reviewing the footage, the bank terminated Vishal’s services and lodged a theft case against him for allegedly misappropriating the money. Currency chest audit began on 9 August After the alleged irregularities involving the housekeeper came to light, the bank launched an audit of its currency chest on 9 August. The audit team matched the cash physically present in the chest with the corresponding records. During the audit, a major irregularity was detected. The team found counterfeit currency notes worth approximately ₹7.40 crore among the cash stored in the currency chest. The discovery of such a large quantity of counterfeit notes raised serious concerns among bank officials. 3 bank officials questioned The investigating officer subsequently questioned officials associated with the currency chest Senior Divisional Manager Ravi Kumar Kans, Currency Chest Manager Sushil Kumar and Currency Chest Manager Amit Kumar, who is posted in Yamunanagar-Jagadhri. They were questioned about how the counterfeit notes entered the currency chest and remained there. According to the investigating officer, none of the three officials could provide a satisfactory explanation. The matter was subsequently brought to the attention of senior bank officials. Departmental inquiry initiated against bank officials Senior Manager Nisha Singh, posted at PNB’s divisional office on Delhi Road, said the bank suspended all three officials after the irregularities came to light. She added that a departmental inquiry is also underway. Police are investigating how such a large quantity of counterfeit notes entered the bank’s currency chest, when and through whom they were placed there, and whether others were involved. DIG says, ‘Case registered against four in currency chest matter’ DIG Abhishek Singh said, Based on a complaint filed by the bank’s chief manager, a case has been registered against three managers. A separate case of theft has also been registered against the part-time housekeeper. The bank is conducting an internal inquiry, while the police are also investigating the matter.

stories.title: Youth sleeping on the roof stabbed to death:Body found 400 meters away in Lucknow, brother said-villagers had threatened him
stories.summary: 25-year-old man was stabbed to death while sleeping on the rooftop of an under-construction house in Lucknow late Sunday night. The incident took place in Ganeshpur village under the Mahingwan police station area. The attackers allegedly stabbed Satish Yadav, causing him to fall from the roof into a field below. Around 2 am, a villager spotted Satish lying unconscious and seriously injured near a field about 400 metres from the house and alerted his family. His father, Shivbalak Yadav, and other relatives rushed to the spot and took him to hospital. With police assistance, Satish was later shifted to the trauma centre, where doctors declared him dead. Satish had left home around 8 pm on Sunday after dinner to sleep at the under-construction house. His brother alleged that some villagers had threatened Satish with serious consequences two days before the murder. Had started working as a watchman just 5 days earlier According to the family, Satish had started working as a watchman at an under-construction house just five days before the incident. The house was located about 1 km from the village, and Satish had been hired by a contractor named Ashok. The house reportedly belongs to a woman who lives in Lucknow. Satish would stay at the site and sleep on the rooftop at night. Threatened after being chased 2 days ago The deceased’s younger brother, Shivam Yadav, said, "Satish had been involved in a long-standing dispute with fellow villagers Sunil and Dheeraj. According to Shivam, the two men chased Satish two days ago and threatened him with dire consequences. The family suspects that the old dispute may have led to Satish’s murder. However, the exact motive has not yet been established. Shivam said the family received information at around 1 am that Satish had been attacked. They rushed to the spot and found him injured. He said Satish had gone to sleep at the under-construction site, where he was allegedly attacked. 2 suspects detained As soon as the incident was reported, Mahingwan Police reached the spot and launched an investigation. Two suspects have been detained and are being questioned. Police are also speaking to people living near the crime scene and examining the old dispute along with other possible angles. DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said, Satish, who sustained knife injuries, died during treatment. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and a case has been registered based on a complaint filed by his family.

stories.title: Cop pulls pistol from youth’s jeans in middle of road:Poses film-style in Agra; 2 cops hold his hands
stories.summary: Agra Police arrested a young man for allegedly possessing an illegal country-made pistol and then staged his arrest in the middle of a busy market. In front of onlookers, two policemen held the man while a sub-inspector dramatically pulled the pistol from his jeans. The sub-inspector then posed for the cameras with the seized weapon in his hand. The incident took place on 29 August. On Monday, Etmadpur Police released a video of the arrest, apparently to highlight the action and receive appreciation for the recovery. However, instead of drawing praise on social media, the video sparked criticism and trolling over the “filmi-style” manner in which the suspect was apprehended and the weapon recovered. First, take a look at these 2 pictures... Now, read the full story Two days ago, Etmadpur Police in Agra received information that a young man was carrying an illegal country-made pistol. During a checking operation, police arrested Deepu alias Devesh near the primary school in Vasawala village. Deepu, a resident of Satta Mohalla in Etmadpur, was allegedly found carrying a .315-bore country-made pistol and two cartridges. Police registered a case against him and sent him to jail. 26-second video goes viral On Monday, a 26-second video showing the entire police action went viral on social media and was widely shared within a short time. The video shows Sub-Inspector Parth Sarathi and constable Vinod Kumar holding a young man in the middle of the village. Moments later, Sub-Inspector Rampoot Gautam arrives in a cinematic manner. He lifts the man’s T-shirt, pulls out the country-made pistol tucked into his waistband and then poses with the weapon while looking at the camera. The person recording the video can then be heard saying, “It’s a .315-bore country-made pistol. Look, sir, make sure it isn’t loaded.” The policemen subsequently search the man and recover two cartridges from the back pocket of his jeans. A crowd of villagers can be seen gathered at the spot throughout the incident. Video draws mixed reactions on social media The video was shared by several users who described the police action as commendable. However, many others criticised the way the arrest and weapon recovery were staged. One user commented, “The script is good, but the acting isn’t.” Another wrote, “Now even the police have caught the reel-making bug.” Meanwhile, ACP Etmadpur Devesh Kumar said police had gone to the village after receiving information about a fight. The accused tried to flee after seeing the police, but two policemen caught him. As the police were taking him away, a villager informed them that he was carrying a country-made pistol. The sub-inspector then recovered the weapon. ACP Kumar said the video was recorded as evidence and confirmed that it was genuine.

Yogi flags off 4 new trains in Bahraich:Nepalgunj linked with Varanasi and Gorakhpur; Vaishnaw says bullet train will run in UP
stories.summary: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath flagged off four new trains from Nepalgunj Road railway station in Bahraich on Monday. Ashwini Vaishnaw joined virtually. He also inaugurated the approximately 56-kilometre-long Nepalgunj Road-Bahraich broad-gauge line, built at a cost of around ₹730 crore, using a remote. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that railway projects worth ₹1.29 lakh crore are currently underway in Uttar Pradesh. The state has 32 Vande Bharat and 46 Amrit Bharat trains in operation. He said that bullet trains will bring major changes to Uttar Pradesh in the coming years. In fact, there are plans to operate bullet trains under the Delhi-Varanasi high-speed rail corridor, with a maximum speed of 300 kilometres per hour. Yogi said that previous governments had made Bahraich synonymous with backwardness. Today, it has been converted from metre gauge to broad gauge. For us, this region has served as the gateway to India. Launch of these 4 trains Trains extended up to Nepalgunj railway station Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that four trains have been launched. With gauge conversion, Nepalgunj, Babaganj, Nanpara, Matera, Risia, and Bahraich will now be connected to the wider railway network. In a way, this program is fulfilling everyone's long-standing demand. I would like to thank the Chief Minister and, especially, Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the excellent planning undertaken for the development of the railway network in Purvanchal and Uttar Pradesh. Find out train schedule 1- Varanasi-Bahraich Express 2- Varanasi-Gorakhpur Express The route of the Varanasi City-Gorakhpur-Varanasi City Express (15132/15131) has been extended to nepalgunj Road. The train will now run from Varanasi to nepalgunj Road and, on its return journey, from nepalgunj Road to Varanasi. The train will have a total of 18 coaches, including General, Sleeper, AC Third, AC Third Economy, and AC Second Class coaches. The train will be operated with an LHB rake. 3- Gonda-Bahraich DEMU The route of the Gonda-Bahraich-Gonda DEMU (75111/75112) has been extended to Nepalgunj Road. Passengers will now have a direct train service from Gonda to Nepalgunj Road. This route extension will provide a direct rail connection for passengers traveling between Gonda, Bahraich, and Nepalgunj Road. 4- Gonda-Bahraich DEMU key points from the CM's speech 1. Mafias were sheltered earlier; now medical colleges are being built In the previous government, people sheltered mafias, but today medical colleges are being built in every district. Did anyone ever imagine that there would be a medical college in Bahraich? Today, Bahraich has a medical college named after Maharaja Suheldev. There are medical colleges in Balrampur and Gonda, an airport has been constructed in Shravasti, and there are also medical colleges in Ayodhya, Sultanpur, and Ambedkar Nagar. 2. Encephalitis, like the mafia, has also been eradicated This region was once affected by diseases such as encephalitis. When children died, the previous government described it as an unknown disease. When the double-engine government came to power in Uttar Pradesh, it said that the disease could not remain unknown; it would be identified and eradicated. Just as the mafia was eliminated from Uttar Pradesh, diseases such as encephalitis have also been permanently eradicated. Now, no father worries that his child might succumb to the disease. 3. Women and traders need not feel afraid Today, no woman, trader, or ordinary citizen needs to fear any mafia member or criminal. These are the achievements of the double-engine government, which are now visible on the ground. 4. Six-lane Lucknow-Bahraich road approved Recently, under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister, the Union Cabinet approved connecting Lucknow to Bahraich by upgrading the road connectivity from four lanes. Road and railway connectivity in every direction is helping realize the vision of development in the new India. Today, almost all railway lines in India have been converted to broad gauge. 5. Grand memorial built for Maharaja Suheldev Maharaja Suheldev freed this land by killing the foreign invader. Under previous governments, fairs and Urs gatherings were held here in the name of Salar Masud, but today a grand memorial dedicated to Maharaja Suheldev has been built on this very land, so that people can learn about their heritage and pride. 6. When railway tracks are broader, roads and markets become larger When the railway tracks are broader, the roads also become wider; when the roads become wider, the markets also expand; and when the markets grow, trade flourishes. This is the path of development under the double-engine government, which is becoming visible through better railway connectivity to nepalgunj Road. 7. We stand with Nepal in this hour of grief Before the program, everyone paid tribute to those who lost their lives in the devastating disaster in Nepal. The Chief Minister said that recently, hundreds of people in Nepal, India, and several other countries around the world had fallen victim to natural disasters. CM expressed condolences to the families who lost their loved ones and assured the people of Nepal that we would stand together through happiness and sorrow. Under the leadership of PM Modi, the Government of India has taken swift decisions and stepped forward to assist the friendly nation of Nepal. Our relationship is not merely political; we also share a cultural heritage. From Lord Pashupatinath to Kashi Vishwanath, and from Gorkha to Gorakhpur and Janakpur to Ayodhya, these sacred places are remembered with reverence. We also visit each other's holy sites to honor our shared heritage.

stories.title: Wife found dead in room, husband flees:Man locked sister-in-law in room in Jhansi; couple had a love marriage 18 months ago
stories.summary: Woman was found dead inside her home in Jhansi on Monday, hours after she allegedly had an argument with her husband. According to her family, the couple went to sleep late on Sunday night, while the woman’s younger sister slept in another room. During the night, the husband allegedly latched both rooms from outside and fled. At around 9 am, the woman’s brother arrived at the house and opened the latch. He found his sister, Shivani, unconscious inside the room, while her younger sister Muskan was asleep in the adjacent room. The family rushed Shivani to the Medical College, where doctors declared her dead. The woman’s brother accused his brother-in-law of strangling Shivani and fleeing the scene. Police are searching for the husband. The incident took place in the Sipri Bazar police station area. Became friends on social media Sudha, also known as Shivani, was a resident of Indergarh in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. Her father, Santram Vanshkar, sells fruit from a cart, while her mother works as a domestic help in Delhi. Shivani was the eldest of four sisters. Her younger sisters, Preeti and Neha, are married. She also had a younger sister, Muskan (18), and two brothers, Aniket (17) and Kapil (14). Muskan said, “Around two years ago, my elder sister Shivani became friends with Yash Thakur (28), a resident of Gwalior, on social media. They eventually fell in love. Yash worked at a clothing store. After some time, they told their families about their relationship, and our family agreed to the marriage. Shivani married Yash around one-and-a-half years ago.” Shivani had been living in Jhansi for three months Muskan said, “After their marriage, Shivani lived with Yash in Gwalior. However, he later started assaulting her over petty issues. Troubled by this, my sister rented a room near Awas Vikas Fauji Tiraha in Jhansi.” Muskan and her brother Aniket also lived with Shivani, while their father and younger brother Kapil stayed in their village. Yash would occasionally visit Shivani in Jhansi. A day before Raksha Bandhan, Shivani went to Gwalior with Kapil. After staying there for two days, she returned to Jhansi with her husband, while Kapil went back to the village. She argued with her husband before her death Muskan said, “On Sunday night, my sister had an argument with her husband. He was hurling abusive remarks at our family. He told her, ‘I have slept with your sister, and I will beat your father with a slipper.’ This led to a heated argument between them. “Our maternal uncle, Santosh, lives nearby. He intervened and calmed my brother-in-law down. After that, Aniket went to our uncle’s house. Things then appeared to return to normal. I went to sleep in my room, while my sister and brother-in-law slept in the other room.” Husband allegedly latched the room from outside Muskan said, “Around 1:30–2 am, my brother-in-law asked for his bag, saying he needed to take some things. We gave it to him, after which he latched the door from outside. “At around 5 am, I tried to open the door to go to the bathroom, but it would not open. I called out to my sister and brother-in-law for around half an hour, but there was no response. I eventually went back to sleep. At around 9 am, my brother returned home and opened the door. I then went into my sister’s room and found her body lying there.”, she added Brother says, ‘Doors of both rooms were latched from outside’ Shivani’s brother Aniket said, “When I reached home at around 9 am, I found the latch of my sister’s room locked from outside. I opened it and entered the room, where I found my sister lying on the floor. Blood was coming from her ear, and there were marks on her neck. The door of the other room was also latched from outside. I opened it and woke my sister Muskan.” Neighbours and family members gathered at the house after the incident. The family rushed Shivani to the Medical College, where doctors declared her dead. Aniket and Muskan alleged that their brother-in-law killed Shivani, latched the room from outside and fled. They demanded his arrest. CO Ramveer Singh said an injury mark was visible on the woman’s neck, while no other injuries were found. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination, and the exact cause of death will be established after the report is received. He said Shivani had been having a dispute with her husband and police teams were searching for him. Post-mortem confirms murder Shivani’s body was examined at night by a two-doctor panel. According to the doctors, she was strangled to death. Five injuries were found on her neck and face. Police suspect that she was strangled with a rope or piece of clothing.

stories.summary: Divya Mittal IAS Resignation: उत्तर प्रदेश कैडर की चर्चित IAS अधिकारी दिव्या मित्तल के इस्तीफे के बाद उनकी प्रशासनिक यात्रा एक बार फिर चर्चा में है। अपने कार्यकाल के दौरान उन्होंने कई जिलों और महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक पदों पर जिम्मेदारी संभाली। हालांकि, इस्तीफे के साथ साझा किए गए अपने भावुक संदेश में उन्होंने खास तौर पर मिर्जापुर और देवरिया का जिक्र किया। दिव्या मित्तल ने मिर्जापुर को लेकर लिखा कि इस जिले ने उन्हें सिखाया कि ‘असंभव’ कोई तथ्य नहीं, बल्कि एक राय है। वहीं देवरिया के लिए उन्होंने कहा कि इस जिले ने उन्हें सिखाया कि सही के साथ खड़ा होना कोई विकल्प नहीं, बल्कि कर्तव्य है। यही वजह है कि उनके इस्तीफे के बाद इन दोनों जिलों से जुड़ी उनकी यादें और अनुभव लोगों के बीच चर्चा का विषय बने हुए हैं।

stories.title: Yogi says opposition spreading misinformation, BJP workers silent:Smriti says speeches won’t work, make videos on govt schemes
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday alerted BJP workers in Lucknow ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He said the opposition was spreading confusion among the public over issues concerning Gen Z, Gen Alpha and the Ram Temple. “But you are silent. Those who are asleep should wake up. Do not sit back complacently, relying only on the government’s work,” he said. Yogi cited a remark by Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar: “We are not as concerned by the insolence of the wicked as we are troubled by the excessive goodness of the virtuous.” The Chief Minister was speaking at a meeting of the BJP’s Seva Sankalp campaign at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani said party workers must counter the opposition’s narrative through videos. “Speeches alone will not work,” she said. Yogi also agreed with Irani’s remarks. Chief Minister Yogi mentions ‘Gen Z’ and ‘Gen Alpha’ Yogi referred to ‘Gen Z’ and ‘Gen Alpha’ in his speech. He said the opposition claims that the current government has done nothing for children’s future or education. “But no one is unaware of the condition of schools run by the Uttar Pradesh Basic Education Council before 2017,” he said. He highlighted the differences between the work done by the Samajwadi Party and BJP governments: Claim of 9.30 lakh government jobs Chief Minister alleged that before 2017, recruitment examinations conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) were marred by open corruption, with merit being sidelined in favour of candidates from “one particular caste”. He claimed that at one point, 56 of the 86 sub-divisional magistrates (SDMs) selected were from the same caste. Yogi claimed that over the past seven to eight years, the state government has provided government jobs to 930,000 young people through a transparent process, without recommendations, financial transactions or discrimination. He said that of the 29,000 Shakti Kendras (groups of polling booths) across the state, there would hardly be one where two to four young people had not secured government jobs. However, he said the organisation had failed to bring the “success stories” of these youths before the public. Yogi targets SP over Ram Temple and encephalitis (brain fever) Chief Minister said efforts were now underway to discredit the Ram Temple project and the arrangements surrounding it, despite the temple’s construction after decades of legal and political hurdles. He accused opposition parties of putting all their strength into the campaign, while BJP workers remained silent instead of responding aggressively. Yogi also targeted the opposition over encephalitis in eastern Uttar Pradesh. He said, “Thousands of poor children used to die of encephalitis every year in Purvanchal, but no opposition leader shed a tear. They remained silent about the safety of daughters. But when our government took action against the mafia, they turned up to mourn them.” Smriti Irani lays out plan for BJP workers BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani laid out a plan for party workers during the meeting. She said speeches alone would not be enough to counter the opposition’s digital narrative. Irani directed the organisation to identify at least 10 “success stories” from each of Uttar Pradesh’s 29,000 Shakti Kendras involving people who have directly benefited from government schemes. These could include a beneficiary who received a house under PM Awas Yojana, an artisan associated with the One District One Product (ODOP) scheme, an entrepreneur who benefited from the MUDRA scheme, or a child studying in a school renovated under Operation Kayakalp. The Chief Minister endorsed the idea and highlighted several major figures related to Uttar Pradesh’s economy and development: ‘Seva Pakhwada’ to begin on PM Modi’s birthday till 1 month During the final phase of the meeting, the BJP finalised the programme for ‘Seva Pakhwada’, which will begin on 17 September till one month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.

stories.title: Varanasi woman lies on railway track:Attempts suicide after being stopped from using Instagram; woman cop saves her life
stories.summary: Young woman allegedly attempted suicide at the Ashapur railway crossing in Varanasi’s Sarnath police station area after her family stopped her from using Instagram. Upset after being scolded, she lay down on the railway tracks. An alert woman police officer reached the spot in time and pulled her to safety, moments before a train passed. Sarnath SHO Pankaj Kumar Tripathi said police received information at around 11:45 pm that a young woman was lying on the tracks near the Ashapur railway crossing. Ashapur outpost in-charge Diksha Pandey immediately rushed to the spot and found the woman lying on the tracks as a train approached from the opposite direction. Showing quick presence of mind, Pandey pulled the woman off the tracks just moments before the train passed through the spot. Police took the woman to the Ashapur outpost and counselled her. After she had calmed down, she identified herself as Pinky (18). Originally from Patna, she currently lives in a rented accommodation in the Ashapur area, where she is reportedly working or studying. Pinky told police that her brother had stopped her from using social media and had severely scolded her the previous night. Upset over the incident, she said she decided to take the extreme step. Following counselling, Pinky acknowledged her mistake and assured police that she would not repeat such an act. Later that night, police contacted her colleagues and handed her over to them to ensure she reached home safely.
