stories.title: Property dealer drugged and shot in car:Lucknow driver threw mobile on train, messaged wife 'Don’t look for me'
stories.summary: Property dealer Dhirendra Pratap Singh, 35, was allegedly kidnapped and murdered by his own driver in Lucknow. Police said the driver, Ravi Tiwari, first made Dhirendra unconscious by making him smell a handkerchief inside the car before shooting him. He then threw Dhirendra’s mobile phone into a moving train to mislead the police, causing its location to shift and eventually showing up in Chandauli, around 350 km away. In an attempt to cover up the crime, Ravi later went to the police station himself and filed a missing person report for Dhirendra. Before throwing the phone onto the train, he also sent a message to Dhirendra’s wife: “I am leaving. Do not look for me and do not tell anyone my location.” After Dhirendra’s body was recovered, Ravi allegedly confessed to the murder during police interrogation and revealed that he was in contact with a man named Monu Singh. Police said he had been promised a house, a shop and ₹12 lakh in cash in Lucknow in exchange for killing Dhirendra. Ravi had worked with Dhirendra for nearly 10 years and had earned his complete trust. Dhirendra would even leave lakhs of rupees in cash with him and share almost all his business-related details. Police said Ravi betrayed that trust for greed. First, know the full case Thirty five year old property dealer Dhirendra Pratap Singh was shot dead in Lucknow. His body was recovered from a small canal in Dubagga, around 22 km from the district headquarters, at 5 pm on Sunday. Bullet wounds were found on his forehead and chest. Dhirendra, a resident of Unnao, was the president of the Maharana Pratap Charitable Foundation and was involved in the property and transport businesses. He lived in Lucknow’s PGI area. On Saturday, his wife lodged a complaint alleging that Dhirendra had been kidnapped by his driver and his associates. The initial investigation suggests that the murder may have been linked to a dispute over a piece of land in Unnao worth around ₹50 crore. Dhirendra had reportedly written a letter to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath raising a complaint over the land dispute. Police have taken Dhirendra’s driver, Ravi Tiwari, and his associate, Omkar, into custody. During questioning, Ravi reportedly confessed to the murder. 4 people suspected of involvement; police searching for 2 According to ADCP South Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar, the names of four people have emerged in the investigation so far. They include Ravi Tiwari, a driver from Nilmatha, and his acquaintance Omkar, a resident of Khargapur. Ravi and Omkar are currently in police custody, while a search is underway for the other two suspects based on information obtained during their interrogation. Police said Ravi had been working as Dhirendra Pratap Singh’s driver for around 10 years and had earned his complete trust. Investigators allege that the conspirators exploited this trust and lured Ravi into the murder plot by promising him a house, a shop and ₹12 lakh in cash in Lucknow. Body dumped 25 km away after murder During police interrogation, the driver allegedly revealed that he first made Dhirendra unconscious by making him smell a handkerchief. He then shot him in the right side of the chest. As Dhirendra collapsed, the driver allegedly fired another shot into the back of his head. The murder took place near Utarethia. He then allegedly carried Dhirendra’s body in a Fortuner to an isolated spot along Kisan Path in Dubagga, around 25 km away. The body was dumped in the Sharda Sahayak Canal, about 50 metres from the road. The driver later abandoned Dhirendra’s Fortuner near Medanta Hospital and allegedly fled with Omkar. Location traced from Lucknow to Amethi within hours Dhirendra had two mobile phones. To mislead the police, the accused allegedly threw one of them onto a moving train, causing its location to keep changing and diverting the investigation. When police tracked the phone, its location was first recorded in Gosainganj, Haidergarh and Jagdishpur in Amethi. Later, its last location was traced to Chandauli, around 350 km from Lucknow. This raised suspicion that the phone had been deliberately moved to another location to mislead investigators. Wife filed kidnapping complaint DCP South Mushtaq said Dhirendra’s wife, Mamta Singh, had lodged a complaint alleging that her husband had been kidnapped by his driver and his associates. Based on the complaint and initial suspicion, police detained driver Ravi Tiwari for questioning. He initially attempted to mislead investigators. During sustained questioning, Ravi allegedly confessed to the murder. Based on information provided by him, police recovered Dhirendra’s body from Dubagga. The investigation indicated that a land dispute in Unnao was allegedly behind the conspiracy and murder. Two accused, including Ravi, are currently in custody. Dhirendra was considered a close aide of former MLA Sengar Dhirendra Pratap Singh was considered a close aide of former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar from the Bangarmau assembly seat of Unnao. It has been reported that while Kuldeep Singh Sengar was lodged in Lucknow District Jail, Dhirendra Pratap Singh often visited him in jail. He also used to advocate for his legal cases. Pictures of Dhirendra Pratap Singh with several prominent BJP leaders are also going viral on social media. Rumors of the murder of a Hindu Yuva Vahini leader spread After the murder of Dhirendra Pratap Singh, the president of Maharana Pratap Charitable Trust, rumors of the murder of his namesake, Hindu Yuva Vahini leader Dhirendra Pratap Singh, spread on social media. Following this, hundreds of people started calling the Hindu Yuva Vahini leader. He informed everyone that he was safe. After this, he made a video of himself being alive and safe and posted it on social media.

stories.title: VIDEO| Drunk Lucknow cop assaults man, damages car:Abuses in uniform caught on camera; DCP attaches him to police lines
stories.summary: Sub-inspector Gopesh Sharma, posted at Naka police station, assaulted a young man while under the influence of alcohol, abused him, and broke his car window. The young man recorded a video of this incident. After the video surfaced, the DCP suspended the sub-inspector to police lines. The incident and the subsequent action took place on Sunday. Rahul Geetam, a resident of Barawan Kala in Dubagga, runs a tiffin service. According to Rahul, he had a prior acquaintance with Sub-Inspector Gopesh Sharma. On Sunday morning, the sub-inspector allegedly arrived at his house in an intoxicated state and asked him to accompany him. After getting into the car, the sub-inspector started assaulting and abusing Rahul. After breaking the car window, he snatched ₹15,000 Rahul alleges that he got out of the car on the way to urinate. During this time, the sub-inspector broke the car's window with a brick. Rahul also accused the sub-inspector of snatching ₹15,000. After this, Rahul took the sub-inspector to the Dubagga police station and filed a complaint regarding the matter. Dubagga Inspector Shrikant Rai stated that a compromise had been reached between both parties. However, after the video of the incident went viral, police officials took it seriously. Western DCP Kamlesh Dixit stated that cognizance of the viral video has been taken. Sub-Inspector Gopesh Sharma has been sent to police lines, and the investigation of the case has been handed over to the ACP of Chowk. Further action will be taken based on the investigation report.

stories.title: Blast at firecracker factory near Prayagraj Air Force Station:11 killed, including 8 children; DM orders bulldozer at warehouse
stories.summary: Massive explosion at a firecracker factory on the Prayagraj-Kaushambi border in Uttar Pradesh on Monday killed 11 people, including eight children, and left five others with burn injuries. Police said the blast was so powerful that the entire factory collapsed. Eight houses within a 100-metre radius were damaged, three of them completely destroyed. The explosion occurred around 12:30 pm in Mohammadpur village in Kaushambi, located on the Prayagraj border and about 2 km from the Air Force station in Manauri. Around 200 personnel from the police, Air Force, NDRF and SDRF are involved in the rescue operation, while 10 bulldozers are being used to clear the debris. Police suspect that more people may be trapped underneath, raising the possibility of a further increase in the death toll. Seven workers were inside the factory when the blast occurred, three of whom were killed. The remaining eight victims were residents of nearby houses. Police are investigating the cause of the explosion. However, Rani, who reached Swaroop Rani Hospital in Prayagraj, said the blast occurred after an electricity pole fell and triggered a powerful explosion in the gunpowder stored inside the factory. Explosion was heard up to 2 km away, and within minutes, a thick cloud of smoke engulfed the area. Villagers were seen carrying injured people on charpoys to get them to safety. The intensity of the blast can be gauged from the fact that it blew an 8-foot-wide hole through the third floor of a nearby house. Single-storey illegal factory was spread across 600 sq ft and was owned by a man identified as Adil. According to police, a new residential settlement was coming up next to the factory. A case has been registered against Adil, his father Naushad, his uncle Shakeel and three women. Four teams have been formed to arrest the accused. District Magistrate Amit Pal Sharma said strict action would be taken against those responsible and their properties would also be attached. Within eight hours of the blast, the DM and SP ordered a bulldozer action against a warehouse located 400 metres from the factory. The warehouse was demolished. See pictures- Deputy CM Keshav meets injured victims Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced compensation for the victims. The families of those killed will receive ₹2 lakh each, while the injured will be given ₹50,000 each. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya visited the injured at SRN Hospital in Prayagraj. He described the deaths of several members of the same family as deeply tragic and heartbreaking. He said the government’s top priority was to save the lives of the injured and ensure they received the best possible treatment. The DM and SSP have been directed to investigate the incident, and strict action will be taken against anyone found responsible. See where the explosion occurred in this graphic...

stories.title: Mayawati launches Uma Shankar Singh’s son:Joins BSP meeting for first time, may contest from father’s seat
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati held a major meeting in Lucknow on Monday, which was attended by Yukesh Singh, the son of late BSP MLA Umashankar Singh. This was the first time Yukesh had been seen at a political event, and he was seated in the front row during the meeting. His appearance is being seen as a possible formal political launch by Mayawati. Yukesh may contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election from his father’s former constituency, Rasra in Ballia. Umashankar Singh (55), who was the only BSP MLA in UP, passed away on 5 August. He had been battling brain cancer for a long time. At that time, Mayawati had said, "Umashankar considered me his own sister. Many people left the party in politics, but he never betrayed the party. If the family wishes, I will give his son every opportunity to move forward in politics and will strive to give him the same respect and importance that Umashankar Singh received." Meanwhile, more than 600 office bearers and workers, including district presidents of all 75 districts of the state, divisional coordinators, and announced assembly in-charges, have reached the state office for this meeting, which began at 11 am. However, Mayawati's nephew, Akash Anand, is not present at this meeting. It has been stated that the focus of today's meeting is solely on UP. In such a situation, Akash will attend the BSP's national executive meeting to be held on 3rd September. The meeting is discussing preparations for the 2027 assembly elections, strengthening the organization at the grassroots level, and the selection of potential candidates. Along with this, Mayawati is reviewing the guidelines given in previous meetings. The BSP chief may give new guidelines to the office bearers for the upcoming elections in the meeting. See pictures of the meeting- Yukesh is the successor to his father's political legacy Umashankar was a three-time MLA from the Rasra seat of Ballia district. His family includes his wife Pushpa Singh, daughter Yamini, and son Prince Yukesh. In 2024, the MLA got Yukesh married to Kanika Singh, the niece of Dinesh Pratap Singh, a Minister of State (Independent Charge) in the UP government. BSP chief Mayawati also attended this wedding. Yukesh is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of his father's company, 'CS Infraconstruction Limited'. After Umashankar's demise, Prince Yukesh is being considered the successor to his political legacy. However, Yukesh has never been seen in active politics. 4 key points from Mayawati’s meeting 1. ‘Stop distributing freebies to women’ Mayawati said the BJP government was trying to influence women voters by distributing “freebies” in the name of welfare schemes to win elections. She demanded that this practice be stopped immediately. She said opposition parties had developed a habit of going back on their promises after elections and warned people of Uttar Pradesh to remain cautious of such “false promises and deception”. 2. ‘Gen Z and Gen Alpha protests are a result of broken promises’ Mayawati said protests by ‘Gen Z’ and ‘Gen Alpha’ were the result of state governments failing to fulfil their promises. She said young people would not have needed to take to the streets if governments had addressed their demands on time. 3. ‘Inflation and unemployment driving migration’ Mayawati said migration from Uttar Pradesh was increasing due to inflation, poverty, unemployment and underdevelopment, with young people and ordinary citizens leaving the state in search of better opportunities. She also announced that the programme marking the death anniversary of Kanshi Ram would be held at the Kanshi Ram Memorial Site in Lucknow on October 9. People from across Uttar Pradesh are expected to attend the event. 4. Tussle over selection of candidates According to sources, party office-bearers told Mayawati during the meeting that they were struggling to find strong candidates who could provide all-round support on weaker seats. Mayawati directed them to finalise the name of the strongest available candidate for now. However, she said the ticket could be changed before the election if a stronger candidate emerged. Some leaders, speaking on condition of anonymity, raised concerns over the possibility of a last-minute ticket change. They questioned what the party would tell a candidate if their ticket was cancelled just before the election. Who said what after the meeting? Read here More than 30 Assembly in-charges announced, 50 names shortlisted The BSP has stepped up preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The party has so far appointed in-charges for more than 30 Assembly constituencies, while over 50 names are reportedly on its shortlist. The appointed in-charges have already begun public outreach and election-related activities in their respective constituencies. BSP national coordinator Akash Anand has also intensified his political activities in western Uttar Pradesh. He has already addressed election meetings in Sadabad in Hathras and Jewar. Meanwhile, western UP in-charge Munkad Ali and state president Vishwanath Pal are announcing the names of Assembly in-charges at workers’ conferences being held across different constituencies. Smita Chand named BSP candidate from Gorakhpur’s Chillupar seat The BSP has also begun working on its electoral strategy in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The party has named former BJP leader Smita Chand as its candidate from the Chillupar Assembly constituency in Gorakhpur. Smita Chand previously served as the state vice-president of the BJP Mahila Morcha. Her father-in-law, Markandey Chand, was once a prominent BSP leader before leaving the party and forming the Janatantrik BSP. Her entry into the BSP is therefore being seen as significant from both a social and political strategy perspective.

stories.title: 2 sisters carrying their mother’s ashes killed in crash:4 relatives also dead as pickup truck rams into vehicle in Kasganj; 20 injured
stories.summary: 6 members of the same family died in a horrific collision between a speeding Max pickup and a truck in Kasganj, UP. 20 others were seriously injured. The people in the pickup were on their way to the Soronji pilgrimage site from Karauli and Bharatpur in Rajasthan for the immersion of ashes early Monday morning. On the Kasganj-Mathura road, the pickup rammed into a truck moving ahead of it from behind. The accident was so severe that the front part of the pickup was shattered. The bonnet was completely crushed. Upon impact, the people sitting in the back were flung about 5 feet away. Those sitting in the front got severely trapped inside the vehicle. Hearing the screams, nearby residents reached the spot and somehow pulled the injured out of the pickup and informed the police. The police reached the spot and, with the help of ambulances, took all the injured to the hospital, where doctors declared 6 people dead. The accident occurred at around 3:45 AM near Mohanpura in the Kasganj Kotwali area, 29 kilometers away from the district headquarters. See pictures of the accident- Now understand the entire incident in chronological order- Sua (30), mother of Ravindra, a resident of Raiwai village under Hindaun police station area in Rajasthan, passed away on August 25 after a prolonged illness. The family members and relatives decided to go to Soronji in Kasganj to immerse Sua's ashes. On Sunday at 5:30 PM, 26 people, including 11 men, 8 women, and 7 children, left for Soronji in a Max pickup (RJ-02 GB-4482). According to the police, the Max pickup had just reached near Shiv Inter College, Katour in Kasganj. During this time, a truck (RJ-36 GB-1404) was being reversed. Suddenly, the pickup rammed into the truck from behind. After the accident, there was an outcry. Upon receiving the information, the police, with the help of local residents, took all 26 injured to the district hospital. Doctors declared Umesh (33), Prem (35), and Nehru (60), residents of Karauli, Rajasthan, dead. Out of the remaining 23 injured, 8 were referred to Aligarh, where Reena (32) from Bharatpur, Ranjeet (33) from Karauli, and Anjali (26) from Dausa succumbed to their injuries. SP-DM reached the hospital to inquire about the condition of the injured After receiving information about the accident, police and administrative officials, including SP OP Singh and DM Pranay Singh, reached the spot. They inspected the incident site. Then, they reached the district hospital to inquire about the condition of the injured. They instructed the doctors to provide better treatment to the injured. The seriously injured have been referred to higher medical centers as per the requirement. All relatives, 7 children also among the injured Pickup driver Bhupendra (27) from Karauli, Hemant (16), Vandana (22), Naitik (12), and Priyansh (3) are undergoing treatment in Aligarh. Ravindra (34), Tejram (60), Karmveer (38), Vimlesh (30), Chandrabhan (25), Rajkumari (25), Seema (25), Sapna (26), Kavita (22), Mayank (12), Lakshya (11), Chirag (5), Reyansh (3), Kanha (2), and Netram (60), a resident of Dausa, are undergoing treatment at the District Hospital. All of them are relatives of Ravindra. Kotwali Kasganj in-charge Jagdish Chandra Rajput said, The police are investigating all aspects of the accident. Both the crashed vehicles have been seized, and legal action is being taken. The situation will become clear only after the investigation. ARTO says, ‘Thar was travelling at around 100 kmph’ Kasganj ARTO Ram Prakash Mishra said an on-site inspection suggested that the pickup was travelling at around 100 kmph. Police suspect the driver may have dozed off, causing the vehicle to lose control and crash into the truck ahead. The pickup collided with the truck’s diesel tank. Fortunately, the tank did not catch fire, which could have made the accident even more serious.

stories.title: Man assaults cop after being asked for RC, DL:Pushes outpost in-charge to ground, breaks uniform emblem
stories.summary: A dispute broke out between the police and some people in Shivpur, Varanasi, when the police seized a motorcycle without a license plate and asked for the RC and driving license. It is alleged that people manhandled police officers during vehicle checking near Gilt Bazaar intersection late Saturday night. Gilt Bazaar outpost in-charge SI Amit Singh was pushed to the ground, and the monogram on his uniform was torn off. One of the accused is also alleged to have pulled a constable's whistle cord. Gilt Bazaar outpost in-charge SI Amit Singh was patrolling with a police team around midnight on Saturday. During this time, a yellow Bullet motorcycle without a license plate was found parked on the road from Gilt Bazaar intersection to Chuppepur. When the police team asked for the motorcycle's documents, the rider was unable to produce them. As the documents were unavailable, the police began seizing the motorcycle. At that moment, the relatives and associates of Rajat Sonkar reached the spot. It is alleged that the accused opposed the seizure of the motorcycle and attempted to stop the police team. When the argument escalated, those people engaged in a physical altercation with the police personnel. It is alleged that Golu alias Kishan Sonkar confronted the police team. During the incident, one of the accused allegedly pushed outpost in-charge Amit Singh, causing him to fall to the ground and sustain injuries. Sub-Inspector's uniform insignia torn off, constable's whistle cord also pulled It is alleged that during the altercation, the insignia on Sub-Inspector Amit Singh's uniform was pulled and torn off. In addition, one of the constables' whistle cords was also allegedly broken. The FIR registered by the police also states that the people present at the scene surrounded the police team, obstructed them in the discharge of their official duties, and threatened to kill them. Case registered against 7 named accused and 5 or 6 unidentified persons In this case, Shivpur police registered an FIR on Sunday based on a complaint filed by outpost in-charge Amit Singh. Seven people, including Rajat Sonkar, Golu alias Kishan Sonkar, Rajat's sister and mother, Shubham Sonkar, and Prince alias Rishabh Sonkar, have been named in the case. In addition, five or six unidentified people have also been made accused.

stories.title: Bihar thief arrested for stealing at railway station:Targeted sleeping passengers in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: To curb incidents of theft of passengers' luggage and mobile phones at Gorakhpur Railway Station, a continuous checking campaign is being conducted by the GRP. During this campaign, on Sunday, 30 August, the police arrested an interstate habitual thief. A stolen mobile phone worth approximately ₹20,000 was recovered from his possession. Caught during the checking of suspects According to the police, under the guidance of Superintendent of Police, Railway Gorakhpur Section, Lakshmi Niwas Mishra, and Deputy Superintendent of Police, Railway, Ashok Kumar Singh, continuous checking of suspicious persons and items was being carried out at Gorakhpur Junction. Under the leadership of Station House Officer Anuj Kumar Singh, Sub-Inspector Arvind Kumar, Sub-Inspector Ankit Pandey, and personnel from the Anti-Drugging Squad were conducting checks at the station. During this time, the police spotted a suspicious youth near the steam engine selfie point at the railway station. After questioning and a search, he was arrested. Accused is a resident of Bihar The arrested accused has been identified as Arjun Kumar Sah, who is a resident of the Mairwa Motichhapar area under the Mairwa police station in Bihar. His age is reported to be around 26 years. The police recovered a mobile phone from his possession, which is valued at approximately ₹20,000. According to the police, this mobile was stolen from Gorakhpur railway station, and a case was already registered in this regard at the GRP police station. Section added to the theft case After the recovery of the mobile, the sections of the case filed against him at the GRP police station, Gorakhpur, were enhanced. The police presented the accused in court, from where he was sent to District Jail, Gorakhpur, in judicial custody. During interrogation, he said - I commit theft on trains and platforms During police interrogation, the accused revealed that he commits theft on trains and railway platforms to cover his expenses. According to the accused, he used to target passengers sleeping on moving trains and platforms. He would sell the mobile phones and other items stolen from passengers to people he met along the way. He used the money earned from selling these items to cover his expenses. Regarding the recovered mobile, the accused told the police that he had stolen it from a passenger at Gorakhpur railway station about 15 to 20 days ago. On Sunday, he had reached Gorakhpur railway station again with the intention of committing theft, but the police caught him during a check. Cases of theft are already registered against him According to the police, the criminal history of the arrested accused has also come to light. Two cases related to theft and possession of stolen property are already registered against him at the GRP Gorakhpur police station. Mobile worth ₹20,000 recovered The police have recovered a mobile phone from the accused, which has an estimated value of ₹ 20,000. The police are now gathering information regarding other cases and theft incidents linked to the accused. Police team that made the arrest The team that arrested the accused included Inspector-in-Charge Anuj Kumar Singh, Sub-Inspector Arvind Kumar, Sub-Inspector Ankit Pandey, Head Constable Guru Prasad, and Constables Vipin Yadav, Ranjeet Yadav, Devendra Singh Yadav, and Avinish Singh.

stories.title: Heavy rain alert in 18 UP districts:Up to 5-ft mud fills homes in Chitrakoot; schools up to Class 8 shut in Sultanpur
stories.summary: A rain alert has been issued in 58 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Very heavy rain is expected in 18 districts, including Prayagraj and Varanasi. Clouds have been covering Lucknow and 10 nearby districts since Monday morning. Due to the heavy rain forecast, schools up to Class 8 have been closed in Sultanpur today. The situation in Chitrakoot had worsened due to continuous rain and water being released from Madhya Pradesh’s Bargi Dam. The river rose by 30 feet. Although the floodwater in the Mandakini River has now receded, the problems have increased. Mud has filled homes up to 5 feet deep in some areas, while roads are covered with debris. Residents are busy clearing water and mud from their homes. Fridges and coolers have been filled with debris. Broken electric poles can be seen at several places. The bridge at Ramghat collapsed and fell into the Mandakini River. A statue of Tulsidas was also damaged, with the portion above the shoulders swept away. Two helicopters and SDRF teams rescued 50 people. In Gobaria village, 12 people who had remained stranded on a peepal tree for nearly four hours were safely rescued. SDRF personnel carried children trapped inside houses in their arms and brought them to safety. See pictures of floods and rain… Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: “The monsoon system over Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and southern Uttar Pradesh has moved ahead. As a result, rainfall activity will decrease until 31 August. After this, another weather system will bring rain again in the first week of September.”

stories.title: CCTV | Thar loses control on expressway:4 killed including 2 brothers; hits divider at 100 kmph, crosses 6 lanes
stories.summary: A Thar travelling at around 100 km/h lost control and crashed into a divider on the Ganga Expressway in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh. Four people were killed in the accident, including two brothers, while one person was seriously injured. All those killed were residents of Badaun and were travelling to Delhi. The accident took place at 11:56 pm on Sunday in the Simbhaoli police station area, around 35km from the district headquarters. CCTV footage of the accident has also emerged. It shows the speeding Thar travelling along the side of the road suddenly losing control, breaking through the divider, crossing all six lanes and crashing into the railing. The impact sent the Thar around 5ft backwards. The crash was so severe that the Thar was completely wrecked. Its roof was torn off, and the bonnet was completely crushed. Eyewitnesses said the occupants were trapped inside the car. They managed to pull them out with difficulty. Police reached the spot after receiving information and took everyone to hospital. 3 pictures of the accident– Injured taken to hospital, 4 declared dead According to police, they received information via Dial-112 that a Thar (DL 8C BL 9822) had crashed and overturned on the Ganga Expressway. A police team immediately reached the spot and took everyone to CHC Sikhera. Doctors there declared Palpur resident Jogendra (26), brothers Sukhwinder (25) and Jaswant (20) from Mewli, and Ravi (20) from Purdalpur dead. Palpur resident Vishnu (17) was seriously injured in the accident. Ravi and Jogendra were maternal and paternal cousins, while the injured Vishnu was their cousin. Station House Officer Arvind Chaudhary said the cause of the accident is being investigated. Police have taken the bodies into custody and sent them for post-mortem. They left home at 9 pm; one of them was married The family members said all of them had left home at around 9 pm. Jogendra worked in farming and owned the Thar. Ravi worked in Delhi, while the others were also employed in Delhi in the plastic and polyester manufacturing industry. The deceased, Sukhbir, was married, while the others were unmarried.

stories.title: Ankit Baliyan murder case:2 Sonipat shooters killed in encounter; over 20 rounds fired, ₹50,000 reward on each
stories.summary: UP Police killed two shooters in an encounter in the Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan murder case. Police identified them as Sumit and Mohit, both residents of Sonipat. A ₹50,000 reward had been announced for each, and they were allegedly linked to the Gogi gang. Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said the two shooters were fleeing towards Sonipat on a motorcycle. Acting on a tip-off, police surrounded them on Monday morning. Fearing arrest, the suspects opened fire. Police retaliated, leading to around 20 rounds being fired from both sides. Sumit and Mohit were shot during the encounter. Police took them to hospital, where doctors declared them dead. The encounter took place in the Industrial police station area. According to police, the two men, along with two other accomplices, had allegedly shot dead Ankit outside a gym five days ago. The other two suspects, Satyam and Aryan, are still absconding. Meanwhile, after the encounter, the singer’s father, Satyaveer, told Dainik Bhaskar: “We have received half justice. Now we are fully hopeful that we will get complete justice. We had hope earlier too, but it was gradually fading. Shoot the others too; only then will we feel satisfied. Our trust in the police and Yogi ji has increased now. If no action had been taken today, our trust would have been broken. Half of the justice is still pending.” See the pictures related to the encounter… Ankit’s father says, ‘We have received only half justice; arrest other two accused too’ Ankit’s father, Satbir, told Dainik Bhaskar, “We have received half justice so far. Now we hope we will get complete justice. Earlier, our hope was gradually fading. The other two accused should also be dealt with; only then will we feel satisfied. Our trust in the police and Yogi ji has increased now. It has been 5–6 days. If no action had been taken today, our trust would have been broken. Half of the justice is still pending.” Read how the encounter unfolded… Barricading continued throughout the night after Ankit Baliyan’s murder Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that after the murder of popular Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan, the SWAT team, surveillance unit, all SHOs, ASPs and COs of the city and Kairana were deployed to crack the case. Special barricading and vehicle checks were ordered across the district from midnight until 6 am to trace the accused. Suspects spotted at 4 am, opened fire at police when stopped According to the SP, suspects riding a motorcycle were spotted coming from the Karnal side at around 4 am. Police teams were immediately alerted. When SHO Dharmendra Gautam, who was checking vehicles at Madra bridge, tried to stop them, the suspects opened fire at the police, shattering the vehicle’s windscreen. Several police teams arrived after wireless alert Following the firing, police immediately issued an alert over the wireless network. The SWAT team, surveillance officer, SHO, ASP, CO City and CO Kairana then reached the spot. During the police cordon, the suspects changed the motorcycle’s route and tried to escape. Both suspects injured in retaliatory firing In the police response, Sumit and Mohit sustained serious gunshot injuries. Police took both of them to the hospital for treatment, where doctors declared them dead. According to police, both suspects suffered more than 20 gunshot wounds. After the encounter, police took control of the site and began an investigation. Weapons and other items recovered from the spot SP Narendra Pratap Singh said the two suspects killed in the encounter were involved in Ankit Baliyan’s murder. Police recovered weapons and other items from the scene. Investigators are now examining the recovered items and other evidence found at the site. Ankit was shot as soon as he came out of the gym. Here is the full case… In Shamli, attackers fired 18 rounds at 32-year-old YouTuber and Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan. He collapsed on the road after being hit by five bullets in the head and abdomen. Police took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Angry over the incident, local people blocked the road demanding the attackers’ arrest. Ankit’s mother sat on the road holding his body in her lap. ADG Meerut Zone Bhanu Bhaskar and DIG Saharanpur Range Abhishek Singh reached Shamli. The officers spoke to Ankit’s father and got the roadblock cleared. Just an hour before his murder, Ankit had posted a song on Instagram in which he was seen sitting in a car and singing, ‘Murder maar denge sadak ke upar’. Ankit often made songs about gun culture. His song ‘Bhari court mein goli marenge’ was released on 15 February 2023 and was later banned. He subsequently became well known in the Haryanvi music industry. Meanwhile, on Thursday, a gang calling itself the Haryana-based ‘Gogi Group’ claimed responsibility for the murder. A person from Sonipat named Bholu Shahpuriya, who is allegedly linked to the gang, shared a post on Instagram saying that Ankit supported their enemies and had made a song about an incident involving their ‘Gogi bhai’. He said Ankit had received the consequences. Later that evening, singer-actor Bhupendra Dhingra posted a video on his Instagram account claiming that he had a dispute with Ankit at the gym and had then called shooters to have him killed. Investigation reveals four shooters were involved in the murder The police investigation has revealed that four shooters carried out Ankit Baliyan’s murder. Of them, Sumit and Mohit were killed in the encounter. The two other alleged shooters, Satyam and Aryan, are now on the police’s radar. Following the deaths of Sumit and Mohit, police teams are searching for Satyam and Aryan. Separate teams are conducting raids at possible hideouts to arrest them. Police are also investigating the route the two suspects took after the murder and where they are currently hiding.

stories.title: Yamuna Expressway crash kills 4:Truck breaks divider, collides with car in opposite lane; bodies stuck to seats
stories.summary: A horrific accident occurred on the Yamuna Expressway in Jewar, Greater Noida, at around 11 p.m. on Sunday. A speeding truck went out of control, broke through the divider, and landed in the opposite lane. It then collided with a car coming from the opposite direction. Four people traveling in the car died on the spot. The accident took place in the Jewar police station area. The collision was so severe that the car was badly damaged. The bodies became stuck to the seats. As soon as they received the information, the Jewar police and rescue team reached the spot. The police cut open the doors to pull out the people trapped inside the damaged vehicles. First, take a look at the three pictures... Long traffic jam on the expressway Traffic came to a standstill on the Yamuna Expressway after the accident. Long queues of vehicles formed on both sides. The police and rescue teams began removing the damaged vehicles to restore traffic flow. Victims' identities not known Police have sent all four bodies for post-mortem examination. As of the time of writing, the deceased had not been identified. Police are working to establish their identities. The preliminary investigation suggests that the accident was caused by the truck going out of control. However, an investigation is underway to determine why the truck lost control.

stories.title: 4 Nishad Party MLAs put up BJP leaders’ photos:Sanjay Nishad angry, says 'ashamed to put party flag; will rethink tickets'
stories.summary: 4 MLAs of the Nishad Party have put up pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on their social media accounts. However, both the name and the flag of the Nishad Party are missing. The party's national president, Dr. Sanjay Nishad, says, "Some MLAs of my party feel ashamed to display their own flag and banner. They do not attend party meetings. We will have to think before giving tickets to such leaders again." The MLAs with whom Sanjay Nishad is upset include Anil Kumar Tripathi, MLA from the Mehdawal seat in Sant Kabir Nagar; Rishi Tripathi from the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj; Vivekanand Pandey from the Khadda seat in Kushinagar; and Ramesh Singh from the Shahganj seat in Jaunpur. First, know how many total MLAs the Nishad Party has in UP In the 2022 UP Assembly elections, the Nishad Party was in an alliance with the BJP. It was allotted 16 seats. There was an agreement of two types regarding these: Now know those MLAs who are not promoting the Nishad Party Nishad Party MLA Anil Kumar Tripathi has been an active worker of the BJP. In the 2022 assembly elections, he was preparing to contest on a BJP ticket. However, the seat went to the Nishad Party's quota in the alliance. Following this, Anil Tripathi contested the election from the Nishad Party and won. His 4.5-year tenure as an MLA has been completed. Now, only the last 6 months remain. However, there is no mention of the Nishad Party in Anil Tripathi's Facebook page bio. The cover of his Facebook page features a picture of all the MLAs sitting in front of the Vidhan Sabha. MLA said - My car has flags of both parties MLA Anil Tripathi says - 'Nishad Party and BJP are alliance partners. My car has flags of both parties. I attend the programs and meetings of both the Nishad Party and the BJP. I actively participate in every program of Dr. Sanjay Nishad's son, Praveen Nishad. I have been the leader of the Nishad Party's legislative party for three years. This is the result of Dr. Sanjay Nishad's trust.' Before contesting the 2022 elections, MLA Rishi Tripathi was active in the BJP organization. He served as the district general secretary. Under the alliance, this seat went to the Nishad Party. Compelled by circumstances, Rishi Tripathi had to join the Nishad Party. Rishi Tripathi has a picture with Home Minister Amit Shah as his Facebook profile cover. A BJP flag is often seen on his vehicle. He is also frequently spotted at BJP meetings. In fact, when MLAs were assigned to the booth campaign, he played an active role as well. 'Technically, I am a Nishad Party MLA' Rishi Tripathi says, ‘Technically, I am a Nishad Party MLA. I have been a General Secretary in the BJP organization. Amit Shah is the Home Minister of the country. The BJP and the Nishad Party are alliance partners. Nishad Party workers had come to meet me regarding the reservation issue. I definitely attend any meeting or program information I receive from the BJP-Nishad Party.’ Nishad Party MLA Vivekanand Pandey is also a person who came from the BJP organization. His Facebook page cover features a picture of him taken with PM Modi. Meanwhile, in his profile picture, he is seen with CM Yogi. However, both the BJP and Nishad Party flags are displayed on his vehicle. 'Both parties in the alliance are like elder and younger brothers' Vivekananda Pandey told Dainik Bhaskar, ''Both parties in the alliance are like elder and younger brothers. I recently attended the party's foundation day. I participate in every event of both parties. I am a person associated with the BJP organization, but I was elected as an MLA from the Nishad Party. For me, the leaders of both parties are worthy of respect.'' Nishad Party MLA Ramesh Singh is currently the leader of the legislative party. His father, Kunwar Haribansh Singh, has been an MP from Pratapgarh Lok Sabha constituency representing Apna Dal (S). Ramesh Singh's Facebook page cover features pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, BJP National General Secretary Nitin Nabin, UP BJP President Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and both Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya. Ramesh Singh is also seen with CM Yogi in his profile picture. 'I keep meeting the CM for development works' MLA Ramesh Singh said, 'The Nishad Party flag is on my car. I will continue to contest elections from the Nishad Party in the future as well. Yogi Adityanath is our CM. We are an ally of the government. Due to development works in the region, I often meet the CM. We provide full support-physically, mentally, and financially-to every conference and program of our party.' Only one MLA who left BJP, stays honestly with the Nishad Party Vipul Dubey, the MLA from the Gyanpur seat of Bhadohi (Sant Ravidas Nagar) district, also left the BJP and joined the Nishad Party before the 2022 elections. He entered active politics in 2015 by winning the Gram Pradhan election. In 2021, he lost the District Panchayat member election. Then, the Nishad Party denied a ticket to its incumbent MLA Vijay Mishra and fielded him instead, and he won. Vipul Dubey has put up a picture of himself with workers wearing Nishad Party caps on the cover of his Facebook page. In his profile picture, he is alone.

stories.title: SP may contest 328 seats in UP polls:Preparing to give 75 seats to Congress; SP candidates may contest some of them
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) may field candidates on 328 seats in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, while 75 seats are being considered for the Congress. However, the Congress is claiming a larger share, seeking to contest around 200 seats. In this situation, what will be the middle ground? Both parties have remained silent on this so far. SP sources say the proposal to give 75 seats to the Congress is under consideration. However, on several of these seats, the Congress could contest under its own symbol while the candidates may be from the SP. Akhilesh Yadav has already hinted at such an arrangement. There is a reason behind this strategy. The Congress still lacks a strong organisational base on the ground in UP, while the state has remained the centre of the SP's politics. The SP recently demonstrated the strength of its organisation during the SIR exercise. Rahul was at the centre in Lok Sabha polls, Akhilesh will lead the Assembly campaign. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Ram Gopal Yadav led the SP's side in the coordination committee, with Udaiveer Singh also playing an important role. Asked how many seats each party would contest in the Assembly elections, Udaiveer said the final decision would be taken by the respective high commands. "Which party will get how many seats in UP will be decided by the high command. Senior leaders continue to meet at the party level and at their residences. The situation during the Lok Sabha elections was completely different from that of the Assembly elections. Rahul Gandhi was kept at the centre of the Lok Sabha campaign. The 2027 election will be fought with Akhilesh Yadav at the centre," he said. On the Congress getting 106 seats in the 2017 Assembly elections, Udaiveer said, "That is history. Circumstances do not remain the same." Congress co-in-charge for UP, Shyam Kumar Daulat, said the alliance in UP was certain, but the final decision on seat-sharing would be taken by Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi. "Both the SP and Congress should have faith in the central leadership," he said. So, understand how the math of 75 seats was calculated SP organization officials say - Congress was given 17 seats in the Lok Sabha elections. One Lok Sabha constituency consists of 5 assembly seats. By this formula, Congress could get 85 seats. According to simple math, 1 assembly seat can be given in every district. But there is a catch here. There are many districts where Congress has no base at all. For example, Mainpuri, Etah, Etawah, Farrukhabad, Firozabad, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Mau, Rampur, and Moradabad. In such a situation, on what basis will seats be given to them in these districts? In such cases, it could be managed by giving Congress more than one seat in certain other districts. According to the SP's formula, some of the potential seats that may go to Congress could be as follows- Congress may also get seats where SP has not been particularly successful. These could include seats in Western UP like Noida, Hapur, Ghaziabad, Bulandshahr, Mathura, and Agra. The BJP has held these for a long time. Additionally, due to the influence of State President Ajay Rai, seats around Varanasi may also go to Congress. These include Rohaniya, Varanasi North, South, Cantt, and Sevapuri. The final talks on seats are to be held in September. Prior to this, the INDIA bloc meeting was held in Delhi on 8 June. At that time, it was decided to hold a meeting once every two months. According to this, the meeting was supposed to take place in August. However, due to the Parliament session and disruptions in the month of August, this meeting could not be held. SP has finalized 150 candidates so far. This includes 100 names who won in the 2022 assembly elections. 45 new faces are included. The official list is yet to be released. 3 reasons are being cited for giving fewer seats to Congress- 1- SP does not want to repeat the mistake of 2017 In the 2017 elections, there was an alliance between SP and Congress. Congress was allocated 105 seats. However, there were 9 seats where, due to the breakdown of the alliance, candidates from both SP and Congress contested against each other. In this way, Congress contested a total of 114 seats. Meanwhile, SP contested 311 seats. Congress could only win 7 seats. 2- SP itself wants Dalit-Adivasi candidates on 100 seats under the PDA factor SP is entering the election with the PDA factor. It wants to field Dalit and Adivasi candidates on about 100 seats itself. These will be separate from the reserved seats. This is also why SP is preparing to contest more seats. 3- Losses due to delays in Bihar The Mahagathbandhan suffered a major loss in Bihar due to delays in seat sharing and contesting seats where Congress had a weak hold. SP wants to avoid this mistake in UP and make decisions in time. SP wants to give Congress only those seats, and only as many, where it has real strength, so that the victory of the alliance can be ensured. Why is Congress forced to accept SP's conditions? In the 2022 assembly elections, Congress got only 2 seats by fighting alone. The 6 seats won in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections were possible only because of the alliance with SP. The Congress leadership will not take the risk of losing like in 2022 by fighting alone, so it will have to agree to SP's conditions. Even if the state unit opposes it, the final decision will be taken by Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav only. At the same time, SP also needs Congress's support to prevent the fragmentation of Muslim voters and to avoid a direct contest.

stories.title: Singer’s wife says, ‘Yogi ji answered in his own style’:After 2 shooters killed in encounter, she says others should meet the same fate too
stories.summary: “The process of getting justice has begun. We have received some relief. CM Yogi ji has responded in his own style and shown what he can do. This is why he is considered so strict on law and order. He took this case very seriously. But the job is not over yet. It will be complete only when everyone involved in this case meets the same fate.” Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema told Dainik Bhaskar this after shooters Sumit and Mohit were killed in an encounter. His sister Reena said, “The deaths of two accused have brought some satisfaction. But we will not be fully satisfied until those behind the entire case are eliminated.” On Monday morning, Shamli police killed the singer’s two alleged shooters, Sumit (24) and Mohit (22), in an encounter. Before the encounter, Seema had said that she would set herself on fire if her husband did not get justice. She had said officials had asked for two days’ time, but no arrests had been made. According to her, they had only given assurances, and the police response appeared sluggish. Read the singer’s wife’s first interview after the encounter Question: Did you not trust the police earlier, when you said you would protest outside CM’s residence? Answer: Twenty rounds were fired in the middle of the city. There must have been, or should have been, police around the area. Despite this, so many shots were fired in broad daylight. So, it was natural to raise questions about the law and order situation. Question: At that time, were there also suspicions about some police personnel? Answer: There was no suspicion that police personnel were involved in the murder. However, they did not handle the case properly. Later, though, the police did a good job. The action has now started on a positive note. Question: It is being said that the shooters were tracking Ankit’s location by installing GPS device in his car? Answer: We come from a rural background and do not know much about things like GPS. If someone installs a GPS device in a car, how would we know? If we had even the slightest hint, we would not have allowed Ankit to go to the gym alone. We would have asked for security or done something else. Neither Ankit nor we had any idea that someone was after his life. Question: Do you also need security? Answer: I feel a little unsafe. We have lost a member of our family. All our faces have also become public. We are afraid that something might happen to us too. But we trust the police administration and CM Yogi ji. We hope that we will remain safe under their protection. Sister says, ‘There was negligence by the police and administration too’ Ankit’s sister Reena said, “What can a sister say after losing her brother? If the criminals’ surveillance had been detected earlier, Ankit’s life could have been saved. There was negligence by the police and administration too. If barricading had been put in place immediately after the incident, the criminals could have been stopped from escaping.” Now, see what the wife says further; Seema said Ankit had dedicated his entire life to sports. He started playing kabaddi at the age of 12–13, and by the age of 17–18, he had represented Delhi at district, state and national levels. He suffered a serious spinal cord injury, with a completely displaced disc, and underwent major surgery. Doctors advised him not to continue playing sports. He then started a business but was unsuccessful. Later, he moved into modelling, where he also faced many struggles. “We started this work together. We would plan everything together, which song to do, how it should be prepared, what the music should sound like and how the video should be made,” Seema said. The couple selected songs together and then got the videos made. They did not have enough money to release a song every month. It took them nearly two to three months to produce one song. Seema invested her own money in the work and also suffered significant losses. Ankit gave several hit songs to the Haryanvi music industry and worked very hard, but he never reached the position he had hoped for. According to Seema, nepotism is widespread in the industry. Seema and Ankit met during kabaddi coaching. Seema’s brother was Ankit’s coach. ‘If Ankit had received any threat, he would definitely have told me’ Ankit’s wife Seema denied any old dispute or threat. She said, “If Ankit had received any kind of threat, he would definitely have told me. We shared everything. I also spoke to Ankit at the gym on the day he was killed. We initially talked about family matters. After that, Ankit told me about his new project. He was discussing a new project with Haryanvi singer Amit Saini Rohtakiya. During the conversation, Ankit said he would call me again in around 10 minutes. After that, the incident happened.” Focused on fitness for 12 years, had not eaten bread for 6 years Ankit had been involved in sports since childhood, so he was very conscious about his health and fitness. For the past 10-12 years, he had devoted himself completely to fitness. His diet was not a normal one; rather, he followed a diet designed for building his body. Ankit had not eaten even roti for the past 5-6 years. He ate rice, salad, and lentils in the afternoon. In the morning, he ate oats. In the evening, he had a light meal or fruit. He followed a fixed diet schedule, eating 5-6 times a day. Ankit had prepared himself to a very high level. No model in Haryana had fitness like his. ‘My brother was a kabaddi coach, and that’s how Ankit and I got together’ My relationship with Ankit came through my brother. My brother was Ankit’s kabaddi coach. We met through him and later got married. What I liked most about Ankit was his dedication. After our marriage, I stood by him in everything he did. I had secured my own job before getting married. I have been working as a government teacher in Delhi since 2019, while we got married in 2020. Preparing to contest district panchayat elections, dreamed of building stadium in his village Ankit did not want to limit himself to just singing and modelling. He was preparing to contest the district panchayat elections. His dream was to have a stadium built in his area so that local children could get opportunities to advance. He wanted children from the area to reach the Olympics and the Asian Games. Ankit wanted to do a great deal for the youth. Not even a single singer from the Haryanvi industry reached out Not a single singer, writer, lyricist, or model from the Haryanvi industry contacted our family. No one even came to ask about the family's well-being. I am shocked to see this attitude of the industry. The industry that stands up for artists in songs and makes grand claims did not stand by the family after the murder of one of its own artists. If Ankit had been a Haryanvi artist, perhaps the industry would have rallied around him. But that did not happen in the case of an artist from Uttar Pradesh. My last wish is for a stadium to be built in Ankit's name Seema said, "My husband struggled continuously from childhood until the age of 28-29. He struggled with society and with his health, but despite this, he kept trying to do something good." He wanted to influence young people through fitness so that they would stay healthy. According to him, he did not receive the necessary help or results from the film industry or elsewhere, but he never stopped trying. It is my wish that a stadium be built in this area in Ankit's name so that his memory lives on. Having some means of remembering him would certainly be a good thing. This stadium would not only commemorate Ankit but also keep his dream alive.

stories.title: Father says, ‘My son was set to return as pilot’:Life betrayed him at the threshold of success; died in Kanpur plane crash
stories.summary: Abhishek Pujari's family was expecting him to return as a pilot in five days, but the training aircraft crash in Kanpur on Thursday afternoon (27 Aug) shattered their hopes. His father, Prabhakar Raju Pujari, told Dainik Bhaskar that the family had spoken to Abhishek a day before the accident, when he said, "I'll be coming back on September 2." Prabhakar said, "He had completed 190 hours of training, with only 10 hours remaining. The family was overjoyed that he was returning as a pilot. But everything fell apart in the accident on Thursday afternoon. Just as he was on the threshold of success, life betrayed him." Abhishek's friend Priyanka was also inconsolable. She repeatedly said, "Does anyone leave like this?" Prabhakar arrived in Kanpur from Maharashtra around noon on Friday (28 Aug) along with his wife Shashikala, younger son and electrical engineer Abhinav, mother-in-law Shankari and Abhishek's friend Priyanka. The family will take Abhishek's body with them on Saturday (29 Aug) after the post-mortem. Meanwhile, a team from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) began investigating the crash at 11am on Friday. To determine the cause of the accident, the team secured the aircraft's recorder, which functions like a black box, along with other equipment. People said carrying one's son's funeral bier on one's shoulders is life's greatest burden At the postmortem house in Swaroop Nagar, Kanpur, even the police officers' eyes filled with tears when they saw Abhishek's family members crying uncontrollably. His father, Prabhakar Raju Pujari, mother Shashikala, and grandmother Shankari became distraught as soon as they saw Abhishek's body. Everyone in the family broke down at the postmortem house. Everyone kept saying that carrying one's son's bier on the father's shoulders is life's greatest burden. May God spare anyone from witnessing such a day. Meanwhile, Abhishek Pujari's family refused to have the postmortem conducted on Friday. They said they would take their son's body to Maharashtra. Their flight was scheduled for 6:30 p.m. on Saturday. Following this, postmortem in-charge Vipul Chaturvedi had the body placed in the mortuary. Pilot Sachin Bhatia's skull bones found shattered The postmortem of Sachin Bhatia, the other pilot who lost his life in the accident, was conducted on Friday. A total of 22 injuries were found on his body. He died due to excessive blood loss. The postmortem report found that the bones in his skull were shattered. Seven bones, including those in his chest, arms, and legs, were fractured. Late Saturday evening, Sachin's family arrived in Kanpur from Vadodara (Gujarat) and reached Bhairav Ghat. He was cremated there. He could have survived if the aircraft had not hit the wall Officials involved in the investigation team said that the cause of the accident will become clear only after the inquiry is completed. The preliminary investigation has found that if the aircraft had not collided with the wall, both people might have survived. The aircraft became uncontrollable over Trans Ganga City. The pilot used his judgment and chose a garden along the Ganga for a safe landing. However, the aircraft was damaged after colliding with the cemented boundary wall of a farmhouse, and both occupants died. All these aspects are being investigated. The aircraft fell from a height of 200-250 feet with a blast Garg Aviation Limited's four-seater trainer aircraft, a Tecnam P-2006T, based at Kanpur Cantonment, crashed at 12:10 p.m. on Thursday. It struck a five-foot-high boundary wall near the Ganga Barrage and fell into a field. The aircraft was completely wrecked. Gujarat pilot Sachin Bhatia (29) and trainee Abhishek Pujari (28), a resident of Panvel, Maharashtra, were taken to the hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. According to eyewitnesses, the aircraft was flying at an altitude of around 200-250 feet. It suddenly began wobbling in the air and fell to the ground with a loud bang. The entire aircraft broke apart on impact, and its parts were scattered over a wide area. However, the aircraft did not catch fire. One pilot was trapped near the cockpit, while the other lay seriously injured and covered in blood a short distance away from the aircraft. One of the aircraft's seats also broke off and was thrown outside. A residential settlement is located 1 km from the crash site The residential settlement is about one kilometer from the site where the accident occurred. Villagers said that the aircraft remained in the air for about 4-5 minutes before suddenly crashing. If it had fallen over the settlement, homes and members of the public could have been harmed. The aircraft belonged to Kanpur-based Garg Aviation Flying Training Academy, which was established in 1995. More than 100 people are undergoing pilot training there. The aircraft took off from the flying academy and crashed 39 km away.

stories.title: Brother-sister bond seen at Gorakhpur jail:1,408 meet inmates; sisters say, ‘Come out soon, brother, we’ll cook your favourite dishes’
stories.summary: Raksha Bandhan was celebrated with joy and emotion at Gorakhpur District Jail on Friday (28 Aug), with sisters arriving at the prison to tie rakhis on their brothers and feed them sweets. They also prayed for their early release, creating a festive atmosphere on the jail premises throughout the day. During the occasion, the sisters said, "Brother, come out after being released, and then we will serve you delicious dishes." On the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, 1,113 women, 271 children, and 24 men arrived to meet inmates in 10 shifts from 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The women tied rakhi on the wrists of their brothers imprisoned in the jail. Meanwhile, 24 men arrived to have their rakhi tied by their sisters incarcerated in the jail. A total of 1,408 people met their relatives during the occasion, and an intensely emotional atmosphere could be seen everywhere. Some pictures from the jail Special Arrangements Made from Outside to Inside the Jail The jail administration had made special arrangements for the inmates and their sisters. Tents, chairs, coolers, and clean drinking water had been arranged for the sisters outside the jail so that they would not face any inconvenience in the sun and heat. Special arrangements had also been made inside the jail for smooth meetings. To ensure that no brother's wrist remained bare, the jail administration had arranged free rakhis, sweets, and roli. On the instructions of SSP Dr Kaustubh, additional female and male police personnel had been deployed for security. Jail Superintendent Extended Greetings Jail Superintendent D.K. Pandey and Jailer Kunj Bihari Singh extended Raksha Bandhan greetings and best wishes to all the incarcerated inmates through the prison radio. On this occasion, a medical team led by Dr Vinay Rai, Senior Consultant, was also deployed to deal with any emergency situation. Jail Superintendent D.K. Pandey, Jailer Kunj Bihari Singh, Deputy Jailers Vijay Kumar and Aditya Kumar, Krishnakumari, and other prison staff remained alert throughout the day to ensure security. The prison administration stated that the entire visitation programme was conducted peacefully, with harmony and affection.

stories.title: Cop holds robber despite being hit with stones:Stops chain snatcher in Lucknow; woman ties Rakhi, says, ‘Brother, you saved me’
stories.summary: A miscreant allegedly snatched a woman’s chain in Lucknow as she was on her way to tie a rakhi to her brother on Raksha Bandhan. Police and traffic personnel chased the accused, and a traffic constable caught him, but the man allegedly struck the constable twice on the nose with a brick while trying to escape. Despite sustaining a bleeding injury, the constable held on to the accused until local police arrived and arrested him. The entire incident was captured on CCTV. See 3 pictures... Attacked with a Brick Immediately After Catching the Criminal At around 12:13 p.m. on Friday (28 Aug), the Madiyaon area was crowded due to Raksha Bandhan. A woman, Ruby Kashyap, was on her way to tie a rakhi on her brother. Meanwhile, near Madiyaon Dhala, a criminal pulled a chain from her neck and began to flee. Police and traffic police personnel on duty saw him and began chasing him. After pursuing him for some distance, traffic constable Naveen Chaudhary caught the accused. CCTV footage also shows him apprehending the criminal. After being caught, the accused tried to escape. When he failed to break free, he picked up a brick lying nearby and struck Naveen Chaudhary on the nose twice. His nose began bleeding due to the injury. Did Not Let Go of the Accused Despite Being Injured Despite the attack, Naveen Chaudhary did not allow the accused to escape his grasp. He continued holding him even while injured. Shortly afterward, the local police arrived at the spot, took the accused into custody, and brought him to the police station. Madiyaon Inspector Shivanand Mishra said, “The accused has been arrested. Action is being taken against him under various sections, including chain snatching. The injured constable was taken to Him City Hospital for treatment. Doctors put two stitches on his nose. After treatment, his condition was reported to be normal.” Ruby said ‘The constable fulfilled his duty like a brother’ Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ruby said, “She lives in Chinhat, Lucknow, and was going to her parental home in Sitapur for Raksha Bandhan. She was standing near Madiyaon to catch a bus when a young man suddenly snatched her chain from behind and started running away.” She added, “The traffic police officer present there tried to stop the miscreant. When he ran away quickly, the constable chased him and caught him after going some distance.” Ruby was also accompanied by her two children. After the incident, she reached the police station with the children, where the police officers helped her. Woman tied a rakhi to the constable After the incident, chain-snatching victim Ruby Kashyap tied a rakhi to traffic constable Naveen Chaudhary. She said that she was on her way to tie a rakhi to her brother on Raksha Bandhan but was attacked by a chain snatcher along the way. The constable helped her by catching the miscreant without caring about his own safety. The woman also tied rakhis to the Madiaon police officers and traffic police personnel and praised their action. She had come from Sitapur to tie a rakhi to her brother, who lives at Madiaon Dhala. DCP Traffic Ravina Tyagi said that, impressed by Naveen Chaudhary's bravery, the Police Commissioner has announced a reward of ₹10,000 and a commendation certificate for him. A commendation is also being recommended for his good work.

stories.title: ₹2.5 crore worth of jewellery stolen from retired cop’s home:70 tola gold, diamonds and 5kg silver looted
stories.summary: Thieves allegedly stole gold, silver and diamond jewellery worth around ₹2.5 crore from the house of a retired sub-inspector in Muzaffarnagar while his family was away. The thieves reportedly broke the lock on the main gate before entering the house, where they broke open four rooms and took jewellery from cupboards and trunks, along with a lehenga and gown bought for the newlywed bride. The incident occurred around 11 p.m. late Thursday night (27Aug) in the Budhana area, about 30 kilometers from the district headquarters. Around 10 days ago, the retired sub-inspector had gone to his brother-in-law's house in Shamli with his wife. On Friday morning (28 Aug), neighbors saw that the lock on the main gate had been broken and called to inform them. When they reached home, they discovered that the thieves had taken all the jewelry. Their only son is getting married in November, and they had purchased and stored jewelry for their future daughter-in-law. See pictures of the incident... Here's the full story... Retired police sub-inspector Deshpal Chaudhary's house is located behind the Budhana tehsil office. He retired from the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2017 after serving at the Jhinjhana police station in Shamli. His family consists of his wife, Kusumlata, two daughters, Neetu and Kamini, and a son, Hemant. Both daughters are married. The younger daughter, Kamini, is an advocate in Delhi, while Neetu's husband is posted with the SOG. His son, Hemant, runs a de-addiction centre in Roorkee, Uttarakhand. Hemant is scheduled to get married in Roorkee itself in November. Deshpal said the thieves broke all the locks and ransacked the house Deshpal Chaudhary said that he and his wife had been staying at his brother-in-law's house in Shamli for the past 10 days. Taking advantage of the house being locked, the thieves broke in at night. They first smashed the main door with a hammer and then cut the inner door with a cutter to enter the house. They then broke the locks on the doors of four rooms. After that, they broke open the locks of the cupboards and trunks and stole jewellery purchased for his daughter's wedding. Jewelry for daughters also stolen along with items for son's wedding According to Deshpal, the thieves took around 60 to 70 tolas of gold jewelry, a diamond necklace, approximately 5 kilograms of silver, ₹250,000 in cash, and expensive sarees. The sub-inspector's daughter, Neetu, said, “Her brother's wedding has been scheduled for November.” The thieves also took a lehenga worth around ₹40,000 that had been purchased for the wedding. A gown worth approximately ₹35,000, bought for the bride, was also stolen. In addition to the jewelry kept at both sisters' homes, the thieves also took their parents' jewelry. According to Neetu, goods worth approximately ₹2.5 crore were stolen in total. Police Scanning CCTV Footage The incident came to light on Friday morning. After seeing the door of the house open, neighbor Vinay called Deshpal Chaudhary and informed him. As soon as they received the information, Budhana CO and Kotwali in-charge Subhash Atri reached the spot with a police force. Fingerprint experts collected evidence from the scene. The police are scanning footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby to find clues about the thieves. Budhana CO Gajendra Pal said- The thieves have taken jewelry worth crores. The forensic and dog squad teams have investigated the scene. The family members have been assured that the case will be solved soon and the stolen items will be recovered.

stories.title: Fragrance Park to spread aroma in old Lucknow:Over 50 fragrant plants across 2.3 acres; opens to public on September 1
stories.summary: A 2.3-acre fragrance park has been developed in Lajpat Nagar, opposite the Hussainabad Clock Tower in old Lucknow, featuring more than 50 varieties of aromatic plants, including jasmine, bela, mogra, night-blooming jasmine and tuberose. Developed at a cost of ₹3.41 crore, the park will be inaugurated by Defence Minister and Lucknow MP Rajnath Singh on August 29 and opened to the public from September 1. In old Lucknow, the fragrance of flowers will now attract people amid the historic buildings as well. The plants have been arranged in different sections so that visitors can experience the fragrance of different flowers while walking around. The park also features facilities such as an amphitheatre, a fountain and a jogging track. The LDA will be responsible for its operation and maintenance. See 3 pictures of the Fragrance Park... More than 50 varieties of fragrant plants More than 50 varieties of fragrant plants have been planted in the park. These include juhi, jasmine, bela, mogra, gandhraj, chandni, night-blooming jasmine, Rangoon creeper, day king, green champa, and tuberose. The plants have been arranged in different sections so that visitors can experience the fragrance of different flowers while walking through the park. Experts from NBRI also contributed to the selection of the plants. NBRI is known for the conservation, research, and horticulture of indigenous and exotic plants. Several species of exotic flowers and plants More than 20 species of exotic flowers and plants have been planted in the park. These include camphor, sweet flag, Mexican mint, star jasmine, lemongrass, garlic chives, Vicks plant, Brunfelsia, ixora, fish mint, candy leaf and smoke bush, among many others. The aim is to familiarise people with different species. Several plants used in household and traditional remedies have also been planted in the park. Plants such as tulsi, brahmi, water brahmi, long pepper, curry leaves, bay leaves and lemongrass will also help people learn about their uses. Greenery will be visible in different seasons The park has been designed to ensure flowers and greenery remain throughout the different seasons. This will make it a new attraction for tourists visiting the heritage area of Old Lucknow. It also features facilities such as an amphitheatre, fountain, cafeteria, public toilets, and a jogging track. Ramps and Braille information panels have been provided for people with disabilities and visual impairments. A new attraction to be added to the heritage area Hussainabad's Bara Imambara, Chota Imambara, and Clock Tower are already major attractions for tourists. The Fragrance Park will offer a new option to explore alongside these sites. Here, people will be able to spend time among plants and flowers as well as historic buildings.

stories.title: Lucknow records first swine flu death:SGPGI also reports 8 cases; hospitals on high alert, isolation wards set up
stories.summary: A woman has died of swine flu in Lucknow. The 50-year-old woman from Indiranagar was admitted to Balrampur Hospital. She passed away on Thursday evening. In view of the rising number of swine flu cases, hospitals in Lucknow have been put on alert. Beds have been reserved. Eight cases of swine flu have also been reported at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI). Experts say that swine flu, or the H1N1 virus, can be dangerous for the elderly, young children, and people suffering from serious illnesses. Cases have been increasing these days, so caution is necessary. If symptoms such as a cold, cough, or fever appear, one should self-isolate for at least three days. Regarding the rising number of swine flu cases, a reporter from Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Dr. Rungmei S.K. Marak, head of the Department of Microbiology at the medical institute SGPGI. She answered important questions related to prevention, testing, and treatment. Read the full report... Swine flu testing being conducted at Lucknow's SGPGI Dr. Marak stated that H1N1 testing is available at SGPGI. The test is conducted through RT-PCR. Samples from both OPD and admitted patients are collected for testing. In recent days, eight H1N1-positive cases have been detected so far. Among the admitted patients, there are two men and two women. Meanwhile, the OPD patients include 3 women and 1 man. In addition, cases of COVID-19 and other viruses such as H3N2 and H3N1 have also been reported. According to Dr. Marak, an average of 20 samples are tested daily. Of these, swine flu is the most common suspected infection. Consult a doctor before getting vaccinated Dr. Rungmei SK Marak said that vaccines are available to protect against the flu and influenza. The vaccine can be particularly beneficial for the elderly and patients suffering from serious illnesses. She advised people to consult a doctor and get vaccinated. She said that this vaccine is generally recommended around April. However, those who have not yet been vaccinated this year can still get it after consulting a doctor. Travel with a mask rather than increasing surveillance at airports When asked about increasing contact tracing at airports and railway stations, Dr. Marak said that it could be considered. However, the most important thing is for people traveling to wear masks when they go out. The likelihood of crowds is higher on flights, trains, or buses. In such cases, it would be better to wear an N95 mask. This will help protect not only you but also the people around you. 'There is no need to panic about swine flu' Dr. Shiv Shankar Tripathi of the Department of Emergency Medicine at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow, says that one needs to remain alert about swine flu, but there is no need to panic. Contact a doctor immediately if oxygen levels drop If you experience difficulty breathing or increased breathlessness during a cold or cough, start checking your oxygen level immediately. If the oxygen level falls below 92, consult a doctor. If the oxygen level is below 88, go to the hospital without delay. Dr. Tripathi said that one should not be careless during this period. Focus on keeping the immune system strong. Consume sufficient fluids and maintain a healthy diet. This helps the body fight infections and recover quickly after an illness. What is the alert regarding swine flu in Lucknow? What is swine flu? Swine flu is commonly known as H1N1 flu. It is a type of influenza A virus. It primarily affects the respiratory tract. In 2009, H1N1 spread widely around the world. After that, H1N1 became part of the seasonal flu viruses that spread among humans. Flu resolves in most people, but some individuals are at a higher risk of developing severe illness. Is every fever H1N1? No. Having a fever, cough, and body aches does not necessarily mean you have H1N1. Similar symptoms can also occur with dengue, COVID, and other viral infections. Therefore, it is not advisable to assume that you have H1N1 without testing or a doctor's advice.
