stories.title: Girls tie rakhis to CM Yogi , take autographs:Long queues outside Lucknow jails as sisters meet jailed brothers; buses packed with passengers
stories.summary: Girls tied Rakhi to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at his official residence in Lucknow on Rakshabandhan and also took his autograph. After receiving the Rakhis, Yogi gave the girls chocolates, envelopes containing shagun and a bag each as gifts. He also spoke to the children during the interaction. Girl asks Yogi how to stay focused in the social media era Shreyasi Singh, a student of Sanskriti School who visited the CM’s residence, asked Yogi how young people could stay focused in the age of social media. Yogi replied, A person like me uses a mobile phone as little as possible. If it is absolutely necessary, I barely spend half an hour on it. I would tell all the children in the state to start reading books instead of wasting unnecessary time on mobile phones. See pictures of Raksha Bandhan... Long queues outside jails as sisters visit brothers Meanwhile, long queues of women were seen outside jails across Uttar Pradesh, including in Lucknow, Mathura and Ayodhya. Women arrived at the prisons to tie Rakhi to their brothers who are serving sentences. The Lucknow jail administration arranged cold drinks for the sisters waiting to meet their brothers. Heavy crowds at markets, buses and trains Markets also witnessed heavy crowds as people turned up to buy sweets and Rakhis. Buses and trains were packed with passengers, making it difficult for people to get inside. In some places, families were seen putting children through windows to get them into buses, while many passengers were forced to travel standing. Baba Vishwanath wears Rakhi in Kashi In Varanasi, Baba Vishwanath was made to wear a Raksha Sutra (Rakhi) after the Mangala Aarti on the final day of Shravan. In the evening, Baba Vishwanath will be seated on a swing with his family, allowing devotees to have darshan.

stories.title: Bank manager's wife's mangalsutra stolen in 6 seconds:Thief bites it off while she performs Jalabhishek at Lucknow temple
stories.summary: While offering prayers at the Budheshwar Temple in Lucknow, a woman cut the mangalsutra of a bank manager's wife with her teeth and stole it in just six seconds. The crowd was so large that she did not even realize it had happened. She continued pouring water over the Shivalinga. The woman who cut the mangalsutra also exited the sanctum sanctorum along with her. The incident took place at around 11:43 a.m. on Wednesday in the Para police station area, about 15 kilometers from the district headquarters. CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced. In the footage, the woman can be seen cutting the mangalsutra from the bank manager's wife's neck from behind. The bank manager has filed an online complaint. The accused woman has not yet been identified. Police are working to identify the suspect based on the footage. Details of the case Ashutosh Pandey, a resident of Jankipuram, is a branch manager at HDFC Bank. His wife, Mamta Pandey, had gone to the Budheshwar Temple for darshan on Wednesday afternoon. A large crowd of devotees gathers at the temple during Sawan. On Wednesday, a crowd of devotees had gathered at the temple since morning. The bank manager's wife moved forward in the queue, reached the sanctum, and began offering prayers. While she bent down to pour water during the worship, another woman took advantage of the crowd and cut the mangalsutra from the back of her neck and stole it. The manager's wife did not even realize that her mangalsutra had been stolen. She completed her prayers and left. The accused woman also casually followed her outside. After they became separated from the crowd, she felt that something was missing from her neck. When she checked, the mangalsutra was gone. She reached home and told her husband the entire incident. After this, the husband filed an FIR online. Following the complaint, police began investigating the matter and obtained the CCTV footage from the temple. They then launched a search for the woman. However, her identity has not yet been established. Several incidents have occurred before as well During the month of Sawan, several complaints have emerged of devotees' motorcycles, mobile phones, wallets, mangalsutras, and gold chains being stolen while they were visiting Budheshwar Temple on Wednesdays. Footage of some thefts that took place inside the sanctum has also surfaced. In fact, just as on Mondays, large numbers of devotees visit Budheshwar Mahadev for darshan on Wednesdays as well, and thieves take advantage of this. Ram Ji, a resident of Alambagh, had his gold chain stolen during darshan on Wednesday. On August 12, Nisha, a resident of Dubagga, reported that her gold chain had been stolen from inside the sanctum sanctorum. The chain of Ganesh Kumar Chaubey, a resident of Satyam City, was stolen near the sanctum sanctorum. Sarojini Devi, a resident of Ajgain, and Sonam Pal, a resident of BKT, also reported chain thefts. Veeru Maurya, a resident of Mank Nagar RDSO, had his mobile phone stolen during darshan. On August 11, Asha, a resident of Mank Nagar Kanausi, had her bag slashed and her purse stolen. The purse contained around ₹1,500, important documents, and a gold locket. Complaints were also received about the theft of purses belonging to Ragini Chaurasia, a resident of Budheshwar, and Mamta Yadav, a resident of Fatehganj. Cash stolen from purses and a bike missing from the parking area Around ₹4,300 was stolen from the purse of Atul Pal, a resident of Hind Nagar, and around ₹3,000 from the purse of Madhuri, a resident of Takrohi-Indira Nagar. The purse of Muskan Rawat, a resident of Mayapuram, Para, was also stolen. Earlier, on August 5, a complaint was reported by Rajajipuram resident Rashmi Mishra regarding the theft of her gold locket and chain. Prabhu Dayal, a resident of Munnu Kheda, had arrived at Budheshwar Temple for worship on August 26. During this time, his Passion Pro bike was stolen from outside the temple.

Engineer swept away with car in Mahoba:Fishermen stranded in river; rain hits Lucknow and 14 other cities, alert in 53
stories.summary: Monsoon rains have caused rivers in UP to swell. In Mahoba, heavy rainfall led to a sudden rise in the water level of a local river, submerging low-lying bridges. Near Kali Pahari village, an engineer was swept away by the strong current. Onlookers rescued him using a rope. In Jhansi, torrential rain over the past 48 hours triggered flash floods in the Sukhnai River. Four fishermen who had gone fishing became trapped in the swift current. They climbed a tree along the bank and cried out for help. On receiving information, an SDRF team arrived and rescued all four. In Jhansi itself, a van was swept away in an overflowing drain, but local residents safely pulled out the six occupants using a rope. Following flash floods along the Nepal–Tibet border on Wednesday morning, bodies are washing up in UP. On Thursday, authorities in Maharajganj and Kushinagar retrieved three bodies each from the Gandak (Narayani) River. None of the bodies have been identified so far. Rescue teams are maintaining continuous monitoring. Meanwhile, light rain has been occurring intermittently in 15 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Moradabad, Barabanki, Sitapur, and Sambhal, since Friday morning. Today, the Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 53 cities. Heavy rainfall warnings have been issued for Chandauli, Mirzapur, and Sonbhadra. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist based in Lucknow, stated: “The depression formed over Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and southern UP has brought heavy monsoon rain across the state so far. However, this system is now moving forward, which will put a break on rainfall activity. Rainfall will subside over the next 2–3 days, until 31st August. Following this, rain spells will resume in the first week of September.”

stories.title: Rape accused arrested after encounter in Varanasi:Police shot him after chase near Varuna bridge; accused raped mentally challenged woman
stories.summary: Varanasi police apprehended a man accused of raping a mentally challenged woman in the Cantt police station area. During an encounter, the police shot the accused in retaliatory action. A bullet hit the accused's leg. He was subsequently arrested along the banks of the Varuna River. Injured, Shubham Bharti, son of Ramesh Bharti and a resident of Gilat Bazaar, was taken to Deendayal Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment. After confirming his identity and conducting an inquiry, the police learned that he had raped a woman on Thursday. The accused's criminal history is being investigated. In the Cantonment police station area of Varanasi, a Jharkhand resident filed a case alleging that his sister had been raped. He stated that he lives in a rented house in a colony in the Nadesar area. A restaurant also operates nearby, and he has been constantly troubled by its employees. Besides his mother, he has a sister who is mentally disabled. She cannot speak, and treatment for her speech impairment is ongoing. At around 5:00 p.m. on August 27, his sister went to the terrace. Taking advantage of the opportunity, restaurant employee Shubham Bharti, son of Ramesh and a resident of Chuppepur, Gilt Bazaar, under Shivpur police station, also went there. Shubham grabbed the girl, threatened her and raped her. When the mother went upstairs after not seeing her daughter downstairs for a long time, she caught Shubham. He then managed to flee when he got the opportunity. The police registered a case on the basis of the complaint and began searching for him. On Thursday night, the police team had an encounter with the accused, in which Shubham Bharti, son of Ramesh Bharti and a resident of Gilat Bazaar, was shot. After his arrest, the accused recounted the entire incident, saying that he had been searching for the young woman for several days and committed the rape as soon as he got the opportunity. The police will send him to jail today under the relevant sections.

Sunil is currently the captain of both the North Eastern Railway and Indian Railways kabaddi teams. His appointment as captain of the Indian team has brought joy among NER officials and staff. Sunil works as a junior clerk in the office of the Principal Chief Commercial Manager of North Eastern Railway. Alongside his job, he has remained active in kabaddi and has represented the Railways at national and international levels. He will now be responsible for providing strong leadership to the Indian team at the Asian Games. Railway job, captaincy on the court Sunil Kumar works as a junior clerk in the office of the Principal Chief Commercial Manager of North Eastern Railway. Despite his job, he has continued to pursue the sport. The North Eastern Railway Sports Association provides players with modern sporting facilities, equipment and training. Railway officials say these facilities have also helped improve the players’ performances. Has represented India at Asian Games before Sunil Kumar has previously been part of the Indian kabaddi team at the Asian Games. He was also a member of the Indian team that won the gold medal. He has now been given the responsibility of leading the team at the same major sporting event. As captain, he will be responsible for building coordination among the players and guiding the team on the court. NER celebrates his selection North Eastern Railway officials and sports association members expressed happiness over Sunil’s selection as captain of the Indian kabaddi team. General Manager and NERSA patron Uday Borwankar congratulated him. Chief Administrative Officer/Construction and NERSA president Anuj Mittal, NERSA general secretary Akshay Mishra, kabaddi secretary A.N. Tripathi, assistant sports officer Chandra Vijay Singh, coach Arvind Pandey and other NERSA officials also congratulated Sunil and wished him success. Modern facilities helping railway players The North Eastern Railway Sports Association provides players with modern sporting facilities, equipment and better training. The Railway says these facilities are helping athletes strengthen their preparations and perform better at national and international competitions. Railway players have continued to perform well in various sports. Sunil Kumar’s appointment as captain of the Indian kabaddi team is also being seen as a result of his sporting talent and consistent hard work.

stories.title: ‘He wanted to join the Army like me’:Haryanvi singer’s father urges govt to fulfil its promise; sister says, ‘I tied Rakhi 2 days ago’
stories.summary: 'Yogiji says that if criminals flee from one intersection, they will be gunned down at the next... Sitting in Lucknow and talking won't achieve anything. Show us what you claim by doing it here. If the administration does not live up to its words, we will take the body on the 5th day, no matter what happens. My son wanted to be a soldier like me. When that dream didn't come true, he started making videos. I am proud of him.' This is the pain and anger of Satbir Baliyan, father of Ankit Baliyan. Haryanvi singer Ankit was shot dead while leaving a gym in Shamli on Wednesday (26 August). We spoke to Ankit's entire family. First, look at these 2 pictures... First, understand the case... 32-year-old YouTuber and Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan was murdered outside a gym in Shamli. The attackers fired 18 rounds. He fell on the road after being hit by 5 bullets in the head and stomach. Police took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Angered by the incident, people blocked the road demanding the arrest of the attackers. Ankit's mother sat on the road with his body in her lap. Meerut Zone ADG Bhanu Bhaskar and Saharanpur Range DIG Abhishek Singh reached Shamli. The officers persuaded Ankit's father and got the road cleared at 12 midnight. Ankit had posted a song on his Instagram just an hour before the murder, in which he was seen sitting in a car singing 'Murder maar de sadak ke upar' (Commit murder on the road). Ankit often made songs promoting gun culture. His song 'Bhari court mein goli maarenge' (Will shoot in a crowded court) was released on 15 February, 2023. This song was banned. After this, he became famous in the world of Haryanvi music. Meanwhile, a gang named 'Gogi Group' from Haryana has claimed responsibility for this murder. A person named Bholu Shahpuria, a resident of Sonipat associated with the gang, shared a post on Instagram writing: Ankit used to support our enemies. He had made a song about the incident that happened with our brother Gogi. He has met his fate. Whoever supports our enemies will face the same consequence. On the other hand, on Wednesday evening, singer-actor Bhupendra Dhingra posted a video on his Instagram handle claiming that I had a fight with Ankit Baliyan at the gym, and then I got him killed by calling shooters. Married 6 years ago, wife is a government teacher Ankit Baliyan was a resident of Bantikheda village in Shamli. He lived in Sonipat, Haryana. However, for the past several months, he had been living in his village with his family. His father, Satbir, is a retired soldier, while his mother, Amresh, is a homemaker. Ankit was the youngest of 4 siblings. His elder brother, Rajiv, is not yet married. He is studying MBBS in Kota. His 2 elder sisters, Reena and Ritu, are married. Ankit married Seema 6 years ago. Seema is a government teacher in Delhi. However, Ankit and Seema do not have any children yet. Father said - Ankit wanted to join the Army like me We first spoke to Ankit's father, Satbir. He said - When Ankit passed 12th grade, he thought of joining the Army because I was also in the Army. He used to play Kabaddi. In the meantime, he suffered a back injury, and one of his discs slipped. He underwent surgery, but after that, it was no longer possible for him to join the Army. Ankit got recognition from his very first song After this, he started keeping dogs. He brought a Pakistani dog and earned ₹4-5 lakh. Then he started a business of mobile accessories and LCDs. The work was going well, but he started making videos. The first song he made was 'Court Mein Goli Maarenge'. The song became very popular. People used to come to me to congratulate me. I was proud of Ankit. We should be given justice by killing the murderers Satbir says - There was nothing like extortion or an old dispute. The song 'Court mein goli marunga' (I will shoot in court) was made a long time ago; what does it have to do with today's incident? Apart from the 4 people who have been caught, some big face is involved in this. The kind of pain our family has received, the same should be given to their families by taking action against the murderers. Elder brother said - First grandmother, then brother murdered Ankit's elder brother Rajiv said - There is nothing in this country, only businesses. My grandmother was also murdered in the past, but nothing has happened to date. The accused are sitting right here in the village. This is a country of brokers. They say they will bring 'Ram Rajya', 'Ram Rajya'. What kind of 'Ram Rajya' will they bring by getting everyone killed? Do you know how much drug abuse there is in my village? Half the people have damaged kidneys and livers. The country's economy is running solely on drugs, gutkha, and tobacco. If you eliminate one gang, 10 new ones emerge If you kill one, if you kill two, then 10 gangs stand up. What comes of this? Everyone just goes to sleep in the evening. Whoever had to die, has died. We can also form a gang tomorrow. Why do riots and disturbances happen in this country? It is precisely because the police do not do their job. Sister said - He had come to get Rakhi tied 2 days ago Elder sister Reena said - My brother Ankit had come to get Rakhi tied 2 days ago. He had brought Ghevar. After getting the Rakhi tied, he went to his younger sister. The atmosphere was very good. Whatever happened to my brother, the same should happen to them. We want justice. Meanwhile, mother Amresh says that my son was lying dead. He had gone to the gym like every other day. I don't know who killed him. Whoever has done it, encounter them. Wife, who arrived from Delhi, is inconsolable Upon hearing the news of Ankit's death, his wife Seema reached the village. Seema is devastated by her husband's death. Her mother-in-law and sisters-in-law are trying to console her. Seema mentioned that Ankit mostly stayed in the village. He used to visit me in Delhi every 2-3 days. Wife said - The killers should also be encountered Seema says that there was nothing like prior threats. Everything happened very suddenly. Regarding the fight at the gym, she said that it does not seem like it could have happened. If there had been a fight, he would have definitely told me. I would just say that justice should be served as soon as possible. The killers should be encountered. My husband used to make normal songs. Every singer in Haryana makes these. He would just make songs based on the lyrics provided to him. There was nothing in that which I would stop or comment on. SP Shamli Narendra Pratap Singh says; Our teams are stationed in Haryana-Panipat to solve the case. Investigation is ongoing on all aspects. The case will be solved soon, and the accused will be arrested.

stories.title: Special TET for 62,000 teachers in UP:How is it different from regular TET, and will it affect their jobs?
stories.summary: More than 62,000 government teachers recruited in UP before 2011 will have to take a special TET. None of them could pass the UP TET held in July. Now, they will have at least 6 opportunities to pass the TET by 31 August, 2028. These include 4 opportunities for the special TET conducted by the UP Education Services Selection Commission (UPESSC) and 2 opportunities for the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET). The Supreme Court has made passing the TET mandatory for teachers teaching classes 1 to 8 under the Right to Education Act. The question is, how different will the special TET be from the general TET? If they fail to pass, will it affect their jobs? Read the report… 62,000 working teachers will take the special TET The general TET is for those who want to achieve eligibility to become teachers, whereas the special TET will be for those teachers who are already teaching in government schools but have not yet passed the TET. Only about 62,000 working teachers will be able to apply for the special TET examination. The general TET consists of 150 multiple-choice questions. Candidates from the general category need at least 90 marks to pass, while 82 marks are required for OBC, SC, ST, disabled, and other reserved categories. According to sources associated with the commission, there is a plan to set the passing marks at 82 for all working teachers in the special TET. The examination will consist of 150 questions and a total of 150 marks. The questions may be easier compared to the general TET. There will be two papers, just like the general TET Like the general UP TET, there will be 2 papers in the Special TET as well. Paper-1: This will be for teachers teaching classes 1 to 5. It will include questions on Child Development and Pedagogy, Hindi as the first language, a choice of either English, Urdu, or Sanskrit as the second language, Mathematics, and Environmental Studies. There will be 30 marks worth of questions from each subject. Paper-2: This will be for teachers teaching classes 6 to 8. In this, one will have to choose Child Development and Pedagogy, Hindi as the first language, and either English, Urdu, or Sanskrit as the second language. Apart from this, one subject will have to be chosen from Mathematics-Science or Social Studies or Social Science. There will be 30 marks each for the first three subjects and 60 marks for the last subject. There will be 2 opportunities to pass TET this year 62,000 teachers have 2 opportunities to pass TET by the end of 2026. First- You can apply for the central CTET until 1st September. The exam may be held in September. Pass this. Second- Apply for the UP Education Selection Commission's special TET. Applications will begin in the last week of September or the first fortnight of October. Will I lose my job if I don't pass TET? CBSE conducts CTET every year. The Supreme Court has also directed state governments to conduct TET every 6 months for working teachers. This means that teachers who do not pass the first special TET will get further opportunities. If a teacher is still unable to pass the TET after this, a decision will be made based on their remaining service period. If more than 5 years of service remain, they can be compulsorily retired. On the other hand, if less than 5 years of service remain, their job will be secure, but they will not receive the benefits of promotion. Other teachers will continue to receive the benefits of increased salary through promotions. A promotion can be obtained later upon passing the TET, but the benefit will be applicable from the month of passing the TET, not from a retrospective date. How many teachers were working in UP without TET? 1 lakh 85 thousand 791 teachers teaching from classes 1 to 8 were working without passing the TET in UP. The CTET result was declared in February 2026. About 20 thousand teachers passed it. Meanwhile, more than 1 lakh teachers have passed the UP TET held in July. Some teachers passed both papers. stories.title: New potatoes made with chemicals, not grown in soil:Risking lives for four times the profit; watch how ‘poisonous’ potatoes are produced
stories.summary: Food officials in Uttar Pradesh seized 75 tonnes of ‘new potatoes’ over the past year that had not been freshly harvested but were processed with chemicals to make old potatoes look like new ones. The practice is driven by the huge price difference between old and new potatoes at the beginning of the season. An old potato selling for around ₹20 per kg can fetch up to ₹80 per kg when sold as a new potato. To make these extra profits, a large network has reportedly emerged in western Uttar Pradesh. The practice can pose health risks because chemicals are used to alter the appearance of old potatoes. The Dainik Bhaskar team conducted an investigation to expose the network. Reporters visited locations where the practice allegedly takes place and used a hidden camera to record how old potatoes are processed to look like fresh produce. A Bhaskar reporter posed as a large potato trader and visited cold storage facilities in Sambhal, Bahjoi and Chandausi. These areas in western UP have high potato production and are also reportedly major centres for making the fake ‘new potatoes’. How old potatoes are made to look new in four steps Step 1: Old potatoes are dried Potatoes stored in cold storages for eight to 10 months are taken out and dried for a day or two. This reduces their moisture content. Step 2: Soil is applied to the potatoes A layer of soil is applied to make the potatoes appear freshly harvested. The soil contains selkhadi powder, a mixture containing hydrated magnesium silicate, along with catechu. These materials stick to the surface of the potatoes. Step 3: Different colours of soil are used The soil used comes in three colours — yellow, black and red — to match the type of soil in different potato-growing regions. For example, potatoes supplied to Lucknow are made to resemble those grown in red soil. Black-soil potatoes are prepared for markets in Bundelkhand, while yellow-soil potatoes are supplied to Delhi. Step 4: Ammonia is sprayed on the potatoes Freshly harvested potatoes generally have partially loose skin. To recreate this appearance, ammonia is sprayed over the soil-coated potatoes. The chemical treatment makes the potatoes wet and causes their skins to start peeling, making them look like freshly harvested potatoes. The entire process of converting an old potato into a fake ‘new potato’ takes around eight to 10 hours. How the network operates The investigation team first reached a cold storage on the Sambhal-Bahjoi highway, around 170 km from Meerut. The facility belongs to Congress leader Mushir Khan Tareen. The cold storage's accountant, Abrar Khan, revealed how the potatoes were processed and supplied. Reporter: “I need potatoes. I am a large commission agent and supply potatoes to all the mandis in Lucknow.” Abrar: “You want the same potatoes that come after being coloured?” (Pointing towards the potatoes spread around the facility) “This is the colour being applied. Did you see it? You can get whatever kind of potato you want.” Reporter: “I need potatoes that look absolutely fresh and new.” Abrar: “Yes. We use Rajasthan soil and mix selkhadi powder (a mixture containing hydrated magnesium silicate) in it. Then we spray ammonia. It gives the potatoes a shine. If you want, we can prepare potatoes with yellow or red soil.” Reporter: “I want hill-grown red potatoes. Red potatoes sell in my area.” Abrar: “Fine, we will make red potatoes for you.” Reporter: “Where do you send this produce?” Abrar: “Delhi — Okhla, Ghazipur and Azadpur.” Abrar then took the team to the area where old potatoes were being coated with soil and chemicals to make them look new. Reporter: “Show us how you make new potatoes.” Abrar: (Coating an old potato with soil) “Look at this. The old potato will look like this. It will appear as if it has just come from the field.” ‘A 50-kg bag reaches Delhi for ₹600’ The following day, the team visited DL Cold Storage in Gannaur, around 50 km from Sambhal. Yellow soil was being applied to potatoes there to make them look like new ones. The team met the storage manager, Mahendra Pal. Reporter: “What is the current rate?” Mahendra Pal: “We deliver a 50-kg bag of potatoes to Delhi for ₹600. During the season, it sells at ₹30-35 per kg in retail. Before the season, it can sell for up to ₹80 per kg.” Reporter: “What price will you charge for delivery to Lucknow?” Mahendra Pal: “It will cost ₹1,200 per quintal.” The team then visited the area where old potatoes were being converted into fake new potatoes and spoke to workers. Reporter: “The soil is only on the surface of these potatoes. How will it spread over the entire potato?” Woman worker: “When we put the potatoes into a sack, they move around. The soil then spreads all over them.” The worker demonstrated the process by filling soil-coated potatoes into a sack and showing how the soil spread across the potatoes. Mahendra Pal: “We will give you potatoes with red soil. They will look completely new.” ‘Once the soil sticks, it does not come off easily’ On the third day, the team reached Haji Kamali Cold Storage on the Sambhal-Chandausi road, where potatoes were being coloured. The team met the storage manager, Hanif Khan. Hanif: “Look here. We are preparing the soil to apply to the potatoes.” Reporter: “How do you apply it?” Hanif: “Take this potato and coat it with the soil. The entire layer sticks to it and will come off only when the potato is washed.” Reporter: “The soil will not come off even after the potatoes are put in a sack?” Hanif: “No, it will not. Once it sticks, no matter how much you shake it, it will not come off.” Reporter: “What is mixed into this soil?” Hanif: “There are three types of soil. First is German soil, second is catechu soil and third is Rajasthani soil.” Reporter: “How will you apply this soil to the potatoes?” Hanif: (Throwing the soil over the potatoes) “Once this soil is applied, it will not come off.” Traders exploit the start of the potato season New potatoes from Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Agra, Mainpuri and Hathras usually begin arriving in November. By December, new potatoes from across Uttar Pradesh reach the market. However, traders looking to make higher profits reportedly bring fake new potatoes to the market as early as September. These potatoes are sold on the claim that some farmers harvested their crop early, which is why the new potatoes have arrived before the normal season. This allows them to be sold at significantly higher prices. Fake new potato trade has grown rapidly in three years The practice of selling fake new potatoes has grown rapidly in Uttar Pradesh over the past three years. In 2022, officials seized 2.5 quintals of fake new potatoes in Gorakhpur. By 2025, the quantity seized across Uttar Pradesh had risen to 750 quintals. Over the past three to four years, the trade has reportedly expanded to more than 20 districts in western Uttar Pradesh, where fake new potatoes are allegedly being prepared openly in cold storages. The potatoes are supplied not only across Uttar Pradesh but also to Delhi, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Expert warns of kidney damage from ammonia exposure Lucknow gastroenterologist Dr Mridul Mehrotra said consuming potatoes treated with ammonia could affect the body's acid-base balance and harm kidney function. “If you consume ammonia along with potatoes, it can disturb the body's acid-base balance. This affects the functioning of the kidneys,” he said. He added that the liver converts ammonia into urea. If excessive amounts of urea accumulate in the body, it can damage the nervous system. ‘We will conduct raids through State-level teams’ Vineet Kumar, Assistant Commissioner of the Food Safety Department in Lucknow, said authorities take action whenever they receive information about such practices. “Whenever we receive such information, district- and State-level teams conduct raids. Routine action is also taken by teams at district, divisional and State levels. Samples are collected and sent for testing, following which action is taken against those responsible,” he said. “If there is a complaint from anywhere, we will take action,” Kumar added.

stories.title: BJP may give 80 seats to allies, contest 328 itself:Why RLD, SBSP and Apna Dal matter so much
stories.summary: For the first time in the history of the last 4 elections, the BJP is preparing to contest the fewest number of seats. In the 2027 assembly elections, the BJP may give 75 to 80 out of the 403 assembly seats to its allies. The BJP itself may field candidates on 323 to 328 seats. A consensus in principle has been reached within the organization. BJP National General Secretary Nitin Navin and General Secretary (Organization) BL Santhosh were on a visit to Lucknow on 4 and 5 July. They met with NDA allies at Hotel Taj. Leaders of RLD, Apna Dal (S), SBSP, and Nishad Party said regarding seat sharing: The elections are approaching. If the seat distribution is done a little earlier, there will be no situation of conflict on the ground. We will get time for preparation. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP contested in an alliance with Apna Dal (S) and the Nishad Party. After the elections, SBSP and RLD joined the NDA. Now there are 4 allied parties. The BJP leadership does not want any dissatisfaction regarding seat sharing or for the allies to drift away. Claims on seats: how many could the allies get... RLD- RLD contested 33 seats in alliance with the SP. 8 candidates won. RLD got one more seat in the by-elections. Now the party is staking a claim on about 20 other seats along with its 9 existing seats. Likelihood of getting seats- May get 20 seats. Apna Dal (S)- In the 2022 assembly elections, Apna Dal (S) contested 17 seats. It won 12 seats. It gained one more seat in a by-election. Now, apart from the 13 existing seats, it has staked a claim on 25 additional seats. Likelihood of getting seats- May get 25 seats. SBSP- In 2022, it contested 17 seats in the SP alliance. It won 6 seats. Now, it is preparing for 65 seats. Likelihood of getting seats- May get 15 to 17 seats in the alliance. Nishad Party- In 2022, the party contested 16 seats and won 6 seats. Now, it is staking a claim on 30 seats. Likelihood of getting seats- May get 15 to 18 seats in the alliance. What is the compulsion behind not upsetting the alliance partners? In Western UP, the BJP is completely dependent on the RLD for the Jat vote bank. At the same time, rallies by the Rajbhar and Nishad parties are putting pressure on the BJP to maintain its hold on the extremely backward vote bank in Purvanchal. These alliance partners become crucial to counter the SP's PDA. After the results of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP does not want to take the risk of upsetting its alliance partners. To avoid conflict in seat sharing and to prevent the rebellious attitude of the allies, the BJP is being forced to offer 70 to 90 seats. BJP's Plan - Will appease alliance partners by giving them lost seats The BJP is working on a strategy to retain its existing 258 seats. According to ministers in the Yogi government, out of the 115 seats the BJP lost in 2022, 65 to 70 are 'C' category seats-meaning areas where victory is considered difficult due to social equations. The BJP intends to offer these specific seats, which it lost in 2017 or 2022, to its allies. What is the challenge before the BJP? The RLD contested 33 seats and won 8. In the 25 seats they lost, their candidate was in the number 2 position. In the 8 seats they won, the BJP candidate was in the number 2 position. There is a risk of rebellion when deciding candidates for seats won or lost by narrow margins. Many of the seats in Purvanchal being claimed by the SBSP and the Nishad Party are considered easy wins for the BJP. If these are given to alliance partners, the party will have to manage the resentment of its own leaders there as well. Adjustment of workers to prevent rebellion A special plan has been devised to prevent rebellion in areas where BJP workers' seats will go to alliance partners. Such workers are being assured that they will be sent to the Legislative Council (MLC) or accommodated in political appointments and commissions once the government is formed. Strategy regarding symbols and candidates What do the alliance leaders say? In 2022, our party received 16 seats in the alliance. We are staking our claim on 32 Nishad-dominated seats. This time, we should get about 32 seats, including our previous ones. -Sanjay Nishad, President, Nishad Party and Cabinet Minister, UP Government Our preparations are underway for all 403 seats. However, we will contest only those seats that we get in the alliance. -Om Prakash Rajbhar, President, SBSP and Minister of Panchayati Raj Apna Dal has completed its election preparations. National President Anupriya Patel is holding worker conferences in the districts. Last time, we contested 18 seats. -Ashish Patel, Vice President, Apna Dal and Minister of Technical Education

stories.title: 30,000 letters and rakhis arrive for Banke Bihari:‘Kanha, find a good girl for my son who believes in you’
stories.summary: "Bihari Ji, please call me to your feet only as a married woman (suhagin). Whenever I leave this world to come to you, let me come as a married woman. Please call me to your feet only after I have seen my children get married and have seen the faces of their children. Lord, please help me sell the property I bought in Uttam Nagar. It is causing a lot of trouble. Please get me a nice house in Hauz Khas. Now it is time for Manav's wedding. Please find him a girl who is a devotee of yours, loves the family, and is cheerful." This emotional letter for Kanha in Mathura has been sent by Rajni Sethi. This letter addressed to Banke Bihari ahead of Raksha Bandhan is just one example. So far, more than 30,000 letters and rakhis have reached the temple. Sisters have also sent letters, rice grains (akshat), vermilion (kumkum), chocolates, and offerings (dakshina) along with the rakhis. The temple priests tie these rakhis on the wrist of Lord Banke Bihari and out the accompanying letters aloud. In these letters sent to Banke Bihari, sisters have expressed their thoughts and wishes. Dainik Bhaskar read these letters. In them, some prayed for the well-being of their families, while others wished for jobs. Some prayed to Kanha for a good marriage, a home, and the health of their loved ones. First, see the 3 pictures Now read some special letters... First letter from Jhansi... A sister from Jhansi wrote - Jai Shri Radhe. Shri Kunj Bihari, Shri Haridas. Respectful touch of feet and prostrate obeisance. How are you? We hope you are doing well. Like every year, we are sending you a Rakhi for Rakshabandhan this time as well. There is also a 'tika' (vermilion) in the envelope. Please get the tika applied by Maharaj Ji on our behalf. Please get the Rakhi tied and eat lots of sweets. Everything is going well with your blessings and grace. Please continue to keep your benevolent gaze upon us like this. It must be raining heavily in Vrindavan, and the weather must have become pleasant too. However, both of you, please take care of your health. Please, with your grace, cause some rain here as well. By your grace, the operation of our new temple has begun. Baba Mahadev has been enshrined. This time, for Sawan, a clay idol of Shankarji has also been made. By your grace, there is joy and enthusiasm among all the colony residents. Once again, I bow down at your holy feet. Millions of salutations at the holy feet of all the residents of Braj, at the holy feet of all the devotees, at the holy feet of all the saints, and at the holy feet of Yamuna Maharani. Second Letter - From Rajni Sethi Whenever I come to your feet, may I come as a happily married woman (Suhagan) Rajni Sethi wrote: “My dear Mohan, Radhe-Radhe. I am sending a Rakhi for you and Kishori Ji. Please tie it on your wrist on Rakshabandhan and have one tied on Kishori Ji’s wrist too. What can I offer you when you sustain the entire universe? I have a long list of wishes. Bihariji, when you call me to you, let me come as a suhagin. Let me see my children get married and meet their children before you call me to your feet. Please help me sell my property in Uttam Nagar, which has caused me much trouble, and find me a good house in Hauz Khas. For Manav, find a cheerful girl who believes in you and loves her family. Raghav is in his final year of college; bless him with success. Keep my husband and children healthy, and bless my brother Shiv with work, prosperity, and the return of his stuck money. Help him support his wife and children. Grant me devotion and help me focus on prayer again. When my time comes, call me to you while I am still active, not bedridden. May my husband’s business flourish and may he and my children live long, healthy lives. If I have made any mistakes, forgive me as your younger sister. Radhe-Radhe.” Third Letter- Husband is ill, son has gone astray, my honor is in your hands Mithilesh wrote: My dear Lord, my dear brother Shri Banke Bihari Ji. I am sending you a Rakhi. Bihari Ji, I do not know if I will be able to see you in this lifetime or not. I cannot tell my pain to anyone; I only tell you. You can even hear the sound of the anklets on an ant's feet. Then why is my cry not reaching you? You know the condition of my husband. He is unwell, burdened by heavy debt, and unable to find work. We struggled for years, but now I am losing hope. Even my wedding jewelry is mortgaged. Our reputation is being tarnished from all sides. The greatest pain is being caused by Monu. He is not coming home from Lucknow. I don't know what kind of bad company he has fallen into. People say he is into drugs. He has no regard for us or our reputation. He has become involved in verbal abuse, physical violence, and fighting. I got him medical treatment and even prayed for him, but he has gone astray. Because of him, our younger daughter Shraddha is also being negatively affected. Her father has gone into shock; now Monu neither comes home nor talks to us. I have been defeated in every way. Now you tell me, how is your sister supposed to survive? My honor is now in your hands, Bihari Ji. Please save my honor, Madhav. Millions of salutations at your feet. Fourth Letter- Show me the way; now my age is also slipping by Your loving sister, Radhe-Radhe. Millions of salutations at the feet of Bihari Ji. I hope you are well. By your infinite grace, we are all doing well too. Heartiest congratulations to you and Radharani on Rakshabandhan. I am sending a Rakhi for you and Radharani. Please tie it on your wrist on Rakshabandhan and call me to Vrindavan. By your grace, everything is going well at work. I had always wished to find a way to join the State Administrative Service, but I am getting older and unable to study. Now, please show me the path you feel is right for me. I know you will always wish for my well-being. So, please do what is best for me and always shower me with your grace and love. Please call me to Vrindavan soon. Lots of love to you and Radharani. Radhe-Radhe. Now, know where these letters are coming from? Sevayat Shri Nath Goswami says that there are many sisters who do not have brothers. They consider Lord Banke Bihari as their brother and send rakhis to him. Some sisters are sending rakhis via post or courier, while many are reaching the temple in Vrindavan for darshan and tying the rakhis there themselves. Women tie rakhis to Bihariji on the temple railing. Along with this, they also express their devotion by showing him offerings (prasad) from a distance. Demand for return gifts for sisters Sevayat and historian Acharya Prahlad Ballabh Goswami Maharaj has reiterated an old demand to the temple's high-powered management committee. He stated that a return gift should be sent by the temple management to all the sisters who send rakhis to Banke Bihari. This should include a grace letter (kripa patra) as a blessing from the deity, a message, and prasad as far as possible. This will inform the sisters that their rakhis have reached the right hands, and they will also receive the divine blessings of the deity.

He argues that her maternal instincts do not absolve her from criminal culpability. While prosecutors assert that Clancy's actions were intentional, her defense is focusing on claims of postpartum psychosis.

His Kick channel remains active, so it is still unclear whether Twitch will replace Kick or become another streaming platform for him.

Dale Sanders, 91, completes 2,193-mile Appalachian trail after 71 falls, reclaims oldest hiker record

Once renovated and modernized, this historic structure, which dates back to 1881, will eliminate the need for congressional approval for a new venue. stories.title: Hollywood actor Joel McCrea bought a California ranch in 1933; his family later donated 74 acres
stories.summary: The former ranch of Hollywood star Joel McCrea has been transformed into a haven for wildlife conservation. His family generously donated the estate to establish a wildlife sanctuary and parkland. The area is home to unique native flora and stunning rock formations. Additionally, the historic ranch structures were handed over to local park authorities for ongoing preservation, while educational initiatives and restoration projects thrive on this safeguarded land.

Found in a box, the 600-year-old Ming dynasty carving is now heading to auction, where the rare black-and-green jade dog, the 8.5cm-long carved animal, is expected to fetch up to £10,000.

In 2008, Allen University moved a 1903 house and promised to restore it; now it is being demolished
stories.summary: A historic 1903 house in Columbia, South Carolina, is being demolished nearly 18 years after Allen University moved it two blocks and promised to restore it. The Robert Weston Mance House was linked to generations of Black community and civil rights leaders. After years of neglect, a legal fight over its future and concerns about safety, the city approved its demolition.

Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them

Residents are advised to avoid consuming or selling these unidentified fish until their safety can be verified. Among these is the goonch catfish, locally called Gochita. Anyone who falls ill after eating these fish is urged to seek medical assistance promptly.

As Haakon takes his constitutional oath, Ingrid Alexandra becomes the country’s first adult heir at the time of succession in modern history. If she becomes monarch, she could be Norway’s first reigning queen in over 600 years.

stories.title: A Staten Island deli manager started paying kids for better report cards 3 years ago
stories.summary: A deli manager on Staten Island has sparked a remarkable movement by rewarding children for their academic achievements. This initiative has successfully gathered an impressive $500,000 to procure school supplies, benefiting numerous students. Thousands received fully stocked backpacks just in time for the new school year, showcasing how community backing can elevate a simple idea into a significant educational support system.

stories.summary: In Brighton, Michigan, a remarkable transformation has taken place with a once-neglected 1970s concrete dome home. Acquired in 2023 for $87,000, this property underwent a meticulous renovation, now boasting four bedrooms infused with modern luxury and eco-friendly features. Now on the market for $499,900, its unique design and energy-efficient qualities are captivating buyers in search of distinctive living spaces.

stories.title: A 19-year-old's girlfriend fell onto train tracks; he jumped down to save her and died after...
stories.summary: A nineteen-year-old man lost his life in a tragic act of courage while on his first subway journey. He leaped onto the tracks after his girlfriend stumbled, attempting to save her. Unfortunately, he came into contact with the electric third rail. Now in critical condition, his girlfriend is hospitalized, spurring urgent calls for better safety measures on subway platforms.

In 1944, Polish priest Henry Denis endured Nazi malaria experiments at Dachau; after surviving he...
stories.summary: Father Henry J. Denis emerged from the horrors of Dachau concentration camp and the inhumane medical experiments conducted there. With a steadfast vow to create a shrine to Mary if he survived, he eventually settled in Nebraska, where he honored that promise. The Our Lady of Fatima Shrine, dedicated in August 1956, serves as a powerful symbol of hope and unwavering faith transcending time and geography.

stories.title: WWII-era plane packed into boxes in 1953 moved with its owner for 50 years before restoration
stories.summary: The WACO UPF-7 was used as a primary trainer from 1941, helping prepare pilots through the US government-backed Civilian Pilot Training Program during the World War II era. Retired in 1953, the aircraft was bought by a Florida owner who dismantled and packed it into boxes, carrying the parts through three moves over 50 years. Rediscovered in 2002, it was later restored by RARE Aircraft and returned to airworthy condition before being displayed at the Historic Flight Foundation.

stories.title: In 1943, two Jewish refugees bought a LA mansion for $9,000; 83 yrs later, Villa Aurora has reopened
stories.summary: Villa Aurora, a historic mansion in Pacific Palisades, has reopened after restoration work following the January 2025 Palisades Fire. The house was bought in 1943 for $9,000 by German Jewish writer Lion Feuchtwanger and his wife Marta, who had fled Nazi persecution. It later became a gathering place for artists and intellectuals and an international artist residency.

The controversy began after a video of fish preparation at a Congress event surfaced. Adityanath had accused Rai of duplicity for attending the event. In 1937, Pittsburgh built a 102-foot water tank that doubled as a park lookout
stories.summary: The historic North Park Observation Tower in Pittsburgh is poised to reopen its doors after being closed for years. A comprehensive restoration effort is underway, focusing on the beloved 1937 building and its staircase, while also enhancing the surrounding park area with fresh landscaping and improved accessibility. Funded by a mix of public and private investments, the landmark is anticipated to welcome guests once more by 2027.

stories.title: Punjab health scheme covers 12,467 sepsis treatments worth Rs 51.58 crore
stories.summary: Punjab's health initiative has successfully treated more than 12,000 cases of severe sepsis and septic shock, allocating over fifty-one crore rupees towards essential patient care. Recognizing sepsis promptly is crucial to avert swift organ failure, especially in newborns who are particularly at risk. This scheme ensures that financial limitations do not obstruct access to critical medical services.

stories.summary: An Arkansas bridge demolition failed unexpectedly on October 11, 2016. Explosives weakened the structure, but it did not collapse as planned. Crews then used barges and cables to bring down the aged structure. A new bridge was constructed and opened to traffic in March 2017. The unusual demolition became a memorable part of the bridge's history.

stories.title: UK researchers made a reef from 50 tonnes of coal waste; marine life arrived within 3 weeks
stories.summary: Researchers created an artificial reef from coal-fired power station waste in Poole Bay. Marine life began colonizing the structure almost immediately after its deployment. Adult lobsters and edible crabs reached the reef within three weeks of its placement. The structure attracted schools of pouting and supported reproduction for several species. This experiment showed industrial waste could become a productive marine habitat.

12,000-year-old skeletons in Italy reveal a mother-daughter relationship
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered two skeletons in an embrace within Romito Cave over twelve thousand years ago. Genetic analysis revealed these individuals were both female and closely related, likely mother and daughter. The younger skeleton showed a rare inherited disorder affecting growth and limb development. This finding confirms the existence of genetic diseases in ancient human populations. The discovery also suggests prehistoric communities provided care for individuals with physical limitations.

20 years ago, Dawn Robinson paid $40,000 for 2.4 acres in New Jersey; Middle Township is now trying to take the land for just $7,000 more

She asserts that the seizure does not serve public interest. Ongoing legal proceedings and negotiations haven't resolved the matter, underscoring the potential consequences of eminent domain on marginalized communities.

stories.summary: A groundbreaking 17-year study on Lake 223 in Ontario revealed a complex response to acid rain. While the water chemistry has recovered since the experiment ended, the ecosystem is lagging behind. Fish numbers have not rebounded as hoped, with growth rates remaining low. This underscores the vital message that true ecological healing involves much more than merely restoring chemical balance.

stories.summary: Lance and Lisa Wheeler's Colorado ranch has transformed into a sanctuary for grassland birds, boasting a remarkable doubling in species detection since 2019. The BJP hailed this achievement as a testament to robust economic governance despite global uncertainties. Meanwhile, the Congress raised questions regarding the tangible benefits of this growth for everyday citizens and farmers. They emphasized apprehensions related to youth employment and wealth disparity, igniting a multifaceted debate on economic priorities and public welfare.

stories.title: Ryan Seacrest sells 40-acre Napa Estate for $18.5M after $22M asking price
stories.summary: In a notable real estate move, Ryan Seacrest has sold his stunning Napa Valley estate for eighteen point five million dollars. He skillfully preserved the original dial and hands while integrating new clockworks. This iconic timepiece now proudly graces Cleveland Street again, bridging the city’s rich history with contemporary usability.

stories.title: Indian consulate in UAE issues warning over biometric fraud targeting nationals
stories.summary: Indian nationals in the UAE are warned against unauthorised agents collecting biometric data. Fraudsters exploit fingerprints and facial scans for financial transactions and loans. Misuse of data can lead to financial liabilities, fines, and travel bans. Biometric information should only be submitted at official UAE government facilities. The consulate urges caution and reporting of suspicious activities to authorities.

Conflicts in West Asia impact global energy security and trade routes. India advocates for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve international tensions. The Prime Minister also highlighted drug trafficking as a serious regional threat.

stories.title: SC asks Centre, states why retail acid sale cannot be completely banned to curb attacks
stories.summary: In a push for better protection, the Supreme Court is scrutinizing the government's decision on retail acid sales, responding to demands from acid attack survivors for a full ban on the over-the-counter sale of acids. The court recommended altering sales regulations to permit purchases only by those over fifty years old and requested an update on survivor rehabilitation programs.

stories.title: Kenney, Sikh leader share dais as Bhagwat makes global Hindu call
stories.summary: Mohan Bhagwat, the RSS chief, delivered an inspiring talk in Canada about the significance of Hindus in fostering exemplary communities worldwide. He portrayed India as a guiding light for humanity, focusing on service over supremacy. Bhagwat elaborated that true Hindu identity is independent of language or ritual and called on Indians abroad to act with honesty and purpose, promoting unity through respect for diversity.

stories.title: Sea otters returned to Canada after extinction; now they protect kelp but threaten a prized 'local delicacy'
stories.summary: Sea otters, once nearly extinct due to excessive hunting, have successfully rebounded in British Columbia, playing a crucial role in stabilizing kelp forests by curbing sea urchin overpopulation. However, their increasing numbers have drawn attention to the plight of northern abalone, a critical food source threatened by otter predation. Finding the right balance in conservation strategies is essential to protect both species from growing pressures.

Tamil Nadu seeks directions for Karnataka to clear backlog in water releases. Karnataka claims it is already releasing more than the stipulated quantity.

stories.title: Brazil’s humpback whales make stunning comeback; population surges from just 2,000 to nearly 35,000
stories.summary: Brazil’s humpback whale population has recovered from about 2,000 to nearly 35,000 after commercial whaling pushed the species close to extinction. Protection measures and a global whaling ban helped the whales return to Brazil’s waters. Scientists are now studying their migration, family links and behaviour, while tracking threats from fishing nets, ships and warming seas.

The court underscored that law enforcement must maintain order and adhere to the law. Notices were sent to the Centre, with the case scheduled for a hearing on September tenth, urging both protesters and law enforcement to comply with legal standards.

One mucus type lubricates movement, while another aids firm surface attachment. Defensive secretions and a shell-sealing epiphragm are also produced. This research reveals nature's sophisticated material creation from simple ingredients.

During the review process, some proposed changes were accepted while others were not. In the end, an unresolved issue led to the book's non-release in India, which the author's team acknowledged.

Nasa scientists grew corn in space and found that microgravity changed root and shoot growth
stories.summary: NASA's recent experiments indicate that corn seeds struggle with directional growth in microgravity environments. Without Earth's gravitational cues, the roots and shoots exhibit erratic growth patterns. Similarly, other plants like Arabidopsis thaliana face similar challenges in space. To prepare for longer missions, NASA is actively designing systems to counterbalance the absence of gravity, underscoring the importance of understanding plant behavior for future food cultivation in space.

Clavicular, whose real name is Braden Peters, has built millions of followers through extreme looksmaxxing content and remains a divisive figure because of his controversial statements, behavior and legal troubles.

Clancy is accused of killing her three children in 2023. Her defense says postpartum psychosis affected her ability to understand her actions, while prosecutors argue she planned the killings. The jury will continue deliberations Tuesday.

stories.title: Bihar, Jharkhand settle 25-year Sone water row
stories.summary: Bihar and Jharkhand resolved a 25-year water dispute on Monday. The Sone river agreement was signed in New Delhi with Union Home Minister Amit Shah. This accord will provide irrigation and drinking water to millions of farmers and residents. The pact ensures adequate water for districts in both Bihar and Jharkhand. This agreement permanently resolves long-standing issues concerning water supplies.

Government terms arbitration award on Indus Waters Treaty ‘illegal’
stories.summary: In a decisive move, India has dismissed an arbitration court's ruling related to the Indus Waters Treaty, asserting that the court lacks authority over sovereign matters. This echoes India's previous stance on a similar arbitration award. The Permanent Court of Arbitration urged India to respect its treaty obligations, but India firmly reaffirms that its suspension of treaty enforcement remains effective.

Cumulative rainfall from June to August shows a significant deficit, impacting agricultural sowing and increasing irrigation costs. Strong El Niño conditions are expected to persist, negatively affecting monsoon rainfall patterns. Neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions will not benefit the monsoon this year.

stories.title: Iran president meets PM Modi, seeks help to end war

India supports all efforts to resolve issues peacefully and swiftly. Discussions also covered expanding cooperation in various key sectors. stories.title: At 19, Baylee Laine gave up scholarship and worked two jobs to take in her four younger siblings
stories.summary: At just twenty-one, Baylee Laine made the extraordinary decision to give up her college sports scholarship, dedicating herself instead to raising her four younger siblings. Working two jobs and sometimes sleeping in her legal office, she fought hard for custody. Her inspiring story of love and sacrifice recently captured the hearts of many on social media, where she now shares her life with her adopted siblings and her own daughter.

The project involves the careful removal of outdated metal supports to enhance the tree’s longevity, while modern support systems and improved soil conditions are being implemented, all in preparation for the upcoming 250th anniversary of the United States.

stories.title: Sea creature near Israel can regrow its entire body in just 40 days
stories.summary: Scientists discovered a sea creature with remarkable body rebuilding abilities. The solitary ascidian Polycarpa mytiligera regenerates from cut pieces into new individuals. Researchers observed fragments healing and developing missing structures over forty days. Major organs like the heart and neural complex were rebuilt by the creature. stories.summary: For over thirteen years, music enthusiasts and dedicated volunteers have joined forces to rejuvenate the dunes at Fort Lauderdale Beach, a tradition that began alongside the Tortuga Music Festival in 2013. By planting resilient sea oats, they bolster coastal defenses against storm surges and erosion, while also creating essential nesting grounds for sea turtles. This inspiring initiative exemplifies how large-scale public events can embrace sustainability.

stories.title: Astronomers hear a mysterious cosmic hum linked to strange dark stars from 13 billion years ago
stories.summary: Astronomers may have found a new way to investigate the Universe's first supermassive black holes. A faint gravitational-wave hum detected through pulsars could contain clues about ancient objects. Hypothetical Dark Stars, powered partly by dark matter, could have left black-hole descendants. These ancient black-hole seeds could grow and merge, producing part of the gravitational-wave background.

stories.title: Northern spotted owl once became a symbol of America’s logging wars; now scientists say it is already functionally extinct
stories.summary: The northern spotted owl, once a revered icon of environmental activism, faces dire circumstances as it becomes functionally extinct in numerous regions. A recent study indicates a severe decline in its populations throughout their historical habitat. Factors such as habitat destruction and rampant wildfires have severely impacted the species over the years, while the encroaching barred owl emerges as a formidable threat.

stories.title: 'We never thought they were Muslims': Mohan Bhagwat recalls 1996 Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat recalled the Charkhi Dadri air disaster while speaking in New York. He highlighted RSS volunteers' immediate humanitarian aid to victims of the 1996 mid-air collision. Bhagwat stated volunteers served injured and deceased without considering their religious identity. He emphasized RSS's philosophy of selfless service and not seeking publicity for its actions. The organization's work aims to foster unity and social change through local initiatives.

stories.title: India, Uzbekistan seal long-term uranium supply deal during PM Modi visit
‘Gang’s name similar to someone in UP’: Akhilesh Yadav’s swipe at Yogi Adityanath over Ankit Balyan murder
Salary deductions for Odisha government employees defaulting on alimony
stories.summary: Odisha government will now deduct alimony directly from employee salaries. This order ensures timely financial support for estranged wives and children. Repeated complaints prompted the chief minister to take this stern stance. Court orders will now be enforced through automated salary deductions. This initiative aims to uphold judicial authority and ease family distress.

stories.title: Indian-origin US politician Anand Shah pleads guilty in illegal gambling case; earned $900,000, used it to fund campaign
SC to hear plea tomorrow against anonymous cash donations to political parties
‘If PM Modi respects Constitution, ensure FIR’: Priyanka Gandhi on Kharge stage ‘shuddhikaran’ row
Chicago physicist’s 20-year-old quantum imaging theory gets experimental proof using superconductors
stories.summary: The University of Illinois Chicago’s Dirk Morr proposed a way to create high-resolution quantum images using superconductors two decades ago. A new experiment by researchers in Germany, supported by Morr’s theoretical model, has now produced quantum imaging similar to what he predicted, providing experimental confirmation of his earlier work.

stories.title: In the 1940s, Nevada’s six-week divorce law turned a 1,627-acre ranch into a refuge for women seeking quick divorces; now it is becoming the state’s 28th park
stories.summary: Transforming from a historic divorce haven into a state park, Nevada's Lower Carson Ranch now spans 1,627 acres alongside the Carson River, preserving crucial wildlife habitats. This transition marks the end of 155 years of private ownership, officially now under Nevada State Parks. While development for future public use is underway and access is limited, the community is actively participating in selecting a new name for the park.

stories.title: Nepal seeks to advance electricity import arrangement due to floods
stories.summary: Nepal has requested advance approvals to import electricity from India starting September 2026. This request stems from generation deficits caused by recent flash floods in Nepal. India will provide any additional electricity that Nepal may need during this period. Major cross-border transmission lines remain operational and unaffected by the local damage. India's national grid capacity can absorb the temporary shortfall without disruption.

stories.title: ‘Order of Oliy Darajali Dustlik’: Uzbekistan confers its highest state honour on PM Modi
stories.summary: During his two-day visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the prestigious Order of Oliy Darajali Dustlik, the highest state honor from Uzbekistan. Presented by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, this award highlighted Modi's role in enhancing the strategic partnership between India and Uzbekistan. The leaders engaged in discussions aimed at boosting bilateral cooperation and aligning their developmental goals.

stories.title: Nepal floods revive Bihar’s annual nightmare: Why the state faces flooding every year
PM Modi in Tashkent: India, Uzbekistan agree to strengthen trade, defence and energy ties
stories.summary: In a significant diplomatic move, India and Uzbekistan announced a commitment to enhance cooperation in essential arenas. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged in meaningful talks focusing on shared development aspirations and a robust strategic partnership. Modi's participation in a yoga session underscored their cultural bonds, ahead of his journey to Kyrgyzstan for the upcoming SCO summit.

stories.title: Trump wants 'Lake America'. Canada puts up a 24-foot sign saying otherwise
Russia prepares for ‘massive strikes’ against Ukraine's energy facilities
stories.summary: Amid rising tensions, Russia announced plans for large-scale attacks aimed at Ukraine's energy infrastructure, following strikes on its own civilian areas. A recent attack in Bucha tragically resulted in thirty-seven fatalities. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called out perceived negligence in ammunition storage practices. As these aerial campaigns escalate, the region faces a deepening crisis with infrastructure under relentless assault.

stories.title: ‘No question of bringing back Article 370’: BJP hits out at Mirwaiz Umar Farooq
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur dismissed Mirwaiz Umar Farooq's appeal for the restoration of Article 370, reinforcing that the Parliament's decision to abrogate it was conclusive and confirmed by the Supreme Court. He cautioned against comments that might threaten peace in the Valley, pointing out that Kashmiri youth are now pursuing educational and employment avenues. Thakur also mentioned that Jammu and Kashmir's statehood would be reinstated when the time is right.

stories.title: Texas WWII veteran’s remarkable century is being celebrated with a heartfelt tribute
stories.summary: Weldon Kenneth Bowen, a centenarian and World War II veteran from Texas, is commemorating his 100th birthday in style. The Texas Veterans Land Board has launched a campaign urging individuals to send 100 birthday cards to this distinguished Marine Corps veteran, who selflessly served during the war’s final months and earned the Good Conduct Medal. This effort not only recognizes his service but also celebrates his extraordinary life.

stories.title: NASA tests GPS-free navigation using other satellites and space debris as landmarks
stories.summary: NASA has tested FALCON, a system that lets satellites navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and orbital debris as reference points. During a three-day test, the system autonomously improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects while also calculating the position of NASA’s Starling spacecraft.

stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops
stories.summary: Nepal and Tibet floods have claimed 750 lives and left over 3,000 missing. Rescuers continue operations amid warnings of fresh flooding and difficult conditions. Hundreds are believed trapped in hydropower tunnels, requiring specialized international assistance. India and China are providing crucial support including forensic experts and relief supplies. Infrastructure damage has cut off communities, while aid efforts are ongoing.

stories.title: 1 in 5 food samples fails: Why so few cases end in conviction
NEET-PG 2026 exam at Jaipur centre rescheduled to September 5 over power outage
stories.summary: The NEET-PG 2026 examination at a Jaipur centre was rescheduled for September 5. This decision followed power outages and technical disruptions during the test on Sunday. Nearly 300 candidates were affected by the rescheduling at the Sitapura centre. Aspirants reported repeated computer shutdowns and system failures during the examination. Officials are investigating the technical arrangements and their impact on the exam's fairness.

stories.title: American startup raises $180 million to drill rock over 5km deep to build world's first superhot geothermal plant at 500 °C
stories.summary: Quaise Energy has successfully raised $180 million for its groundbreaking superhot geothermal plant initiative. Utilizing cutting-edge microwave technology, the project vaporizes rock instead of using conventional drill bits. Collaboration with Nabors Industries will provide essential drilling expertise and equipment. The Obsidian Project, located in Oregon, is set to generate 50 MW by 2030, paving the way for a sustainable energy future.

stories.title: A Colombian man struggling to build his own home created Lego-like bricks from recycled plastic
stories.summary: A Colombian architect helped develop Lego-like building blocks made from recycled plastic and rubber to create temporary and permanent homes. The system was used to build shelters for 42 displaced families in Guapi in 2015. Four people could assemble a 40-square-metre house in five days, without using glue, cement or water.

stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln sails past Singapore on way home after gruelling Middle East deployment
stories.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, an aircraft carrier, is heading back home after more than 250 days of supporting operations in the Middle East, recently passing by Singapore. Despite reports of declining crew morale and supply difficulties, US Navy representatives have rejected the idea of a widespread mental health crisis. The ship is expected to stop in Thailand before concluding its journey back to the US.

stories.title: ‘Identify your real enemy’: Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to unite, defend each other
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader urged Gulf rulers to identify their real enemy and confront it. He also called for Muslim unity and mutual defense against external threats. The message comes amid ongoing war and significant economic pressure on Iran. Iranian President dismissed speculation about the leader's health, stating he is healthy. Diplomacy and defense remain Iran's complementary approach to national interests.

stories.title: 'Drug-free India' to 'vocal for local': Key quotes from PM Modi’s 137th Mann Ki Baat
stories.summary: In the latest episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Modi focused on grassroots movements and national initiatives, emphasizing the role of technology in preserving history alongside the importance of a drug-free India. The contributions of women street vendors and sanitation campaigns were also highlighted. The Prime Minister called for greater support for local products as the festive season approaches, encouraging individuals to transform environmental stewardship into thriving businesses.

stories.title: A 55-year-old Missouri official reached the 13,804-foot summit of Wyoming's highest mountain
stories.summary: In a remarkable tale of survival, a Missouri deputy attorney general was found alive after an arduous five-day ordeal on Gannett Peak. Despite achieving his goal of reaching the summit, he faced severe dehydration and confusion near Scott Lake. Fortunately, search teams successfully located him amidst the challenging terrain, and he is now in recovery, expressing heartfelt gratitude to his rescuers for their relentless efforts.

stories.title: Indian-origin teen accused of killing family allegedly used ChatGPT for ‘fantasy stories’
stories.summary: A tutor's alarming visit in Acton, Massachusetts, unveiled a grim double homicide involving a mother and her young son. The police later apprehended the grieving elder sibling in his mother's car nearby. Disturbingly, prosecutors disclosed that the teenager employed AI and ChatGPT to delve into hypothetical murder scenarios, prompting a critical examination of artificial intelligence's influence on harmful behaviors.

stories.title: Billboard removal row: Abhishek Banerjee receives police notice over office scuffle
stories.summary: Billboard removal row: Abhishek Banerjee receives police notice over office scuffle

4.9-magnitude earthquake hits Afghanistan near Hindu Kush
Kim Jong UN shakes up North Korea’s military, dismisses defence minister No Kwang Chol
stories.summary: North Korea has shaken up its military hierarchy by removing the defense minister, a move approved by Kim Jong Un in a recent leadership meeting. This change mirrors advancements at the nation's weapons research center, which has introduced new combat weapon systems. As tensions rise, trilateral military drills involving South Korea, the US, and Japan will carry on, designed to counter North Korea's ongoing nuclear and missile provocations.
