High-level review meet held over proposed 'ARISE' project for coastal projection and climate resilience in Odisha
Fontana, Italian master of colour photography, dies
Risk of lake burst near Nepal disaster site wanes
England’s water network buckles under sudden summer drought
Zimbabwe crash involving church minibus kills 27
US set to take control of major portion of Venezuelan oil wealth
Russia is teaching its children to fight the wars of the future
Trump-Putin-Zelenskyy summit floated in secret Moscow talks: Report
stories.summary: John Ratcliffe, the CIA Director, is advocating for a trilateral summit involving the US, Russia, and Ukraine, with hopes of revitalizing diplomatic negotiations aimed at resolving the ongoing conflict. He recently conferred with Russian intelligence heads to discuss strategies for encouraging President Putin to engage in talks. US officials have updated President Zelenskyy about these ongoing discussions, yet skepticism amongst Ukrainian officials persists regarding Russia's motives amid potential escalations.

stories.title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
stories.summary: Slippages on the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway suggest design issues, not construction defects. Affected stretches will require rebuilding from the ground up, officials stated. A preliminary investigation identified weak, plastic soil as a primary cause. Poor drainage also contributed to the expressway's structural problems. The government awaits a final report on the detailed investigation.

stories.title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
stories.summary: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal may revive their alliance for upcoming Punjab assembly elections. Both parties acknowledge this partnership as their strongest option despite seat-sharing disagreements. Talks have intensified since Prime Minister Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal recently. The BJP seeks a larger seat share and greater government role, reflecting its increased vote share.

stories.title: Congress & BJP clash over Haldwani ‘purification’ row, Rahul seeks FIR
stories.summary: BJP and Congress clashed over allegations of rally venue purification. Rahul Gandhi demanded an FIR, linking it to untouchability practices. BJP rebutted charges, showing organizers' videos and questioning the delay. Organizers stated a hawan followed cleaning for Ramlila, denying BJP links. Both parties exchanged accusations regarding caste divisions and past incidents.

stories.title: August rainfall fails to reduce India's monsoon deficit
stories.summary: India's cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit remains despite August's better-than-expected rains. This deficit has caused a significant acreage gap in kharif crop sowing. Paddy and maize acreage have both reported notable declines compared to last year. Erratic rainfall distribution prevented increased acreage for most kharif crops. Several states, including Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, face substantial rainfall deficits.

stories.title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has issued prohibition orders against two spice companies. Everest Food Products and Laljee Godhoo and Company faced these orders for non-compliance issues. Samples of compounded asafoetida and hing powder did not meet alcohol-soluble extract requirements. Earlier reviews also found violations in other masala products from Everest. These actions highlight ongoing food safety scrutiny within the Indian market.

stories.title: Man on Phuket-B’luru flight tries to hide drugs in overhead panel, held
stories.summary: A passenger flying from Phuket to Bengaluru allegedly tried to hide narcotics. He attempted to conceal thirteen packets of contraband substance in an overhead panel. The passenger then discarded some of the substance into the lavatory bin. Upon landing in Bangalore, customs officials arrested the individual at the aerobridge. Air India Express is cooperating with authorities in the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: BJP president pulls up 3 Delhi MPs for visiting Sajjan Kumar’s house
stories.summary: Nitin Nabin, the BJP president, took disciplinary action against three Delhi MPs who visited the recently deceased Sajjan Kumar's home. Kumar, notorious for his conviction in the anti-Sikh riots, passed away at the age of eighty. This controversial visit comes at a crucial time for the party as they prepare for the Punjab assembly elections.

stories.title: Will work with SCO to free region from terror: PM Modi ahead of summit
stories.summary: On his diplomatic mission to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Modi aims to bolster India's regional aspirations and forge stronger ties. At the SCO summit, he will advocate for collective efforts against terrorism and initiate dialogue on trade and strategic collaboration. This trip underscores India’s dedication to nurturing historical connections and fostering prosperity for all involved nations.

stories.title: FBI lowers hiring bar: Getting services from prostitutes, stealing from employer, bestiality not automatic deal-breakers
An entrepreneur began melting discarded plastic; within three years his startup had built...
stories.summary: In a remarkable daily effort, workers in Mexico convert plastic waste into robust building panels, driving change for impoverished families. Spearheaded by the social enterprise EcoDom, this eco-friendly solution tackles pressing issues of pollution and inadequate housing. Informal waste collectors benefit significantly from improved purchasing deals, and this sustainable model aims to reach broader audiences worldwide, striving to alleviate waste and poverty challenges.

stories.title: Unfinished for nearly 30 years, Hollywood Video’s founder's Oregon mansion is up for $4.7 million
stories.summary: A nearly 52,000-square-foot mansion in West Linn, Oregon, has remained unfinished for almost 30 years and is now listed for $4.7 million. Hollywood Video founder Mark Wattles bought the 32-acre property for $1.25 million in 1994 and spent about $12 million on the project. Two later owners also had plans for the estate, but the mansion was never completed.

stories.title: In 2020, four engineers started Moment Energy in a British Columbia garage; 6 years later...
stories.summary: Moment Energy has launched its most extensive second-life battery manufacturing plant, transforming used electric vehicle batteries into essential energy storage systems. This innovative facility aims to deliver backup power for various crucial facilities across North America. The company has successfully obtained considerable funding and safety certifications, while also planning to broaden its manufacturing operations into Texas.

'If any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he's not Hindu': RSS' Mohan Bhagwat in US
Haunted Drake’s Island with Grade-II listed house, 6.4-acre site, tunnels goes on sale for over £2M
stories.summary: Drake’s Island, a 6.4-acre historic island in Plymouth Sound, Devon, has gone on sale for offers above £2 million. The former military site features a Grade-II listed Governor’s House, underground tunnels, Tudor fortifications and planning consent for a 43-bed hotel. Fortified in the 16th century, the island also has a mysterious, reportedly haunted past.

No one calls UP 'Bimaru' state anymore: CM Yogi inaugurates Rs 305 cr projects in Deoria, says mafia crushed; encephalitis eradicated
stories.summary: Addressing a programme in Deoria, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth ₹305 crore, Adityanath said encephalitis was not merely a disease but reflected what he described as the "sick mindset" of previous Samajwadi Party and Congress governments.

‘No threat to UP from Nepal floods’: State Jal Shakti minister says authorities remain on alert
'We do not want to burden people': Auto, taxi unions oppose CNG hike in Delhi
Haiti gang frees 13 women and children days after raid that killed at least 47 people
stories.summary: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violence impacting children across Haiti. The region has faced numerous fatalities and displacement due to gang activities, although mass abductions are less frequent and often yield unpredictable results for those abducted.

From 'khana bana leti ho' to 'will our lives fit together?' How India's marriage biodata is evolving
Hurricane Katrina forced New Orleans’ Charity Hospital to close in 2005; now it is being transformed into a $500 million medical research hub
stories.summary: The historic Charity Hospital in New Orleans is set to undergo a remarkable transformation into a cutting-edge medical research facility. Spearheaded by Tulane University, this ambitious $500 million project aims to establish a vibrant biomedical innovation hub, with construction kicking off this fall and projected completion by 2029. This redevelopment not only honors the landmark's legacy but also demonstrates a robust commitment to improving healthcare for the Gulf South community.

stories.title: Virginia farmer helps create 2,500-acre wildlife corridor through conservation
stories.summary: Two innovative farmers in Virginia are taking strides to connect wildlife habitats on their private lands. Their commitment to blending agriculture with biodiversity creates crucial corridors for wildlife, allowing seamless movement between expansive protected areas. Backed by various scientific and conservation programs, their initiative protects about 2,500 acres of important terrain, fostering a sustainable environment for diverse species.

stories.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator fined $65,000 for betting on Trump speeches
'Strikes not just near LoC': Ex-Army chief Naravane details how India changed tactics in Op Sindoor
324-million-year-old insect still had swimming paddles
stories.summary: A remarkable fossil unearthed in Texas sheds light on the evolutionary journey of insects transitioning from aquatic to terrestrial life. This ancient species featured paddle-like limbs designed for swimming and additional legs on its abdomen, indicating a semi-aquatic lifestyle in shallow coastal regions. This find is crucial in understanding the slow, gradual adaptations insects underwent over millions of years in their evolutionary history.

‘Do ministers feed their own children expired food?’ Abhijeet Dipke during ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign

Burnham differs from Starmer on assisted dying bill, will skip vote to avoid influencing debate
43-acre Virginia farm behind an inclusive riding programme for people with disabilities listed for $8.4 million
stories.summary: Wheatland Equestrian's historic Virginia property is being sold for approximately $8.4 million. This sale will support the Faith and Family Foundation's long-term mission. The organization began in 1999, offering inclusive equestrian opportunities for all riders. It gained national recognition as a USEF Para-Dressage Center of Excellence. The proceeds will ensure continued services for children and adults with disabilities.

stories.title: ‘UP no longer Bimaru state’: CM Yogi says mafia crushed, encephalitis eradicated; Akhilesh flags gaps
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated the state has shed its "Bimaru" image. He highlighted improvements in healthcare, connectivity, and law and order across Uttar Pradesh. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticized the state's healthcare system. Yadav alleged significant shortages of doctors and paramedical staff in government hospitals. He promised free treatment and medicines for the poor if his party returns to power.

stories.title: Minnesota removed common carp; lake clarity rose nearly 600% afterward
stories.summary: Pickerel Lake, Minnesota, has battled significant water quality and algal bloom problems for decades, primarily due to invasive common carp taking over the shallow waters. After their removal in 2009, the lake underwent a remarkable ecological revival, with water clarity significantly improving and native aquatic plants flourishing once more. This successful restoration highlights the pivotal role of addressing invasive species in revitalizing ecosystems.

stories.title: Viking woman’s clothes preserved by her jewellery for 1,300 years
stories.summary: Danish archaeologists discovered rare Viking textile remains near Varde. Corrosion from jewelry preserved these ancient wool and linen fragments. This discovery offers a rare glimpse into Viking dress from 1,300 years ago. Researchers will analyze the fibers and teeth for more information. Dating the textiles will reveal if ornaments were new or inherited.

stories.title: Aviation pioneer Glenn L. Martin donated over 2,500 acres in 1954, helping create a refuge for migratory birds
stories.summary: A former private hunting preserve now serves as a vital wildlife refuge. This refuge protects tidal marshes and wooded ridges for migratory birds. Established in 1954, it has since expanded significantly in size. The area provides seasonal shelter for waterfowl and nesting grounds for many birds. It also supports mammals, reptiles, and marine species, preserving the bay's natural landscape.

stories.title: 'Not interested right now': Rahul Gandhi on Sonia Gandhi memoir row, cites 'crime' against Kharge
stories.summary: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi declined to comment on the controversy surrounding his mother Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, "Belonging," saying his focus was on the “crime” against party president Mallikarjun Kharge. The remarks came amid a row over the book’s publication and editorial changes that were reportedly rejected by Sonia Gandhi.

stories.title: 'Gang of dacoits': Yogi Adityanath says Akhilesh must apologise for UP 'loot and extortion'
stories.summary: In a harsh rebuke, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath labeled the Samajwadi Party a 'gang of dacoits' for allegedly plundering the state treasury during its rule. He proudly showcased the advancements in development and security achieved during his leadership, drawing sharp contrasts with the chaos of previous administrations. Adityanath also referenced the tragic encephalitis fatalities linked to earlier governments, emphasizing the need for responsible governance.

stories.title: No surrender, no dissent: How six months of war hardened Iran’s leadership
stories.summary: Iran's leadership has appointed hard-line military and security officials to key positions. These moves signal a resistance to US pressure and a crackdown on domestic dissent. The new appointments come as Iran faces prolonged confrontation and economic pressure. Hardliners are tightening their grip around the new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. This consolidation aims to maintain unity and prepare for potential unrest and further conflict.

stories.title: 'Will you suspend them for backstabbing Sikhs?' AAP asks BJP over MPs' visit to Sajjan Kumar's home
McDonald's-backed grants unlock $99.1m for conservation across 100,650 US acres
stories.summary: McDonald's and its partners are actively funding conservation easements throughout the United States. With these grants, they will preserve over 100,000 acres of essential grasslands, providing support for ranching communities and a variety of wildlife. The initiative seeks to secure important habitats and migration paths for numerous species while promoting sustainable practices in beef cattle production.

stories.title: ‘Do you feel you are a lord?’ Bombay HC slams FDA, clears reopening of 5 eateries
A wooden relic that survived the sack of Jerusalem's First Temple was unearthed by archaeologists, now they are finding shocking answers
stories.summary: In a remarkable find, archaeologists uncovered ancient wooden beams from the destruction of Jerusalem's First Temple, dating back over 2,600 years to 586 B.C. These preserved sycamore beams, covered in melted plaster, are believed to have supported the roof of an inner courtyard. By analyzing the growth rings, researchers have accurately dated this crucial archaeological evidence, providing an extraordinary link to Jerusalem's rich and ancient history.

stories.title: Scientists find 1.55 million cubic metres of hidden ice beneath Utah mountain
Present tense, future perfect: Zurich Airport sees 'slower ramp-up' in Noida Airport traffic
stories.summary: The ramp-up of traffic at Noida International Airport is lagging behind expectations, primarily due to the withdrawal of a launch airline and the existing Delhi airport operating under capacity. In its opening month, the new airport managed 104 flights and accommodated 25,000 passengers. Connectivity hurdles and strong competition from Delhi present notable challenges. Despite this, Zurich Airport remains optimistic about the Indian aviation sector's long-term growth outlook.

stories.title: Three forgotten kings may change the accepted timeline of ancient Assyria
stories.summary: Research indicates that ancient Assyrian king lists could have neglected to mention several ephemeral rulers. Evidence points to three monarchs who temporarily ascended the throne amid turbulent political times. Their short reigns might have been intentionally omitted from the official historical timeline, raising questions about the accuracy of Assyria's established chronology.

stories.title: 'Suddhikaran another name for untouchability': Rahul Gandhi accuses BJP, RSS of discrimination against Kharge
Scientists spent 100 years discovering animals, reshaping where we see Earth’s biodiversity hotspots
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study has unveiled that taxonomic advancements have reshaped worldwide biodiversity maps over the last century. While reptile and amphibian diversity has markedly changed, bird and mammal distributions have remained mostly unchanged. Australia and Southeast Asia have been identified as key biodiversity hotspots for these groups. Moreover, factors influencing species richness are also shifting, with precipitation emerging as more crucial.

stories.title: They were digging a sewer when they found gold worth $10.4M
stories.summary: While digging trenches for a new sewage system in Belgium, construction workers stumbled upon an astonishing treasure worth over ten million dollars. This remarkable find consisted of various gold bars and coins. Authorities have secured the precious haul in a high-security federal vault, adhering to Belgian regulations that permit rightful owners a five-year window to claim their treasure.

stories.title: Flyer on Phuket-Bengaluru flight 'tries to hide' drugs in lav overhead panel, held on arrival
Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel thanks India for 'generous support and solidarity' after floods
Nagendra resigned to avoid embarrassment to Congress: DK Shivakumar
stories.summary: B Nagendra has submitted his resignation from the Karnataka cabinet. He cited avoiding embarrassment to the Congress party as his reason. Opposition parties had protested his alleged involvement in an Rs 89 crore scam. Nagendra stated he was voluntarily tendering his resignation after being hurt. The final decision on his resignation will be made after consulting the party high command.

stories.title: In 2002, Alabama architecture students stacked 72,000 worn carpet tiles into the walls of a family home
stories.summary: Students at Rural Studio have transformed donated carpet tiles into the innovative Lucy Carpet House, providing a vital home and prayer space for the Harris family. This initiative is part of a broader effort that has resulted in over 200 projects within Hale County, enabling students to gain hands-on experience while tackling the challenges of affordable housing in rural communities.

stories.title: SC to hear plea seeking mandatory disclosure of ethanol content in petrol on Aug 31
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a petition on August 31 regarding ethanol labelling. The plea seeks mandatory disclosure of ethanol percentages on petrol nozzles. It also requests a public database for vehicle compatibility with ethanol blends. An expert committee will examine E20's real-world impact on vehicles. The court will review policy files supporting the E20 rollout.

stories.title: A former Illinois school is now a $1.35M accessible park with an inclusive playground and splash pad
stories.summary: On August 26, Galesburg proudly unveiled Cooke Park, a fully accessible neighborhood space built on the site of the former Cooke Elementary School. This ambitious $1.352 million project features an inclusive playground and splash pad, showcasing the community's dedication to inclusivity. The ribbon-cutting ceremony was attended by local officials and community leaders, marking a significant partnership between the government and residents.

stories.title: Rakshabandhan in NYC: Zohran Mamdani celebrates with South Asian seniors
stories.summary: During a heartfelt celebration of Rakshabandhan at India Home, NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani emphasized the festival's profound themes of protection, support, and unity. Drawing parallels to the rakhi's significance, he reaffirmed his dedication to ensuring the welfare of all New Yorkers. The mayor commended India Home for nurturing a sense of community and belonging among seniors, encouraging residents to foster these values citywide.

stories.title: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visits Iskcon’s birthplace in New York, joins food distribution drive
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited the New York Iskcon temple during his US tour. He participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless individuals. Bhagwat spoke about Krishna consciousness and its role in overcoming global conflicts. The visit precedes his address to the Indian diaspora at Madison Square Garden. Iskcon aims to promote shared values amid world polarization and conflicts.

stories.title: No escape for Trump in hush money case as US judge blocks bid to shift federal court
US to establish first space academy, expand "far beyond the Moon"
stories.summary: President Trump has taken a monumental step by signing an order to create America's inaugural space academy, designed to elevate the nation's future leaders in space exploration. In a momentous interaction, he engaged with astronauts on the International Space Station. This initiative follows prior plans for lunar missions and commercial ventures, culminating in the recognition of the Artemis II crew with the prestigious Congressional Space Medal of Honour.

stories.title: PM Modi begins four-day Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit for SCO summit; what's on agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. He will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent. Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.

stories.title: An 11,000-year-old statue of a human riding a leopard was found at Karahantepe
'I still struggle': Landlady recalls Saudi man who brought 9/11 hijackers to her office
Pakistani drone detected in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
stories.summary: Security forces are on high alert after a Pakistani drone was detected near the LoC. Military personnel tracked the unmanned aerial vehicle over the Rajouri sector on Friday evening. This incident follows several other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir recently. Security forces have intensified search operations in forward areas to detect any dropped materials. Border monitoring remains active as authorities await further official updates on the situation.

stories.title: Ancient Greeks wore jewellery forged from meteorite iron, study finds
Maya Higa Reveals Engagement: Streamer shares ‘best surprise of my life’; fans quiz Caleb vs FaZe Adapt
stories.summary: Maya Higa has announced her engagement to her longtime partner Caleb, sharing proposal photos and calling it the “best surprise” of her life. Unlike the popular streamer, Caleb maintains a largely private life and does not appear to be a prominent content creator. Higa previously revealed they met through mutual friends at a bar and had been together for about a year by 2023. Fans briefly mistook Caleb for streamer FaZe Adapt.

stories.title: Flash floods put focus on India's glacial lakes
stories.summary: Nepal's alarming glacial lake outburst flood serves as a wake-up call for India, which is home to about 200 vulnerable glacial lakes in the Himalayas. The GLOF incident in Sikkim resulted in severe damage, highlighting the urgency of proactive measures. In response, the Indian government has launched a National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme focused on thorough assessments, continuous monitoring, effective early warnings, and raising awareness within local communities.

stories.title: Government tightens norms for e-cycles, e-bikes
Junk foods will soon have labels warning of high salt, sugar and fat
stories.summary: Junk foods will soon feature prominent red warning labels on their packaging. These labels will highlight high levels of salt, sugar, and fat content. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has agreed to this new regulation. This move aims to help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions. The phased implementation will allow the industry time to adjust product formulations.

stories.title: Clean energy push unfair on developing nations: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Speaking at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, CJI Kant said, “Countries that are finally industrialising are being asked to move rapidly towards renewable power, and are often made to bear the brunt of criticism when they cannot move fast enough.” “The challenge, therefore, is to reconcile the urgency of the clean energy transition with the principles of fairness and shared responsibility that must underpin it,” the CJI said.

stories.title: Nilekani committee seeks public ideas to fix exams
stories.summary: The panel, headed by Infosys co-founder and technology expert Nandan Nilekani, was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month amid heightened scrutiny of the examination system following NEET-UG paper leak controversy and youth protests over alleged lapses in the test’s conduct. It will also look at measures to improve accessibility and inclusion, while factoring in student well-being during the examination process.

stories.title: National Testing Agency gets three senior officers amid exam overhaul
stories.summary: IPS officer Ravi Kumar Singh and IAS officer Prasanna Venkatesh V have been appointed directors at NTA, while Amit Samdariya, a 2016-batch Indian Revenue Service (customs and indirect taxes) officer, will join as joint director. The appointments were cleared through separate personnel ministry orders dated August 27. The personnel ministry has directed all three officers to take charge within three weeks.

stories.title: Sonia memoir row deepens, Congress alleges government pressure
stories.summary: Penguin Random House India has made the decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir, leading to allegations from Congress regarding external pressure to omit references to Modi and China. In response, Penguin emphasized its commitment to editorial integrity and its role in verifying facts. They remain open to publishing the memoir in India, but uncertainties linger surrounding the rights for its release in the country.

stories.title: From Reds to NGOs: RSS weekly expands ‘dimagi Naxal’ label
stories.summary: In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.

stories.title: Nepal floods: Spooked by visuals & reports, tourists cancel bookings, tour operators hit
stories.summary: A Darjeeling couple had planned a 15-day trip to Mansarovar via Kerung in Sept. The Rs 4.4-lakh tour package included permits for entering Tibet. They cancelled the trip after watching videos of Kerung being swept away. Kolkata travel agents Anil Punjabi and Anjani Dhanuka had furrowed brows over rising cancellations even as many sought updates on the safety of other Nepal destinations like Kathmandu, Pokhara, Patan and Lumbini.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Michael Jordan: "You must expect great things of yourself before…"
Who is Milo Yiannopoulos, far-right British commentator, detained by ICE? Former Trump supporter faces deportation
In 2024, a Minnesota dairy began turning manure from more than 2,000 cows into renewable gas
stories.summary: In Minnesota, a pioneering dairy farm is transforming cow manure into ultra-low-carbon fuel for vehicles. This innovative facility processes thousands of gallons of manure each day, producing biomethane that enters interstate natural gas pipelines. By capturing methane—a significant greenhouse gas—before it escapes into the atmosphere, this project not only aids the environment but also provides a vital income stream for local dairy farmers.

stories.title: Las Vegas Valley converted 250 million sq ft of lawn to save water, saving 203 billion gallons
stories.summary: Las Vegas is making headlines for its initiative to remove grass lawns, which has successfully conserved billions of gallons of water. Nevertheless, this environmental strategy has led to a concerning increase in local summer land-surface temperatures, soaring by around 20 degrees Celsius. As a response, water agencies are now promoting the use of water-efficient landscaping and shade trees, and new guidelines prevent grass installations in residential yards.

stories.title: Harmeet Dhillon reacts to Ankit Gupta-YC controversy: American employers cannot discriminate against US citizens
Second excavation phase at Kashmir Buddhist site starts today
Ladakh LG welcomes President’s nod for J&K High Court bench in Ladakh
H-1B loses 60-day grace period as White House office appoves plan: Indian-American entrepreneur says big tech won't lobby against it
Day after Farooq dare, Srinagar MP Mehdi decides to quit Lok Sabha, NC over Article 370
Barron Trump leads reclusive life amid Iran threats, avoids public outings: Report
72-year-old South Korean entered Japan on 15-day visa, lived there 33 years
Tim Curry bought a $650K LA home in 1993; after his death, the $7.5M property found a buyer
stories.summary: Tim Curry’s historic Los Feliz home has come under offer for $7.5 million, just hours after the actor’s death at 80. Curry bought the 1922-built property for $650,000 in 1993 and spent years restoring its original details. The Spanish-inspired residence was later owned by stars including Robert Pattinson, Jim Parsons and Aaron Paul.

stories.title: Jason Arday plagiarism accuser Nathan Cofnas faced doubts over expertise, 'far-right agenda' at Ghent
Indian-origin New York teen and her mother among Americans missing in Nepal: Rashi wanted to do a solo Hindu pilgrimage
Nepal floods: Kathmandu agrees to foreign rescue help after pressure; India acts on its 'request'
'NC’s position no different from BJP': Srinagar MP accepts Farooq Abdullah's challenge, likely to resign
UNCCD concludes COP17 with new drought resilience and land restoration initiatives
stories.summary: The recently concluded UNCCD conference in Mongolia set the stage for enhanced global drought resilience with innovative initiatives. Highlighted was a significant $1.3 billion commitment for land restoration and drought resilience projects. The newly introduced Drought Resilience Index will aid nations in evaluating their strategies, while the Drought Resilience Investment Facility seeks to attract public and private funding for impactful projects, aiming to scale solutions worldwide.

stories.title: Kentucky police officer Asad Zahir claimed he made 2048 Flock searches to track two vehicles for drug investigation. He was tracking his ex-girlfriend
Punjab BJP cracks down on 3 leaders over statements on internal affairs
Uttarakhand CM Dhami announces free bus travel, Pink e-Buses for women on Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: In a significant announcement, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami revealed a series of initiatives aimed at empowering women. Notably, women aged sixty and older will enjoy free travel on Roadways buses. Additionally, ten electric buses in Dehradun are designated as Pink e-Buses for women’s convenience. Moreover, the loan limit for women's self-employment schemes has been raised to Rs 2.

stories.title: A Houston lawyer bought a 15,000-sq-ft mansion listed for $15.5 million just to demolish it
stories.summary: In River Oaks, Houston lawyer Tony Buzbee has bought a mansion primarily for property expansion. Teaming up with Habitat for Humanity, he aims to salvage valuable construction materials, which will provide substantial support—millions of pounds worth—for affordable housing projects. The planned demolition will allow for the development of a larger private garden estate while enhancing his family's legacy through philanthropic efforts.

stories.title: Two resignations, same scam: Why B Nagendra quit Karnataka cabinet again
Yogi Adityanath participates in Snehbandhan programme on Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath led Raksha Bandhan celebrations in Lucknow by participating in the Snehbandhan programme, while Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini marked the festival at Sant Kabir Kutir in Chandigarh, where schoolgirls tied rakhis to him.

stories.title: Punjab: MMSY beneficiaries get post-discharge calls from 104 health helpline
stories.summary: In an effort to enhance patient care, beneficiaries of the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana in Punjab are receiving follow-up communications from the 104 Health Helpline. The objective is to collect valuable feedback concerning their treatment journeys and medications. Such insights enable officials to identify potential post-treatment challenges and gauge satisfaction with healthcare services. Furthermore, the helpline facilitates free medical consultations and information regarding the scheme.

stories.title: Last known location-Hotel Kailash: NRI couple from Canada Dhaval Shah, Megha missing in Nepal
The Dalit enigma: Why Mayawati is going solo in Punjab
stories.summary: Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party will contest Punjab's 2027 elections alone. This move highlights the difficulty of forming a unified Dalit vote bloc. Punjab has India's highest Scheduled Caste population, yet it remains divided. Mainstream parties like AAP and Congress have appealed across caste lines. The Bahujan Samaj Party's gamble tests its ability to unite this diverse electorate.

stories.title: 'Free insulin for life': Amit Shah celebrates Rakshabandhan with girls diagnosed with diabetes
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah marked Raksha Bandhan by spending time with young girls battling Type 1 diabetes, revealing that the government will provide them with free insulin for their lifetimes. This initiative is designed to alleviate the financial stresses of ongoing treatment, showcasing the government's dedication to the health and protection of daughters while building on current measures to manage diabetes among youth nationally.

stories.title: In 2024, a Colorado county paid $34 million for a 650-acre ranch owned for more than a century
stories.summary: In a momentous conservation victory, a historic ranch in Colorado has been designated as protected wilderness. This expansion secures an impressive 530 acres of public land, which local officials successfully purchased through a record-breaking deal two years prior. After being privately held for more than a century, this acquisition ensures the enduring protection of crucial wildlife habitats and public access to the land.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: 320 Indians still missing as Nepal flood death toll rises; Penguin clarifies it's not publishing Sonia Gandhi’s memoir & more
stories.summary: Nepal's devastating floods have left 320 Indian nationals missing and claimed 547 lives. ICIMOD had previously warned of rising Himalayan glacier disaster risks months before the floods. Penguin Random House India denied dropping Sonia Gandhi's memoir over editorial changes. Jio Platforms received Sebi approval for its substantial $3.8 billion IPO. Annamalai questioned the CBFC's clearance for Yash's film Toxic due to its content.

stories.title: NTA gets 3 senior officers amid exam overhaul
Nilekani panel seeks public ideas to fix exam system
stories.summary: The task force, spearheaded by Nandan Nilekani, is actively engaging citizens in discussions for examination reforms set to reshape the entire assessment landscape nationwide. Suggestions are welcomed until September 13 through various channels, aimed at establishing a secure and transparent public examination process. This initiative responds to recent youth protests and controversies surrounding examination integrity.

stories.title: Valmiki scam: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns; breaks down on camera
stories.summary: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigned Friday amid scam allegations. He alleged a conspiracy targeting him as a tribal man. Nagendra had been re-inducted into the cabinet earlier this month. The controversy involves alleged diversion of corporation funds totaling Rs 89.63 crore. Opposition parties had demanded his resignation over the issue.

stories.title: Flock CEO Garrett Langley's address leaked online after he urged Americans to 'compromise' between privacy and safety
Texas farmer loses 600 acres to Google data centre, given just 60 days to leave
stories.summary: In rural Texas, expansive tracts of farmland are increasingly being repurposed for technology ventures, primarily data centers by major tech enterprises. This shift is impacting farmers, especially with resource competition over vital necessities like water. Concerns have been raised by state officials regarding the permanent loss of fertile land, highlighting a significant transition in the region's agricultural landscape.

stories.title: 'Engine issue at 31,000 feet': New Jersey-bound United Airlines flight makes emergency landing in Nevada
Japan killed 14,000+ bears after record attacks; 6 people died despite cull, 8,800 more targeted
stories.summary: Japan is currently grappling with a significant rise in bear conflicts, with incidents surging alarmingly. Conservationists are voicing urgent concerns regarding the extensive culling of endangered bear populations. Factors such as extreme heat and declining food sources are pushing bears into human territories in search of food. While the government’s response aims at curtailing bear numbers, critics label this approach as ineffective.

stories.title: In 1856, one of Northern California’s oldest cattle ranches was established; 170 years later...
stories.summary: In a landmark initiative, the Wildlands Conservancy is set to acquire the AP Ranch in Northern California, establishing an impressive public preserve in Siskiyou County. This strategic 14,177-acre purchase will unite with an existing land reserve, exceeding 20,000 acres in total. The project aims to protect essential wildlife corridors and headwaters within the Scott River watershed, while also facilitating habitat restoration and free recreational access for visitors.

stories.title: 'What exactly needed fact-checking?' Amit Malviya jibes amid Sonia Gandhi memoir row
US judge blocks Trump admin's Anthropic sanctions, calls them unlawful
'21 Indians back, 320 still untraceable': MEA updates on Nepal floods devastation
Green Party leader Zack Polanski calls for data centre freeze in England; says they 'guzzle' energy, water
61% of children in India exposed to one more month of heat stress due to climate change: Study
stories.summary: New research reveals 61 percent of Indian children face extra heat stress annually. Climate change has doubled young children's exposure to dangerous heat levels. This exposure outpaces all other age groups, affecting millions of youngsters. Future warming scenarios project even greater heat stress for Indian children. Developing nations and younger populations bear a disproportionate burden of this threat.

stories.title: Expert’s opinion to HC contradicts govt stand on patented cancer drug
Belgian farmer hasn't irrigated crops in 26 years; soil remains moist just 5-10 cm below surface
stories.summary: Belgium’s Diederik Steyaert has successfully farmed without irrigation for over two decades. His dedication to organic practices ensures that the soil remains healthy and retains moisture efficiently. By eliminating ploughing and incorporating organic matter, Steyaert cultivates robust plants that adapt to stress and drought. This innovative approach showcases vital strategies for addressing agricultural challenges in water-limited environments.

stories.title: In 2017, wildfire neared Roslyn; 9 years later, the town burned 500+ acres to prevent future fires
stories.summary: Washington communities are increasingly implementing prescribed burns as a strategy to mitigate wildfire risks. By imitating natural fire cycles, this method effectively decreases fuel accumulation. Roslyn, a town previously devastated by a wildfire, has embraced this practice extensively, fostering collaboration among various agencies and private landowners. This innovative strategy provides a fresh perspective on coexisting with wildfire threats.

stories.title: Scuffle with police at TMC office: FIRs against Abhishek Banerjee, two others; 13 arrested
After 45 months of observation, capuchins increasingly hunted small animals when fruit became scarce
stories.summary: In Brazil, capuchin monkeys exhibit remarkable adaptability by hunting small animals when fruit supplies dwindle. This shift highlights their versatile omnivorous diet and responsiveness to environmental changes. Interestingly, adult males were observed hunting vertebrates more often than younger females. Furthermore, when alternative food sources were available, the monkeys relied less on hunting, presenting intriguing implications for understanding the dietary evolution of early human ancestors.

stories.title: Creek water DNA helps scientists find Australian frogs thought to have disappeared
1850: 45 sheep came to San Miguel Island; 6,000 followed by 1862
Delhi Police bust Pakistan-backed espionage network, couple arrested on spying charges
Carpenter turned his Niagara Falls home into a colourful religious art landmark
Two vacant Connecticut office buildings will become 286 apartments in a $120 million conversion, reusing 511,000 sq ft instead of tearing them down
stories.summary: Transforming the urban landscape, two idle office buildings in Connecticut are set to be revitalized into vibrant apartments. With a projected budget of $120 million backed by Bank OZK, this redevelopment will introduce 286 loft-style residential units, complete with modern facilities. The project emphasizes the importance of reusing existing properties, offering excellent rail connectivity to surrounding urban centers and major thoroughfares.

stories.title: 'Need overhaul of education system': Dipke on IIT Delhi suicide protest
India’s GLOF panel working on disaster mitigation at 200 high-risk glacial lakes
Concerned over build quality of e-ways, NHs, govt ropes in third party inspection agency
stories.summary: A comprehensive audit of nearly five thousand kilometers of highway projects will be carried out by a third-party inspection agency. Engineers India Ltd has been chosen for these essential quality checks, aiming to rectify issues related to project shortcomings and untimely road failures. The focus will be on expressways along with six-lane and four-lane national highways, ensuring elevated quality standards in infrastructure development.

stories.title: 'Name dates back 400 years': Carney rejects Trump's 'Lake Ontario' name change
Nepal floods swept ​bodies 200km downstream, 3 found in UP
stories.summary: A significant collapse in the Himalayan region caused a seismic disturbance, leading to a violent flood surge that reached Rasuwagadhi at the Nepal-Tibet border within a mere seven minutes. Recovery efforts extended across multiple districts in both Nepal and India. Alarmingly, Nepal’s flood authorities were only informed after the surge had already impacted Bhote Koshi. In response, SMS warnings were promptly issued to those residing along the riverbanks.

stories.title: PM Modi on 4-day visit to Uzbekistan, Kyrgyz Republic - what's on agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1. He will hold talks in Tashkent to strengthen bilateral ties and explore new economic opportunities. Discussions will cover trade, critical minerals, and healthcare cooperation between the nations. In Bishkek, he will attend the SCO Summit and highlight India's priorities. The visit also includes the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

stories.title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT ads in India, over 50 brands on board
stories.summary: From Sept 4, businesses will also get access to a self-serve ChatGPT ads manager, with daily campaign budgets starting at Rs 725, potentially opening the platform to smaller advertisers alongside large brands. An OpenAI spokesperson told TOI that the company expects early advertiser interest across travel, financial services, retail, and health and beauty.

stories.title: Supreme Court issues directions to expedite dowry trials
stories.summary: The bench also directed states/Union territories and high courts to conduct periodic training and sensitisation programmes for judicial officers, police officials, prosecutors, protection officers, counsellors through judicial academies, police training institutions and other appropriate bodies. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said there was a need for time-bound completion of trial in dowry cases and directed the high courts to periodically review pending criminal appeals.

stories.title: India’s petroleum products’ exports surge 8% in July
stories.summary: Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year, while total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70% premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners despite the windfall gains tax govt brought in to ensure adequate domestic stocks.

stories.title: PM Modi to meet Russia's Putin on SCO meeting sidelines
stories.summary: PM Modi’s bilateral with Putin, the first since the Russian President visited India in Dec 2025 for the annual summit, will follow external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Moscow this week for a meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation during which he also called on Putin.

stories.title: Nepal floods: No adverse impact of flash floods on Indian side, says NDRF
stories.summary: NDRF has deployed 20 teams — 11 in UP and nine in Bihar — for evacuation, relief and rescue operations in case these areas experience floods and waterlogging. These include an NDRF team deployed in Kushinagar district, near Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh. In a media briefing, NDRF IG Narendra Bundela said floods have caused massive destruction in Nepal with hundreds of people, including Indian tourists, reported missing.

stories.title: Hours after blocking, X restores account of organisation hosting Bhagwat in New York
stories.summary: The @AheadForum1 handle of American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD Forum) became unavailable Wednesday, three days before Bhagwat’s address at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theatre. Seeking restoration, AHEAD Forun had earlier said that the suspension “may have occurred in error” and its communications promoted “universal peace, oneness, harmony” and interfaith dialogue. No public evidence links X’s action to protests around the programme.

stories.title: BJP cites ‘jhooth ki goonj’ site to hit out at Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: “Rahul’s every lie will be countered with facts. The ‘jhooth ki goonj’ website is exposing every lie of his. The louder propaganda echoes, the faster truth will emerge,” BJP spokesperson Anil Banluni said. Party neta Sudhanshu Trivedi said Rahul is full of frustration and envy vis-a-vis PM Modi, but every lie of his is being exposed.

stories.title: Join sports, playgrounds more important than PlayStation: PM to youth
stories.summary: Speaking at the Khelo India dialogue, he said, “More important than screens are sports centres. More important than PlayStation is the playground. And this will happen only when the youth embrace this approach.” Lamenting India’s absence from almost half of Olympic sports, he said that is why he had announced a talent hunt for children in the 5-15 years age bracket.

stories.title: Govt plans to engage third-party auditor to inspect NHs, e-ways
stories.summary: EIL had earlier carried out the task of third-party quality check during the construction of the Golden Quadrilateral, the country’s first flagship highway development programme under the then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee. In recent years, increased instances of deficiencies in NH projects have become a cause of concern, as these have attracted criticism from the public.

stories.title: Parliament may be reconvened, hints Rijiju, brings delimitation bill in focus
stories.summary: Though Rijiju made no categorical comment about an immediate session to take up the constitutional amendment bill to implement the law from 2029 with a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, he said Parliament has been reconvened in the past after a session was not prorogued. The monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.

stories.title: BPCL CMD says mulling E10 petrol option, then walks back
stories.summary: “We are looking into various related aspects but nothing has been finalised yet,” said the chief of the oil marketing company that is the leading coordinator for the ethanol blending programme. However, a few hours later, amid growing scrutiny, he claimed that he had been misquoted. “His response is being misquoted to suggest as if E10 is being considered as an option, which is not correct, it said.

stories.title: An Oklahoma woman opened a $1,373 electric bill, including a $598 deposit after late payments
stories.summary: As intense summer heat sweeps through the region, many households are grappling with skyrocketing electricity bills. Raelynn McMurchy's monthly statement doubled, igniting discussions on much-needed policy reforms. Oklahoma's power provider continues to disconnect customers in alarming numbers, leaving local charities to struggle for emergency support. Residents are calling for robust measures to prevent power shutoffs during the scorching months.

stories.title: Death penalty sought for man who killed Indian-origin grocery store owner Suresh Patel in Tennessee; shot Bangladeshi immigrant Shahed Rana Mohsin at a gas station
Nepal flood toll hits 392; 288 Indians among 1,468 missing
stories.summary: Latest available National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority tally put 910 people missing or “out of contact” in Nepal, which includes MEA’s assessment of 288 Indian citizens remaining “uncontactable” as of late Thursday evening. Nepal has not released a nationality-wise breakup of those dead, leaving the number of Indian fatalities, if any, unconfirmed. Across the border in Tibet, Chinese authorities reported 558 people missing as of Thursday morning.

stories.title: In 2020, Albany brought 1,500 feet of Patroon Creek back above ground after decades in a pipe
stories.summary: Engineers in Albany revitalized Patroon Creek by daylighting it, restoring its natural flow and creating vital green spaces. This innovative project significantly bolstered flood protection for surrounding neighborhoods. Post-restoration water monitoring assured that the creek effectively managed heavy rains, tackling water quality concerns while promoting a healthier aquatic ecosystem. The initiative not only enhances the environment but also provides recreational opportunities for the local community.

stories.title: An Ohio couple spent 30 years in the country for pieces of an amusement park that closed in 1984
stories.summary: Completion of the exterior work at Youngstown's Idora Park museum marks a significant milestone, with the Mahoning Valley Historical Society now moving forward into the interior design stage. The museum is dedicated to exhibiting a diverse collection of park artifacts collected through the years. Fundraising initiatives are actively underway to support the project's financial objectives, reinforcing the museum's mission to honor and convey Youngstown's vibrant cultural history.

stories.title: In 2021, Pennsylvania removed a 128-year-old dam; Sterry Creek’s original channel was still intact
stories.summary: The Nature Conservancy has successfully revitalized the O'Conner Reservoir dam from the late 1800s, allowing Sterry Creek to revert to its natural course. By lowering the reservoir's water levels and excavating the embankment, they eliminated the need for a costly artificial channel, thus improving local water health. This project also established a natural floodplain and reconnected important stream habitats to the expansive Lackawanna River watershed.

stories.title: Indian-origin grandmother with Green Card allowed to leave ICE detention but her immigration case continues. DHS calls her flight risk
India, US officials discuss nuclear energy cooperation in Washington
Cong declines NC invite to join Omar govt, cites ‘principled stand’ on J&K’s statehood
Kishtwar forced abortion death: Three more held; total arrests now 5
DPDP Act compliance gets Cabinet Secretary’s push; ministries, states put on timeline
'I stopped all my internet accounts': 70-year-old Australian man falls in love with six-fingered deepfake, transfers $180,000
US man arrested with gun near Trump’s LA golf course sent for mental health evaluation
160 district hospitals to get emergency trauma care boost by March 2027
A London apartment burned down in 2024 and left more than 80 people homeless
stories.summary: Residents of London are still obligated to pay mortgages on homes that were ruined by fire, despite the complexities in the ongoing legal struggles involving insurers and administrators. The building's freeholder has gone into administration following the destruction. Consequently, residents are stuck facing demands for unpaid service charges relative to properties that no longer exist, intensifying pressure on the government regarding building safety and restitution for the affected individuals.

stories.title: In 1776, a Gettysburg minister built his stone home; 200 years later a young couple saved it from...
stories.summary: Celebrating its 250th anniversary, Gettysburg's historic Dobbin House hosted a memorable consecration ceremony. Originally completed in 1776, this iconic building has played various roles over the centuries. In the 1970s, local patrons Jacqueline and Gary White saved it from being demolished. The upcoming unveiling of Dobbin House Square promises new museum exhibits. The anniversary festivities will include reenactments, enchanting music, and a ceremonial cannon salute.

stories.title: NTPC working to reach 244-GW capacity by 2037
'If they speak Hindi, we'll beat them up': MNS warns auto drivers, takes shot at CM Fadnavis
14-year-old New Hampshire gamer built 3D-printed VR controller after he couldn't grip a standard one
stories.summary: Fourteen-year-old Scott Merrow from Auburn, New Hampshire, could not grip the standard left-hand controller used for virtual reality games because of his “little hand”. Instead of giving up gaming, he worked with his mechanical engineer uncle to develop an adaptive VR controller. After three prototypes, Scott created a 3D-printed arm sleeve with a sensor that lets him control the game using pressure.

stories.title: Florida couple declared dead in helicopter crash in Kenya; thieves break in their house, steal Porsche, Land Rover in less than 24 hours. Then comes a twist in court
How Zohran Mamdani mastered Trump's 'Art of the Deal'
stories.summary: Interestingly, Donald Trump laid down 11 rules for successful deal-making inThe Art of the Deal. Mamdani’s first eight months as mayor suggest that he has followed Trump’s rules more faithfully than most people who actually work for Trump.

stories.title: More than 100 years ago, red mangroves were introduced to Hawaii; now crews are trying to...
stories.summary: In Hawaii, environmental teams are embarking on an ambitious project to eradicate invasive red mangroves, targeting nearly two miles of waterways in Kailua. This initiative is vital for preserving endangered native waterbirds while simultaneously addressing environmental degradation. The involvement of community volunteers and organizations is essential for this extensive, multi-year effort, funded by national foundations and set to commence in September 2026.

stories.title: Malaysian university fires professor who claimed Malays could fly; they taught Romans shipbuilding
Cyberattack hits 3 UK airports, data of 8.7m customers leaked; spokesperson says 'no operational disruption'
Thieves stole 400,000 oysters worth about $350,000 from an Australian farm; the grower says...
stories.summary: Waterborne thieves stole 400,000 young oysters from a New South Wales farm. This large-scale theft wiped out a third of the grower's total stock. The stolen oysters were valued at approximately $350,000 AUD and were crucial for Christmas sales. Police are investigating the incident, which could set the business back years. The theft highlights concerns about agricultural crime in Australia's aquaculture industry.

stories.title: Texas officer indicted on 100 felony counts after 45,000 database searches
From today, households across Great Britain can plug solar panels into a standard socket
stories.summary: New regulations have been established, permitting plug-in solar kits of up to 800 watts in residential settings. These systems promise substantial annual savings on electricity expenses, making renewable energy more attainable for renters and flat owners alike. Rigorous safety standards are in place to ensure secure connections, mitigating any electrical risks. This breakthrough aligns with Great Britain's rising demand for sustainable residential solar energy solutions.

stories.title: Hegseth asked top US military general to drop Kid Rock helicopter probe before firing him: Report
Meet Daniel Janzen, the ecologist restoring 169,000 hectares of Costa Rica
stories.summary: Daniel Janzen, a pioneering biologist, significantly advanced tropical ecosystem research and conservation initiatives. Through his innovative work in Costa Rica's Guanacaste Conservation Area, he fostered collaboration with local communities. For many years, Janzen scrutinised the intricate dynamics between flora and fauna, culminating in a large-scale conservation area and establishing a notable legacy in science that underscores the importance of ecosystem comprehension for ongoing protection.

stories.title: PM Modi to meet Putin on SCO summit sidelines during Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit
In a 1st, TN CM Vijay ditches his chair, sits with ministers in assembly
Evening news wrap: China warns barrier lake near Nepal border could breach; 288 Indians unaccounted for in Nepal floods, and more
stories.summary: A critical situation is unfolding as a barrier lake close to the Nepal border risks a breach within a mere three days. Recent floods and mudslides have tragically resulted in over 273 fatalities and 1,300 individuals still unaccounted for. In a response effort, India is seeking to trace 288 missing citizens and has dispatched vital relief supplies.

stories.title: In 1904, this 1,227-foot Cincinnati warehouse was among the world’s longest; 210 feet are now gone
stories.summary: Longworth Hall in Cincinnati, once 1,227 feet long and among the world’s longest buildings, has been shortened by about 210 feet for a new Ohio River bridge. The historic 1904 railroad warehouse will retain most of its structure, while bricks from the demolished section will be reused to rebuild its east end.

stories.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat's US event organiser AHEAD’s X account suspended ahead of programme
'It's your sense of entitlement': US officials slam Indian-origin entrepreneur Ankit Gupta over H-1B comments
stories.summary: Ankit Gupta found himself under fire for his controversial social media posts about H-1B visas. The Inspector General of the US Department of Labor condemned his comments, while FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson voiced strong disapproval of Gupta's perspectives on American labor. His defense of H-1B worker hiring sparked accusations of disrespect towards American citizens, leading many social media users to urge Y Combinator to take action against him.

stories.title: US citizenship applicants face renewed neighbourhood scrutiny under new USCIS guidance
Researchers examined whales stranded around Hawaii that had swallowed marine debris, including...
stories.summary: Discarded fishing nets and plastic bags are wreaking havoc on marine ecosystems in the Pacific. A comprehensive thirteen-year study revealed that pilot whales have ingested alarming amounts of synthetic debris. Researchers found thousands of plastic fragments lodged within the stomachs of the examined whales. Such plastic pollution brings grave long-term health risks to these mammals, underscoring the critical need to combat ocean waste.

stories.title: 'Nation is confused': Congress alleges 'plan to change narrative' on China role in Op Sindoor
'Cordial discussions': JP Nadda meets anti-reservation group after Jantar Mantar protest
Nepal flood fury: How it started
Tourists carved 350 bamboo stalks in Japan; officials now want the grove out of reach
stories.summary: Kyoto’s famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is facing growing damage from tourists carving names and other writing into bamboo stalks. A city inspection found around 350 damaged plants since spring 2025. In response, Kyoto officials plan to cut about 30 sq m of bamboo as a special preservation measure and move the grove further away from the path to prevent visitors from reaching the stalks.

stories.title: A Chinese American Army veteran turned a mountain into a ski resort; it’s now joining a state park
stories.summary: In the 1950s, Chinese American Army veteran Joseph Tso bought a mountain property near Ellenville, New York, and developed a hotel and ski area there. The resort became the country’s only Chinese American-owned and operated ski resort. In 2026, the 440-acre Mt. Cathalia property was acquired for $3.3 million and is planned to become part of Minnewaska State Park Preserve.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Isaac Asimov: "The saddest aspect of life right now is…"
stories.summary: Humanity gains knowledge rapidly, but wisdom lags behind societal needs. Technological advancements offer immense possibilities, yet ethical considerations remain crucial. Wisdom involves understanding consequences and societal impact beyond immediate gains. The information age amplifies this gap, making context and analysis vital. Progress requires reflection and experience, not just accelerated creation.

stories.title: Delhi HC quashes criminal defamation case against senior advocate Pinaki Misra
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has dismissed the criminal defamation case against senior advocate Pinaki Misra, stating that there was insufficient evidence to support the accusation that he harmed the complainant's reputation. The court emphasized that allowing the case to proceed would not serve justice and would unnecessarily place Misra on trial.

stories.title: Russian military lieutenant colonel killed in St Petersburg car blast, wife injured
‘Worst 24 hours of my life’: Indo-American doctor appeals for help after parents go missing in Nepal floods
'Issue of enormous significance': Kharge writes to PM Modi, demands 25-year delimitation freeze
'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Massachusetts officer resigns after allegedly using police databases to track ex-partner
Quote of the day by Plutarch: "The mind is not a vessel to be filled, but a fire..."
US college student shot dead by police after knocking on wrong house amid burglary call
Hindu priest arrested in Canada for sexually assaulting woman under guise of healing
North Carolina student to build first SparkNC VR learning unit
In 2025, a US startup used ‘underground lightning’ to crack rock and unlock hydrogen
stories.summary: Eden GeoPower is investigating an innovative hydrogen generation technique by employing electrical pulses to crack deep-seated rock formations. This groundbreaking approach paves the way for water to interact with minerals, leading to enhanced hydrogen production as observed in laboratory tests. Ongoing field trials aim to determine the commercial feasibility of this promising method.

stories.title: Yellowstone visitors used Handkerchief Pool like washing machine; cleanup removed 1.5 bushels debris
stories.summary: Yellowstone’s Handkerchief Pool was once a popular attraction where visitors put handkerchiefs into its water and watched them disappear and return. Its activity stopped after a log blocked the pool in 1926. A 1929 cleanup removed 1.5 bushels of debris, including over 100 hairpins, coins and a horseshoe.

stories.title: From E coli to amenity gaps: What CAG found beyond the railway makeover
Garg Aviation’s trainer aircraft crashes in Kanpur, 2 killed
stories.summary: A training aircraft crashed near Kanpur Civil Airport on Thursday. The Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft was on a local training flight when it went down. Both the trainee and instructor pilots on board sustained fatal injuries in the accident. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and its circumstances. This crash follows a previous incident involving the same aircraft in June 2026.

stories.title: Apollo 15’s Genesis Rock, found in 1971, revealed a piece of the Moon’s 4-billion-year-old crust
stories.summary: Apollo 15 astronauts discovered an unusually bright rock near Spur Crater on the Moon. This sample, known as the Genesis Rock, is an anorthosite and about four billion years old. Scientists believe it represents a piece of the Moon's primordial crust. Its mineral composition offers valuable clues about early lunar geological history. This ancient sample continues to aid understanding of the Moon's evolution.

stories.title: Australian platypuses rescued during drought quickly rebuilt their home ranges after returning to the wild
stories.summary: Following a five-month recovery from severe drought conditions, platypuses were reintroduced to their original habitats. In an eighteen-month study, researchers tracked their activities as they reintegrated into the wild. The animals displayed quick adaptation, rediscovering their typical movement patterns and preferred foraging spots, thereby emphasizing the importance of effective conservation efforts for aquatic wildlife amidst environmental stressors.

stories.title: Who are India's NEET youth? What NITI's 8.7 crore figure really tells us
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog report identifies significant barriers to youth employment and skilling in India. Existing skilling programs often lack outcome orientation and placement support for participants. The report suggests affordable training and combining learning with earning opportunities. Bridging this gap is very important for realizing India's demographic dividend by 2047.

stories.title: Over 76 lakh women registered under Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna: Punjab CM Mann
stories.summary: In Punjab, more than 76 lakh women have successfully registered for the Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, with the state government allocating an impressive Rs 2,381 crore to support 68.06 lakh beneficiaries. Under this initiative, women from the general category receive Rs 1,000 a month, while those from the Scheduled Caste category benefit with Rs 1,500. Additionally, 'Satkar Sakhis' have been rewarded with Rs 52.

stories.title: Powai teenager wins ten awards at the prestigious Shanmukhananda annual music competition 2026
Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Only 20% LPG consumers applied for PNG connections
stories.summary: The transition from LPG to piped gas has seen a mere 20% uptake among eligible consumers, which remains a concern for the government despite extensive promotional efforts. Households have been targeted with informational notices and camps, but the challenge persists. To spur conversion, new incentives for distributors are being rolled out, complemented by the introduction of nodal officers to enhance administrative support in the field.

stories.title: Mohan Bhagwat in US: Hindu American Foundation issues security advisory ahead of RSS event
stories.summary: The Hindu American Foundation issued an advisory for an upcoming RSS event in New York City. Activists have attempted to disrupt and cancel the celebration, prompting calls for vigilance. New York City Mayor Mamdani expressed no support for the event but cited jurisdictional limitations. The USCIRF urged US government sanctions against the RSS for alleged religious freedom violations.

stories.title: COP17: New global architecture for drought resilience launched at UNCCD meet
stories.summary: The UNCCD has launched a Drought Resilience Index and Investment Facility. This initiative aims to strengthen global drought resilience by 2050. New AI tools will help countries assess and manage drought risks effectively. The facility will unlock finance for water security and land restoration projects. India advocates for proactive, technology-enabled drought preparedness over reactive relief.

stories.title: Nepal floods: India steps in with emergency helplines for stranded nationals
Over 10,000 lucky coins removed from Giant’s Causeway to protect ancient rocks
From Tokyo to London, heatwaves send men to work in shorts
stories.summary: Japan’s capital led the way. This year the metropolitan govt’s long-standing no-tie, no-jacket “Cool Biz” campaign took a step further by encouraging its staff to ditch long trousers, and even try T-shirts and sneakers. As heatwaves mounted across Europe, other workers followed in Tokyo’s wake, sometimes with the encouragement of authorities and management, sometimes without.

stories.title: Qatar PM to visit Tehran as Iran-US tensions persist over Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: The latest visit comes as the conflict approaches its sixth month. Although major fighting has largely stopped, the two sides have yet to make progress towards a lasting diplomatic settlement. One of the biggest unresolved issues is the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which a major share of the world's oil supplies normally passes.

stories.title: Over 61,000 wait for kidney transplants
stories.summary: The committee on health and family welfare has recommended that kidney transplant facilities be expanded to at least three govt medical colleges in large states and one in every small state and UT, besides setting time-bound targets to increase organ retrieval centres and transplant infrastructure, particularly in underserved and hilly regions.

stories.title: Caste count method in Census ‘misleading’: Congress letter to PM
stories.summary: “We don’t approve of the caste census being done through this methodology. Govt should cancel the present questionnaire and prepare a fresh one through consultations with political parties, experts, and the public so that a correct headcount of every caste and community is collected and the caste census is precise, relevant, and beneficial,” it said.

stories.title: ‘Jhooth ki goonj’ site ‘fact-checks’ Rahul’s student meet claims
stories.summary: The digital counterpunch against Rahul’s campaign obviously complements BJP’s efforts, but the party has denied any association with the website. The website itself makes no direct mention of the people behind it, but as it trended on social media, some attributed its creation to “nationalist researchers” and Gen Z-ers, the very generation Rahul is targeting in his hops across cities.

stories.title: Dissidents push for Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee chief to end Punjab crisis
stories.summary: A group of dissidents that includes senior netas like Charanjit Channi and Sukhjinder Randhawa has been seeking the replacement of state chief Amarinder Raja Warring ever since the AICC announced a clutch of poll-related panels while sticking with Warring at the helm two months ago. Now, sources said, the dissidents themselves have proposed that a Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief be appointed.

stories.title: Nepal flood: Centre puts Bihar & UP on high alert as NDRF deploys teams
stories.summary: “Govt of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis. I spoke with CMs of Bihar and UP regarding the disaster in Nepal. In border areas likely to be affected, local administration and rescue teams, along with NDRF, have been placed on high alert,” Shah said on X, expressing condolences to families of those who lost their loved ones in the disaster.

stories.title: Man searching Polish scrapyard finds 1,800-year-old Roman shield with human bones
160 killed in deadly Nepal deluge; at least 133 Indians among 844 missing
stories.summary: Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.

stories.title: UN panel report on minorities is politically motivated: Govt
stories.summary: UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination had “highlighted” in a report the increase in law enforcement operations targeting “Rohingya, Bengali-speaking Muslims, migrants and asylum-seekers, particularly following the 2017 home affairs order and the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in Kashmir”. Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “India rejects any politically motivated, highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves.”

stories.title: 3 lakh tonnes of refined sugar to enter market
stories.summary: Govt had allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar and also allowed the processors to sell some refined sugar, which was meant for export only, in the domestic market. Officials and industry insiders said at least 3 lakh tonnes of processed sugar could come into the market quickly. The subsequent import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will help tide over any supply issue. Meanwhile, the ex-mill price of sugar has gone down by 20% in the past 10 days.

stories.title: As obesity rises, Supreme Court puts govt on notice over junk food labels
stories.summary: The order, in response to a PIL filed by NGO ‘3S and Our HEALTH Society’ which moved SC through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi, comes as govt has seemed reluctant to implement front-of-pack warning labels on junk food. SC said food with high salt, sugar, saturated fat and calories could lead to health risks and clearer nutrition information must be displayed to help to make healthier choices.

stories.title: Low beam by default: Centre to tighten headlamp norms
stories.summary: The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules. Amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made because efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.

stories.title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
stories.summary: These included advancing consultations for an “early and substantial harvest” of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing the ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, and expanding trans-border trade and river cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the talks.

stories.title: SC judge complains against Rajasthan acting CJ; CJI Surya Kant seeks response
stories.summary: ustice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC. CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said.

stories.title: In 1952, one of England’s rarest moths was last recorded at a Northumberland estate
stories.summary: Conservationists have triumphantly rediscovered a rare moth population that had been missing for seventy years at the National Trust's Wallington Estate in Northumberland. Thanks to extensive habitat restoration efforts, this elusive species, once threatened by extinction in England, has made a hopeful return, inspiring optimism for uncovering other hidden insect populations.

stories.title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
stories.summary: “Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to. The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found.

stories.title: Yale researchers find a new way to make PFAS easier to remove and destroy
6 dead, 3 hurt as vehicle falls into gorge in J&K’s Poonch
stories.summary: The accident occurred around 5.30pm. Officials suspected the driver had lost control of the vehicle, which rolled into the gorge, killing six occupants — Mohd Shafiq (32), Nazakat Hussain (34), Sheraz Ahmed (30), Musarat Naz (19), Mohd Fareed (21), and Zulfat Bi (25) — on the spot, police said. Upon receiving information, cops reached the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of locals.
